name: docker.engine.dockerd-plugins-api
observations: dockerd plugin API: Pluggable extension surface for storage, volume, network, log, authorization. Plugins registered via `docker plugin install` or via daemon-side `authorization-plugins` config. Source of failures when a third-party volume/log driver is misconfigured (daemon won't start, or `docker volume create -d <plugin>` errors).

name: docker.engine.image
observations: Image: A read-only template comprising an ordered stack of layers + a config blob (entrypoint, env, exposed ports, default user). Identified by a content-addressable digest (sha256:…) and 0+ tag references. The thing `docker pull`/`docker build` produces and `docker run` consumes. Stored under `/var/lib/docker/<storage-driver>/` (classic) or `/var/lib/containerd/` (containerd image store).

name: docker.engine.storage-driver
observations: Storage driver: The pluggable component that manages how image layers and the container writable layer are stored on disk for the legacy 'classic' image store. Configured via daemon.json `storage-driver`. Drivers: overlay2 (default for upgraded installs), fuse-overlayfs (rootless fallback pre-5.11 kernels), btrfs, zfs, vfs (no copy-on-write — only for testing/debug), windowsfilter (Windows). Switching requires daemon stop, data-root migration. Docker Engine 29.0+ uses containerd snapshotters by default for fresh installs.

name: docker.engine.btrfs-driver
observations: btrfs storage driver: Storage driver using btrfs subvolumes/snapshots for layer separation. Requires `/var/lib/docker/` to live on a btrfs filesystem. Block-level CoW; better than overlay2 for write-heavy workloads but requires significant memory tuning.

name: docker.engine.seccomp-profile
observations: seccomp profile (engine usage): Kernel syscall filter applied to a container. Docker ships a default profile blocking ~50 syscalls. Override per-container via `--security-opt seccomp=<path-to-profile.json>` (or `unconfined`). Daemon-wide default switchable via daemon.json `seccomp-profile`. Profile schema (defaultAction, syscalls[], etc.) catalogued in docker/security.

name: docker.engine.container-state-running
observations: Container state: running: `status=running`. Container's pid 1 is alive. The default 'happy path' state. Reflected in `State.Running=true` of `docker inspect`.

name: docker.engine.container
observations: Container: A running (or stopped) instance of an image — a process tree wrapped in namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, and a layered filesystem (image's lowerdirs + a writable upperdir). Has an id, optional name, status, exit code, networks, mounts, log driver. The unit `docker ps` lists; the unit `docker run` creates.

name: docker.engine.bind-mount
observations: Bind mount: Direct mount of a host-fs path into a container, bypassing Docker-managed storage. Specified via `--mount type=bind,src=<host-path>,dst=<container-path>` or `-v <host-path>:<container-path>`. Best for sharing source code in dev or sharing host config files (`/etc/resolv.conf`-style). Failure mode: with `-v`, missing host path is auto-created as a directory; with `--mount`, missing host path errors out unless `bind-create-src` is set.

name: docker.engine.overlay2-driver
observations: overlay2 storage driver: Default classic storage driver on most Linux distros. Uses kernel OverlayFS to union-mount image layers (lowerdir, read-only) under a per-container writable layer (upperdir). Requires kernel ≥ 4.0 (RHEL/CentOS 3.10.0-514). Supports xfs (with d_type=true / ftype=1) and ext4. Up to 128 lower layers. Stores data under `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/<id>/{lower,merged,upper,work,diff,link}`. Page-cache shared across containers — memory-efficient. Copy-up on first write of an image-layer file.

name: docker.engine.userns-remap
observations: User namespace remapping: Daemon option `userns-remap` mapping container root (uid 0) to a non-zero uid on the host. Reduces container-escape blast radius. Requires `/etc/subuid` + `/etc/subgid` entries. `userns-remap: default` uses `dockremap` user; `userns-remap: testuser` uses a named user. Bind-mounts and volumes get owned by the remapped uid — common foot-gun. Mutually exclusive with `--privileged`, `--ipc=host`, `--net=host`, `--pid=host` containers.

name: docker.engine.daemon-json
observations: daemon.json: The Docker daemon configuration file. Linux: `/etc/docker/daemon.json`. Rootless Linux: `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` (honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Windows: `C:\ProgramData\docker\config\daemon.json`. Plain JSON. Re-read on daemon (re)start; `systemctl reload docker` works for some keys (proxies, debug, log-level), full restart needed for others. Daemon refuses to start on invalid JSON OR when the same option is given both as a flag and in the file.

name: docker.engine.cgroup-fs
observations: cgroup filesystem: `/sys/fs/cgroup/`. Where the kernel exposes cgroup controllers (cpu, memory, pids, blkio, freezer, devices). Docker creates a per-container cgroup under `/sys/fs/cgroup/<controller>/docker/<container-id>` (cgroup v1) or `/sys/fs/cgroup/<slice>/docker-<id>.scope` (cgroup v2 + systemd). Modify a container's resource limits at runtime by writing to these knobs (or use `docker update`).

name: docker.engine.container-state-created
observations: Container state: created: `docker container ls -a --filter status=created`. The container has been created (`docker create`) but not started. Has an id and config but no running process. Resources allocated; rootfs prepared; pid namespace not yet entered.

name: docker.engine.slim-image
observations: Slim container image: A container image stripped of build tools, package managers, and shells — only the application binary and its runtime deps. Smaller (faster pulls, less network), more secure (smaller attack surface). Trade-off: missing `ps`, `cat`, `bash` etc. makes debugging hard. Counterstrategies: ephemeral debug sidecars sharing the target's pid/network namespace.

name: docker.engine.journald-log-driver
observations: journald logging driver: Sends container logs to the host's systemd-journald. Each entry tagged with container_id, container_name. Filterable via `journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=…`. `docker logs` still works (daemon reads journal). Useful when the host already centralizes logs via journald.

name: docker.engine.fluentd-log-driver
observations: fluentd logging driver: Forwards container logs to a Fluentd daemon over forward protocol. Requires fluentd reachable at `fluentd-address` (default localhost:24224). `fluentd-async=true` decouples container start from fluentd availability. Optional buffer with `fluentd-buffer-limit`, retry policy via `fluentd-max-retries` + `fluentd-retry-wait`. `docker logs` does NOT work for containers using fluentd — daemon doesn't keep a local cache.

name: docker.engine.ipv6-support
observations: IPv6 support: Linux-only. Enabled per-network via `docker network create --ipv6` or daemon-wide for the default bridge via daemon.json `ipv6: true` + `fixed-cidr-v6` (e.g. `2001:db8:1::/64`). `ip6tables: true` (default) controls iptables-based v6 packet filtering. `default-address-pools` defines pools for dynamic /64 allocation; without v6 pools, Docker falls back to ULA (`fd00::/8`-derived) addressing. Requires `ip6_tables` kernel module loaded (auto-loaded on most distros; needs `modprobe ip6_tables` inside DinD).

name: docker.engine.tls-mtls-daemon-socket
observations: TLS / mTLS for daemon socket: Default daemon socket is the unprotected `/var/run/docker.sock` (root-equivalent for whoever can write to it). Listening on TCP without TLS = remote root. Enable TLS via daemon.json `tls`, `tlsverify`, `tlscacert`, `tlscert`, `tlskey` (or `dockerd --tls --tlsverify --tlscacert=… --tlscert=… --tlskey=…`). Default ports: 2376 with TLS, 2375 without. Client picks via `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` + `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`.

name: docker.engine.default-cgroupns-mode
observations: Default cgroup namespace mode: `default-cgroupns-mode` daemon-config controlling whether new containers get a private cgroup namespace (`private`) or share the host's (`host`). With cgroupv2-only kernels, private cgroupns is the modern default. Per-container override: `docker run --cgroupns=host|private`.

name: docker.engine.docker-root-dir
observations: Docker root dir: The on-disk directory the daemon stores everything under. Default `/var/lib/docker/` (Linux) / `C:\ProgramData\docker\` (Windows). Configured via daemon.json `data-root` (formerly `graph`). Subdirs include `image/`, `<storage-driver>/`, `volumes/`, `containers/`, `network/`, `swarm/`, `tmp/`. With containerd image store, image layers live under `/var/lib/containerd/` instead.

name: docker.engine.dockerignore
observations: .dockerignore: Build-context exclusion file (gitignore-style). Pattern matched against the build context root before transmission to the daemon/builder. Critical for build performance — without it, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, etc. get sent over the socket and slow every build. Engine perspective: implicit; the build engine reads it.

name: docker.engine.cgroup-v1
observations: cgroup v1: Legacy multi-hierarchy cgroup ABI. Per-controller subtrees (`/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu`, `…/memory`, etc.). Still in use on older distros; expected to be phased out. Engine resource flags map onto v1 controllers when v1 is active.

name: docker.engine.capability
observations: Linux capability (engine usage): Subdivision of root privileges. Docker drops most capabilities by default (drops include CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_MODULE). Re-add via `--cap-add=` (e.g., `--cap-add=NET_ADMIN` for tcpdump in container); drop further via `--cap-drop=ALL` + selective `--cap-add=`. `--privileged` ≈ all capabilities + access to host devices + AppArmor/Seccomp disabled.

name: docker.engine.container-state-paused
observations: Container state: paused: `status=paused`. Container processes frozen via cgroup freezer (v1) or cgroup.freeze (v2). Filesystem and network state preserved; processes don't run. `docker pause` / `docker unpause`. Rare in production; useful for snapshotting.

name: docker.engine.dockerfile
observations: Dockerfile: Build-recipe text file. Each instruction (FROM, RUN, COPY, ADD, CMD, ENTRYPOINT, ENV, ARG, LABEL, EXPOSE, VOLUME, USER, WORKDIR, HEALTHCHECK, ONBUILD, STOPSIGNAL, SHELL) becomes (potentially) one image layer. Engine perspective: the artifact `docker build`/`docker buildx build` consumes; full instruction surface is catalogued in docker/build-buildkit.

name: docker.engine.anonymous-volume
observations: Anonymous volume: A volume without a user-given name — Docker generates a random uuid. Created when `docker run -v /path` (no name before colon) or `--mount type=volume,dst=/path` (no src). Removed automatically only when the creating container was started with `--rm`. Otherwise must be pruned explicitly (`docker volume prune`); easy to leak.

name: docker.engine.devicemapper-driver
observations: devicemapper storage driver: Legacy block-level storage driver using LVM thin provisioning (devmapper-thinpool). Once the only RHEL/CentOS option pre-overlay2 on old kernels. Mostly retired; tunables `dm.basesize`, `dm.thinpooldev` retained for legacy installs.

name: docker.engine.restart-policy
observations: Restart policy: Per-container daemon-managed restart behavior. `--restart no` (default), `on-failure[:N]`, `always`, `unless-stopped`. Restart is by the daemon, NOT the OCI runtime — if dockerd is down, restarts pause. With Swarm, the equivalent is `deploy.restart_policy` and is managed by the swarm orchestrator instead.

name: docker.engine.container-state-stopped
observations: Container state: stopped: Filter alias — UI-side same as 'exited'. `State.Status=exited`, `State.Running=false`. Container's writable layer remains; restartable via `docker start`.

name: docker.engine.image-layer-digest
observations: Image layer digest: Content-addressable identifier for an image layer (`sha256:<hex>`). Two flavors: 'diff_id' (sha256 of the uncompressed tarball) and 'descriptor digest' (sha256 of the on-wire compressed blob). The pair is how the daemon dedupes layers across images and verifies pull integrity.

name: docker.engine.debug-sidecar
observations: Debug sidecar: A second container sharing the target container's namespaces (`--pid=container:<id>`, `--network=container:<id>`) used to bring in debug tooling without modifying the target. Pattern: `docker run -it --rm --pid=container:my-app --network=container:my-app nicolaka/netshoot bash` to run tcpdump/strace/ss against the slim target. iximiuz/cdebug automates this.

name: docker.engine.docker-build-context
observations: Docker build context: The directory tree the docker CLI sends to the daemon/builder when running `docker build .`. Filtered by `.dockerignore`. Engine perspective: streamed over the API; the size of the context is a real perf factor (slow build = wasted time on a 2GB context). Local context (`.`), URL contexts (`https://github.com/foo/bar.git#main:subdir`), stdin (`-`) all supported.

name: docker.engine.docker-cli
observations: docker CLI: User-facing client (`docker`) that talks to dockerd over the API. Stateless beyond the per-user `~/.docker/config.json`. Honors `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY`, `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_API_VERSION`, `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM`, `DOCKER_BUILDKIT`. When `docker ps` returns 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon', the CLI couldn't reach the socket — daemon-side, not client-side.

name: docker.engine.vfs-driver
observations: vfs storage driver: Storage driver of last resort. No copy-on-write — every layer is a full copy. Massive disk usage, slow. Works on any filesystem (no kernel features required). Use only for debugging or environments where no other driver is supported.

name: docker.engine.json-file-log-driver
observations: json-file logging driver: Default logging driver. Caches container logs as JSON under `/var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log`. Each line is a JSON object with `{log, stream, time}`. Default has NO rotation — daemon never trims the file; long-running containers can fill the disk. Set `max-size` and `max-file` log-opts to enable rotation. Stays default for backwards compat with Kubernetes.

name: docker.engine.copy-on-write
observations: Copy-on-write (CoW): Pattern: shared read-only data; write triggers a private copy. Image layers are CoW. overlay2 copies the WHOLE FILE on first write (file-granular CoW), so writing a single byte in a 1GB log file copies the full GB to the upperdir. Block-level CoW drivers (btrfs/zfs) don't have this problem but have other ones. For write-heavy workloads, prefer volumes (bypass storage driver entirely).

name: docker.engine.image-pull-policy
observations: Image pull policy: `docker run --pull` controls when to fetch the image: `missing` (default — pull if not present locally), `always` (always check the registry), `never` (use only local). Same semantics as Kubernetes `imagePullPolicy`. Critical for reproducible deploys (always vs missing) and air-gapped envs (never).

name: docker.engine.docker-image-history
observations: Image history: `docker history <image>` shows each layer with its created-by command and size. Useful to find the layer that bloated an image (e.g., a leaked apt cache, a forgotten temp file). When chasing 'why is this image 2GB', `docker history` + a known-good base = a 5-second diagnosis.

name: docker.engine.named-volume
observations: Named volume: A volume with an explicit user-given name (`docker volume create my-vol` or `docker run -v my-vol:/data`). Survives container removal indefinitely; must be removed explicitly via `docker volume rm` or pruned via `docker volume prune`.

name: docker.engine.local-log-driver
observations: local logging driver: Recommended replacement for json-file. Performs log rotation by default (max-size=20m, max-file=5, compress=true). Uses a more efficient binary file format. Same `docker logs` UX as json-file. Doesn't ship a separate read API beyond the daemon's.

name: docker.engine.health-check
observations: Health check: Per-container probe defined either by HEALTHCHECK in the Dockerfile or via `--health-cmd` + `--health-interval`/`--health-retries`/`--health-timeout`/`--health-start-period`. Surfaces in `docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}'` as starting/healthy/unhealthy. Compose `depends_on.<svc>.condition: service_healthy` builds on it.

name: docker.engine.docker-sock
observations: docker.sock: The Unix domain socket the docker CLI talks to dockerd over. Default `/var/run/docker.sock`. Owned by `root:docker` typically; membership in the `docker` group = root-equivalent on the host (a container can be launched with the host fs bind-mounted). 'Got permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket' = client uid not in `docker` group OR socket file's group is wrong.

name: docker.engine.oci-state-json
observations: OCI state.json: Per-container runtime state OCI runtimes maintain. Returned by `runc state`. Surface stays in docker/runtime; engine consumes it indirectly through containerd's task service.

name: docker.engine.container-state-exited
observations: Container state: exited: `status=exited`. Process completed (cleanly or via signal). `State.ExitCode` populated. Common values: 0 (clean), 1 (generic error), 125 (docker daemon error pre-runtime), 126 (entrypoint not executable), 127 (entrypoint not found), 137 (SIGKILL — usually OOM), 139 (SIGSEGV), 143 (SIGTERM). Containers in this state still consume disk for their writable layer until removed.

name: docker.engine.container-state-dead
observations: Container state: dead: `status=dead`. Container partially-removed and unable to be stopped/started. Usually indicates a daemon bug or stuck mount. Mitigation: `docker rm -f <id>`; if that fails, restart the daemon.

name: docker.engine.content-addressable
observations: Content-addressable storage: The principle that an image / layer / blob is identified by the hash of its bytes. Two pulls of the same digest are guaranteed identical bits. Foundation for layer dedup, pull-cache, and signing. Tags are mutable references to digests; pinning to digests gives reproducibility tags can't.

name: docker.engine.docker-engine
observations: Docker Engine: Umbrella term for the daemon-plus-runtime stack that runs containers on a host: dockerd (HTTP/REST API + image/volume/network management) on top of containerd (lifecycle, snapshotters) on top of an OCI runtime (runc by default). The product surface a Linux user installs as the `docker` package or via Docker Desktop. The 'engine' leaf focuses on dockerd and its on-host responsibilities; runtime internals (runc/containerd) are catalogued in the docker/runtime leaf.

name: docker.engine.runc
observations: runc: The default OCI runtime — a lightweight CLI that spawns and runs containers from an OCI bundle (`config.json` + rootfs). Invoked by the containerd shim. Exit code 137 = OOM (128+9). Fully detailed in docker/runtime; here only the engine-perspective: it's the thing that actually applies namespaces/cgroups/capabilities/seccomp to a container's pid 1.

name: docker.engine.crun
observations: crun: runc-compatible alternative OCI runtime written in C. Faster startup, lower memory than runc. Drop-in via daemon.json `runtimes` entry pointing `path` to the `crun` binary, then `docker run --runtime crun`. Equivalent surface to runc (config.json, capabilities, etc.); choice is mostly performance/footprint.

name: docker.engine.docker-context
observations: docker context: A named profile bundling endpoint URL + TLS materials, used to switch the CLI between local and remote daemons (or between rootful and rootless dockerds). `docker context ls` / `docker context use`. `DOCKER_CONTEXT` env var picks one for a single command. Avoids the foot-gun of forgetting `DOCKER_HOST` between shells.

name: docker.engine.image-layer
observations: Image layer: One unit in an image's stacked rootfs — corresponds to one Dockerfile instruction (FROM, RUN, COPY, ADD). Stored as a tarball under the storage driver's diff dir. Identified by a sha256 digest of its uncompressed content (diff_id). Layers are deduplicated across images; pulling a new image only fetches layers not already on disk.

name: docker.engine.container-process
observations: Container process (pid 1): The first process inside a container's pid namespace — what the entrypoint+cmd resolve to. By default, signals to the container (`docker stop`) go only to pid 1; if pid 1 doesn't propagate them, child processes don't see SIGTERM and the 10s grace period elapses to a SIGKILL. With `--init`, docker-init becomes pid 1 and forwards signals + reaps zombies.

name: docker.engine.gelf-log-driver
observations: gelf logging driver: Sends container logs to a Graylog/Logstash-compatible endpoint over UDP/TCP using the GELF format. Configured via `gelf-address`, `gelf-compression-type`, `gelf-tcp-max-reconnect`, `gelf-tcp-reconnect-delay`.

name: docker.engine.union-fs
observations: Union filesystem: The technique behind layered images: stack N read-only directories under one writable directory and present a single merged view. Implementations: OverlayFS (overlay2 driver), btrfs/zfs subvolumes, devicemapper thin-provisioning. Performance characteristic: read of an unmodified file resolves through the lowerdirs; first write triggers copy-up to the upperdir.

name: docker.engine.entrypoint-vs-cmd
observations: ENTRYPOINT vs CMD: ENTRYPOINT is the binary; CMD provides default arguments. `docker run <image>` runs `ENTRYPOINT CMD`. `docker run <image> bash` runs `ENTRYPOINT bash` (CMD is replaced). `docker run --entrypoint=sh <image>` overrides ENTRYPOINT to `sh`. Common confusion: shell-form (`CMD echo hi`) wraps in `/bin/sh -c`; exec-form (`CMD ["echo", "hi"]`) doesn't — only exec-form forwards signals correctly.

name: docker.engine.image-tag-mutability
observations: Image tag mutability: Tags are mutable refs in registries. `nginx:latest` today and `nginx:latest` tomorrow can be different bytes. Reproducibility / supply-chain best practice: pin to digest (`nginx@sha256:…`). The daemon's local image cache mitigates this slightly — once pulled, your local tag points at a fixed digest until you re-pull.

name: docker.engine.syslog-log-driver
observations: syslog logging driver: Sends logs to a syslog daemon (local socket or remote tcp/udp/tls endpoint). Configured via `syslog-address`, `syslog-facility`, `syslog-format` (rfc5424 vs rfc3164). TLS via `syslog-tls-ca-cert`, `syslog-tls-cert`, `syslog-tls-key`.

name: docker.engine.selinux-label
observations: SELinux label (engine usage): On SELinux-enabled distros, the daemon-wide `selinux-enabled: true` (and per-container `--security-opt label=…`) controls how container processes and files are labeled. Bind-mount `:z` / `:Z` modifies host labels (shared / private). Bind-mounting system dirs with `:Z` can render the host inoperable.

name: docker.engine.attached-vs-detached
observations: Attached vs detached: `docker run` without `-d` attaches the CLI to the container's stdio — when the CLI exits, the container is sent SIGTERM. `docker run -d` runs detached; the CLI returns immediately and the container keeps running. `docker attach <id>` re-attaches an existing container (lossy: the attach might receive partial historical output). For long-lived stuff, prefer `-d` + `docker logs -f`.

name: docker.engine.tmpfs-mount
observations: tmpfs mount: In-memory mount; data lives in container memory and is destroyed when the container stops. `--mount type=tmpfs,dst=/path` or `--tmpfs /path`. Configurable via `tmpfs-size` (bytes) and `tmpfs-mode` (octal). For non-persistent state — caches, runtime files — that you don't want hitting the writable layer (avoids storage-driver overhead for hot paths).

name: docker.engine.mount-point
observations: Mount point: The container-side path where a volume / bind / tmpfs is attached, plus its mode (RW or RO), driver, propagation. Surfaced as the `Mounts[]` array in `docker inspect`. Each mount point records `Type` (volume/bind/tmpfs), `Source` (host path or volume mountpoint), `Destination` (container path), `Mode`, `RW`, `Propagation`.

name: docker.engine.zfs-driver
observations: zfs storage driver: Storage driver using zfs datasets/snapshots for layers. Requires `/var/lib/docker/` on a zfs filesystem. Block-level CoW. Good for high-density (PaaS) workloads. Requires substantial RAM (ZFS ARC).

name: docker.engine.iptables-management
observations: iptables management: Daemon-managed iptables rules for NAT, filtering, isolation between user-defined networks. Toggled via daemon.json `iptables: true` (default). Disabling means you own the rules — `docker run -p 80:80` won't actually publish without your DNAT. Detail-level chains (DOCKER, DOCKER-USER, DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1/2) live in docker/networking. Engine perspective: a daemon switch, off by default risks no-network at all.

name: docker.engine.oom-score-adj
observations: OOM score adjustment: `oom-score-adjust` daemon-config sets dockerd's own kernel OOM-killer score (-1000..1000); `--oom-score-adj` per-container does the same for the container init. Lower = less likely to be killed by the OOM killer. Default 0; -500 commonly used to keep dockerd alive when host is under memory pressure.

name: docker.engine.signal-propagation
observations: Signal propagation: `docker stop` sends SIGTERM (configurable via `--stop-signal` or Dockerfile STOPSIGNAL) to the container's pid 1, waits the grace period (`--stop-timeout`, default 10s), then SIGKILL. If pid 1 is a shell wrapping the real binary, the signal often goes to the shell, not the binary. Two fixes: exec-form ENTRYPOINT (`["binary"]`), or `--init` (docker-init forwards signals to all processes in the container's pgrp).

name: docker.engine.containerd
observations: containerd: The container lifecycle daemon Docker delegates to for create/start/stop/exec. Below dockerd; above runc. Owns its own snapshotters, content store, and image store. Reachable on its own socket (`/run/containerd/containerd.sock`). When you see 'containerd image store', this is the storage backend; when you see 'containerd snapshotter', this is the per-driver layer manager (overlayfs, native, btrfs, zfs, devmapper). Detailed surface lives in docker/runtime.

name: docker.engine.containerd-shim
observations: containerd shim: A small per-container process that decouples a container's lifecycle from the containerd daemon. Lets containerd be restarted without killing every container. Standard shim is `containerd-shim-runc-v2`; alternative shims (kata, gVisor, Wasm runtimes) implement the v2 shim API and ship as `containerd-shim-<name>-v1` binaries placed on PATH. Picked via `--runtime <fully-qualified-name>` on `docker run` or via daemon.json `runtimes` map.

name: docker.engine.linux-namespace
observations: Linux namespace (engine usage): Kernel isolation primitive Docker uses to give each container its own view of pids/networking/mounts/uts/ipc/users/cgroups/time. Per-container engine flags: `--pid=`, `--ipc=`, `--network=`, `--userns=`, `--cgroupns=` accept either a private namespace, `host` (share with the host), or `container:<id>` (share with another container). The container/host duality is the most common cause of 'pid 1 inside the container is not really pid 1 of the host' confusion.

name: docker.engine.apparmor-profile
observations: AppArmor profile (engine usage): LSM profile applied per container on AppArmor-enabled distros (Ubuntu, Debian). Docker generates a default profile; override via `--security-opt apparmor=<profile-name>`. Detail in docker/security.

name: docker.engine.distroless
observations: Distroless image: A class of slim images (gcr.io/distroless/*, Chainguard Images) with no shell, no package manager, no debug tools — only the language runtime + app. `docker exec -it <distroless> sh` fails with `OCI runtime exec failed: exec: "sh": executable file not found`. Debug variants (e.g. `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs:debug`) include busybox; pure ones require sidecar-based debugging.

name: docker.engine.network
observations: Network (engine-perspective): A Docker-managed network endpoint a container attaches to. From the engine's point of view, just a logical attachment with an id, driver name, and per-container IP/MAC. The on-host implementation (linux-bridge, vxlan, ipvlan parent interface, iptables chains) lives in docker/networking. Engine surfaces it via `--network`, `docker network ls`, and the `NetworkSettings` block of `docker inspect`.

name: docker.engine.metrics-endpoint
observations: Daemon metrics endpoint: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint on the daemon. Configured via daemon.json `metrics-addr` (e.g. `127.0.0.1:9323`). Exposes `engine_daemon_*`, `engine_*`, build, network metrics. Bound to loopback by default — exposing on `0.0.0.0` opens an information-leak surface; consider an SSH tunnel or reverse-proxy. Metric names are explicitly subject to change (active development).

name: docker.engine.exit-code
observations: Container exit code: `docker inspect --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}' <id>`. Conventional codes: 0 success; 1 generic error; 125 daemon-side error before the entrypoint ran; 126 entrypoint exists but not executable; 127 entrypoint not found; 128+N indicates termination by signal N (137 = SIGKILL/OOM, 139 = SIGSEGV, 143 = SIGTERM). The most-asked production debugging question is 'why exit code 137' — answer is almost always cgroup memory limit hit (OOM-killer).

name: docker.engine.nicolaka-netshoot
observations: nicolaka/netshoot: De-facto-standard 'fat' debugging image: ip, ss, tcpdump, dig, nslookup, mtr, iperf, drill, ngrep, nmap, lsof, strace, busybox. Run as a debug sidecar to investigate slim containers, or to check networking from inside an overlay. Image at `nicolaka/netshoot`; ~50MB.

name: docker.engine.dockerd
observations: dockerd: The persistent Docker daemon process. Listens on a Unix socket (default `/var/run/docker.sock`) for the Docker Engine API; configurable to also listen on TCP for remote clients. Reads `/etc/docker/daemon.json` at startup; flag-form configuration overrides JSON. Reload-via-SIGHUP semantics for some keys; full restart required for others. The first thing to inspect when containers refuse to start, the API socket is denied, or images won't pull.

name: docker.engine.docker-init
observations: docker-init (tini): Minimal pid1-replacement injected via `--init` (or daemon-wide `init: true` in daemon.json). Reaps zombies and forwards signals so processes that don't expect to be pid1 don't leak children or ignore SIGTERM. Path configurable via `init-path`. Solves the 'docker stop hangs for 10s then SIGKILLs' symptom for naive entrypoints.

name: docker.engine.experimental-features
observations: Experimental features flag: Daemon-level `experimental: true` (or `dockerd --experimental`) gating non-stable features. Examples: containerd image store on older versions, certain BuildKit/Buildx behaviors. Required for some `metrics-addr` features. Per-CLI counterpart used to live in `~/.docker/config.json` `experimental: enabled`.

name: docker.engine.oci-image
observations: OCI image format: The image format Docker has aligned to since 2017 (Docker manifest v2-2 ≈ OCI image spec). Two manifest forms: per-platform manifest (descriptor list of layer descriptors + config descriptor) and image index (multi-arch — descriptor list of per-platform manifests). Detail in docker/runtime; engine perspective is 'this is what `docker pull` retrieves and `docker image inspect` displays'.

name: docker.engine.volume
observations: Volume: Docker-managed persistent storage outside any container's writable layer. Created via `docker volume create` or implicitly by `docker run -v name:/path`. Stored under `/var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data/`. Persists across container removal (unless container created with `--rm` and volume is anonymous). Preferred over bind mounts for portability — works the same on Linux/Windows hosts.

name: docker.engine.image-tag
observations: Image tag: A mutable human-readable name pointing at an image digest, e.g. `nginx:1.27`, `myapp:latest`. Stored in the daemon's image-reference index. `docker pull` resolves a tag to a digest; the tag-to-digest mapping can change (the registry may push a new image to the same tag) — the same `docker pull nginx:latest` two days apart can fetch different bytes. Pin to digests for reproducibility.

name: docker.engine.live-restore
observations: Live restore: Daemon configuration `live-restore: true` (or `dockerd --live-restore`) that lets containers keep running across daemon restarts/upgrades. On daemon upgrade the running containers don't lose their network interfaces or storage mounts. Patch upgrades only (`YY.MM.x`); skipped major upgrades may break the daemon's reconnect. Daemon-options that change (bridge IP, graph driver) prevent the reconnect — containers must be stopped manually. Linux-only; Swarm services excluded.

name: docker.engine.init-process-injection
observations: Init process injection: Daemon-level `init: true` (and `init-path` to swap the binary) injects docker-init / tini as pid 1 of every container so naive entrypoints get correct signal forwarding and zombie reaping. Per-container override: `docker run --init`.

name: docker.engine.containerd-sock
observations: containerd.sock: containerd's grpc socket (`/run/containerd/containerd.sock`). dockerd connects to it for container lifecycle ops. Diagnosing a 'docker daemon ok but containers won't start' often means inspecting this socket and the containerd logs separately.

name: docker.engine.pid1-zombie-reaping
observations: pid 1 zombie reaping: On Linux, pid 1 must reap orphaned children — otherwise the kernel leaves <defunct> entries indefinitely (kernel pid table fills). Most app servers (`node`, `python`, `java`) don't expect to be pid 1 and don't reap. Symptom: thousands of <defunct> child processes inside the container, or apparent FD/process exhaustion. Fix: run with `--init` (docker-init/tini becomes pid 1 and reaps) or use a runtime like supervisord/systemd inside.

name: docker.engine.tty-allocation
observations: TTY allocation: `-t` / `--tty` allocates a pseudo-TTY for the container's stdio. Combined with `-i` / `--interactive`, gives an interactive shell. Without `-t`, output isn't line-buffered the same way and many programs detect they're not on a terminal and don't print colors / prompts. Detached (`-d`) containers don't get a TTY — `docker logs` reads from the captured streams.

name: docker.engine.logging-driver
observations: Logging driver: Pluggable component that consumes container stdout/stderr. Default is json-file (no rotation — disk-fill foot-gun); local recommended for new installs. Configured per-daemon via daemon.json `log-driver` + `log-opts`, overridable per-container via `--log-driver` + `--log-opt`. Drivers: json-file, local, journald, syslog, fluentd, gelf, awslogs, splunk, etwlogs, gcplogs, none.

name: docker.engine.none-log-driver
observations: none logging driver: Discards all container logs. `docker logs` returns nothing. Used when you intentionally don't want stdout captured (the application logs elsewhere, e.g., directly to a log shipper from inside the container).

name: docker.engine.docker-config-dir
observations: Docker config dir (~/.docker/): Per-user CLI config: `~/.docker/config.json` (auths, default plugins, experimental, credsStore), contexts (`~/.docker/contexts/`), daemon-cert-dir (`~/.docker/<host>/{ca,cert,key}.pem`). `DOCKER_CONFIG` env var overrides.

name: docker.engine.oci-config-json
observations: OCI bundle config.json: The OCI runtime spec file dockerd writes per-container before invoking runc. Lives in the runtime bundle dir. Lists args, env, capabilities, namespaces, mounts, cgroups, hooks. Engine doesn't expose it directly; runc reads it. Detail in docker/runtime.

name: docker.engine.cgroup-v2
observations: cgroup v2: Unified cgroup hierarchy at `/sys/fs/cgroup/` (single mount). Required by some recent features (memory.events psi, io.cost). Modern distros default to v2-only. Container resource limits (`--memory`, `--cpus`, `--pids-limit`) translate to v2 knobs.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-network
observations: Network namespace: OCI namespace `type: network`. Each ns has its own interfaces, routing, iptables rules. Detail of how Docker wires veths into bridges lives in docker/networking.

name: docker.runtime.runc-state-created
observations: runc state: created: After `runc create` returned but before `runc start`. Container's resources (namespaces, cgroups, mounts) are in place; the user-specified process has not been exec'd. `runc state` returns this until `start` fires.

name: docker.runtime.runc-state-running
observations: runc state: running: After step 8 — user process has been exec'd and hasn't exited. `pid` field is set in the state JSON.

name: docker.runtime.oci-lifecycle
observations: OCI container lifecycle: The 13-step lifecycle: create → prestart hooks → createRuntime hooks → createContainer hooks → start → startContainer hooks → exec user process → poststart hooks → process exits → delete → poststop hooks. Each numbered step in `oci-runtime-spec-runtime`. Hook failures jump to step 12 (destroy).

name: docker.runtime.range-request
observations: Range request (registry pull): `Range: bytes=START-END` on `GET /v2/<name>/blobs/<digest>` for partial blob retrieval. Used by tools that resume failed pulls or stream-decompress layers.

name: docker.runtime.subreaper
observations: subreaper: Linux PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER prctl: marks a process as the reaper of orphaned descendants in its subtree (similar to pid 1 but local). runc uses one to reap reparented processes; `runc run --no-subreaper` disables it.

name: docker.runtime.containerd-shim-runc-v2
observations: containerd-shim-runc-v2: Per-container shim binary that owns the container's pid 1 from containerd's perspective. Decouples container lifetime from containerd's: containerd can be restarted without killing every container (the shim continues holding the pid). Implements the containerd shim v2 API. Alternative shims (e.g. containerd-shim-kata-v2, containerd-shim-runsc-v1, containerd-shim-wasmtime-v1) are how runtimes other than runc plug in.

name: docker.runtime.containerd-content-store
observations: containerd content store: Content-addressable blob store (`/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.content.v1.content/blobs/<algorithm>/<digest>`). Holds image manifests, configs, and compressed layer tarballs keyed by digest. Garbage collection per labels; references from snapshotters / image store keep blobs alive.

name: docker.runtime.image-manifest
observations: OCI image manifest: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json` document describing one platform-specific image: schemaVersion=2, config descriptor (points to the image config blob), layers[] (descriptors of layer tarballs), optional subject (referrers chain), optional annotations. The thing pulled by digest from a registry; binds a config to its layer set.

name: docker.runtime.layer-tarball
observations: Layer tarball: The compressed tarball that materializes one image layer's filesystem changeset. Two media types in common use: `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip` and `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+zstd` (newer, faster). The body is a tar of additions/changes/deletes (whiteout files for deletes) relative to the parent layer.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-uts
observations: UTS namespace: OCI namespace `type: uts`. Hostname + domainname isolation. Set via `hostname`/`domainname` in config.json.

name: docker.runtime.native-snapshotter
observations: native snapshotter: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.native`. Like vfs — full file copy per layer. Used as a fallback when no other snapshotter is available.

name: docker.runtime.chunked-upload
observations: Chunked blob upload: Multi-PATCH protocol for layer uploads. `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/` returns a `Location:` URL; client `PATCH`es with Content-Range; final `PUT ?digest=sha256:...` finalizes. Resumable; required for very large layers over flaky links.

name: docker.runtime.monolithic-upload
observations: Monolithic blob upload: Single-request blob upload: `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/?digest=sha256:<digest>` with body. Faster than chunked when bandwidth and the layer fit. Server may not support it; fall back to chunked.

name: docker.runtime.terminal-pty
observations: Terminal / pty: `process.terminal: true` requests a pty pair. The runtime opens a pty master in the runtime namespace and exposes it via `--console-socket` (an AF_UNIX socket the caller listens on). The container side gets the pty slave as fd 0/1/2.

name: docker.runtime.console-socket
observations: console-socket: AF_UNIX socket path passed to runc `--console-socket` to receive the pty master fd via SCM_RIGHTS. The piece of plumbing that makes `runc run -t` actually deliver an attached terminal to the caller. Detail in `docs/terminals.md` upstream.

name: docker.runtime.containerd-snapshotter
observations: containerd snapshotter: containerd plugin that provides image-layer storage as snapshots. Built-in: overlayfs, native, btrfs, zfs, devmapper, fuse-overlayfs. Each snapshotter exposes prepare/view/commit/remove ops; lifetime is per-key under /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.<name>/. Default per-runtime snapshotter is configurable in CRI plugin. The runtime-leaf analogue of docker/engine's storage-driver concept.

name: docker.runtime.image-layout
observations: OCI image layout: Filesystem layout for a portable image directory: `oci-layout` file (version), `index.json` (top-level index with descriptors), `blobs/<algorithm>/<digest>` files. Produced by `docker save` (in OCI mode), consumable by `docker load` / `skopeo copy oci:dir`. The on-disk shape of an image archive.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-cgroup
observations: Cgroup namespace: OCI namespace `type: cgroup`. Hides the host's cgroup tree; container sees only its own subtree at root. Required for cgroup-delegation in unprivileged contexts.

name: docker.runtime.cgroup-controller
observations: cgroup controller: Kernel cgroup subsystem (cpu, memory, pids, blkio, freezer, devices, hugetlb, perf_event, net_cls, net_prio, rdma). Each enforces one resource axis. config.json's `linux.resources.<controller>.*` sets per-container limits. cgroup v1 = multiple hierarchies, one per controller; v2 = unified hierarchy.

name: docker.runtime.manifest-list
observations: Manifest list (multi-arch): `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json` — Docker's multi-arch wrapper. Each entry has a per-platform descriptor + platform={os, architecture, variant}. OCI equivalent is `image-index`. Modern registries return one or the other depending on Accept header.

name: docker.runtime.oci-distribution-error-codes
observations: OCI distribution error codes: Standard error codes registries return: BLOB_UNKNOWN, BLOB_UPLOAD_INVALID, BLOB_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN, DIGEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_BLOB_UNKNOWN, MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_UNKNOWN, NAME_INVALID, NAME_UNKNOWN, SIZE_INVALID, UNAUTHORIZED, DENIED, UNSUPPORTED, TOOMANYREQUESTS. Returned in JSON `{errors: [{code, message, detail}]}` body of 4xx responses.

name: docker.runtime.exit-code-128-plus-signum
observations: Exit code 128+signum convention: POSIX shell convention: process killed by signal N exits with status 128+N. Hence 137=SIGKILL(9), 139=SIGSEGV(11), 143=SIGTERM(15), 130=SIGINT(2). The thing the harness uses to translate `docker inspect ExitCode` into 'OOM-killed' / 'segfaulted' / 'cleanly stopped'.

name: docker.runtime.containerd-events
observations: containerd events service: grpc event stream for lifecycle events (image pull, container create/start/exit, snapshot prepare/commit, etc.). Consumers: dockerd, kubelet, observability sidecars. `ctr events` to tail the stream.

name: docker.runtime.oci-manifest
observations: OCI manifest: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json`. Same shape as docker v2-2 but media types under `vnd.oci.*`. Most registries accept both; OCI is the future-default.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-mount
observations: Mount namespace: OCI namespace `type: mount`. Isolated mount table — bind mounts/volumes are visible only inside.

name: docker.runtime.fuse-overlayfs-snapshotter
observations: fuse-overlayfs snapshotter: FUSE-mode overlay for rootless containerd. Slower than kernel overlayfs but doesn't require CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Selected automatically in rootless mode where overlayfs needs kernel ≥ 5.11.

name: docker.runtime.manifest-v2-2
observations: Docker manifest v2-2: `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json`. Docker's pre-OCI manifest format; OCI image manifest v1 is binary-compatible. Most registries accept both; pulls succeed regardless. Specific compatibility quirks (history, fsLayers) are docker-v2-1-only.

name: docker.runtime.referrers-api
observations: Referrers API: `GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest>`. Returns an OCI image-index of manifests whose `subject` field references the supplied digest. Foundation for SBOM / signature attachment to images. Modern registries; fallback via `referrers` tag schema for older.

name: docker.runtime.poststop-hook
observations: poststop hook: Runs after the container is destroyed (step 13). Failures only logged as warnings — lifecycle continues. Used for cleanup (release GPUs, release netns, etc.).

name: docker.runtime.oci-platform
observations: OCI platform: {architecture, os, os.version?, os.features?, variant?} tuple per platform-specific manifest. Must match GOOS/GOARCH values: amd64, arm64, arm/v7, arm/v6, ppc64le, s390x, riscv64, mips64le, etc. Platform mismatch = registry returns the closest manifest or errors.

name: docker.runtime.runc
observations: runc: Reference OCI Runtime CLI. Reads an OCI bundle (config.json + rootfs) and uses Linux primitives (namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor) to create and run a container. Default low-level runtime under containerd. Operations: create, start, run, exec, kill, delete, state, spec, list, ps, update, pause, resume, checkpoint, restore. Self-managing: each run leaves on-disk state under /run/runc/<id>/. Engine perspective in docker/engine; this leaf catalogs the OCI-runtime-spec contract it implements.

name: docker.runtime.linux-capability
observations: Linux capability (runtime view): Subdivision of root power applied per container: bounding, effective, inheritable, permitted, ambient sets. config.json's `process.capabilities` enumerates them. The runtime applies them via prctl + setuid sequencing.

name: docker.runtime.oom-killer
observations: Linux OOM killer: Kernel's response to memory exhaustion in a memory cgroup. Picks a process by `oom_score`; sends SIGKILL. Container exits with `State.OOMKilled=true` and ExitCode 137. Tunable via cgroup `memory.oom.group` (kill all-or-none) and `oom_score_adj`.

name: docker.runtime.maskedpaths-readonlypaths
observations: maskedPaths / readonlyPaths: Container hardening: `linux.maskedPaths[]` bind-mounts /dev/null over each path (typical: /proc/kcore, /proc/keys, /proc/timer_list, /proc/scsi, /sys/firmware). `linux.readonlyPaths[]` remounts paths read-only (typical: /proc/asound, /proc/bus, /proc/fs, /proc/irq, /proc/sys, /proc/sysrq-trigger). The reason `cat /proc/kcore` inside a default container shows nothing.

name: docker.runtime.oci-runtime-cli-contract
observations: OCI runtime CLI contract: The general-operation contract every OCI-compliant runtime implements: create / start / kill / delete / state / exec. NOT a specific CLI surface — an abstract API. Each runtime exposes it via its own command line (runc, crun, youki, runsc); shims invoke runtimes through this contract. Defined in `oci-runtime-spec-runtime`.

name: docker.runtime.image-index
observations: OCI image index: `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json` — the multi-arch "fat manifest". Contains a manifests[] array of descriptors, each with a platform (os, architecture, variant). Registry returns this for a single tag like `nginx:1.27` so a pull can pick the right per-arch manifest. Equivalent to Docker's manifest-list-v2.

name: docker.runtime.image-descriptor
observations: OCI content descriptor: The pointer used everywhere in OCI to reference content: {mediaType, digest, size, urls?, annotations?, data?, artifactType?}. Unique because it carries both the type and the cryptographic hash — content can be located + verified from any source. Used in manifests, indexes, the referrers API.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-pid
observations: PID namespace (runtime view): OCI runtime-spec namespace `type: pid`. Container processes only see their own pid tree; container's pid 1 is not host's pid 1. Joining another's via `path: /proc/<pid>/ns/pid`.

name: docker.runtime.overlayfs-snapshotter
observations: overlayfs snapshotter: containerd snapshotter plugin `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs`. Default on Linux. Backed by kernel OverlayFS (same primitive as the engine-side overlay2 storage driver). Per-snapshot dirs at /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/<id>/{fs,work}. Engine-perspective in docker/engine; this is the runtime-leaf view.

name: docker.runtime.auth-bearer-token
observations: Registry bearer-token auth: OAuth2-style flow used by Docker Hub / GHCR / GCR. Client gets `401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=...,service=...,scope=...`, fetches a token from the realm, retries with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The reason an `unauthorized: authentication required` shows mid-pull when a token expired.

name: docker.runtime.createRuntime-hook
observations: createRuntime hook: Replaces prestart for runtime-namespace work. Runs after container namespaces created, before pivot_root. Same execution context as prestart but properly named.

name: docker.runtime.createContainer-hook
observations: createContainer hook: Runs in the container namespace before pivot_root. Has access to the container's mounts at their pre-pivot paths (i.e. /rootfs/...). For modifying container fs before the user process sees it.

name: docker.runtime.layer-chain-id
observations: Layer ChainID: Recursive sha256 over a stack of DiffIDs: ChainID(L₀)=DiffID(L₀); ChainID(L₀..Lₙ)=Digest(ChainID(L₀..Lₙ₋₁) + " " + DiffID(Lₙ)). The unambiguous identifier for an applied stack of layers (vs. a single layer's DiffID, which doesn't capture order).

name: docker.runtime.media-type
observations: OCI media type: RFC-6838 MIME-style type carried by every descriptor. Compatibility matrix: `application/vnd.oci.image.{manifest,index,config,layer.v1.tar[+gzip|+zstd]}.v1+json` are OCI; Docker compat: `application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.{v1,v2}+json`, `application/vnd.docker.image.rootfs.diff.tar.gzip`, etc. Unknown types MUST be passed through unchanged — the spec forbids erroring on unknown.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-time
observations: Time namespace: OCI namespace `type: time`. Container can have its own clocks; offsets per clock via `timeOffsets`. Newer kernel feature; not all runtimes implement.

name: docker.runtime.pivot-root-vs-no-pivot
observations: pivot_root vs --no-pivot: Standard runc switches the rootfs via pivot_root(2) syscall. `--no-pivot` falls back to chroot+chdir for environments where pivot_root is unavailable (e.g. RAM-disk or some container-in-container setups). Officially noted as 'may be unsafe from the security standpoint'.

name: docker.runtime.startContainer-hook
observations: startContainer hook: Runs in the container namespace, after pivot_root, immediately before the user-specified program is exec'd. Last chance to set up environment from inside the container.

name: docker.runtime.containerd-tasks-service
observations: containerd tasks service: grpc service inside containerd for managing running container processes ("tasks"). Distinguished from "containers" (configured but not running) — `ctr container ls` vs `ctr task ls`. Tasks have pids, exit codes, and metrics endpoints. Operations: create, start, kill, delete, exec, pause, resume, checkpoint, metrics.

name: docker.runtime.task
observations: containerd task: A running container instance from containerd's POV. `ctr container create` makes a container record; `ctr task start <id>` materializes a Task that has a pid and OS-level resources. Task lifecycle is independent of the container record — you can delete the task and re-start it from the same container.

name: docker.runtime.process-spec
observations: OCI process spec: `config.json` `process` block: terminal, user{uid,gid,additionalGids}, args, env, cwd, capabilities (bounding/effective/inheritable/permitted/ambient), rlimits, noNewPrivileges, apparmorProfile, selinuxLabel, oomScoreAdj. Override-able via `runc exec --process <process.json>` for one-off exec ins.

name: docker.runtime.btrfs-snapshotter
observations: btrfs snapshotter: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.btrfs`. Requires /var/lib/containerd on btrfs. Uses btrfs subvolumes/snapshots; block-level CoW.

name: docker.runtime.zfs-snapshotter
observations: zfs snapshotter: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.zfs`. Requires zfs filesystem. Block-level CoW; high RAM (ARC).

name: docker.runtime.linux-spec
observations: OCI linux spec: The `linux` block of config.json — namespaces, uidMappings, gidMappings, devices, cgroupsPath, resources, intelRdt, seccomp, maskedPaths, readonlyPaths, mountLabel, rootfsPropagation, sysctl. THE block runc applies on Linux hosts.

name: docker.runtime.runc-state-stopped
observations: runc state: stopped: Container process has exited (cleanly, error, or via `runc kill`). Resources still on-disk until `runc delete`.

name: docker.runtime.prestart-hook
observations: prestart hook: OCI hook (deprecated in newer spec but still supported by runc). Runs in the runtime namespace, after the container's namespaces are created but before pivot_root. Failure → runtime errors out, container destroyed. Used historically for `nvidia-container-runtime-hook`.

name: docker.runtime.runtime-platform
observations: Runtime platform spec: Platform-spec object in the OCI runtime spec (linux | windows | solaris | vm). Selects which top-level config block applies. Linux has the richest schema; runc only implements linux.

name: docker.runtime.namespace-ipc
observations: IPC namespace: OCI namespace `type: ipc`. SysV IPC and POSIX message-queue isolation.

name: docker.runtime.devmapper-snapshotter
observations: devmapper snapshotter: `io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.devmapper`. Uses LVM thin-pool. Per-container thin volume; configurable basesize. Legacy on most distros.

name: docker.runtime.www-authenticate
observations: WWW-Authenticate challenge: Header in a registry's 401 response telling the client where to fetch a token from and which scope to request. Standard format: `Bearer realm="https://auth.docker.io/token",service="registry.docker.io",scope="repository:library/nginx:pull"`.

name: docker.runtime.containerd
observations: containerd: Container lifecycle daemon — process supervisor + content store + image store + snapshotter manager + grpc API. Sits between dockerd / kubelet and runc. Listens on `/run/containerd/containerd.sock`. State under /var/lib/containerd, runtime under /run/containerd. Plugin architecture: each major subsystem (snapshotter, runtime, content store, metadata, CRI) is a plugin; configurable via /etc/containerd/config.toml.

name: docker.runtime.blob
observations: Content blob: A single content-addressable file in the content store / image layout / registry. Three flavors as far as images are concerned: layer (compressed tarball), config (json), manifest/index (json). Identified by digest; size and media-type carried in the descriptor that points to it.

name: docker.runtime.image-tag-ref
observations: Image tag reference: Mutable named pointer (`<registry>/<repo>:<tag>` or `<repo>@<digest>`) at a registry. The bytes resolved by a tag can change over time; a digest reference is immutable. The referrers API extends this with a third form (subject-relations).

name: docker.runtime.namespace-user
observations: User namespace: OCI namespace `type: user`. Container uid/gid → host uid/gid mapped via `uidMappings[]` / `gidMappings[]` (containerID, hostID, size triples). Foundation for rootless and userns-remap. Number of mapping entries kernel-limited.

name: docker.runtime.image-id
observations: ImageID: sha256 of the image config blob. Content-addressable identifier of a fully-realized image (config + ordered diff_ids). What `docker image ls` shows (truncated) under IMAGE ID. NOT the same as the layer digests in the manifest.

name: docker.runtime.layer-diff-id
observations: Layer DiffID: sha256 of the UNCOMPRESSED layer tarball. Stable across compression algorithms; sits in `image-config.rootfs.diff_ids[]`. Distinct from the layer descriptor's digest, which is over the on-wire compressed bytes.

name: docker.runtime.image-config-history
observations: Image config history: `history[]` array in the image config: per-layer {created, created_by (Dockerfile instruction), author?, comment?, empty_layer?}. Surfaced by `docker history <image>`. The ground truth for 'why is this layer 800MB'.

name: docker.runtime.cri-plugin
observations: containerd CRI plugin: containerd's built-in implementation of the Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface (CRI). Lets kubelet talk to containerd directly via grpc on `/run/containerd/containerd.sock`. Configured under [plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri"] in containerd's config.toml. Owns sandbox-pause-image, default runtime selection, registry mirrors, image decryption, snapshotter choice. The reason `dockerd` is no longer needed for k8s nodes since k8s 1.24.

name: docker.runtime.oci-bundle
observations: OCI bundle: On-disk directory comprising a `config.json` (the OCI runtime config) plus a `rootfs/` directory (the container's filesystem). The unit `runc create <id> <bundle>` consumes. dockerd/containerd assemble it dynamically from the image; standalone runc usage does it by hand (`docker export | tar -x`, `runc spec`, edit, `runc run`).

name: docker.runtime.runc-state-creating
observations: runc state: creating: OCI runtime state during step 2 of the lifecycle — env being set up. `runc create` not yet returned. Brief; container has an ID but no pid yet.

name: docker.runtime.cross-repository-mount
observations: Cross-repository blob mount: `POST /v2/<name>/blobs/uploads/?mount=<digest>&from=<other-repo>`. Lets a push reuse a blob already present in another repo on the same registry, without re-uploading. The reason `docker push` is fast for a layer-shared image to a different repo on the same registry.

name: docker.runtime.exit-status
observations: Exit status: `runc exec` exits with the user command's exit status (or 255 on internal error). Detail of conventional codes lives in docker/engine (137 = OOM, 139 = SEGV, 143 = SIGTERM, 128+N = signal-N termination).

name: docker.runtime.digest-sha256
observations: sha256 digest: `sha256:<64 hex chars>` — the registered OCI digest algorithm. Verifies content integrity end-to-end. Other registered algos: sha512, blake3. Implementations SHOULD pass through unrecognized algorithms if they comply with the digest grammar.

name: docker.runtime.content-addressable-storage
observations: Content-addressable storage: Files keyed by hash of their content. Two pulls of the same digest = identical bytes. Foundation for layer dedup, registry caching, image signing. Also surfaced from docker/engine; here the runtime-leaf view (containerd content store, blob layout).

name: docker.runtime.tar-split
observations: tar-split: Library for reproducibly serializing tar headers separately from file contents so a layer's diff_id is stable across compress/decompress cycles. Required to compute consistent diff_ids, which feed into ChainID, which feeds into ImageID.

name: docker.runtime.seccomp-syscall-action
observations: seccomp syscall action: What seccomp does on a matching syscall: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW, SCMP_ACT_ERRNO[(errno)], SCMP_ACT_KILL, SCMP_ACT_KILL_PROCESS, SCMP_ACT_LOG, SCMP_ACT_TRACE[(ret)], SCMP_ACT_NOTIFY, SCMP_ACT_RET. config.json's `linux.seccomp.defaultAction` + per-syscall `syscalls[].action`. Detailed schema in docker/security.

name: docker.runtime.signal-stoptimeout
observations: Signal + stop timeout: OCI runtime: `runc kill <id> <signal>` sends signal to pid 1; default SIGTERM. No grace-period concept at runc layer — that lives in containerd / dockerd. Image's StopSignal sets the default kill signal; daemon's stop-timeout sets the grace before SIGKILL.

name: docker.runtime.image-config
observations: OCI image config: `application/vnd.oci.image.config.v1+json` blob describing the runtime defaults of an image: created, author, architecture, os, os.version, os.features, variant, config{User, ExposedPorts, Env, Entrypoint, Cmd, Volumes, WorkingDir, Labels, StopSignal}, rootfs{type="layers", diff_ids[]}, history[]. Content of `docker inspect`'s Config block.

name: docker.networking.ipam-pool
observations: IPAM pool: A {subnet, ip-range?, gateway, aux-addresses} tuple defining the IP space a network can hand out. One pool per IPv4/IPv6 leg per network. Daemon-wide pool defaults via `default-address-pools`; per-network override via `--subnet/--ip-range/--gateway/--aux-address` on `docker network create`.

name: docker.networking.iptables-nat-table
observations: iptables nat table: Where Docker installs PREROUTING/OUTPUT/POSTROUTING rules for port-publish DNAT and bridge SNAT (masquerade). `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` shows them. The table where `-p 80:80` becomes a DNAT to the container's 172.x.0.x:80.

name: docker.networking.linux-bridge
observations: Linux bridge (host-side): The kernel software bridge that bridge-driver builds on. Default `docker0`; user-defined networks get bridges named like `br-<network-id-prefix>`. Inspectable with `ip link show type bridge`, `bridge link show`, `brctl show`. Containers' veth ends are slaved to this bridge.

name: docker.networking.mtu-network
observations: network MTU: Per-network MTU set via `-o com.docker.network.driver.mtu` or daemon-wide `--mtu`. Default 1500. Lower (1450) on hosts behind GRE/IPsec/VXLAN tunnels — without this, large packets are silently dropped by the encap path. Symptom: small TCP flows work, large writes hang.

name: docker.networking.default-address-pools
observations: default-address-pools: Daemon-level `default-address-pools` controls which IP ranges get sliced into per-user-defined-network subnets. e.g. `[{base: 10.10.0.0/16, size: 24}]` carves out /24s from 10.10.0.0/16. CRITICAL when on-prem ranges collide with default 172.17–172.31 / 192.168.x.x picks.

name: docker.networking.iptables-mangle-table
observations: iptables mangle table: Used by Swarm routing mesh and by `bridge-accept-fwmark` to handle marked packets. Less common in single-host Docker but visible on swarm nodes.

name: docker.networking.veth-pair
observations: veth pair: Linux virtual ethernet pair: two interfaces, packets out one come in the other. Per container endpoint Docker creates one veth pair: container side moved into the container's netns (named `eth0` typically); host side stays in the root netns slaved to the bridge.

name: docker.networking.network-encryption-overlay
observations: overlay encryption: `--opt encrypted` on `docker network create -d overlay` — IPsec at the VXLAN layer. Non-trivial CPU cost; not supported on Windows containers. Use only when host-to-host links are untrusted.

name: docker.networking.iptables-DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2
observations: DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2 chain: Filter-table chain paired with STAGE-1 to enforce inter-bridge isolation. Drops if output bridge differs from input bridge for FORWARD-ed packets.

name: docker.networking.sysctl-ip-forward
observations: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward: Kernel sysctl that enables IP forwarding (host acts as router between interfaces). Docker auto-enables on dockerd start (and also `net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding`). When Docker enables it, it also installs a default-DROP FORWARD policy unless `ip-forward-no-drop` is set. Critical: disabling kills all bridge-network outbound.

name: docker.networking.overlay-driver
observations: overlay driver: Multi-host network across Swarm members. VXLAN tunnel (default UDP 4789) carries traffic between hosts. Required for Swarm services or for standalone containers that need to talk across hosts (`--attachable`). Optional `--opt encrypted` enables IPsec at the VXLAN layer (non-trivial perf cost; not supported for Windows containers). Required ports between hosts: 2377/tcp (control plane), 4789/udp (data), 7946/tcp+udp (gossip).

name: docker.networking.container-ip
observations: container IP: The per-endpoint IP assigned to a container on a network. Comes from the network's IPAM pool by default; pin with `docker network connect --ip <addr>` or `docker run --ip <addr>` (only works on user-defined networks with `--subnet`).

name: docker.networking.legacy-link
observations: legacy `--link`: Deprecated. On the default bridge, `--link source:alias` injects /etc/hosts entries and shares env vars. User-defined bridges' DNS-by-name supersedes this; `--link` is preserved for the default bridge only.

name: docker.networking.ip-range
observations: IP range: `--ip-range <CIDR>` carves out a sub-range of `--subnet` from which Docker auto-assigns container IPs. Containers can still be statically pinned outside the range (via `--ip`).

name: docker.networking.ipam-config
observations: IPAM config: The {subnet, ip-range, gateway, aux-addresses} bundle a network commits to. Surfaced as `IPAM.Config[]` in `docker network inspect`.

name: docker.networking.routing-table
observations: routing table: Per-netns route table. `ip route` inside a container; multi-network containers have one route per attached subnet plus a default via the gateway of the first network. `ip rule` for policy routing.

name: docker.networking.port-publish-explicit-host-ip
observations: port publish — explicit host IP: `-p <host-ip>:<host-port>:<container-port>[/proto]`. Restricts publish to a specific host IP. Common pattern: `-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` to expose Postgres only to local clients on the host.

name: docker.networking.port-conflict
observations: port conflict: `Bind for 0.0.0.0:80 failed: port is already allocated`. Caused by another process (or another container) holding the host port. Diagnose: `ss -tlnp | grep :80`, `docker ps --filter publish=80`. Fix: stop the holder, or pick a different host port.

name: docker.networking.ipvlan-driver
observations: ipvlan driver: L2 or L3 network virtualization on top of a parent host interface (no Linux bridge in between). Lighter than bridge; container interfaces attach directly to the host NIC's L2 / L3 path. `-o parent=eth0` selects the parent. Containers cannot ping the host on the same parent (kernel filter). No port-publishing needed in L2 (containers get routable IPs).

name: docker.networking.ipvlan-l3-mode
observations: ipvlan L3 mode: Routed (L3) variant of ipvlan. The host acts as a router between container subnets. Container traffic is forwarded by the host's routing table; no broadcast/multicast leaks across `parent` interfaces. Different containers can sit on different L3 subnets sharing one parent. Useful when you want isolated L3 segments without L2 exposure.

name: docker.networking.ipam-driver
observations: IPAM driver: The IP-address-management plugin a network uses (`default` is built-in). Pluggable for vendor IPAM (e.g. Calico's IPAM). Configured via `--ipam-driver` + `--ipam-opt` on `docker network create`.

name: docker.networking.docker-port-shortcut
observations: `docker port` shortcut: `docker port <container> [<port>[/<proto>]]` reads back the live `hostIP:hostPort` for a published container port. Useful when `-P` was used (port is randomized).

name: docker.networking.nftables-table
observations: nftables table (docker): Modern alternative to iptables. Selectable via daemon `firewall-backend: nftables`. Same logical rule set; uses single nftables table with chains for prerouting/postrouting/forward/output. Different toolchain (`nft list ruleset`).

name: docker.networking.embedded-dns-resolver
observations: embedded DNS resolver: Per-bridge in-kernel DNS server at 127.0.0.11 in user-defined bridges. Resolves container names and aliases on the network; falls back to host's resolver for everything else. The mechanism behind `db` resolving to the db container's IP from the web container.

name: docker.networking.vxlan-tunnel
observations: VXLAN tunnel: L2-over-UDP encapsulation used by overlay networks. Default UDP port 4789. Each overlay's traffic carries its VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier). Inspect on the host with `ip -d link show vxlan0`.

name: docker.networking.bridge-driver
observations: bridge driver: Default Docker network driver. Creates an in-kernel Linux bridge (default `docker0`) plus per-container veth pairs. IPv4 subnet (and optional IPv6 subnet); per-container interface in that subnet; embedded DNS for user-defined bridges (containers reach each other by name). User-defined bridges > the default bridge: scoped isolation, automatic name DNS, configurable per-network, attach/detach on the fly. Docker manages an `iptables` (or `nftables`) ruleset for NAT/masquerade/ICC.

name: docker.networking.iptables-DOCKER-USER-chain
observations: DOCKER-USER chain: User-editable chain in the `filter` table, traversed BEFORE DOCKER. Only place you can safely add rules that affect Docker traffic without Docker overwriting them. e.g. drop external-source packets to specific published ports.

name: docker.networking.network-namespace-runtime
observations: network namespace (runtime): Each container endpoint lives in a network namespace (its own routing table, iptables rules, interfaces). For bridge networks, container netns contains the eth0 (one end of the veth) + lo. Inspect with `nsenter --net --target <pid>` or `ip netns list`.

name: docker.networking.embedded-dns
observations: embedded DNS feature: Daemon-side DNS server at 127.0.0.11 inside containers on user-defined bridges/overlays. Resolves container names + aliases; forwards everything else to the host's resolvers. Disable per-container with `--dns` to provide custom servers.

name: docker.networking.proxy-arp
observations: proxy ARP: Kernel feature where one host answers ARP for IPs that don't live on its interfaces. Used by ipvlan-l3 + macvlan setups so the upstream router can reach container IPs on the parent interface. `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.proxy_arp=1`.

name: docker.networking.none-driver
observations: none driver: Container has only `lo` — no other network interface, no internet, no DNS. Used for batch/CPU jobs that mustn't reach the network, or as a base for hand-crafted netns wiring. `docker run --network=none …`. Detail in `docker-docs-network-none`.

name: docker.networking.network-alias
observations: network alias: Additional hostname for a container on a network. Set via `--network-alias <name>` or `docker network connect --alias`. Useful for blue/green or canary patterns where multiple containers should resolve at the same name.

name: docker.networking.nat-traversal
observations: NAT / SNAT for containers: Bridge driver SNATs container-originated traffic to the host's IP via iptables MASQUERADE in POSTROUTING. Toggleable per-network via `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` or daemon-wide via `--ip-masq`. Disabling = container packets keep internal IP, often filtered by external networks.

name: docker.networking.published-port
observations: published port: A container port that's been opened to outside-the-container clients via `-p`. Distinct from EXPOSE (which is just metadata). Format `[hostIP:][hostPort]:containerPort[/proto]`; missing hostPort = random ephemeral port; missing hostIP = all interfaces.

name: docker.networking.network-endpoint
observations: network endpoint: A container's attachment to one network — its veth pair, IP, MAC, aliases. A container can have N endpoints (N networks). Surfaced as `NetworkSettings.Networks.<name>` in `docker inspect`. Each endpoint has its own IPAddress, Gateway, MacAddress, Aliases.

name: docker.networking.port-binding
observations: port binding: A daemon-managed mapping `hostIP:hostPort -> containerIP:containerPort/proto`. Created by `-p`/`--publish`/`-P`. Implemented as DNAT in iptables (or nftables) plus userland-proxy for loopback. Visible in `docker port` and `docker inspect`'s NetworkSettings.Ports.

name: docker.networking.docker0-interface
observations: docker0 interface: The default-bridge's host-side interface. `ip addr show docker0` shows it; default IPv4 = first /16 not colliding (172.17.0.1/16). Renaming/customizing requires daemon restart with `--bridge` flag (rare).

name: docker.networking.iptables-DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1
observations: DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1 chain: Filter-table chain that drops packets between different bridge networks. Stage 1 matches input bridge; stage 2 matches output bridge. Together they enforce per-bridge isolation.

name: docker.networking.swarm-routing-mesh
observations: swarm routing mesh: Swarm-built ingress overlay network: `docker service create --publish` exposes a port on every Swarm node, routing requests to a healthy task replica anywhere. Implemented as a special `ingress` network created automatically; uses iptables marks + IPVS.

name: docker.networking.arp-table
observations: ARP table: Per-netns mapping of IP→MAC. `ip neigh` (or `arp -an`) inside a container's netns shows it. Stale entries cause ~3s pauses on inter-container connect; `gc_thresh*` sysctls tune kernel cache. Helpful debug step on flaky bridge networks.

name: docker.networking.host-driver
observations: host driver: Removes network isolation between container and host: container shares the host's network namespace. No port mapping needed; container can `bind 0.0.0.0:80` directly to the host's interfaces. No iptables rules created for host networking. Linux-only; on Docker Desktop runs through the VM. Use for ultra-low-latency or when port-mapping overhead is intolerable.

name: docker.networking.docker-network
observations: docker network (object): A Docker-managed network — driver name + scope + subnet(s) + gateway + IPAM config + per-network options. Listed by `docker network ls`; created by `docker network create`. From the engine, just an attachment endpoint; from the networking leaf, the concrete on-host construct (a Linux bridge, an overlay VXLAN, a parent-attached ipvlan).

name: docker.networking.gateway-ip
observations: gateway IP: The network's gateway address — typically `.1` of the subnet. The container's default route. For bridge networks, this is also the host's interface IP on the bridge (containers reach the host via this address).

name: docker.networking.iptables-DOCKER-chain
observations: DOCKER chain: Custom chain in `nat` and `filter` tables Docker manages for port-publish DNAT and bridge filter rules. Append-only by Docker itself; user rules don't go here. Inspect: `iptables -t nat -L DOCKER -n`.

name: docker.networking.userland-proxy
observations: userland proxy: Per-published-port `docker-proxy` process bridging hairpin/loopback traffic that NAT can't handle (e.g. container hitting its own published port from the host's loopback). Toggleable via `--userland-proxy=false`. Disabling pushes work into iptables but breaks some odd cases. The reason `ps -ef | grep docker-proxy` shows one process per published port.

name: docker.networking.connection-tracking
observations: conntrack: Kernel connection-tracking subsystem. Docker's NAT depends on it. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` to see live entries; bumping `nf_conntrack_max` is the fix for 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' on heavy port-published hosts.

name: docker.networking.macvlan-driver
observations: macvlan driver: Each container gets a unique MAC address on the host's physical network — appears as a fully separate device to the LAN. Modes: bridge (default), private, vepa, passthru. Requires the host NIC to allow promiscuous mode (or many MACs); cloud providers often disallow. Best for legacy apps that expect to be directly on the LAN.

name: docker.networking.user-defined-bridge
observations: user-defined bridge: A bridge created via `docker network create -d bridge <name>`. Embedded DNS (containers resolve each other by name/alias). Configurable per-network. Containers can be attached/detached on the fly via `docker network connect/disconnect`. Effectively all-ports-open between same-network containers; need explicit `--publish` for outside reach.

name: docker.networking.iptables-filter-table
observations: iptables filter table: Where Docker installs FORWARD chain rules to enforce inter-network isolation and let port-published traffic through. The table that drops cross-bridge traffic by default unless explicitly accepted via DOCKER-USER.

name: docker.networking.port-publish-host-binding
observations: port publish host-binding: Default behavior of `-p 80` / `-p 8080:80` — bind the published port to ALL host addresses (0.0.0.0 and ::). Override per-network via `com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4` or per-port via `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:80`.

name: docker.networking.multi-network-attach
observations: multi-network attach: A single container can be attached to N networks. Done either at create time (`--network` repeatable) or after start with `docker network connect`. Each attach creates a new endpoint with its own IP; routing inside the container picks the appropriate interface per destination subnet.

name: docker.networking.ipv6-bridge
observations: IPv6 on bridge: Per-network `--ipv6` enables a v6 subnet (auto-pick a ULA, or `--subnet 2001:db8::/64`). Daemon-wide `ipv6: true` + `fixed-cidr-v6` for the default bridge. ip6tables rules managed by Docker (toggle via `ip6tables: true` / `--ip6tables=false`).

name: docker.networking.subnet-cidr
observations: subnet (CIDR): `--subnet <CIDR>` defines the address space a network's containers draw from. One IPv4 + one IPv6 subnet per network max. CIDR collisions with on-prem subnets break routing — pin with `default-address-pools` to avoid surprises.

name: docker.networking.default-bridge
observations: default bridge (`bridge`): The bridge network Docker auto-creates: name `bridge`, host interface `docker0`. Containers without `--network` join it. Configurable only via `daemon.json` (bip, mtu, fixed-cidr, ip-masq, icc) — needs daemon restart. Considered legacy; prefer user-defined bridges. Lacks DNS-by-name (containers must be `--link`'d to resolve by name).

name: docker.networking.port-mapping-record
observations: PortMap record: The `HostConfig.PortBindings` and `NetworkSettings.Ports` shape: a JSON object keyed by `<port>/<proto>`, value is an array of {HostIp, HostPort}. Empty array = all interfaces, ephemeral host port. The structural representation of a port binding.

name: docker.networking.host-port
observations: host port: The host-side port a published port lands on. With `-P` (`--publish-all`), each EXPOSE'd port gets a random high port from the ephemeral range. Inspect with `docker port <container>` or `docker ps`'s PORTS column.

name: docker.compose.compose-application
observations: Compose application: A platform-agnostic container-based application defined as a set of containers that run together with shared resources + comms. Authored as one or more YAML files conforming to the Compose Specification. The unit `docker compose up` brings up.
