name: docker.compose.service-depends-on
observations: depends_on: Service-level dependency declaration. Compose creates services in `depends_on` order, removes in reverse. Two forms: list (`depends_on: [db, redis]`) or map with conditions. Without conditions, only ordering — Compose doesn't wait for app readiness, just for the container to be running.

name: docker.compose.service-deploy-strategy
observations: service deploy strategy: Service-level `deploy.mode` (`replicated` or `global`). Replicated runs N replicas anywhere; global runs one per node. Swarm-only at runtime; non-Swarm Compose sees these as advisory.

name: docker.compose.compose-anchor-yaml
observations: YAML anchors + aliases: Standard YAML `&anchor` / `*alias` works in compose.yaml. Combined with `<<: *anchor` for map merging. Pattern: define `x-shared-env: &shared { ... }` and reuse via `environment: *shared`.

name: docker.compose.compose-tmpfs
observations: compose tmpfs: `services.<name>.tmpfs` (string or list) mounts an in-memory fs at the given path. Cleaned on container stop. Distinct from a volume — no persistence, no driver.

name: docker.compose.compose-tty
observations: tty: `services.<name>.tty: true` allocates a pseudo-TTY. Useful for shell-on-PID-1 services (interactive).

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-start-interval
observations: healthcheck.start_interval: Probe cadence during start_period. Faster than `interval` so health is detected quickly post-boot.

name: docker.compose.compose-extension-x
observations: Compose extension fields (x-*): Any top-level or service-level field starting with `x-` is a Compose-spec extension. Ignored by the spec; useful for tool-specific metadata, YAML anchors, and template patterns (`x-base: &base ...`).

name: docker.compose.service-replicated-mode
observations: deploy.mode: replicated: Service runs `deploy.replicas` instances. Default. Most common for stateless services.

name: docker.compose.deploy-global
observations: global deploy mode: deploy.mode=global. One container per node. Used for node agents.

name: docker.compose.compose-config-source
observations: config source vs target: `services.<name>.configs` entries: `{source: <config-name>, target: <container-path>, uid, gid, mode}`. Default target `/<source>`. The decoupling means the same config can land at different paths in different services.

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-test
observations: healthcheck.test: Either `["NONE"]` (disable an image's HEALTHCHECK), `["CMD", arg, ...]` (exec form), or `["CMD-SHELL", "shell line"]` (shell form — wraps in /bin/sh -c). Exit 0 = healthy, 1 = unhealthy.

name: docker.compose.var-env-file-loading
observations: --env-file / .env loading: Compose loads `.env` from project dir by default (CLI: `--env-file <path>`). KEY=VALUE per line; comments with `#`. Loaded BEFORE interpolation so vars are visible to `${VAR}`. Distinct from `services.<name>.env_file` (that one populates the container's env, not the YAML's).

name: docker.compose.service-init-vs-container-init
observations: init (compose vs container): `services.<name>.init: true` runs an init process as pid 1 (forwards signals + reaps zombies). Equivalent to `docker run --init`. Don't confuse with the daemon's `init: true` (sets default) or top-level `name: init` (project name).

name: docker.compose.service-depends-on-condition-started
observations: depends_on condition: service_started: Default condition. Wait for the dependency's container to be `running` (NOT for app readiness). Equivalent to bare `depends_on: [name]`.

name: docker.compose.compose-restart-on-failure
observations: restart on-failure: `services.<name>.restart: on-failure[:N]` — restart up to N times if container exits non-zero. Limit isn't supported by all platforms; without N, retry indefinitely.

name: docker.compose.compose-network
observations: Compose network: A platform-capability abstraction for IP routing between services. Top-level `networks.<name>`. Maps to a Docker network of the chosen driver (default `bridge`). Services attach via `services.<name>.networks`. Implementation details (driver, options) live under the network entry.

name: docker.compose.compose-watch
observations: Compose watch: `develop.watch[]` rules: file-watcher hooks. Each rule has path, target, action (sync|rebuild|sync+restart), ignore[], exclude[]. Triggered by `docker compose watch` (or `docker compose up --watch`). Foundation for hot-reload dev workflows.

name: docker.compose.compose-build-context
observations: build context (compose): `services.<name>.build` either a string (=context dir) or a structured object. Compose builds the image locally instead of pulling. Build args, secrets, ssh, cache_from/cache_to, target stage, platforms — all available.

name: docker.compose.var-error-if-empty
observations: interpolation: ${VAR:?msg} vs ${VAR?msg}: Distinction: `:?` errors on unset+empty; `?` errors only on unset. Same difference applies to `:-`/`-`.

name: docker.compose.compose-merge
observations: Compose file merging: Multiple `-f`/`--file` files (or env `COMPOSE_FILE`) merge into one model. Override files (the second+ file) replace simple values, append to lists, deep-merge maps. Last writer wins on scalar conflicts. The mechanism behind the `compose.yml` + `compose.override.yml` pattern.

name: docker.compose.service-depends-on-condition-completed-successfully
observations: depends_on condition: service_completed_successfully: Wait for the dependency to run to successful completion (exit 0). Pattern: a one-shot migration / seed service the main app waits on.

name: docker.compose.deploy-replicated
observations: replicated deploy mode: deploy.mode=replicated + deploy.replicas=N. Standard for stateless services. Combine with deploy.update_config for rolling updates.

name: docker.compose.deploy-rollback-config
observations: rollback_config: deploy.rollback_config: same shape as update_config. Triggered by failure_action: rollback, or by `docker service rollback`. Defines how to revert a botched deploy.

name: docker.compose.compose-network-default
observations: default network: If a project doesn't declare networks, Compose creates a default user-defined bridge named `<project>_default` and attaches all services to it. So services resolve each other by name out of the box.

name: docker.compose.compose-volume-driver-local
observations: local volume driver: Default volume driver on `local` Compose. Maps to `docker volume create -d local`. Driver-opts pass through (type=nfs, device=:/path, o=addr=...). Cross-host volumes need NFS/CIFS or another driver.

name: docker.compose.compose-fragment-anchor-merge
observations: YAML << merge: `<<: *anchor` injects an anchor's keys into the current map. Combined with extension fields (`x-base: &base { ... }`) gives a 'mixin' pattern for shared service config.

name: docker.compose.compose-include
observations: Compose include: Top-level `include` reads in additional Compose files. Each entry can be a string path or `{path, project_directory, env_file}`. Each include is resolved as a sub-project; conflicts with the parent are errors. Lets large applications stitch together vendor-supplied compose snippets.

name: docker.compose.service-depends-on-restart-true
observations: depends_on restart: true: Restart the dependent service when the dependency restarts (e.g. `docker compose restart db` triggers `web` restart). Ensures connections/dependencies are re-established.

name: docker.compose.compose-extends
observations: extends: `services.<name>.extends`: import a service definition from another Compose file (or same file). Merge with local overrides. Distinct from include (which brings in whole sub-projects).

name: docker.compose.compose-build-vs-image
observations: build vs image: `build` and `image` can both be specified — Compose builds, then tags the result as the `image` value (so subsequent runs can `pull` instead). Without `image`, the built image gets a Compose-managed name like `<project>-<service>`.

name: docker.compose.deploy-placement-constraint
observations: deploy.placement: deploy.placement: constraints (label-match expressions), preferences (spread by node attribute), max_replicas_per_node. Pin services to nodes by labels — e.g. `node.role==manager` or `engine.labels.zone==eu-west-1`.

name: docker.compose.var-substring
observations: interpolation: substring ops: Bash-style param expansion: `${VAR#prefix}`, `${VAR##prefix}`, `${VAR%suffix}`, `${VAR%%suffix}`, `${VAR/pattern/replacement}`. Implemented per-platform; portable subset is the unset/empty operators.

name: docker.compose.compose-project
observations: Compose project: An individual deployment of a Compose application on a platform. Top-level `name` (or `-p`/`--project-name` flag, or env `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`) — used to prefix all resource names + label `com.docker.compose.project`. Lets the same compose.yaml be deployed twice on the same host without collision. Project names: lowercase letters, digits, dashes, underscores; must start with a letter or digit.

name: docker.compose.compose-volume
observations: Compose volume: Top-level `volumes.<name>` declaration of a persistent filesystem mount. Services reference it via `services.<name>.volumes`. Driver-options pass through to the volume driver. Read+write (configs/secrets are read-only).

name: docker.compose.compose-secret
observations: Compose secret: Top-level `secrets.<name>` for sensitive data — same shape as a config but with platform-specific secure storage. Mounted as files at `/run/secrets/<name>` by default. Read-only.

name: docker.compose.service-depends-on-condition-healthy
observations: depends_on condition: service_healthy: `condition: service_healthy` waits for the dependency's `healthcheck` to pass before starting the dependent service. The recommended way to handle 'app starts before DB is ready'.

name: docker.compose.deploy-replicated-job
observations: replicated-job deploy mode: deploy.mode=replicated-job. One-shot job that runs N times across the swarm and exits. Newer mode.

name: docker.compose.deploy-update-config-rolling
observations: rolling update_config: deploy.update_config: parallelism, delay, failure_action (continue|rollback|pause), monitor, max_failure_ratio, order (start-first|stop-first). The Swarm-style rolling-update knob set.

name: docker.compose.compose-stdin-open
observations: stdin_open: `services.<name>.stdin_open: true` keeps stdin open. Combined with tty=true mirrors `docker run -it`.

name: docker.compose.compose-yaml-shape
observations: compose.yaml top-level shape: Top-level keys: `name` (project), `services`, `networks`, `volumes`, `configs`, `secrets`, `include`, `x-*`. The legacy `version` field is now ignored. Convention: `compose.yaml` (or `compose.yml`); legacy filenames `docker-compose.yaml`/`yml` still picked up.

name: docker.compose.compose-profile
observations: Compose profile: Set of named profiles activating subsets of services. Services without `profiles` are always enabled; services with `profiles` are only enabled when one of them is active. Activated via `--profile <name>` (repeatable) or `COMPOSE_PROFILES`. Targeting a profile-bound service explicitly auto-activates its profiles.

name: docker.compose.service-healthcheck
observations: service healthcheck: Service-level `healthcheck`: test, interval, timeout, retries, start_period, start_interval, disable. Override the image's HEALTHCHECK or define one for an image without. `service_healthy` depends_on condition uses this.

name: docker.compose.compose-service
observations: Compose service: An abstract computing component implemented by running the same container image (and config) one or more times. Top-level `services.<name>` map. Each service maps to one or more containers (per `deploy.replicas` or scale). Ports, volumes, networks, env, depends_on attached here.

name: docker.compose.compose-config
observations: Compose config: Top-level `configs.<name>` for non-sensitive runtime configuration data. Mounted into containers as a file (default 0444). Distinct from a volume because the platform may source it from a config service rather than a filesystem path. `external: true` to reference an existing platform config.

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-retries
observations: healthcheck.retries: Consecutive failures before container is marked unhealthy.

name: docker.compose.var-default-value
observations: interpolation: ${VAR:-default}: `${VAR:-default}` — use `default` if VAR is unset OR empty. `${VAR-default}` — use default only if VAR is unset (empty allowed).

name: docker.compose.service-shutdown-order
observations: service shutdown order: Reverse of startup — `web` (which depends on `db`) is removed first, then `db`. SIGTERM grace from `stop_grace_period` (default 10s) before SIGKILL.

name: docker.compose.service-global-mode
observations: deploy.mode: global: Service runs exactly one instance per Swarm node. Used for node agents (monitoring, log collectors).

name: docker.compose.multi-file-merge
observations: multi-file merge: `docker compose -f base.yml -f override.yml up`. Override file's values: scalars replace, lists append, maps deep-merge. Production-vs-dev pattern: `compose.yml` + `compose.dev.yml`.

name: docker.compose.deploy-resource-reservation
observations: deploy.resources.reservations: deploy.resources.{limits, reservations}.{cpus, memory, pids, devices, generic_resources}. Limits = hard cap (cgroup); reservations = scheduler hint (Swarm scheduling, not enforced at runtime).

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-interval
observations: healthcheck.interval: Time between health-check runs. Format: `30s`, `1m30s`. Default 30s.

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-timeout
observations: healthcheck.timeout: Max time per probe. Probe killed + counted as failure if exceeds.

name: docker.compose.service-restart-policy
observations: service restart policy: Two ways: top-level `restart: no|always|on-failure[:N]|unless-stopped` (Compose-managed; runs on host docker), OR `deploy.restart_policy` (Swarm-managed). They have different semantics — `restart` is the docker-engine-level policy; `deploy.restart_policy` adds delay/max-attempts/window/condition.

name: docker.compose.deploy-global-job
observations: global-job deploy mode: deploy.mode=global-job. One-shot job, one execution per node.

name: docker.compose.var-default-empty
observations: interpolation: ${VAR}: Bare `${VAR}` — empty string if unset (warning logged). For required vars, use `${VAR:?}` instead.

name: docker.compose.service-startup-order
observations: service startup order: Compose creates services in `depends_on` topological order. Cycles are errors. Without `condition`, dependency = 'created and running' (NOT app-ready). On `down`, services are removed in reverse order.

name: docker.compose.compose-secret-mode-bits
observations: secret mode bits: `services.<name>.secrets[].mode` (octal) sets the file mode of the mounted secret in the container. Default `0444`. Lower bits useful when an app refuses to read world-readable files (e.g. ssh keys: 0400).

name: docker.compose.healthcheck-start-period
observations: healthcheck.start_period: Initial wait before counting failures. Lets the app boot without flapping unhealthy. Default 0s.

name: docker.compose.var-required
observations: interpolation: ${VAR:?error}: `${VAR:?error}` — error out if VAR is unset OR empty. `${VAR?error}` — error only on unset. Use to fail-fast on missing required env.

name: docker.compose.service-pull-policy
observations: service pull_policy: `services.<name>.pull_policy`: missing|always|never|build|if_not_present. Default `missing`. `if_not_present` is an alias for `missing`. `build` says: rebuild from `build` block instead of pulling.

name: docker.security.dockerd-tls-listener
observations: dockerd TLS listener: The mTLS-secured TCP socket dockerd opens when configured with `--tlsverify` + cert pair. Default port 2376 (vs 2375 for unencrypted). Mandatory in modern Docker — daemon refuses to start with a plain TCP listener.

name: docker.security.dct-passphrase
observations: DCT passphrase: Per-key passphrase encrypting the on-disk PEM. Env vars to supply non-interactively: `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_REPOSITORY_PASSPHRASE`, `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_OFFLINE_PASSPHRASE`, `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_TARGETS_PASSPHRASE`. Required for CI signing.

name: docker.security.daemon-socket-attack-surface
observations: daemon-socket attack surface: `docker.sock` is root-equivalent for whoever can write to it. Mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` into a container = handing the container root on the host. Common foot-gun in 'CI runner' containers. Mitigation: use a docker-in-docker setup with strict TLS, OR use an authorization plugin to gate the API.

name: docker.security.cgroup-delegation-systemd
observations: cgroup delegation (systemd): systemd's `Delegate=yes` on a user-mode service lets it own its cgroup subtree. Required for rootless dockerd to enforce per-container resource limits. v2 unified-hierarchy only.

name: docker.security.image-signing-cosign
observations: image signing (cosign / sigstore): Modern alternative to DCT/Notary: keyless OIDC-based signatures (cosign) attached as referrers to the image manifest in OCI registries. Verified via `cosign verify`. Replaces TUF-based DCT for many supply-chain teams.

name: docker.security.tuf-targets-key
observations: TUF targets key: Top-level targets key — controls which delegations/keys are trusted to sign tags. Held offline alongside root.

name: docker.security.image-supply-chain
observations: image supply chain: The full path from source code to running container: source repo → CI build → base-image source → registry → puller → runtime. Each hop is an attack surface. DCT / cosign sign each hop's output; provenance attestations document the build environment; SBOM lists ingredients.

name: docker.security.kernel-vulnerability-exposure
observations: kernel vulnerability exposure: Containers share the host kernel — a kernel CVE that lets a privileged-enough syscall escape namespace = container escape. Default seccomp blocks the worst offenders (kexec_*, init_module, perf_event_open, …). Defense: keep kernel patched, run with seccomp on, drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: docker.security.rootless-userland-runtime
observations: rootless userland runtime: The dockerd-rootless wrapper (`dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh`) that launches dockerd inside a user namespace using `newuidmap` / `newgidmap`. Runs as user-mode systemd service under `~/.config/systemd/user/docker.service`. Uses `slirp4netns` (or `vpnkit` on Mac) for unprivileged networking.

name: docker.security.capability-bounding-set
observations: capability bounding set: Per-process kernel limit on which capabilities a process and its descendants can ever hold. Docker default-drops most caps, leaving only: chown, dac_override, fowner, fsetid, kill, setgid, setuid, setpcap, net_bind_service, net_raw, sys_chroot, mknod, audit_write, setfcap. Override via `--cap-add` / `--cap-drop`.

name: docker.security.subgid-file
observations: /etc/subgid: Same as subuid for GID ranges. `usermod --add-subuids/--add-subgids` or manual edits.

name: docker.security.cgroup-v2-vs-v1-security
observations: cgroup v2 vs v1 security: v2 unified hierarchy supports cgroup-delegation (an unprivileged user can manage their own subtree). v1's per-controller hierarchies don't — rootless dockerd needs v2 for full functionality. Per docker docs, 'Cgroup delegation is not secure in cgroups v1.'

name: docker.security.slirp4netns
observations: slirp4netns: Userspace TCP/IP stack (TUN-based) used by rootless dockerd to give containers network access without CAP_NET_ADMIN. Slower than kernel-bridge networking; `--rootless` containers route through it. Configurable via `DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_NET=slirp4netns`.

name: docker.security.userns-remap-mode
observations: userns-remap mode: Daemon-level user-namespace remapping. Configured via daemon.json `userns-remap: "default"` (uses `dockremap` system user) or `userns-remap: "<user>:<group>"`. Container root (uid 0) maps to host's non-zero uid. Mutually exclusive with `--privileged`, `--ipc=host`, `--net=host`, `--pid=host` containers. Bind-mount/volume ownership becomes the remapped uid — common foot-gun.

name: docker.security.rootless-mode
observations: rootless mode: Run the daemon AND containers WITHOUT root privileges. Distinct from userns-remap, where dockerd is root but containers are remapped. Rootless = dockerd as a normal user inside its own user namespace. Limits: cgroup v1 doesn't support cgroup-delegation in rootless; AppArmor not supported on Debian-derived; checkpoint/restore unsupported; no overlay2 on kernels < 5.13 (uses fuse-overlayfs).

name: docker.security.mtls-daemon-socket
observations: mTLS daemon socket: Mutual-TLS on dockerd's TCP listener. Daemon: `--tlsverify --tlscacert=ca.pem --tlscert=server.pem --tlskey=server-key.pem -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2376`. Client picks via `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY=1` + `DOCKER_CERT_PATH=…`. Mandatory for any production TCP exposure — daemon refuses non-TLS TCP listeners.

name: docker.security.tuf-delegation-key
observations: TUF delegation key: Per-delegated-role signing key (e.g. `targets/<delegation>`). Lets repo owners scope signing capability to subsets of tags or specific signers. Useful for CI signing limited tag ranges.

name: docker.security.least-privilege
observations: least privilege: Drop everything by default; add only what the workload needs. `--cap-drop=ALL` + selective `--cap-add` is the canonical knob. Same idea applies to volumes (read-only), network (--network=none unless needed), and seccomp (custom profile blocking unused syscalls).

name: docker.security.notary-server
observations: Notary server: The TUF-based signing service Docker Content Trust talks to. Stores signed metadata (root.json, snapshot.json, timestamp.json, targets.json) for image-tag → digest mappings. Configurable via `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST_SERVER` (default `https://notary.docker.io` for Docker Hub).

name: docker.security.linux-uid-mapping
observations: UID mapping (security view): User-namespace mapping `containerID hostID size` written to `/proc/<pid>/uid_map`. Container root (uid 0) → some non-zero host uid (e.g. 165536). Without CAP_SETUID, only `newuidmap` SETUID binary can write multi-range mappings (consults /etc/subuid).

name: docker.security.linux-gid-mapping
observations: GID mapping (security view): Same pattern for groups via `/proc/<pid>/gid_map` and `newgidmap`.

name: docker.security.no-new-privileges
observations: no-new-privileges: Sets `no_new_privs` bit on the container's pid 1. Prevents setuid binaries from gaining new caps via execve. Enable per-container with `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`; daemon-wide via daemon.json `no-new-privileges: true`. Cheap, strong baseline hardening.

name: docker.security.selinux-enforcement
observations: SELinux enforcement: Daemon-level `selinux-enabled: true` enables container_t labeling. Containers are then confined by the SELinux policy (RHEL/CentOS/Fedora). Bind mount `:z` (shared label) / `:Z` (private label) modifies the host label. WARNING: bind-mounting system dirs with `:Z` can render the host inoperable.

name: docker.security.tls-pin
observations: TLS certificate pinning: Trusting only a specific CA cert (or even leaf cert) for the daemon socket. Defends against rogue CAs. Configured via `--tlscacert` on both daemon and client. With `tlsverify` on, anything not chained to the pinned CA is rejected.

name: docker.security.unprivileged-userns
observations: unprivileged user namespaces: Kernel feature that lets non-root users create user namespaces. Required by rootless mode. Some distros disable it (`/proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone=0`); enable with `sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` (Debian) or `user.max_user_namespaces` tuning.

name: docker.security.tuf-root-key
observations: TUF root key: Top-level offline-stored signing key. Signs `root.json` (the trust anchor). Compromise = full takeover; rotation requires offline ceremony. Generated with `docker trust key generate`. Format: encrypted PEM under `~/.docker/trust/private/<sha256>.key`.

name: docker.security.cosign-keypair
observations: cosign keypair: `cosign generate-key-pair` produces `cosign.key` (encrypted) and `cosign.pub`. Signature attached as a referrer manifest to the image. Or keyless: OIDC token from a CI provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) signs ephemerally — Fulcio mints a short-lived cert.

name: docker.security.container-escape
observations: container escape: A class of vulns where a process inside a container gains code execution outside it. Vectors: kernel CVE + permissive seccomp; CAP_SYS_ADMIN + setns; mounting host-fs paths inside a privileged container; runc CVEs. Each class is mitigated by a different layer of defense-in-depth.

name: docker.security.signed-image-pull
observations: signed image pull: With `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1`, `docker pull <repo>:<tag>` resolves the tag through Notary instead of trusting the registry's tag-to-digest mapping. Rejects pulls of unsigned tags. The user-facing piece of DCT.

name: docker.security.cert-rotation
observations: certificate rotation: Daemon TLS certs rotate via daemon restart with a new key/cert pair (graceful rotation requires brief overlap). Notary timestamp/snapshot keys rotate automatically server-side. Long-lived offline root keys are the rotation pain point.

name: docker.security.selinux-context
observations: SELinux context: Type-enforcement label on processes and files. Format `user:role:type:level`. Docker assigns `container_t` to container processes by default on SELinux-enabled hosts; bind mounts get `container_file_t`. `:z` / `:Z` on a `-v` mount relabels the host path.

name: docker.security.tuf-repository-key
observations: TUF repository key (targets-of-targets): Per-image-repository signing key (a.k.a. tagging key). Created on first push of a repo with DCT enabled. Signs `targets/releases.json`. Held by repo maintainers.

name: docker.security.tuf-snapshot-key
observations: TUF snapshot key: Signs `snapshot.json` — the consistent hash of all metadata at a point in time. By default held by Notary server (so it can rotate frequently); can be moved client-side for stricter posture.

name: docker.security.tuf-timestamp-key
observations: TUF timestamp key: Signs `timestamp.json` — short-lived signature attesting freshness. Always held server-side (must rotate continuously). Defends against replay attacks.

name: docker.security.cri-vs-docker-engine
observations: CRI vs docker-engine attack surface: On k8s nodes since 1.24, kubelet talks to containerd via CRI directly (no dockerd). Removes the docker.sock attack surface entirely. Trade-off: lose `docker` CLI on the node — `crictl` is the equivalent. Important context for Kubernetes hardening.

name: docker.security.subuid-file
observations: /etc/subuid: Per-user subordinate UID range allocations. Format `username:start:count` per line. Required for userns-remap mode (`dockremap` user) and rootless mode. Need ≥ 65,536 subordinate UIDs.

name: docker.security.notary-signer
observations: Notary signer: The notary component that holds the snapshot+timestamp signing keys server-side (so they can rotate automatically without dropping clients). Distinct from the user-controlled root/targets keys.

name: docker.security.tuf-repository
observations: TUF repository: The Update Framework metadata layout DCT uses: a hierarchy of signed JSON files (root → targets → delegations → snapshot → timestamp) that together attest a specific image-tag → digest binding. Industry-standard, designed to survive a partial key compromise.

name: docker.security.seccomp-profile
observations: seccomp profile (security view): JSON-format syscall filter loaded into the kernel via the `seccomp()` syscall. Docker's default profile (moby/profiles/seccomp/default.json) blocks ~44 of 300+ syscalls. Allowlist semantics: defaultAction `SCMP_ACT_ERRNO` (deny+EPERM); per-syscall overrides to `SCMP_ACT_ALLOW`. CONFIG_SECCOMP=y kernel + Docker built with seccomp required.

name: docker.security.content-trust-DCT
observations: Docker Content Trust (DCT): Image signing via TUF. Set `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1` in the env to enable; affected commands: `pull`, `push`, `build`, `create`, `run`. With DCT on, pulls reject unsigned images; pushes auto-sign. Tag-to-digest binding becomes immutable.

name: docker.security.defense-in-depth
observations: defense in depth: Layered hardening: namespaces (isolation) + cgroups (resource limits) + capabilities (privilege fragmentation) + seccomp (syscall filter) + AppArmor/SELinux (LSM) + read-only rootfs + no-new-privileges + signed images. Each layer only has to slow an attacker down; together they make container escape very expensive.

name: docker.security.xdg-runtime-dir
observations: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: Per-user runtime dir (`/run/user/<uid>`). Rootless dockerd uses it for sockets, pid files, etc. Must be writable by the user; cleaned at logout. Persistent rootless services need `loginctl enable-linger <user>` so the dir survives logout.

name: docker.security.default-seccomp-profile
observations: default seccomp profile: `moby/profiles/seccomp/default.json` is auto-applied to every container. Blocks ~44 syscalls (acct, add_key, bpf, clock_settime, create_module, init_module, kexec_*, keyctl, mount, ptrace under restrictive caps, reboot, swap*, sysctl, umount, unshare, …). Disable with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`; replace with `--security-opt seccomp=<file>`.

name: docker.security.path-traversal-volume-mount
observations: path-traversal via volume mount: Class of attack where a malicious image / Dockerfile mounts `/` (or `/etc`, `/var/lib`) from the host and reads/writes outside the container's intended scope. Mitigation: never run untrusted images with `--privileged`, audit `-v` / `--mount` carefully, use userns-remap so container writes aren't host root.

name: docker.security.vpnkit
observations: vpnkit: Mac-equivalent of slirp4netns used by Docker Desktop. User-space VPN+TUN that forwards container traffic from the Linux VM to the host.

name: docker.security.default-apparmor-profile
observations: default AppArmor profile: `docker-default` profile loaded by dockerd at startup on AppArmor-enabled hosts. Generated programmatically; can be regenerated and tweaked. Per-container override: `--security-opt apparmor=<name>` or `apparmor=unconfined`.

name: docker.security.read-only-rootfs
observations: read-only rootfs: `docker run --read-only` mounts container root as RO. Combine with explicit `--tmpfs /tmp` for writable scratch space. Stops attackers from persisting payloads in the container's writable layer.

name: docker.security.cap-drop-all-baseline
observations: cap-drop=ALL baseline: Hardening pattern: `--cap-drop=ALL` then selective `--cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE` (etc.). The least-privilege baseline. Combined with `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true` and `--read-only`, gives a strong minimal-privilege container.

name: docker.security.apparmor-profile
observations: AppArmor profile: LSM profile loaded into the kernel via `apparmor_parser`. Docker auto-loads `docker-default` and applies it per container; override with `--security-opt apparmor=<name>`. Profile DSL: capabilities, file rules, network rules, mount/ptrace/signal/dbus access. Ubuntu/Debian default; SUSE optional.

name: docker.security.tmpfs-mount-noexec
observations: tmpfs noexec: Default tmpfs flags Docker applies: `rw,noexec,nosuid,size=65536k`. The `noexec` is the security-relevant bit — prevents executing dropped binaries from /dev/shm or /tmp.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildkit-llb
observations: BuildKit LLB: Low-Level Build — protobuf-based intermediate format defining a content-addressable dependency graph of build operations. The thing every frontend compiles to. Concurrently executable, efficiently cacheable, vendor-neutral. 'LLB is to Dockerfile what LLVM IR is to C.'

name: docker.build-buildkit.inline-cache
observations: inline cache: `--cache-to type=inline` embeds the cache manifest in the pushed image (extra layer with cache metadata). Pull the image to get the cache. Simplest sharing pattern for CI; slightly larger images.

name: docker.build-buildkit.workdir-instruction
observations: WORKDIR: `WORKDIR <path>`. Sets cwd for subsequent instructions. Auto-creates if missing.

name: docker.build-buildkit.bake-target-matrix
observations: bake target matrix: `docker buildx bake` uses HCL/JSON/Compose to define a build matrix. `target.<name>` per build target; `group.<name>.targets` for groups; `variable.<name>` for parameterization. CI driver for multi-target / multi-platform builds.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cache-key-derivation
observations: cache key derivation: BuildKit derives a cache key per LLB op from: the op type, its args, the SHA of any input mounts, and the SHA of mount sources. Change any input → new cache key → re-execution. The reason `COPY package.json` before `RUN npm install` makes npm install cacheable across most builds.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd-instruction
observations: CMD: Default args to entrypoint. Forms: `CMD ["executable","arg"]` (exec — preferred), `CMD ["arg"]` (default args to ENTRYPOINT), `CMD command arg` (shell — wraps in /bin/sh -c). Replaced when `docker run <image> <override>`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.user-instruction
observations: USER: `USER <uid|name>[:<gid|group>]`. Sets the user for subsequent RUN/CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Hardening best practice: drop to non-root (`USER 1000:1000`) before CMD.

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-cache-shared
observations: shared build cache: `--cache-from` + `--cache-to` push/pull cache to a shared backend. CI builds reuse cache across runners. Combined with `mode=max` to save intermediate layers.

name: docker.build-buildkit.frontend-image-pinning
observations: frontend image pinning: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.6.0` pins to an exact frontend version. Reproducibility + new-feature gating. Trade-off: pin-too-tight = miss security fixes; pin-too-loose = nondeterministic builds.

name: docker.build-buildkit.dockerfile-frontend
observations: Dockerfile frontend: The default frontend that parses Dockerfiles to LLB. Released as `docker/dockerfile` images; latest stable: `docker/dockerfile:1`. Newer features land here first, available to anyone via `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:<version>`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.bind-mount-build
observations: bind mount (build): `RUN --mount=type=bind,source=<context-path>,target=<path>` exposes context-side files into the RUN without making a layer copy. Read-only by default; `,rw` for writable. Replaces COPY for build-only access patterns.

name: docker.build-buildkit.local-cache-export
observations: local cache: `--cache-to type=local,dest=<path>` writes cache to a local directory. `--cache-from type=local,src=<path>` reads it. Useful when a registry isn't available; caches must be persisted between CI runs (cache action).

name: docker.build-buildkit.copy-instruction
observations: COPY: `COPY [--from=<stage|image>] [--chown=<user:group>] [--chmod=<mode>] [--link] <src> [<src>...] <dest>`. From context (default) or another stage/image. `--link` decouples the copy from previous-layer cache invalidation (faster rebuilds).

name: docker.build-buildkit.dockerfile-instruction
observations: Dockerfile instruction: A single line in a Dockerfile (FROM, RUN, COPY, etc.). Each becomes one LLB op (and potentially one image layer for FS-modifying instructions). Order matters — caching is from-the-top, so any change invalidates downstream.

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-secret
observations: build secret: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=<name>` mounts a secret as a tmpfs file inside the RUN. Source from CLI (`--secret id=<name>,src=<path>` or `,env=<env-var>`). Secret content NEVER ends up in image layers — solves the 'secret in ARG leaks via `docker history`' problem.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cache-mount
observations: cache mount: `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=<path>[,id=<id>][,sharing=shared|private|locked]` reuses a writable directory across builds. Used for package-manager caches (`/root/.cache/go-build`, `/var/cache/apt`). Per-builder; not part of any image layer.

name: docker.build-buildkit.env-instruction
observations: ENV: `ENV KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE...]`. Sets env vars in the image AND for subsequent build steps. Persists into the running container. Distinct from ARG.

name: docker.build-buildkit.mount-cache-id-shareable
observations: --mount=type=cache sharing: `RUN --mount=type=cache,id=<id>,sharing=shared|private|locked,target=<path>`. `shared` = concurrent builds share; `private` = each build's own; `locked` = serialize concurrent access. The `id` namespace lets multiple builds share the same package-manager cache safely.

name: docker.build-buildkit.entrypoint-vs-cmd-form
observations: ENTRYPOINT/CMD shell vs exec form: Exec form (`["binary","arg"]`) execs directly — pid 1 IS the binary, signals propagate. Shell form (`binary arg`) wraps in /bin/sh -c — pid 1 is sh, your binary is sh's child, SIGTERM goes to sh and is dropped. Always prefer exec form for production.

name: docker.build-buildkit.output-tarball
observations: output tarball: `--output type=docker|oci,dest=<file>.tar` exports the build result as a tarball instead of (or in addition to) loading into the local image store. Forms: `type=image` (default), `type=local,dest=<dir>`, `type=tar,dest=-`, `type=registry`, `type=docker`, `type=oci`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.registry-cache
observations: registry cache: `--cache-to type=registry,ref=<image>,mode=max` pushes the cache as a separate manifest in a registry. `--cache-from type=registry,ref=<image>` pulls it. `mode=max` saves all layers including intermediate; `mode=min` (default) only the final layers.

name: docker.build-buildkit.gha-cache
observations: GitHub Actions cache: `--cache-to type=gha,scope=<>,name=<>` writes to GitHub Actions' cache backend (env GITHUB_TOKEN required). Tightly integrated with `actions/cache`. Experimental.

name: docker.build-buildkit.from-instruction
observations: FROM: `FROM <image>[:<tag>|@<digest>] [AS <stage-name>]`. Sets the base image for the next stage. Multiple FROM = multi-stage. `FROM scratch` = empty rootfs (smallest possible image). Pin to digest for reproducibility.

name: docker.build-buildkit.expose-instruction
observations: EXPOSE: `EXPOSE <port>[/<proto>]` declares ports the image listens on. Pure metadata — doesn't actually publish. `-P` consumes EXPOSE entries (auto-publishes to ephemeral host ports).

name: docker.build-buildkit.healthcheck-instruction
observations: HEALTHCHECK: `HEALTHCHECK [OPTIONS] CMD <command>` defines an in-image health probe. Options: `--interval`, `--timeout`, `--retries`, `--start-period`, `--start-interval`. `HEALTHCHECK NONE` clears any inherited check.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildx-driver-kubernetes
observations: buildx driver: kubernetes: Runs buildkitd as a Kubernetes Deployment / StatefulSet — for shared CI builders. Configurable replicas, node selector, rootless mode. `docker buildx create --driver kubernetes`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.tmpfs-mount-build
observations: tmpfs mount (build): `RUN --mount=type=tmpfs,target=<path>` mounts an in-memory tmpfs for the duration of the RUN. Useful for scratch / disposable temp dirs that mustn't pollute layers.

name: docker.build-buildkit.add-instruction
observations: ADD: Like COPY but also supports URL fetch (`ADD https://...`) and tar auto-extract (`.tar.gz` etc.). `--checksum=sha256:<hex>` for integrity check on URL fetch. Generally prefer COPY unless you need ADD's special features.

name: docker.build-buildkit.entrypoint-instruction
observations: ENTRYPOINT: Binary the container runs. Exec form (`["binary","arg"]`) preferred — signals propagate properly. Shell form wraps in /bin/sh -c (PID 1 = sh, signals don't reach the binary).

name: docker.build-buildkit.stopsignal-instruction
observations: STOPSIGNAL: `STOPSIGNAL <signal>` sets the kill signal for `docker stop` (and the image's StopSignal config field). Default SIGTERM. e.g. nginx uses SIGQUIT for graceful shutdown.

name: docker.build-buildkit.oci-image-format-vs-docker-v2-2
observations: OCI vs docker v2-2 image format: Two manifest formats, mostly compatible. BuildKit defaults to OCI; legacy builder used Docker v2-2. Cross-references in `docker.runtime.media-type`. Some old registries reject OCI-only manifests; force docker format with `--provenance=false --output type=docker`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildx-driver-docker-container
observations: buildx driver: docker-container: Runs buildkitd inside a container managed by buildx. Most-used driver for advanced features: multi-platform, cache export, custom buildkitd config. Created via `docker buildx create --driver docker-container`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-context
observations: build context: The directory tree the build sees as `.`. Streamed to buildkitd by buildx (incrementally — only changed files since last build). Filtered by `.dockerignore`. Forms: local path, git URL, URL+ref+subdir, named (additional) context.

name: docker.build-buildkit.run-instruction
observations: RUN: `RUN <command>` (shell form, wraps in /bin/sh -c) or `RUN ["exec","args",...]` (exec form). Creates a new layer with command output. Mounts: `RUN --mount=type=bind|cache|secret|ssh|tmpfs`. Network isolation: `RUN --network=default|none|host`. Privilege: `RUN --security=insecure|sandbox` (insecure requires --allow=security.insecure on build).

name: docker.build-buildkit.here-doc-syntax
observations: heredoc syntax: `RUN <<EOF` / `COPY <<EOF` writes inline multi-line content. Supports `<<-EOF` (strip leading tabs), `<<"EOF"` (no-interpolation). Cleaner than `RUN echo "line1" && echo "line2"` chains.

name: docker.build-buildkit.dockerignore-patterns
observations: .dockerignore patterns: `.dockerignore` (in build context root) excludes paths from the context BEFORE upload. Patterns: `*` (any chars in name), `?` (single char), `**` (any nested dirs), `!pattern` (negate), `# comment`. Critical for build perf — without it, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, etc. get streamed every build.

name: docker.build-buildkit.frontend-syntax-directive
observations: # syntax= directive: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` (or :1.6, or @sha256:...) at the top of a Dockerfile. Pins the frontend image. Lets new Dockerfile features land without daemon upgrade. Pin to a specific minor for reproducibility; use :1 to auto-upgrade within v1.

name: docker.build-buildkit.dockerfile-stage
observations: Dockerfile stage: A `FROM <image> [AS <name>]` block in a Dockerfile. Multi-stage builds chain stages; later stages can `COPY --from=<stage>` from earlier ones. Unused stages are skipped; independent stages run in parallel. Build target via `--target <stage>`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.escape-directive
observations: # escape= directive: Top-of-file `# escape=\\` (default) or `# escape=`` ` ``. Sets the line-continuation character for the rest of the Dockerfile. Use backtick for Windows where backslash is path separator.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildkit-frontend
observations: BuildKit frontend: A pluggable component that converts a human-readable build format (e.g. Dockerfile) to LLB. Distributed as container images (`docker/dockerfile:1.6`); user pins a specific version via `# syntax=`. The reason newer Dockerfile features (RUN --mount=, here-docs, etc.) work without upgrading buildkitd.

name: docker.build-buildkit.s3-cache
observations: S3 cache: `--cache-to type=s3,region=<>,bucket=<>,prefix=<>,name=<>`. Experimental. Useful when CI is on AWS and you want shared org-wide cache.

name: docker.build-buildkit.label-instruction
observations: LABEL: `LABEL key=value [key=value...]`. Adds metadata labels to the image. Standard keys: `org.opencontainers.image.{title,description,authors,vendor,licenses,source,documentation,version,revision,created}`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.parallel-stage-execution
observations: parallel stage execution: BuildKit runs independent stages concurrently. Final stage waits on its dependencies (`COPY --from=<x>` or `RUN` in stages it depends on). Big speedup for monorepos.

name: docker.build-buildkit.here-document
observations: here-document: YAML/shell-style multi-line literal: `<<EOF ... EOF`. Inside a Dockerfile RUN/COPY: provides the content of a file or multi-line script. Variants: `<<-EOF` (strip leading tabs), `<<"EOF"` (literal — no var interpolation).

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildx-driver-docker
observations: buildx driver: docker: Default `docker buildx` driver. Uses the BuildKit library bundled with dockerd (no external buildkitd). Limited: doesn't support multi-platform, cache exports, or experimental Dockerfile features. Auto-selected when no other driver is configured.

name: docker.build-buildkit.onbuild-instruction
observations: ONBUILD: `ONBUILD <instruction>`. Triggers when a downstream image uses this image as base. Used in language-base images: 'whoever uses me must have a package.json' patterns. Often ill-advised — surprising behavior for downstream users.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cross-platform-build
observations: cross-platform build: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm/v7 .` builds a multi-arch image and pushes a manifest list. Uses QEMU-static for non-native arches OR remote builders. `BUILDPLATFORM` (where it runs), `TARGETPLATFORM` (what it builds for) ARGs auto-injected.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildkitd
observations: buildkitd: BuildKit daemon. gRPC API on `/run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock` (Linux) or `npipe:////./pipe/buildkitd` (Windows). Two worker backends: OCI (runc) and containerd; OCI default. Reads `/etc/buildkit/buildkitd.toml`. Listens on Unix socket by default; can expose TCP via `--addr tcp://...` (use TLS).

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-arg
observations: build arg (ARG): Build-time variable declared with `ARG NAME[=default]`. Pass via `--build-arg NAME=val`. Visible only AFTER the ARG declaration; an ARG before FROM is global. Distinct from ENV — ARG values aren't baked into the resulting image (so secrets via ARG leak via `docker history`).

name: docker.build-buildkit.oci-cache
observations: OCI cache: `--cache-to type=oci,dest=<dir>` writes cache as an OCI layout dir. Used by tools that consume the OCI format directly.

name: docker.build-buildkit.arg-instruction
observations: ARG: `ARG NAME[=default]`. Build-time variable. Visible after declaration (or globally if before first FROM). Pass via `--build-arg`. Common globals: `BUILDPLATFORM`, `TARGETPLATFORM`, `TARGETOS`, `TARGETARCH`, `TARGETVARIANT` (auto-set in multi-platform builds).

name: docker.build-buildkit.image-layer-deduplication
observations: layer deduplication: Same layer (by content-addressable digest) is stored once on disk regardless of how many images reference it. Engine + registry both dedupe. The reason 100 images sharing `ubuntu:24.04` only cost the layer's size once.

name: docker.build-buildkit.azblob-cache
observations: Azure Blob cache: `--cache-to type=azblob,account_url=<>,account_name=<>,name=<>,prefix=<>`. Azure equivalent of S3 cache. Experimental.

name: docker.build-buildkit.parser-directive
observations: parser directive: Top-of-file `# directive=value` lines. Three: `# syntax=`, `# escape=`, `# check=`. Must be at the very top — first non-directive line ends parser-directive parsing.

name: docker.build-buildkit.dockerfile-comment
observations: Dockerfile comment: Lines starting with `#` (and not matching parser directive form) are comments. `#` mid-line isn't a comment — only at start. Backslash continuations (`\`) work for multi-line instructions.

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-args-from-env
observations: build args from env: `docker buildx build --build-arg HTTP_PROXY` (no `=`) pulls value from caller's env. Useful for proxy / token passthrough without baking the value into a CI script.

name: docker.build-buildkit.experimental-syntax
observations: experimental Dockerfile syntax: `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1-labs` opts into experimental features (new instruction forms, mount types). Lands in `:1` mainline once stable.

name: docker.build-buildkit.volume-instruction
observations: VOLUME: `VOLUME <path>` declares a path as a volume mount point. At `docker run`, an anonymous volume is auto-created if no `-v`/--mount targets the path. Foot-gun: makes the directory unmodifiable in subsequent layers.

name: docker.build-buildkit.secret-not-in-layer
observations: secrets not in layers: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=token` mounts a secret as a tmpfs file for one RUN. Secret content is NEVER captured in image layers. Solves 'secret leaked via `docker history`' problems caused by --build-arg.

name: docker.build-buildkit.shell-vs-exec-form
observations: shell vs exec form (rules): Shell form: arguments are a single string passed to /bin/sh -c. Exec form: JSON array, NO shell — env vars NOT expanded by shell, signals direct. Mix-up causes 'why doesn't $HOME expand?' on exec-form RUN.

name: docker.build-buildkit.buildx-driver-remote
observations: buildx driver: remote: Connects to a pre-existing buildkitd over TCP/socket. Used for shared org-wide builders. e.g. `docker buildx create --driver remote tcp://buildkit.example.com:1234`. Pairs with TLS for production.

name: docker.build-buildkit.build-ssh-mount
observations: build SSH mount: `RUN --mount=type=ssh` forwards the host's SSH agent socket to a build step. Lets `git clone` private repos without baking the key. CLI: `--ssh default` (uses host SSH agent) or `--ssh <id>=<path-to-key>`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.shell-instruction
observations: SHELL: `SHELL ["executable","arg",...]`. Override the shell used for shell-form RUN/CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Default Linux: `["/bin/sh","-c"]`. Common Windows: `["powershell","-Command"]` or `["cmd","/S","/C"]`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.multi-stage-build
observations: multi-stage build: Multiple `FROM` blocks; later stages `COPY --from=<earlier-stage>`. Final image only contains what's in the last stage (or `--target=<stage>`). Drastic image size reduction (build tools left in early stage, only the binary copied to the final).

name: docker.build-buildkit.image-tag-vs-digest
observations: image tag vs digest: `FROM nginx:1.27` (mutable) vs `FROM nginx@sha256:...` (immutable). For reproducible builds, pin to digest. CI updates the pin on a schedule (renovate / dependabot) so security patches still land.

name: linux.primitives.clone-syscall
observations: clone(2) syscall: Creates a new process or thread with selectable resource sharing via the CLONE_* flags. Foundation of every container start: runc invokes clone with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWNET (and CLONE_NEWCGROUP on cgroup v2) to put the new process in fresh namespaces. clone3() is the modern variant accepting a struct clone_args. Failure path: EPERM when caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN for namespace creation flags; EINVAL when an invalid flag combination is passed (e.g. CLONE_THREAD without CLONE_VM).

name: linux.primitives.fork-syscall
observations: fork(2) syscall: Creates a new process by duplicating the calling process via copy-on-write. The child gets a copy of the parent's address space, file descriptors, signal dispositions, and most attributes. Returns 0 in child, child PID in parent, -1 on error. Modern Linux implements fork() as a thin wrapper around clone() with no CLONE_* flags. Failure path: EAGAIN when the per-user RLIMIT_NPROC is hit or system fork-bomb-protection trips.

name: linux.primitives.execve-syscall
observations: execve(2) syscall: Replaces the current process image with a new program. Preserves PID, parent PID, file descriptors (unless O_CLOEXEC was set), and most signal masks. RESETS effective UID to file's setuid owner if setuid bit is set, EXCEPT when caller has PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS — the cornerstone of why containers set no_new_privs. Capability sets are recomputed via the cap-transition formula (see capabilities(7)). Failure modes: ENOEXEC (binary format unrecognized), ETXTBSY (binary open for writing), EACCES (no execute permission).

name: linux.primitives.unshare-syscall
observations: unshare(2) syscall: Disassociates parts of the calling process's execution context from a previously shared one — creates new namespaces in-place without forking. Takes the same CLONE_NEW* flag set as clone(). Useful for setting up a fresh namespace before exec'ing into a container payload. CLONE_NEWUSER must be the first/only flag in single calls; combine others in a second unshare after entering the user namespace.

name: linux.primitives.setns-syscall
observations: setns(2) syscall: Joins the calling process to an existing namespace identified by a file descriptor opened on /proc/<pid>/ns/<type>. Order matters when joining multiple: user namespace first to acquire credentials, then mount/pid/net/etc. The mechanism behind nsenter(1) and the runtime entrypoint of `docker exec`. Failure: EPERM when caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the target user namespace.

name: linux.primitives.pivot-root-syscall
observations: pivot_root(2) syscall: Atomically switches a mount namespace's root filesystem from one mount to another, moving the old root to a designated subdirectory. The clean container-init pattern: mount new rootfs, chdir into it, pivot_root, umount the old root. Safer than chroot because the process can't see/escape to the old root once unmounted. Used by runc; replaces the older chroot+mount-move dance.

name: linux.primitives.seccomp-syscall
observations: seccomp(2) syscall: Configure secure-computing state on the calling thread. Modes: SECCOMP_MODE_STRICT (only read/write/_exit/sigreturn allowed) and SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER (BPF-program-driven syscall filtering). Once set, can only be tightened (no relaxation), and PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS must be set or caller needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Foundation of Docker's default seccomp profile (~330 syscalls allowed) and Kubernetes' RuntimeDefault profile.

name: linux.primitives.prctl-syscall
observations: prctl(2) syscall: Multiplexed process-control syscall. Operations selected by first arg: PR_SET_NAME (thread name), PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (signal on parent death), PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (one-way bit forbidding privilege gain via execve), PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER (zombie reaping), PR_CAPBSET_DROP (capability bounding set drop), PR_CAP_AMBIENT (ambient capability manipulation), and dozens more. Single most-used 'misc process attribute' interface.

name: linux.primitives.keyrings-syscall
observations: keyctl(2)/add_key(2)/request_key(2): In-kernel key-management syscalls. add_key creates a key in a keyring; keyctl manipulates keyring permissions, links, revocations; request_key asks the kernel to find or instantiate a key (possibly invoking userspace via /sbin/request-key). Foundation of dm-crypt key passing, NFSv4 idmap, and per-process secret stores.

name: linux.primitives.signal-handler-installation
observations: sigaction(2) signal handler installation: Establishes a handler for a signal via struct sigaction (sa_handler/sa_sigaction + sa_flags + sa_mask). Replaces the older signal(2) interface, which has portability quirks. Critical flags: SA_RESTART (restart interrupted syscalls), SA_SIGINFO (3-arg handler with siginfo_t), SA_NOCLDWAIT (auto-reap zombies for SIGCHLD). Non-async-signal-safe code in handlers is undefined behavior.

name: linux.primitives.signal-mask-manipulation
observations: sigprocmask(2)/pthread_sigmask(3) signal-mask manipulation: Per-thread signal mask manipulation. Blocks/unblocks specified signals during critical sections. Inherited across fork; preserved through execve. SIG_BLOCK/SIG_UNBLOCK/SIG_SETMASK are the operations. SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be blocked — definitional unkillable property.

name: linux.primitives.capset-capget
observations: capset(2)/capget(2) capability syscalls: Set/get the four capability sets of a thread (effective, permitted, inheritable, ambient). The libcap helper functions wrap these. The kernel enforces strict subset rules: P' (permitted) must be a subset of bset∩(P∪I-already-granted); E (effective) is a subset of P. Bounding set is per-thread and never increases.

name: linux.primitives.process-credential-syscalls
observations: setuid/setgid/setresuid family: setuid(2), seteuid(2), setreuid(2), setresuid(2) (and gid equivalents) manipulate the real, effective, saved, and filesystem UIDs of the calling process. Required CAP_SETUID for asymmetric changes. Used by su/sudo/login transitions. Capability set is recomputed on UID 0 ↔ non-zero transitions unless KEEP_CAPS securebit is set.

name: linux.primitives.setrlimit-getrlimit
observations: setrlimit(2)/getrlimit(2) resource limits: Per-process soft/hard resource limit knobs. Soft is enforced; hard is the ceiling for raising soft (lowering hard is one-way unless caller has CAP_SYS_RESOURCE). RLIMIT_NOFILE (max FDs), RLIMIT_NPROC (max processes per real UID), RLIMIT_AS (max virtual memory), RLIMIT_STACK, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_CORE, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE, RLIMIT_NICE, RLIMIT_RTPRIO, RLIMIT_RTTIME, RLIMIT_SIGPENDING. systemd unit `LimitNOFILE=` etc. set these per-service.

name: linux.primitives.pthread-create
observations: pthread_create(3) thread creation: POSIX thread creation primitive — wrapper around clone(2) with CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_SYSVSEM|CLONE_SETTLS|CLONE_PARENT_SETTID|CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID. All threads in a process share the PID (TGID); their per-thread ID is the kernel's PID. SIGSTOP/SIGCONT and most fatal signals affect the whole thread group.

name: linux.primitives.pthread-join
observations: pthread_join(3): Wait for a joinable thread to terminate, optionally retrieving its exit value. Calling join on a detached thread is undefined. Forgetting to join a joinable thread leaks resources (thread stack, TLS).

name: linux.primitives.pthread-detach
observations: pthread_detach(3): Mark a thread as detached so its resources are auto-released on termination. Once detached, no longer joinable. Equivalent to creating with attr.detachstate=PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED.

name: linux.primitives.pthread-cancel
observations: pthread_cancel(3): Request cancellation of another thread. Cancellation is delivered at predefined cancellation points (most blocking syscalls: read, write, sleep, wait). Disabled per-thread via pthread_setcancelstate. Cancellation type (deferred vs asynchronous) governed by pthread_setcanceltype. Asynchronous cancellation is dangerous — handlers can run between any two instructions.

name: linux.primitives.cap-effective-set
observations: Effective capability set (E): The set of capabilities currently active for permission checks. Subset of permitted. A thread can flip caps in/out of E without privilege so long as they're in P. The set the kernel checks against on each privileged operation.

name: linux.primitives.cap-permitted-set
observations: Permitted capability set (P): The 'master' set: capabilities the thread is allowed to make effective. Bounded above by the bounding set. Permanently lost after `capset(P, …)` removes a cap unless ambient or file-cap bestowal restores it.

name: linux.primitives.cap-inheritable-set
observations: Inheritable capability set (I): Set of capabilities preserved across execve. For non-root execs, only caps in (I ∩ file-inheritable) survive into the new program's permitted set. UID-0 execs can promote everything in P. Original mechanism for capability transition; mostly superseded by the ambient set in modern setups.

name: linux.primitives.cap-bounding-set
observations: Capability bounding set: Per-thread upper bound on the inheritable and permitted sets. Drops are one-way (PR_CAPBSET_DROP); never grows. Container runtimes use this to permanently strip CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_TIME, etc. from container init. systemd's `CapabilityBoundingSet=` directive is exactly this.

name: linux.primitives.cap-ambient-set
observations: Ambient capability set: Per-thread set of capabilities that are preserved across non-setuid execve into permitted+effective. The post-2016 mechanism for 'I want this non-root program to have CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE permanently.' Capabilities raised via PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE; cleared on UID change. systemd's `AmbientCapabilities=` directive.

name: linux.primitives.process-effective-uid
observations: Effective UID (EUID): The UID the kernel uses for permission checks (file access, signal sending, IPC). Initially equals real UID; setuid binaries set it to file owner. Returned by geteuid(2). Container processes inside a userns have a UID inside the container that maps to a different host UID per /proc/<pid>/uid_map.

name: linux.primitives.process-real-uid
observations: Real UID (RUID): The UID identifying the user who started the process. Used by the kernel for accounting (RLIMIT_NPROC) and for SIGCHLD attribution. Returned by getuid(2). Stays stable across setuid transitions; only setuid(2) with CAP_SETUID can change.

name: linux.primitives.process-saved-uid
observations: Saved set-user-ID (SUID): Records the EUID at the time of a setuid execve so the program can later swap back to it via setuid/seteuid. Enables the 'temporarily drop privileges' pattern in setuid programs without permanent loss.

name: linux.primitives.process-fs-uid
observations: Filesystem UID (FSUID): Per-thread UID used only for filesystem permission checks. Linux-specific; allows NFS server processes to act as another user for FS operations without becoming that user for signal-receiving purposes. Equals EUID by default; setfsuid(2) decouples them.

name: linux.primitives.signal-disposition
observations: Signal disposition: Per-process attribute mapping each signal to one of: default action (SIG_DFL — Term, Core, Ign, Stop, Cont as defined per signal), ignore (SIG_IGN), or a user-installed handler. Reset to SIG_DFL on execve unless the disposition was SIG_IGN (preserved). Installed via signal(2) (legacy) or sigaction(2) (modern).

name: linux.primitives.signal-pending-set
observations: Pending signal set: Per-thread (and per-process for shared signals) bitmap of signals delivered but not yet handled because they're masked. Standard signals do not queue — multiple deliveries while blocked count as one. Realtime signals (SIGRTMIN..SIGRTMAX) DO queue, up to RLIMIT_SIGPENDING.

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-v2
observations: cgroup v2: The unified cgroup hierarchy: a single tree where every controller (cpu, memory, io, pids, hugetlb) operates on the same cgroups. Mounted at /sys/fs/cgroup. Replaces the v1 multi-hierarchy mess (one tree per controller). Controllers enabled per-subtree via cgroup.subtree_control. Required for full container resource accounting on modern systemd. systemd uses 'unified' (v2-only) or 'hybrid' (v2 + v1) modes; pure v1 is the 'legacy' mode.

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-v1
observations: cgroup v1: The original multi-hierarchy cgroup model: each controller (cpu, cpuacct, memory, blkio, devices, freezer, hugetlb, net_cls, net_prio, perf_event, pids, cpuset) mounts a separate hierarchy under /sys/fs/cgroup/<controller>/. A process can be in a different cgroup per controller. Deprecated in favor of v2 but still widely deployed; Docker on older kernels and some Kubernetes node pools.

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-hierarchy
observations: cgroup hierarchy: A tree of cgroups, each containing a set of processes. Children inherit (and can further constrain) the limits of parents. v2 has exactly one tree; v1 has one per controller. Membership lookup via /proc/<pid>/cgroup.

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-controller
observations: cgroup controller: A kernel subsystem that constrains or accounts resources for processes in a cgroup. v2 controllers: cpu, memory, io, pids, hugetlb, rdma, misc, cpuset. Enabled per-subtree by writing the controller name (e.g. '+memory') to cgroup.subtree_control. Cannot be enabled in a cgroup that contains processes (the 'no internal processes' rule for non-root cgroups).

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-delegation
observations: cgroup delegation: Granting an unprivileged user write access to a cgroup subtree so they can manage their own sub-cgroups. Requires write access to cgroup.procs, cgroup.threads, cgroup.subtree_control, and the cgroup.* control files of children. The mechanism systemd uses to let user units self-manage their resource limits without root.

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-no-internal-procs
observations: No-internal-processes rule (cgroup v2): In cgroup v2, a non-root cgroup with controllers enabled cannot contain processes directly — only its leaf descendants can. Forces a clean tree shape for resource accounting. Common surprise when migrating from v1 (where processes could live anywhere); systemd-cgls makes the layout visible.

name: linux.primitives.namespace-isolation-model
observations: Linux namespace isolation model: Per-process scoping of kernel resources so different processes see different views. 8 namespace types: mount (filesystem mounts), pid (process IDs), uts (hostname/domainname), ipc (System V IPC + POSIX msg queues), net (interfaces, sockets, routing), user (UID/GID mappings + capabilities), cgroup (cgroup root view), time (CLOCK_MONOTONIC offsets). Container = a process in a fresh set of all 8.

name: linux.primitives.pid-namespace
observations: PID namespace: Isolates the process ID number space. Processes inside see different (usually lower) PIDs than their host PIDs. The first process in a new pid namespace becomes pid 1 — gains init responsibilities (zombie reaping, signal-default behavior: ignored signals don't kill it). PID-1 death = entire namespace dies. Hierarchical: parent namespace can see and signal child-namespace processes (via host PIDs).

name: linux.primitives.pid-1-init-semantics
observations: PID 1 init semantics: The first process in a PID namespace has special kernel behavior: ignored signals (no handler installed) are silently dropped instead of being delivered with default action; orphaned children reparent to it; if it exits, every other process in the namespace receives SIGKILL. This is why container init processes that don't reap zombies leak them indefinitely (defunct processes accumulate) and why naive entrypoints don't respond to `docker stop` (SIGTERM is dropped). Solved by tini/dumb-init/--init.

name: linux.primitives.pid-namespace-translation
observations: PID translation across namespaces: A single process has different PIDs in each PID namespace it belongs to (its own and all ancestors). /proc/<host-pid>/status NSpid line lists all of them. Tools like nsenter use the host PID; commands inside the container reference container-namespace PIDs. Source of confusion in 'process X is running' — depends on the PID namespace you're asking from.

name: linux.primitives.user-namespace
observations: User namespace: Isolates UID/GID number spaces and the capability set within. A process can be UID 0 inside its userns (full caps inside) while being an unprivileged UID outside. Foundation of rootless containers: the dockremap user (or rootless dockerd's owning user) provides the host range that container UIDs map to via /etc/subuid + /etc/subgid + /proc/<pid>/uid_map. Userns nesting is supported (configurable max via user.max_user_namespaces sysctl).

name: linux.primitives.user-namespace-uid-mapping
observations: User namespace UID mapping: Per-userns mapping table from container-internal UIDs to host UIDs. Written once to /proc/<pid>/uid_map (and gid_map). Format: 'inside-uid host-uid count' lines. Writing requires CAP_SETUID in the parent namespace OR (for unprivileged users) restricted to a single 1:1 mapping unless /proc/<pid>/setgroups was first written 'deny'. The /etc/subuid range handed out by newuidmap(1) per user.

name: linux.primitives.mount-namespace
observations: Mount namespace: Per-process view of the mount-point hierarchy. New mounts inside don't affect outside (and vice versa) — modulated by mount propagation flags (shared/private/slave/unbindable). Set up by container runtimes to give each container its own rootfs without polluting the host's /mnt tree.

name: linux.primitives.mount-namespace-propagation
observations: Mount propagation (shared/private/slave/unbindable): Per-mount attribute controlling cross-namespace mount-event visibility. SHARED: events propagate both ways with peers. PRIVATE: no propagation. SLAVE: receives events from master but doesn't send back. UNBINDABLE: cannot be bind-mounted. Container runtimes typically make the container's /sys/fs/cgroup slave so host cgroup-mount changes are visible without container changes leaking back. Source of the 'docker volume mount changes don't appear on host' surprise when propagation is wrong.

name: linux.primitives.network-namespace
observations: Network namespace: Isolates network devices, addresses, routing tables, ports, sockets, /proc/net/*, /sys/class/net/*. Each netns has its own loopback. veth pairs link two namespaces; one end goes inside, the other lives in the host bridge (docker0). Per-netns iptables/nftables rulesets. The whole network leaf operates within this primitive.

name: linux.primitives.uts-namespace
observations: UTS namespace: Isolates the hostname and NIS domainname (uname() fields). The smallest namespace by surface area — just 2 strings. Why `hostname` inside a container differs from the host without affecting it.

name: linux.primitives.ipc-namespace
observations: IPC namespace: Isolates System V IPC objects (shared memory segments, message queues, semaphores) and POSIX message queues. /dev/shm is per-IPC-namespace. ipcs(1) inside a container shows only that namespace's IPC objects. Containers default to a private ipcns; opt out with `--ipc=host` (and lose the isolation).

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-namespace
observations: cgroup namespace: Virtualizes the cgroup-tree view in /proc/self/cgroup. Inside the namespace, the process sees its cgroup as the root (a chrooted view of the cgroup tree). Hides the host's cgroup hierarchy from container processes — important for rootless and security-sensitive containers.

name: linux.primitives.linux-security-module
observations: Linux Security Module (LSM): Hook framework in the kernel that lets security modules (SELinux, AppArmor, Smack, TOMOYO, BPF-LSM, Yama, Landlock) impose mandatory access control on top of DAC. LSMs are stackable in modern kernels (5.x+). A syscall must pass DAC then every active LSM check. The reason 'permission denied' isn't always about file mode — could be selinux denial in audit.log.

name: linux.primitives.selinux-policy-model
observations: SELinux policy model: Type-enforcement-based MAC: every process and resource has a context (user:role:type:level). Policy rules say which type can do what to which other type. Modes: enforcing (deny on violation + audit), permissive (audit only), disabled. `setenforce 0/1` toggles enforcing/permissive at runtime. ausearch on AVC denials surfaces violations. The dominant LSM on RHEL/Fedora-derived distros.

name: linux.primitives.apparmor-profile-model
observations: AppArmor profile model: Pathname-based MAC: profiles enumerate file paths a binary may access and capabilities it may use. Profiles loaded into the kernel via apparmor_parser. Modes: enforce, complain (audit-only), unconfined. Default LSM on Ubuntu/SUSE. Docker ships a default-docker profile applied to every container.

name: linux.primitives.seccomp-strict-mode
observations: seccomp SECCOMP_MODE_STRICT: Original seccomp mode: only read(2), write(2), _exit(2), and sigreturn(2) are allowed. Any other syscall sends SIGKILL. Useful for sandboxing fully-trusted compute (CPU-bound code that uses pre-opened FDs). Largely superseded by filter mode for general-purpose sandboxing.

name: linux.primitives.seccomp-filter-mode
observations: seccomp SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER: BPF-program-driven syscall filtering. The program inspects syscall number and (limited) arg registers; returns one of SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS, KILL_THREAD, TRAP, ERRNO, USER_NOTIF, TRACE, LOG, ALLOW. Multiple filters are AND-stacked (lowest action wins). The mode container runtimes use; Docker's default profile is a single filter against ~330 syscalls.

name: linux.primitives.seccomp-bpf-program
observations: seccomp-BPF program: A classic-BPF (cBPF, NOT eBPF) program of up to 4096 instructions, attached via prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER, ...) or seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER, ...). Read-only access to syscall number, arch, instruction pointer, and 6 arg registers via the seccomp_data struct. Cannot dereference user-space pointers (preventing TOCTOU on string args).

name: linux.primitives.seccomp-user-notification
observations: seccomp user-notification (SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF): Filter return value that suspends the syscalling thread and forwards the request to a userspace supervisor over a notification FD. The supervisor inspects the call, decides allow/deny/emulate, and replies. Foundation of unprivileged Docker rootless's mount(2)/iptables emulation, and tools like systemd-userdbd.

name: linux.primitives.signal-async-safety
observations: Signal async-safety: The set of functions that can safely be called from a signal handler — strictly: those whose internal state is reentrant and whose interruption can't corrupt the rest of the program. signal-safety(7) lists ~80 functions (write, _exit, kill, sigaction, fork, …); printf, malloc, and most of glibc are NOT in the set. Violating async-safety = silent corruption + heisenbugs.

name: linux.primitives.signal-handler-vs-action
observations: signal(2) vs sigaction(2): signal(2) is the historical, portability-fraught interface (handler reset to SIG_DFL after first delivery on some systems; Linux uses BSD semantics by default but System V semantics under _XOPEN_SOURCE). sigaction(2) is the canonical: explicit sa_flags, deterministic across UNIX. Always use sigaction for new code.

name: linux.primitives.keyring-trust-domain
observations: Keyring trust domain: A keyring identifies a trust scope: thread-keyring (per-thread), process-keyring, session-keyring, user-keyring, user-session-keyring, persistent-user-keyring (cross-session), .dns_resolver / .request-key-auth (system). Permissions per-key control read/write/search/link/setattr/view bits separately for possessor/user/group/other.

name: linux.primitives.credential-inheritance
observations: Credential inheritance across exec/clone: How RUID/EUID/SUID/FSUID and capabilities propagate. fork/clone: copied verbatim. execve: reset per the cap-transition rules in capabilities(7) sections 'Capabilities and execution of programs by root' and 'Transformation of capabilities during execve()'. Setuid bit re-sets EUID/SUID to file owner unless caller has PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (then setuid is no-op).

name: linux.primitives.set-no-new-privs
observations: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit: One-way per-thread bit (set via prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1)) that causes execve(2) to NOT grant privileges via setuid bits or file capabilities. Inherited across fork/clone/execve. Required for unprivileged seccomp filter installation. The cornerstone of confined process startup; systemd's `NoNewPrivileges=yes` and Docker's default for non-root containers set it.

name: linux.primitives.process-image-replacement
observations: Process image replacement (execve semantics): Calling execve(2) replaces the entire address space (text/data/heap/stack/mmaps) with the new program's, while preserving PID, parent, file descriptors not marked O_CLOEXEC, signal masks (but not handlers — those reset to defaults), and resource limits. The reason 'fork+exec' is the universal Unix process-creation idiom — the fork is for keeping the parent alive; the exec is the actual program switch.

name: linux.primitives.copy-on-write-fork
observations: Copy-on-write fork semantics: fork(2) doesn't physically duplicate the parent's address space — it shares the pages read-only and copies on write. RSS of the child immediately after fork is near-zero; only modified pages get duplicated. This is why fork+exec is cheap for shells (no real copy, then execve discards everything) but costly when the parent has a large heap that the child mutates.

name: linux.primitives.vfork-stack-sharing
observations: vfork(2) parent-blocking semantics: Legacy fork variant where the child shares the parent's address space (not COW — actually shared) until the child calls execve or _exit. The parent is suspended. Modern Linux implements vfork() as clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK|SIGCHLD). Faster than fork on systems without COW; obsolete on COW systems but still useful in narrow exec-immediately patterns.

name: linux.primitives.dac-permission-model
observations: DAC (discretionary access control) model: Classic Unix file permissions: owner/group/other × read/write/execute, plus setuid/setgid/sticky. Each process has UID + GIDs; each file has owner UID + group GID + 9 mode bits. Per-file ACLs (xattrs) extend this. Capabilities augment for fine-grained privileged operations. LSMs add MAC on top.

name: linux.primitives.posix-acl-vs-dac
observations: POSIX ACLs vs DAC mode bits: ACLs are stored in xattrs (system.posix_acl_access, system.posix_acl_default) and let you grant per-user/per-group permissions beyond the owner/group/other tuple. Mask entry caps the effective permissions of all named entries. Detail in linux/filesystem.

name: linux.primitives.oom-killer
observations: OOM killer: Kernel mechanism that selects and SIGKILLs a process when memory cannot be allocated and overcommit can't be honored. Score per process: oom_score (sum of factors) adjusted by oom_score_adj (-1000 to +1000; -1000 is OOM-immune). MemoryMax in cgroup v2 triggers a per-cgroup OOM kill. Containers see exit code 137 (128 + 9 = SIGKILL).

name: linux.primitives.oom-score-adj
observations: oom_score_adj: Per-process tunable bias (-1000 to +1000) added to the OOM score. -1000 = never kill. +1000 = kill first. Set via /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj or systemd's OOMScoreAdjust=. Container runtimes often set the container init's adj to -500 so the OOM killer prefers user processes.

name: linux.primitives.unified-vs-legacy-cgroup
observations: Unified vs legacy cgroup controllers: v2 introduces a few new controllers (io supersedes blkio with better tracking), reuses some (cpu, memory, pids), and drops some (net_cls, net_prio went to BPF/eBPF; devices went to BPF-LSM). 'Hybrid' mode mounts v2 + v1 simultaneously but a controller can be active in only one. Migration is one-way per-controller.

name: linux.primitives.namespace-fs-membership
observations: Namespace FS membership via /proc/<pid>/ns/: Each namespace appears as a magic symlink in /proc/<pid>/ns/{pid,user,mnt,ipc,uts,net,cgroup,time}. The link target is a unique 'ns:[<inode>]' identifier; two processes in the same namespace have identical targets. setns(2) takes an open FD on these. nsenter -t PID -p -m -n is just open()s of these files plus setns().

name: linux.primitives.cgroup-v2-pressure-stall
observations: Pressure Stall Information (PSI): Per-cgroup metric exposing how much time tasks were blocked on CPU/memory/IO contention. /sys/fs/cgroup/<cg>/cpu.pressure, memory.pressure, io.pressure. Format: 'some avg10=… avg60=… avg300=… total=…' and 'full avg10=…'. The data behind systemd's MemoryPressureWatch and oomd's killing decisions.

name: linux.primitives.process-lifecycle
