observations: Service Type=notify: Service uses sd_notify(3) to tell systemd it's READY=1. Until then, dependents wait. Best mode for graceful startup of complex daemons (PostgreSQL, nginx-with-warmup).

name: linux.systemd.service-type-dbus
observations: Service Type=dbus: Considered started when BusName= appears on the system bus. For dbus-activated daemons.

name: linux.systemd.service-type-idle
observations: Service Type=idle: Like simple but delays exec until all jobs are dispatched. Cosmetic — keeps shell text from interleaving with boot output.

name: linux.systemd.restart-policy
observations: Restart= policy: When to auto-restart on exit: no (never), always, on-success, on-failure (non-zero exit / signal / watchdog), on-abnormal (signal / timeout / abort), on-watchdog, on-abort. The most-tuned directive for resilience.

name: linux.systemd.restart-rate-limit
observations: StartLimit (restart rate limit): StartLimitIntervalSec=10s + StartLimitBurst=5 — if unit starts >5 times in 10s, it goes to 'failed' permanently (until reset-failed). Prevents restart loops from masking deeper bugs.

name: linux.systemd.exec-environment
observations: Exec environment: Per-service env: Environment=, EnvironmentFile= (read from path), PassEnvironment= (inherit named host env vars). UnsetEnvironment= removes. systemctl show-environment / set-environment for the manager-wide global.

name: linux.systemd.exec-stdio
observations: Exec stdio handling: StandardInput=, StandardOutput=, StandardError= each set per-fd: null, tty, journal (default), syslog (deprecated), kmsg, journal+console, file:PATH, append:PATH, socket, fd:NAME. Default journal sends to journald.

name: linux.systemd.exec-user-group
observations: User= / Group= directives: Drop privileges to specified user/group before ExecStart. systemd creates dynamic user (DynamicUser=yes) for ephemeral identity if requested. Works with SupplementaryGroups= for additional GIDs.

name: linux.systemd.exec-dynamic-user
observations: DynamicUser=yes: Allocate a transient UID/GID for the service runtime. UID picked from 61184-65519 range. Useful for sandboxing without managing static users. Implies several hardening directives by default (RemoveIPC=, PrivateTmp=, NoNewPrivileges=).

name: linux.systemd.dependency-wants
observations: Wants= (soft dependency): Want a unit started; if it fails, current unit still proceeds. Soft dependency. Implemented via .wants/ directory — symlink to target unit.

name: linux.systemd.dependency-requires
observations: Requires= (hard dependency): Want a unit started; if it fails or stops, this unit is also stopped. Hard dependency. Use Wants= for resilience.

name: linux.systemd.dependency-requisite
observations: Requisite= (must-already-be-started): Like Requires but doesn't start the dependency — fails this unit if dependency isn't already active.

name: linux.systemd.dependency-binds-to
observations: BindsTo=: Like Requires but ALSO stops this unit if the dependency goes inactive (not just fails). The strictest dependency.

name: linux.systemd.dependency-conflicts
observations: Conflicts=: Cannot be active at same time as listed unit. Starting one stops the other.

name: linux.systemd.ordering-before-after
observations: Before= / After=: Ordering relationship (independent of Wants/Requires). After=foo.service means 'wait for foo.service to be active before starting me'. Doesn't IMPLY a dependency — combine with Wants/Requires for full effect.

name: linux.systemd.condition-vs-assert
observations: Condition* vs Assert*: ConditionX= (e.g. ConditionPathExists=) — if false, unit silently skipped (still 'active (exited)'). AssertX= — if false, unit FAILS. Assert is for catching configuration errors loudly; Condition for opportunistic activation.

name: linux.systemd.cgroup-integration
observations: systemd cgroup integration: Every service runs in its own cgroup under its slice's cgroup. systemd manages cgroup creation/deletion automatically. Resource control directives (MemoryMax=, CPUQuota=, etc.) translate to cgroup v2 control files (memory.max, cpu.max, etc.).

name: linux.systemd.cgroup-slice-tree
observations: systemd cgroup slice tree: Top-level: -.slice. Children: system.slice (services), user.slice (per-user user-UID.slice with session-N.scope), machine.slice (containers via systemd-machined). Each unit's cgroup nested under its slice.

name: linux.systemd.transient-unit
observations: Transient unit: Unit created at runtime (no on-disk file). Created via `systemd-run` or systemd's D-Bus API. Used for ad-hoc execution under systemd's resource control. Does not survive systemd reload unless made persistent.

name: linux.systemd.drop-in
observations: Drop-in directory (.d): UNIT.service.d/ directory containing override.conf or per-purpose .conf files. Layered on top of base unit file — directives can extend (Environment=, list-valued) or override (scalar). systemctl edit creates this.

name: linux.systemd.specifier
observations: systemd unit specifier: %-prefixed substitution in unit files. %u = user, %i = instance (template), %h = home dir, %t = runtime dir, %T = tmp dir, %v = kernel version, %m = machine ID, %H = hostname, %p = prefix, %P = unescaped prefix, %n = full unit name, %N = unescaped, %j = final component, %J = unescaped, %s = shell, %L = log dir, %S = state dir, %C = cache dir, %E = config dir.

name: linux.systemd.template-instance
observations: Template + instance units: Template unit foo@.service can be instantiated as foo@arg.service — %i = arg in unit file. Used for per-X services (getty@tty1.service, dhcpcd@eth0.service).

name: linux.systemd.socket-activation
observations: Socket activation: systemd opens the listening socket; on first connect, starts the service and passes the FD. Service inherits via LISTEN_FDS env var + sd_listen_fds(3). Saves boot time (services start lazily) and supports auto-restart without dropped connections.

name: linux.systemd.notify-protocol
observations: sd_notify protocol: Service writes status messages to NOTIFY_SOCKET (env-var path). Supported messages: READY=1, RELOADING=1, STOPPING=1, STATUS=string, ERRNO=N, BUSERROR=string, MAINPID=PID, WATCHDOG=1, EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC=N. Type=notify makes systemd wait for READY.

name: linux.systemd.watchdog
observations: systemd watchdog: WatchdogSec= sets ping interval. Service must sd_notify(WATCHDOG=1) within. Failure → Restart=on-watchdog → kill+restart. Hardware watchdog (RuntimeWatchdogSec=) reboots on systemd hang.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-private-tmp
observations: PrivateTmp=: Mounts a fresh private /tmp + /var/tmp namespace for the service. Other services can't see its temp files. Default for many vendor units.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-private-network
observations: PrivateNetwork=: Service runs in fresh netns with only loopback. Cuts off network entirely — perfect for batch jobs that don't need it.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-private-devices
observations: PrivateDevices=: New /dev with only minimal devices (null, zero, full, urandom, tty, ptmx). Hides hardware.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-protect-system
observations: ProtectSystem=: strict (RO mount of entire FS except /dev /proc /sys), full (RO of /usr /boot /efi), true (RO of /usr /boot), false (default off). Major hardening for services that don't write FS.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-protect-home
observations: ProtectHome=: yes (no /home access), read-only, tmpfs (empty tmpfs at /home), false. Stops services from rummaging in user data.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-no-new-privs
observations: NoNewPrivileges=: Sets the prctl PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit. setuid binaries don't gain privs in this service. Required for running unprivileged seccomp filters.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-syscall-filter
observations: SystemCallFilter=: Per-service seccomp filter. Allowlist syntax (positive list), denylist with ~ prefix. Pre-defined groups: @system-service, @network-io, @file-system, @basic-io, @io-event, @ipc, @timer, @resources, @setuid, @raw-io, @reboot, @swap, @clock, @cpu-emulation, @debug, @keyring, @memlock, @mount, @module, @obsolete, @pkey, @privileged, @process, @sandbox.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-cap-bounding-set
observations: CapabilityBoundingSet=: Cap-bounding-set for the service (whitelist style, prefix with ~ for denylist). e.g. `CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` lets service bind <1024 but nothing else.

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-ambient-caps
observations: AmbientCapabilities=: Set ambient capabilities for the service. Capabilities preserved into permitted+effective across non-setuid execve. The mechanism for non-root services with elevated caps (e.g. CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE).

name: linux.systemd.sandboxing-readwrite-paths
observations: ReadWritePaths= / ReadOnlyPaths= / InaccessiblePaths=: Per-path overlays on the FS namespace. ReadWritePaths exposes specific dirs as RW under ProtectSystem=strict. InaccessiblePaths blocks specific paths. ReadOnlyPaths makes specific dirs RO.

name: linux.systemd.resource-memory-max
observations: MemoryMax=: Hard memory limit for the cgroup. Process exceeding triggers per-cgroup OOM killer. Maps to cgroup v2 memory.max. Suffixes: K/M/G/T (1024-base) or 'infinity'.

name: linux.systemd.resource-memory-high
observations: MemoryHigh=: Throttle threshold (kernel aggressively reclaims when exceeded). No OOM. Maps to memory.high.

name: linux.systemd.resource-cpu-quota
observations: CPUQuota=: Percentage of one CPU (e.g. 50% = half a CPU; 200% = 2 CPUs). Maps to cgroup cpu.max via period/quota math.

name: linux.systemd.resource-cpu-weight
observations: CPUWeight=: Relative CPU share weight under contention (1-10000, default 100). Maps to cgroup cpu.weight.

name: linux.systemd.resource-tasks-max
observations: TasksMax=: Max tasks (processes/threads) in the unit's cgroup. Maps to pids.max. Hitting it causes fork() to return EAGAIN.

name: linux.systemd.resource-io-weight
observations: IOWeight= / IODeviceWeight=: Relative IO share. Maps to cgroup io.weight / io.weight per device.

name: linux.systemd.resource-io-max
observations: IOReadBandwidthMax= / IOWriteBandwidthMax= / IOReadIOPSMax= / IOWriteIOPSMax=: Per-device IO bandwidth/IOPS ceilings. Maps to cgroup io.max.

name: linux.systemd.exec-private-mounts
observations: PrivateMounts=: Service runs in fresh mount namespace (MS_PRIVATE) — its mounts don't leak to host. Default for many sandbox-aware services.

name: linux.systemd.exec-protect-kernel
observations: ProtectKernel{Tunables,Modules,Logs}=: yes = forbids writes to /proc/sys, /sys/kernel; module loading; reading kernel ring buffer (dmesg). Hardening for non-admin services.

name: linux.systemd.kill-mode
observations: KillMode=: control-group (default: SIGTERM all in cgroup, then SIGKILL after TimeoutStopSec), process (only main process), mixed (SIGTERM main, SIGKILL the cgroup), none (no kill). control-group is usually what you want for clean shutdowns.

name: linux.systemd.kill-signal
observations: KillSignal= / RestartKillSignal=: Signal to send on stop (default SIGTERM). RestartKillSignal for restarts. Some daemons want SIGINT or SIGQUIT for graceful (nginx wants SIGQUIT).

name: linux.systemd.timeout-stop-sec
observations: TimeoutStopSec=: Grace period after SIGTERM before SIGKILL escalation. Default 90s. Set higher for slow shutdowns (DB checkpointing).

name: linux.systemd.timeout-start-sec
observations: TimeoutStartSec=: Max time for unit to reach 'active'. Default 90s. Longer for cold-start daemons (Java warmup, Postgres recovery).

name: linux.systemd.timer-on-calendar
observations: OnCalendar= timer expression: Wall-clock schedule. Format: DOW YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Parts can be wildcard (*) or list (1,3,5) or range (8..18) or step (*/15). Examples: hourly = *-*-* *:00:00; daily = *-*-* 00:00:00; weekly = Mon *-*-* 00:00:00; *-*-* 08..18:00:00 = every hour 8-18.

name: linux.systemd.timer-persistent
observations: Persistent=yes: For OnCalendar= timers: if missed (system off when scheduled), run on next boot. Critical for daily backup-style timers.

name: linux.systemd.timer-randomized-delay
observations: RandomizedDelaySec=: Random delay 0-N before timer fires. Spreads load when many hosts have same OnCalendar=.

name: linux.systemd.socket-listen-stream
observations: ListenStream= / ListenDatagram=: Socket address spec: PORT (TCP/UDP), [::]:PORT (IPv6), /path/to/socket (unix), @abstract (Linux abstract unix), vsock:CID:PORT, fd:NAME (inherited).

name: linux.systemd.socket-accept
observations: Accept=yes vs no: yes = systemd accept()s each connection and forks a service@N.service per conn (inetd-style). no (default) = pass listen-FD to single service which calls accept() itself (more efficient for high conn rates).

name: linux.systemd.journal-fields
observations: Journal fields: Each journal entry has multiple fields. Trusted (kernel-set, '_'-prefixed): _PID, _UID, _GID, _COMM, _EXE, _CMDLINE, _CAP_EFFECTIVE, _SYSTEMD_UNIT, _SYSTEMD_SLICE, _SYSTEMD_CGROUP, _SYSTEMD_INVOCATION_ID, _BOOT_ID, _MACHINE_ID, _HOSTNAME, _SELINUX_CONTEXT, _AUDIT_SESSION, _AUDIT_LOGINUID. Application fields: MESSAGE, PRIORITY, SYSLOG_*, CODE_*, ERRNO.

name: linux.systemd.journal-priority
observations: Journal priority levels: PRIORITY field (matches syslog severity): 0 emerg, 1 alert, 2 crit, 3 err, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 info, 7 debug. journalctl -p N filters; -p err shows ≤3.

name: linux.systemd.journal-cursor
observations: Journal cursor: Opaque token uniquely identifying an entry. Used to resume reads (journalctl --cursor=...). Survives rotation.

name: linux.systemd.journal-storage
observations: Journal Storage= mode: persistent (write to /var/log/journal/), volatile (only /run/log/journal/, lost on reboot), auto (persistent if /var/log/journal/ exists, else volatile), none (drop entries). Default 'auto'.

name: linux.systemd.journal-rate-limit
observations: Journal rate limiting: RateLimitIntervalSec=30s + RateLimitBurst=10000 = each unit can log up to 10000 messages per 30s; beyond that, journald drops + logs '<unit>: Suppressed N messages from /SYSTEMD_UNIT'. Per-unit, not global.

name: linux.systemd.journal-vacuum
observations: Journal vacuum: Free old journal data: --vacuum-size=200M (max total), --vacuum-time=2weeks (delete older), --vacuum-files=20 (max archive count).

name: linux.systemd.coredump-handling
observations: Core dump handling (systemd-coredump): systemd installs '|/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-coredump %P %u %g %s %t %c %h' as kernel.core_pattern. On crash, kernel pipes core to systemd-coredump which compresses + stores under /var/lib/systemd/coredump/. coredumpctl(1) queries and extracts.

name: linux.systemd.tmpfiles-d
observations: tmpfiles.d: systemd-tmpfiles creates/removes/cleans files+dirs at boot and periodically. Configured via /etc/tmpfiles.d/*.conf, /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/. Each line: TYPE PATH MODE UID GID AGE ARGUMENT.

name: linux.systemd.user-scope
observations: User scope (per-user systemd): Each logged-in user gets a systemd --user instance via user@UID.service (PAM session). Manages user-level services (~/.config/systemd/user/). systemctl --user. Per-user units run inside user-UID.slice.

name: linux.systemd.machine-scope
observations: Machine scope (systemd-machined): Tracks running 'machines' (containers, VMs registered via sd_notify). machinectl(1) lists/inspects/shells into. The cgroup tree under machine.slice — used by systemd-nspawn, libvirt, container runtimes that integrate.

name: linux.systemd.runtime-state-runtime-dir
observations: RuntimeDirectory=: Auto-create /run/<UNIT>/ at start, owned by service user, deleted at stop. Replaces hand-rolled tmpfiles for runtime-state needs (sockets, lock files). Companion: StateDirectory=, CacheDirectory=, LogsDirectory=, ConfigurationDirectory= for /var/lib, /var/cache, /var/log, /etc respectively.

name: linux.systemd.boot-target
observations: Boot target (default.target): What systemd boots into. /etc/systemd/system/default.target is a symlink (set via systemctl set-default). graphical.target → multi-user.target → basic.target → sysinit.target → local-fs.target → ... ordering chain.

name: linux.systemd.shutdown-target
observations: Shutdown / poweroff / reboot targets: shutdown.target (Conflicts= with everything to stop services), poweroff.target / reboot.target / halt.target (all alias for shutdown.target with different final action). systemctl reboot/poweroff/halt invokes them.

name: linux.systemd.journald-subsystem
observations: systemd-journald: Logging daemon. Receives messages via /run/systemd/journal/socket (sd_journal_send), kmsg (kernel), audit (auditd), syslog (forwarded). Stores in binary journal at /run/log/journal/ or /var/log/journal/. Indexed for fast queries.

name: linux.systemd.logind-subsystem
observations: systemd-logind: Session/seat/user manager. Tracks logins via PAM, manages session scopes, handles inhibition (suspend/poweroff blockers), seat assignment for multi-seat hosts.

name: linux.systemd.coredump-subsystem
observations: systemd-coredump: Core-dump handler invoked via kernel.core_pattern pipe. Captures + compresses + journals + indexes core dumps. coredumpctl is the query frontend.

name: linux.systemd.tmpfiles-subsystem
observations: systemd-tmpfiles: Service that creates/cleans /tmp /run /var per tmpfiles.d/ rules. Runs at boot (--create), periodically via timer (--clean), and on shutdown (--remove).

name: linux.systemd.analyze-subsystem
observations: systemd-analyze: Performance + correctness inspection tool. Subcommands: time/blame (boot timing), critical-chain, plot (SVG boot timeline), dump, verify (lint unit files), security (sandboxing audit per service), cat-config, exit-status.

name: linux.systemd.run-subsystem
observations: systemd-run: Launch transient unit (or service/scope/timer) for ad-hoc execution under systemd's resource control. Useful for one-off command with MemoryMax= / CPUQuota=, or scheduling via --on-calendar.

name: linux.systemd.dbus-api
observations: systemd D-Bus API: Manager + per-unit D-Bus objects on system bus (org.freedesktop.systemd1). All unit operations (Start/Stop/Reload/Restart, get state, set property) go via D-Bus. systemctl is a D-Bus client.

name: linux.systemd.journal-format
observations: Journal binary format: Custom binary log format with structured fields, deduplicated values, hash chaining (Forward Secure Sealing). Compact, indexed for queries by field. Files: system.journal (root), user-UID.journal, plus archived user-UID@TIMESTAMP.journal-INDEX rotations.

name: linux.systemd.unit-file
observations: /etc/systemd/system/<unit>: Admin-installed unit files. Override + augment vendor units in /usr/lib/systemd/system/.

name: linux.systemd.vendor-unit-file
observations: /usr/lib/systemd/system/<unit>: Vendor-shipped unit files (package-managed). Don't edit directly — use drop-ins or copy to /etc/systemd/system/ to override.

name: linux.systemd.runtime-unit-file
observations: /run/systemd/system/<unit>: Runtime-generated unit files (transient units, generators). Cleared on reboot. Higher precedence than /usr/lib/systemd/system/, lower than /etc/systemd/system/.

name: linux.systemd.journal-dir
observations: /var/log/journal/<machine-id>/: Persistent journal storage. Per-machine-id dir; system.journal + user-UID.journal files inside. /run/log/journal/ for volatile.

name: linux.systemd.coredump-dir
observations: /var/lib/systemd/coredump/: Where systemd-coredump stores compressed cores. Filename: core.<COMM>.<UID>.<BOOTID>.<PID>.<TIMESTAMP>.zst.

name: linux.systemd.tmpfiles-dir
observations: /etc/tmpfiles.d/ + /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/: tmpfiles.d configuration dirs. systemd-tmpfiles applies rules to manage runtime files.

name: linux.systemd.journald-conf-file
observations: /etc/systemd/journald.conf: journald configuration. Drop-ins via /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/.

name: linux.systemd.system-conf
observations: /etc/systemd/system.conf: Manager (PID 1) configuration: DefaultLimitNOFILE, DefaultMemoryAccounting, RuntimeWatchdogSec, etc.

name: linux.systemd.cgroup-driver
observations: cgroup driver: systemd manages cgroups via direct file ops (write to cgroup.procs, etc.) and notifies via cgroup.events for tracking. Pure-v2 mode (DefaultCPUAccounting=yes etc. require v2). docker/cri-o coordinate via the 'systemd' cgroup driver vs 'cgroupfs' driver.

name: linux.systemd.journal-storage-driver
observations: Journal storage driver: Backend for journal entries. persistent (disk), volatile (tmpfs), auto, none. Compression (Compress=yes), Forward Secure Sealing (Seal=yes).

name: linux.systemd.timer-scheduler-driver
observations: Timer scheduler: Per-timer state machine — next-elapse computation from OnCalendar/OnBootSec/OnUnitActiveSec. Persistent= bookkeeping in /var/lib/systemd/timers/.

name: linux.systemd.systemd-subsystem
observations: systemd (PID 1): The init/service manager. Replaces SysV init/upstart on most distros. Manages units, dependencies, sockets, cgroups, timers, mounts. D-Bus API at /run/systemd/private and the system bus.

name: linux.filesystem.vfs
observations: VFS (Virtual Filesystem Switch): Kernel layer abstracting concrete filesystems (ext4, xfs, btrfs, tmpfs, NFS, etc.) behind a uniform API. Every syscall (open, read, write, stat, mount) goes through VFS. Per-FS modules implement vfs_ops. Concepts: superblock (per-mount), inode (per-file), dentry (path component cache), file (per-open).

name: linux.filesystem.inode
observations: Inode: Per-file metadata structure: mode, uid/gid, size, timestamps (atime/mtime/ctime), block addresses, link count, device. Doesn't include filename (that's in dentry). Number reused after delete. ls -i shows inode number; df -i tracks inode usage (filesystems can run out of inodes before bytes).

name: linux.filesystem.dentry
observations: Dentry (directory entry): VFS cache mapping a name to an inode within a directory. Speeds up path resolution. dcache size visible via slabtop. Negative dentries cache 'this name doesn't exist' for failed lookups.

name: linux.filesystem.superblock
observations: Superblock: Per-filesystem metadata: filesystem type, block size, total blocks, free blocks, mount options, magic number. Read on mount, written on superblock-changing ops + sync. Backup copies in ext4 (mke2fs -n shows locations) for recovery.

name: linux.filesystem.file-handle
observations: File handle / file descriptor: Per-process integer (FD) referencing an open file via the per-process FD table → file struct → inode. Limit per-process by RLIMIT_NOFILE; system-wide by fs.file-max. lsof lists.

name: linux.filesystem.path-resolution
observations: Path resolution: How kernel walks /a/b/c: starts at root (or CWD for relative), looks up 'a' in root's dentry, descends, etc. Symlinks followed up to MAXSYMLINKS (40). Crosses mountpoints. Mount-namespace isolation means 'absolute path' depends on which namespace.

name: linux.filesystem.mount-syscall
observations: mount(2) syscall: Attach a filesystem to a path. Args: source, target, fs-type, flags (MS_*), data (fs-specific options). Requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN (or be in user namespace owning the mountns). Modern interface: open_tree(2), fsopen(2), fsmount(2), move_mount(2), fspick(2) for finer control.

name: linux.filesystem.umount-syscall
observations: umount(2) / umount2(2) syscall: Detach filesystem. EBUSY if files in use; umount2 with MNT_FORCE for unkillable mounts; MNT_DETACH for lazy unmount (returns immediately, actually detaches when last use closes).

name: linux.filesystem.open-syscall
observations: open(2) / openat(2) syscall: Open a file, returning FD. Flags: O_RDONLY/O_WRONLY/O_RDWR; O_CREAT (create if missing — needs mode), O_EXCL (fail if exists with O_CREAT), O_TRUNC, O_APPEND, O_NONBLOCK, O_SYNC, O_DIRECT, O_NOFOLLOW, O_CLOEXEC. openat takes dirfd + relative path.

name: linux.filesystem.openat2-syscall
observations: openat2(2) syscall: Modern open with explicit how struct: flags + mode + RESOLVE_* bits (RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT, RESOLVE_CACHED). Designed for safe path-resolution in untrusted contexts (containers, sandboxes).

name: linux.filesystem.stat-syscall
observations: stat(2)/fstat/lstat/fstatat: Get file metadata. stat follows symlinks; lstat doesn't; fstat takes FD; fstatat takes dirfd + path + AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW flag. Returns struct stat with all inode fields. statx(2) is the modern enriched version.

name: linux.filesystem.statfs-syscall
observations: statfs(2)/fstatfs/statvfs: Get FILESYSTEM stats: type, block size, total/free/avail blocks/files, fsid. statfs vs statvfs differ slightly in struct layout. The data behind df.

name: linux.filesystem.fsync-syscall
observations: fsync(2)/fdatasync/syncfs: Force writeback of cached writes for an FD (fsync = data + metadata; fdatasync = data + critical metadata; syncfs = entire filesystem). Required for crash-consistent data. Slow on rotational disks; modern flash much faster.

name: linux.filesystem.mmap-mappings
observations: mmap memory mappings: Map file pages into process address space. PROT_READ/WRITE/EXEC; MAP_SHARED (changes write back to file) vs MAP_PRIVATE (COW). MAP_ANONYMOUS for anon (heap-style) memory not backed by file. /proc/<pid>/maps lists.

name: linux.filesystem.symlink
observations: Symbolic link: File whose contents are a path string. Path resolution follows symlinks (up to MAXSYMLINKS=40). Crosses filesystems. Created by symlink(2) / ln -s. Read by readlink(2). Stat (vs lstat) follows.

name: linux.filesystem.hard-link
observations: Hard link: Multiple directory entries referring to the same inode. Inode link count = number of hard links. File 'deleted' only when count reaches 0 AND no FDs open. Doesn't cross filesystems. Created by link(2) / ln (no -s).

name: linux.filesystem.bind-mount
observations: Bind mount: Make a path visible at another path (mount --bind src dst). Same inode reachable via two paths. Used by container runtimes for volume mounts. Recursive variant: --rbind. mount(8) + MS_BIND flag.

name: linux.filesystem.tmpfs
observations: tmpfs: In-memory filesystem. Backed by VM (page cache + swap). Sized via mount option size=N (default ~50% RAM). Cleared on unmount/reboot. /tmp, /run, /dev/shm typically tmpfs on modern systems.

name: linux.filesystem.proc
observations: procfs (/proc): Pseudo-filesystem exposing kernel and per-process info. Not real files — generated on read. /proc/N/* per process; /proc/sys/* sysctls; /proc/net/* network state; /proc/cpuinfo/meminfo/stat etc. The kernel-introspection backbone.

name: linux.filesystem.sysfs
observations: sysfs (/sys): Pseudo-filesystem exposing kernel objects (devices, drivers, classes, buses, modules). /sys/class/net/, /sys/block/, /sys/devices/. Many writable for runtime tuning (sysfs interface vs sysctl interface).

name: linux.filesystem.devtmpfs
observations: devtmpfs: Pseudo-fs at /dev. Auto-populates device nodes on hotplug events from kernel. Replaces older udev-managed /dev with an in-kernel base layer (udev still adds symlinks/persistent names on top).

name: linux.filesystem.cgroup-fs
observations: cgroupfs (/sys/fs/cgroup): Pseudo-fs interface to the cgroup subsystem. Mount of type 'cgroup2' (v2) or 'cgroup' (v1, per-controller). Read/write cgroup.* files to manage. (Concept fully covered in linux/primitives.)

name: linux.filesystem.bpffs
observations: bpffs (/sys/fs/bpf): Pseudo-fs for pinning BPF objects (programs, maps, links). Allows objects to outlive the loading process. mount -t bpf bpffs /sys/fs/bpf.

name: linux.filesystem.fuse
observations: FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace): Bridge that lets userspace processes implement filesystems. Kernel module + libfuse. Used by sshfs, ntfs-3g, gvfs, mergerfs. Performance penalty vs native; correctness flexibility wins for many use cases.

name: linux.filesystem.ext4
observations: ext4: Default Linux filesystem since ~2010. Extents (vs ext3 block-mapped), delayed allocation, journaling (data=ordered/writeback/journal modes), 1 EiB max FS size. Mature, stable, well-understood. mkfs.ext4, tune2fs, e2fsck.

name: linux.filesystem.xfs
observations: XFS: High-performance scaling filesystem. Allocation groups for parallelism; B+tree indexed. 8 EiB max. Strong on large files + parallel IO. Less common for /, common for /var or /data on busy servers. mkfs.xfs, xfs_repair, xfs_growfs.

name: linux.filesystem.btrfs
observations: Btrfs: Copy-on-write filesystem with snapshots, subvolumes, RAID, integrity (checksums + scrub), online resize. Heavy in Fedora workstations and openSUSE. Reputation: amazing-when-it-works, painful-when-it-doesn't (esp. RAID5/6).

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs
observations: OverlayFS: Union mount: stack a writable upperdir on top of one or more read-only lowerdirs. Reads check upper then lower; writes go to upper (with copy-up). The mechanism behind every modern container's image-layer + writable-layer model. Mount type 'overlay' with options lowerdir=,upperdir=,workdir=.

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs-lowerdir
observations: OverlayFS lowerdir: Read-only base layer(s). Multiple : separated. First (leftmost) wins for files present in multiple. Container images: each layer is one lowerdir.

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs-upperdir
observations: OverlayFS upperdir: Read-write top layer where modifications go. Container 'writable layer'. Empty initially.

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs-workdir
observations: OverlayFS workdir: Empty dir on same FS as upperdir. Used internally for atomic operations (rename for copy-up). User shouldn't touch.

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs-copy-up
observations: OverlayFS copy-up: On first write to a lower-only file, the file is copied to upperdir then modified. Subsequent reads/writes use upper. Slow on large files (entire file copied even for small change).

name: linux.filesystem.overlayfs-whiteout
observations: OverlayFS whiteout: Special character device (mode 0, major:minor 0:0) in upperdir marking a lower file as deleted. Lookup returns ENOENT. Visible via ls -la in upperdir but invisible in merged view.

name: linux.filesystem.ramfs
observations: ramfs: Simpler than tmpfs — no swap backing, no size limit (will eat RAM until OOM). Used internally for initial rootfs (rootfs is ramfs-with-no-mount-namespace), early initramfs.

name: linux.filesystem.initramfs
observations: initramfs: Initial RAM-disk filesystem the kernel mounts as rootfs at boot. cpio archive embedded in or alongside kernel; loaded into ramfs. Init script switches to real root via switch_root. Distros use dracut, mkinitcpio, initramfs-tools to generate.

name: linux.filesystem.lvm
observations: LVM (Logical Volume Manager): Layer between block devices and filesystems: PV (physical volume) → VG (volume group) → LV (logical volume). Lets you resize, snapshot, mirror, stripe across underlying disks dynamically. lvm/pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate.

name: linux.filesystem.lvm-snapshot
observations: LVM snapshot: COW snapshot of an LV at a point in time. Initially shares all blocks with origin; only changed blocks consume snapshot space. Used for backups (snapshot, dump from snapshot, drop snapshot). Thin snapshots (thin pool) are common in modern setups.

name: linux.filesystem.dm-crypt
observations: dm-crypt / LUKS: Block-level encryption. cryptsetup luksFormat creates LUKS header + sets up key slots. luksOpen creates /dev/mapper/<name> mapped device. Filesystem mounted on top. Used for full-disk encryption.

name: linux.filesystem.loop-device
observations: Loop device: Block device backed by a regular file. losetup -f assigns a /dev/loopN; -d detaches. Used to mount disk images, raw container images, encrypted containers.

name: linux.filesystem.block-device
observations: Block device: Disk-like device exposed via /dev/<name> (sda, nvme0n1, vda). Read/write in blocks (typically 512B or 4K). Major:minor identifies driver+instance. lsblk shows hierarchy.

name: linux.filesystem.partition
observations: Disk partition: Logical subdivision of a disk. MBR (legacy, 4 primary + extended, 2TB max) or GPT (modern, 128 partitions, multi-PB). Each appears as /dev/<diskN><part> (sda1, nvme0n1p2). Tools: fdisk/gdisk/parted/sfdisk.

name: linux.filesystem.uuid
observations: Filesystem UUID: 128-bit identifier in superblock. Used in /etc/fstab as `UUID=...` so mounts work regardless of /dev/sdaN renumbering. blkid lists; tune2fs -U / xfs_admin -U change.

name: linux.filesystem.label
observations: Filesystem label: Human-readable name in superblock. Same role as UUID for mounting (LABEL=root in fstab). Limited length per FS (ext4: 16 chars; xfs: 12). e2label / xfs_admin -L.

name: linux.filesystem.mountpoint
observations: Mountpoint: Directory where a filesystem is attached. Original contents become hidden until unmount. Modern systemd unit name = encoded path (var-lib-foo.mount).

name: linux.filesystem.fstab
observations: /etc/fstab: Boot-time mount declarations. 6 fields per line: device, mountpoint, fstype, options, dump-frequency, pass-order. systemd auto-generates .mount units from this. Edit with care — broken fstab can prevent boot.

name: linux.filesystem.mtab-mountinfo
observations: /etc/mtab and /proc/mounts vs /proc/self/mountinfo: /etc/mtab: legacy text file (now usually symlink to /proc/mounts). /proc/mounts: kernel's view of host's mountns (via /proc/self/mounts). /proc/self/mountinfo: per-process mount-namespace view with full per-mount detail (id, parent, optional fields, propagation type) — what container debugging needs.

name: linux.filesystem.acl
observations: POSIX ACL: Per-file extension to DAC mode bits, stored in xattrs (system.posix_acl_access, system.posix_acl_default). Per-user / per-group permissions beyond owner/group/other. Mask entry caps named entries. getfacl/setfacl tools.

name: linux.filesystem.xattr
observations: Extended attributes (xattr): Per-file key-value metadata. Namespaces: user.* (free), system.* (kernel uses for ACLs, etc.), security.* (SELinux/IMA/file caps), trusted.* (root-only). getfattr/setfattr tools.

name: linux.filesystem.inotify
observations: inotify: Per-watch filesystem event notification. inotify_init1, inotify_add_watch, read events from FD. Watches don't follow symlinks; can't watch entire subtrees recursively (must add per-dir). fs.inotify.max_user_watches limits.

name: linux.filesystem.fanotify
observations: fanotify: More powerful filesystem notification. Recursive (whole-mount or whole-FS scope), can permission-block events (FAN_OPEN_PERM), reports PID. Used by AV, file-integrity monitors. Requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: linux.filesystem.io-uring
observations: io_uring: Async IO syscall family (5.1+). Two ring buffers shared kernel↔user: submission queue (SQ) for ops, completion queue (CQ) for results. Avoids syscall-per-op overhead. Operations: read, write, fsync, sendmsg, recvmsg, accept, connect, openat, close, etc. The future of async on Linux.

name: linux.filesystem.direct-io
observations: O_DIRECT (direct IO): Bypass page cache — IOs go straight from user buffer to disk. Buffers must be aligned (typically 512B); size must be multiple of FS block size. Used by databases that manage their own cache (Oracle, PostgreSQL with effective_io_concurrency, MySQL InnoDB).

name: linux.filesystem.sparse-file
observations: Sparse file: File with 'holes' — regions never written, reported as zeros, take no disk space. Created by seek-past-end + write, or fallocate(2) FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE. cp --sparse, tar --sparse handle correctly. df shows actual usage; ls shows logical size.

name: linux.filesystem.reflink
observations: Reflink (cp --reflink): Copy-on-write file copy (xfs, btrfs, ocfs2, bcachefs). Source + dest share blocks until one is modified. Constant-time copy regardless of size. cp --reflink=always.

name: linux.filesystem.subvolume
observations: Subvolume (btrfs): Independent mountable filesystem-tree within a btrfs filesystem. Has own seed/inode space. Snapshotted independently. Used for installer rollback (snapper), per-container rootfs (podman btrfs driver).

name: linux.filesystem.journaling
observations: Journaling: Write-ahead log of metadata (and optionally data) changes. On crash, replay journal to bring FS to consistent state. ext3/ext4: data=writeback (no data, fastest, weakest), data=ordered (data before metadata, default), data=journal (full data journal, slowest). XFS: metadata-only journal.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-quota
observations: Filesystem quotas: Per-user/per-group/per-project block + inode limits. Soft limit (warning + grace period) + hard limit. quotaon enables; edquota edits; quotacheck rebuilds. XFS has built-in (no quotacheck needed), ext4 needs quota mount option.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-state-clean
observations: Filesystem state: clean: Successfully unmounted; no replay needed on next mount. Tracked in superblock (ext4 s_state has EXT4_VALID_FS).

name: linux.filesystem.fs-state-dirty
observations: Filesystem state: dirty: Mounted (or wasn't unmounted cleanly). On next mount, journal replay runs (ext4) or fsck must run (non-journaled fs).

name: linux.filesystem.fs-state-error
observations: Filesystem state: error: Kernel detected corruption (bad block read, inconsistent metadata) and marked FS errored. errors=remount-ro (default for ext4) remounts RO; errors=panic crashes; errors=continue logs and continues. Read superblock with tune2fs -l.

name: linux.filesystem.mount-state-mounted
observations: Mount state: mounted: Active mount. Visible in /proc/mounts and findmnt.

name: linux.filesystem.mount-state-busy
observations: Mount state: busy (EBUSY): umount returns EBUSY when files open / processes have CWD inside / active sub-mount. lsof / fuser identifies blockers. umount -l (lazy) detaches anyway.

name: linux.filesystem.disk-state-readonly-remount
observations: Filesystem auto-remounted RO: errors=remount-ro triggered. Symptoms: writes fail with EROFS. Common after disk errors, RAID degradation. Diagnose: `mount | grep ro,`; `dmesg | grep -i 'EXT4-fs error'`. Fix: unmount, fsck, remount.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-pid-fd
observations: /proc/<pid>/fd/: Symlinks per open FD pointing to file/socket/pipe/etc. ls -l reveals what's open. Crucial for debugging FD leaks, finding deleted-but-held files.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-pid-maps
observations: /proc/<pid>/maps: VMAs of process: address-range, perms (rwxp), offset, dev:inode, path. Shows mmap'd files, shared libraries, heap, stack, [vdso], [vsyscall].

name: linux.filesystem.proc-pid-mountinfo
observations: /proc/<pid>/mountinfo: Per-process-mountns mount table with full detail. Format: mount-id parent-id major:minor root mountpoint mount-options optional-fields - fs-type source super-options. Source of findmnt's data.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-pid-mountstats
observations: /proc/<pid>/mountstats: Per-mount stats (esp. for NFS): bytes-read/written, RPC counts, latency histograms.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-diskstats
observations: /proc/diskstats: Per-block-device IO counters: reads/writes (counts, merges, sectors, ms), in-flight, ms-doing-io. The data behind iostat.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-mounts
observations: /proc/mounts: Symlink to /proc/self/mounts. Active mounts in current mountns. Source: kernel's mount table.

name: linux.filesystem.proc-filesystems
observations: /proc/filesystems: Filesystem types the kernel can mount. 'nodev' prefix = no block device required (tmpfs, proc, sysfs).

name: linux.filesystem.dev-block
observations: /dev/<disk> block device nodes: Per-disk device node. /dev/sda for SATA/SCSI; /dev/nvme0n1 for NVMe; /dev/vda for virtio. Created by devtmpfs at boot, persistent symlinks added by udev (/dev/disk/by-uuid/, by-label/, by-id/, by-path/).

name: linux.filesystem.sys-block
observations: /sys/block/<disk>/: sysfs interface to block device — queue/* tunables (scheduler, nr_requests, read_ahead_kb), device/model, size, removable. Writable for runtime tuning.

name: linux.filesystem.sys-class-net
observations: /sys/class/net/<iface>/: sysfs per-interface (cross-ref linux/networking — mostly there). Mode/MTU/MAC/operstate/statistics writable + readable.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-feature-discard
observations: discard / TRIM: Tell SSD which blocks are no longer in use (FITRIM ioctl, mount option discard, fstrim(8)). SSD wear-leveling benefits. Modern: weekly fstrim.timer (instead of mount discard which is per-delete = lots of small TRIMs).

name: linux.filesystem.fs-feature-encryption
observations: fscrypt (filesystem-level encryption): Per-directory transparent encryption (ext4/f2fs/ubifs). Different from dm-crypt: one FS, multiple encryption policies; integrates with kernel keyring. Used by Android/ChromeOS.

name: linux.filesystem.bind-mount-recursive
observations: Recursive bind mount (rbind): mount --rbind src dst — bind src AND all its sub-mounts at dst. Container runtimes use this for host-fs passthrough. Without -r, only src itself is bound (sub-mounts invisible at dst).

name: linux.filesystem.mount-id-peer-group
observations: Mount peer group: Mounts in same propagation peer group share events (when one mounts/unmounts, others see it). Created via MS_SHARED. Distinct from MS_PRIVATE/SLAVE/UNBINDABLE. (Cross-ref linux/primitives mount-namespace-propagation.)

name: linux.filesystem.mount-id
observations: Mount ID: Per-mount unique integer (rotates after umount). Visible in /proc/self/mountinfo first column. Useful for distinguishing two mounts of same FS at different points.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-feature-extended-attribs
observations: Extended file attributes (chattr): Per-file attribute bits. ext4: i (immutable — can't modify/delete even by root), a (append-only), A (no atime updates), S (sync), j (journal data), c (compress). chattr +i / lsattr.

name: linux.filesystem.umask
observations: umask: Per-process bitmask removed from new file/dir mode. Default 022 → files 644, dirs 755. Set per-shell (umask command), per-systemd-service (UMask= directive), per-PAM (pam_umask).

name: linux.filesystem.access-time-modes
observations: Access time modes (atime/relatime/noatime): strictatime: every read updates atime (slow). relatime (default): atime updated only if older than mtime/ctime or > 24h. noatime: never. nodiratime: only files. Mount options.

name: linux.filesystem.fanotify-permission
observations: fanotify permission events: FAN_OPEN_PERM/FAN_ACCESS_PERM — kernel suspends syscall, asks userspace listener (FAN_ALLOW or FAN_DENY). Used by AV scanning. Process blocked until response.

name: linux.filesystem.cryptsetup-luks
observations: LUKS header: On-disk header for cryptsetup. Holds master-key encrypted by per-keyslot passphrases (8 slots LUKS1; 32 slots LUKS2). luksDump shows slots + cipher + KDF.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-bcachefs
observations: bcachefs: Newer COW filesystem (mainlined 6.7). Snapshots, native multi-device, encryption, compression. Still maturing — production-ready debate ongoing. Not in our focus corpus.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-zfs
observations: ZFS: Out-of-tree filesystem (CDDL license incompatible with GPL). OpenZFS Linux port (ZoL) widely used for storage servers. Pool-based: zpool/zfs commands. Not a kernel-tree FS but ubiquitous in storage/Proxmox setups.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-squashfs
observations: squashfs: Read-only compressed filesystem. Used for live-distro ISOs, container image layers (podman/docker overlay2 stores layer tars; some other tools use squashfs directly). mksquashfs creates.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-nfs
observations: NFS (Network File System): Network filesystem. v3 (stateless, UDP/TCP), v4 (stateful, TCP, idmap, ACLs, delegations). mount -t nfs server:/path /mount. Common D-state-stuck culprit when server unreachable. nfsstat for stats.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-cifs
observations: CIFS / SMB: Windows network FS. mount -t cifs //server/share /mount -o username=. cifs.ko or ksmbd.ko (in-kernel server).

name: linux.filesystem.fs-ext2-ext3
observations: ext2 / ext3: Predecessors of ext4. ext2 = no journal; ext3 = added journal. Modern systems mount as ext4 (ext4 driver handles all three formats). Still seen on /boot or USB drives.

name: linux.filesystem.fs-image-disk
observations: Disk image (raw, qcow2, vmdk): File representing a block device. raw = sparse file = direct dd. qcow2 = QEMU's COW format with snapshots, compression, encryption. vmdk = VMware. Mountable via losetup or qemu-nbd.

name: linux.filesystem.dm-driver
observations: device-mapper (dm): Kernel block-layer mechanism for stacking transformations: dm-linear (LVM linear), dm-stripe (LVM stripe), dm-mirror, dm-crypt (LUKS), dm-thin (thin pool), dm-cache, dm-snapshot, dm-multipath. /dev/mapper/<name>. dmsetup CLI.

name: k8s.core.pod
observations: Pod: Smallest deployable unit. One or more containers sharing network namespace (same IP+ports), IPC namespace, optionally PID namespace and volumes. Scheduled to a single node. Identified by namespace/name. Has phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown) + conditions (PodScheduled, Initialized, ContainersReady, Ready). Lifecycle: Pending → Running → terminal.

name: k8s.core.pod-spec
observations: PodSpec: The .spec field of a Pod. Holds containers[], initContainers[], volumes[], nodeName, restartPolicy, terminationGracePeriodSeconds, hostNetwork, dnsPolicy, schedulerName, tolerations, affinity, priorityClassName.

name: k8s.core.container
observations: Container (in Pod): Single container within a pod's containers[] or initContainers[] list. Has image, command, args, env, envFrom, resources, volumeMounts, ports, livenessProbe, readinessProbe, startupProbe, lifecycle, securityContext.

name: k8s.core.init-container
observations: Init container: Container in pod's initContainers[] list. Run sequentially before app containers start. Each must complete successfully (exit 0). On failure: pod fails or restarts (per restartPolicy). Used for setup tasks, schema migrations, secret pre-population.

name: k8s.core.sidecar-container
observations: Sidecar container: Native sidecar (1.28+) — initContainer with restartPolicy=Always. Starts before app, stays alive throughout pod lifetime, terminates AFTER app. Replaces the older 'just an extra container in spec.containers' pattern. Used for log shippers, service meshes (Envoy), volume sync.

name: k8s.core.ephemeral-container
observations: Ephemeral container: Special container type for debugging running pods. Added to a running pod via `kubectl debug`; not part of pod spec. Cannot specify ports, probes, resources. Cannot be removed once added. Useful when pod has no shell or for inspecting distroless containers.

name: k8s.core.pod-phase-pending
observations: Pod phase: Pending: Accepted by cluster but not all containers running. Common reasons: image pulling, init containers running, scheduling failure (insufficient resources, no matching node). Diagnose via `kubectl describe pod` Events.

name: k8s.core.pod-phase-running
observations: Pod phase: Running: Bound to node, all containers created. At least one is running, starting, or restarting.

name: k8s.core.pod-phase-succeeded
observations: Pod phase: Succeeded: All containers terminated successfully (exit 0) and won't restart. Terminal phase. Common for Jobs.

name: k8s.core.pod-phase-failed
observations: Pod phase: Failed: All containers terminated; at least one failed (non-zero exit or system kill). Terminal.

name: k8s.core.pod-phase-unknown
observations: Pod phase: Unknown: Pod state could not be obtained — typically node communication failure (NotReady, network partition).

name: k8s.core.pod-condition-podscheduled
observations: PodCondition: PodScheduled: True once scheduler has assigned node. False with reason 'Unschedulable' = no fit found.

name: k8s.core.pod-condition-initialized
observations: PodCondition: Initialized: True once all init containers completed successfully.

name: k8s.core.pod-condition-ready
observations: PodCondition: Ready: True when ALL containers' readiness probes pass. Service endpoints filter by Ready=True.

name: k8s.core.pod-condition-containersready
observations: PodCondition: ContainersReady: True when all containers are ready (similar to Ready but doesn't include readiness gates).

name: k8s.core.container-state-waiting
observations: ContainerState: Waiting: Not running. Has 'reason' field: ContainerCreating, ImagePullBackOff, ErrImagePull, CrashLoopBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError. The most-debug-relevant container state.

name: k8s.core.container-state-running
observations: ContainerState: Running: Running. startedAt populated.

name: k8s.core.container-state-terminated
observations: ContainerState: Terminated: Exited. exitCode, signal, reason (Completed/Error/OOMKilled/ContainerCannotRun), startedAt, finishedAt populated. Exit 137=OOMKilled+SIGKILL, 143=SIGTERM, 139=SIGSEGV.

name: k8s.core.crash-loop-backoff
observations: CrashLoopBackOff: Container repeatedly crashing. Kubelet applies exponential backoff between restart attempts (10s → 20s → 40s → cap 5min). Visible as Waiting reason. Diagnose: `kubectl logs --previous` for crashed-container logs.

name: k8s.core.image-pull-back-off
observations: ImagePullBackOff: Image pull failed; kubelet backing off. Causes: bad image name/tag, registry auth missing (ImagePullSecrets), private registry unreachable, rate limits. Diagnose via `kubectl describe pod` Events.

name: k8s.core.deployment
observations: Deployment: Higher-level controller for stateless apps. Manages a ReplicaSet which manages Pods. Supports rolling updates, rollback, scaling. Strategy: RollingUpdate (default) or Recreate. Stored revisions for rollback.

name: k8s.core.replicaset
observations: ReplicaSet: Maintains a stable set of pod replicas. Owned by a Deployment usually (don't create directly). Selector matches pods; controller creates/deletes to match replicas count.

name: k8s.core.statefulset
observations: StatefulSet: Manages stateful pods with stable network identity (pod-N.service-name) + ordered creation/deletion + per-pod PVC. Used for databases, message queues, anything needing identity. Pods have stable PVC binding via volumeClaimTemplates.

name: k8s.core.daemonset
observations: DaemonSet: One pod per node (matching nodeSelector/tolerations). Used for node-level agents: log shippers (fluent-bit), monitoring (node_exporter), CNI components, kube-proxy.

name: k8s.core.job
observations: Job: Run pod(s) to completion. completions= total successful runs needed; parallelism= concurrent pods. backoffLimit= retry count before Job marked Failed. Pod restartPolicy must be OnFailure or Never.

name: k8s.core.cronjob
observations: CronJob: Job on a cron schedule. Spec: schedule (cron expr), startingDeadlineSeconds, concurrencyPolicy (Allow/Forbid/Replace), successfulJobsHistoryLimit, failedJobsHistoryLimit. Creates Jobs at scheduled times.

name: k8s.core.namespace
observations: Namespace: Cluster-internal scope for naming + isolation. Default namespaces: default, kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease. RBAC, ResourceQuota, LimitRange, NetworkPolicy scoped per-namespace.

name: k8s.core.configmap
observations: ConfigMap: Non-secret key-value pairs. Mountable as env vars (envFrom.configMapRef, env.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef) or files (volume.configMap). Updates: env vars don't refresh (pod restart needed); mounted files DO refresh (kubelet sync, ~minute).

name: k8s.core.secret
observations: Secret: Like ConfigMap but base64-encoded by default + RBAC-restricted. Types: Opaque (default), kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (image pull), kubernetes.io/tls, kubernetes.io/service-account-token. Stored in etcd encrypted-at-rest if EncryptionConfiguration set.

name: k8s.core.service
observations: Service: Stable IP+port for accessing pods (selected by labels). Types: ClusterIP (cluster-internal, default), NodePort (per-node port), LoadBalancer (cloud LB), ExternalName (CNAME). Implements via kube-proxy iptables/IPVS.

name: k8s.core.serviceaccount
observations: ServiceAccount: Identity for pods. Per-namespace. Auto-mounted as JWT token (TokenRequest API) at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. Used by RBAC for in-cluster API access.

name: k8s.core.role
observations: Role / ClusterRole: RBAC permission set. Role = namespace-scoped; ClusterRole = cluster-scoped. Rules: apiGroups, resources, verbs, resourceNames. Built-in: cluster-admin, admin, edit, view.

name: k8s.core.rolebinding
observations: RoleBinding / ClusterRoleBinding: Bind Role/ClusterRole to subjects (User, Group, ServiceAccount). Without binding, role has no effect. RoleBinding can reference ClusterRole (gives cluster-role permissions in a single namespace).

name: k8s.core.label
observations: Label: Key=value tag on objects. Used by selectors (Service → Pod, ReplicaSet → Pod). Recommended labels: app.kubernetes.io/name, /instance, /version, /component, /part-of, /managed-by.

name: k8s.core.annotation
observations: Annotation: Key=value metadata. Not used by selectors. For tools to attach extra info: kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision, prometheus.io/scrape.

name: k8s.core.label-selector
observations: Label selector: Query language for matching labels. Equality (key=value, key!=value) and Set-based (key in (v1,v2), key notin (v1)). Used by Service spec.selector, NetworkPolicy podSelector, Deployment spec.selector.matchLabels/matchExpressions.

name: k8s.core.field-selector
observations: Field selector: Query by intrinsic field (vs label). Examples: status.phase=Running, spec.nodeName=worker-1, metadata.namespace!=default. Limited per-resource — kubectl get pods --field-selector.

name: k8s.core.api-group
observations: API group: REST API grouping. Core (legacy) /api/v1; named groups /apis/<group>/<version> (e.g. apps/v1, batch/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1, rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1).

name: k8s.core.api-version
observations: apiVersion field: Manifest field naming the API: 'v1' (core), '<group>/<version>'. Migrating versions: alpha (v1alpha1, opt-in, can change), beta (v1beta1, on by default), stable (v1).

name: k8s.core.crd
observations: CRD (CustomResourceDefinition): Extends Kubernetes API with new resource types. After CRD applied, kubectl get/describe/apply/delete work on the new type. Combined with controllers (Operators) to implement custom logic.

name: k8s.core.controller
observations: Controller: Reconciliation loop watching resources via API and acting to drive observed state → desired state. Built-in: Deployment, StatefulSet, Job. Custom: Operators. The control-loop pattern is the heart of Kubernetes.

name: k8s.core.operator-pattern
observations: Operator pattern: CRD + Controller combination implementing app-specific knowledge (e.g. PostgreSQL operator handles failover, backup, version upgrade). The way to encode 'how to operate this app' as code.

name: k8s.core.api-server
observations: kube-apiserver: Front-door for the cluster. REST API; admission control; auth; etcd persistence. Multiple replicas behind LB. Stateless (state in etcd).

name: k8s.core.etcd
observations: etcd: Distributed key-value store. The source of truth for cluster state. All API objects stored here. Quorum-based (3 or 5 members). Performance-sensitive (latency = control-plane latency).

name: k8s.core.scheduler
observations: kube-scheduler: Watches unscheduled pods + nodes; computes binding via filtering + scoring. Filters: PodFitsResources, MatchNodeSelector, taints/tolerations, NoVolumeZoneConflict. Scoring: BalancedAllocation, NodeResourcesLeastAllocated.

name: k8s.core.controller-manager
observations: kube-controller-manager: Runs built-in controllers: Deployment, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, Job, CronJob, Endpoints, Namespace, ServiceAccount, Node, GarbageCollector. Single binary running many controller loops.

name: k8s.core.cloud-controller-manager
observations: cloud-controller-manager: Cloud-provider-specific controller logic: Node (init from cloud metadata), Route, Service (LoadBalancer provisioning), Volume. Replaces in-tree cloud code.

name: k8s.core.kubelet
observations: kubelet: Per-node agent. Watches Pods scheduled to its node. Uses CRI to start/stop containers. Reports status back. Runs probes. Manages volume mounts. Cgroup setup.

name: k8s.core.kube-proxy
observations: kube-proxy: Per-node networking agent. Implements Service abstraction via iptables/IPVS/eBPF rules. Routes ServiceIP:port to backend pod IPs.

name: k8s.core.cri
observations: CRI (Container Runtime Interface): gRPC API between kubelet and container runtime (containerd, CRI-O). Two services: RuntimeService (containers + sandboxes), ImageService. Unix socket /run/containerd/containerd.sock typical.

name: k8s.core.containerd
observations: containerd (in K8s): Default container runtime since Docker dropped from kubelet. CRI plugin in containerd handles RuntimeService + ImageService. crictl is the debugging client.

name: k8s.core.cri-o
observations: CRI-O: Alternative container runtime, OCI-conformant, K8s-focused. Smaller scope than containerd. Default on RHEL/Fedora/OpenShift.

name: k8s.core.kube-scheduler-priority
observations: PriorityClass: Per-pod priority value. Higher priority pods can preempt lower (evict to fit). Built-in: system-cluster-critical, system-node-critical (for control-plane). Custom: define PriorityClass with value (1-10^9).

name: k8s.core.preemption
observations: Pod preemption: Scheduler evicts lower-priority pods to fit higher-priority ones. Triggered when pod can't schedule + preemption would help. Eviction respects PodDisruptionBudget.

name: k8s.core.eviction
observations: Eviction: Pod removal scenarios: API-initiated eviction (kubectl drain, voluntary), node-pressure eviction (kubelet kills under resource pressure), preemption (scheduler), taint-based (taint with NoExecute effect).

name: k8s.core.node-pressure-eviction
observations: Node-pressure eviction: Kubelet evicts pods to reclaim resources when thresholds breached. Signals: memory.available, nodefs.available, nodefs.inodesFree, imagefs.available, pid.available. Soft (grace period) vs hard (immediate).

name: k8s.core.taint
observations: Taint: Per-node attribute repelling pods unless they tolerate it. Format: key=value:effect. Effects: NoSchedule (filter), PreferNoSchedule (soft), NoExecute (also evict running pods that don't tolerate).

name: k8s.core.toleration
observations: Toleration: Per-pod field allowing scheduling onto tainted nodes. Match on key, value, effect, operator (Equal/Exists). tolerationSeconds for NoExecute timed eviction.

name: k8s.core.node-selector
observations: nodeSelector: Per-pod simple node-label match. spec.nodeSelector: {disk: ssd}. Hard requirement. Use affinity for richer expressions.

name: k8s.core.node-affinity
observations: nodeAffinity: Richer node selection. requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (hard), preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (soft, weighted). matchExpressions: key + operator (In/NotIn/Exists/DoesNotExist/Gt/Lt) + values.

name: k8s.core.pod-affinity
observations: podAffinity / podAntiAffinity: Schedule based on other pods' labels. podAffinity: 'place me near pods matching X'. podAntiAffinity: 'place me away from pods matching X'. topologyKey: zone/region/host scope.

name: k8s.core.qos-guaranteed
observations: QoS class: Guaranteed: Pod's containers ALL have CPU+memory requests=limits. Last evicted under node-pressure. Highest priority for scheduling reservations.

name: k8s.core.qos-burstable
observations: QoS class: Burstable: At least one container has requests but not all are requests=limits. Default for most pods. Evicted before Guaranteed.

name: k8s.core.qos-besteffort
observations: QoS class: BestEffort: No requests or limits set. Evicted FIRST under node-pressure. Avoid for production.

name: k8s.core.requests
observations: resources.requests: Per-container resource reservation. Scheduler uses for fitting. Maps to cgroup soft constraints (cpu.shares ratio in cgroupv1; cpu.weight in v2).

name: k8s.core.limits
observations: resources.limits: Per-container hard cap. CPU = throttled at limit (CFS quota). Memory = OOM-killed if exceeded.

name: k8s.core.cpu-throttling
observations: CPU throttling: When container hits cpu limit, kernel throttles. Visible in cpu.stat 'nr_throttled' and 'throttled_usec'. Cause of mysterious latency without OOM. Fix: raise limit, OR remove limit (let burstable workload use idle CPU).

name: k8s.core.oom-kill
observations: OOMKilled: Container exceeded memory limit, kernel SIGKILL'd. Exit 137. Visible in container state's reason field. Fix: raise memory limit OR find leak.

name: k8s.core.resource-quota
observations: ResourceQuota: Per-namespace caps on aggregate resource usage. Hard limits: cpu.requests, memory.limits, pods, secrets, services.loadbalancers, persistentvolumeclaims, count of resources by type.

name: k8s.core.limit-range
observations: LimitRange: Per-namespace default + min/max for pod/container/PVC resources. Applied at admission. Use to enforce 'every container has limits' policy.

name: k8s.core.priority-class
observations: PriorityClass (object): Object defining numeric priority + globalDefault flag. Pods reference via spec.priorityClassName. Higher = preempts lower.

name: k8s.core.liveness-probe
observations: livenessProbe: Health check; failure → kubelet restarts container. Methods: httpGet (HTTP 200-399), tcpSocket (TCP connect succeeds), exec (cmd exits 0), grpc (gRPC health-check). initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, failureThreshold.

name: k8s.core.readiness-probe
observations: readinessProbe: Failure → pod removed from Service endpoints (no traffic) but NOT restarted. Recovers on success. Use for 'temporarily can't serve' (e.g. warming cache, dependent service down).

name: k8s.core.startup-probe
observations: startupProbe: Runs before liveness/readiness. Allows slow starters longer initial grace. Once succeeds once, hands off to liveness/readiness.

name: k8s.core.deployment-rollout
observations: Deployment rollout: Rolling update strategy. Spec: maxSurge (extra pods during update, default 25%), maxUnavailable (max down at once, default 25%). New ReplicaSet created; scaled up; old scaled down. revisionHistoryLimit (default 10) keeps old RS for rollback.

name: k8s.core.deployment-rollback
observations: Deployment rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/X`. Switches back to previous ReplicaSet. Annotations record revision history.

name: k8s.core.recreate-strategy
observations: Recreate strategy: Alternative to RollingUpdate — kill all old pods first, THEN start new. Used when app can't run multiple versions simultaneously (e.g. DB schema migrations). Causes downtime.

name: k8s.core.statefulset-ordinal
observations: StatefulSet ordinal: Pods named <statefulset>-0, -1, -2 in order. Created/scaled-up in order; deleted in reverse. Stable identity = stable DNS, stable PVC.

name: k8s.core.headless-service
observations: Headless service: Service with clusterIP: None. DNS returns each pod's IP directly (vs single VIP). Required for StatefulSet stable DNS (pod-N.service-name.ns).

name: k8s.core.persistent-volume
observations: PersistentVolume (PV): Cluster-wide storage resource. Provisioned by admin (static) or by StorageClass (dynamic). Independent of pod lifetime.

name: k8s.core.persistent-volume-claim
observations: PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC): Pod's request for storage (size, accessMode, storageClass). Bound to a PV. Pod mounts via spec.volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName.

name: k8s.core.storage-class
observations: StorageClass: Provisioner + parameters for dynamic PV creation. e.g. AWS EBS gp3, Azure Disk, GCE PD, NFS, Ceph. reclaimPolicy: Delete (PV gone with PVC) or Retain.

name: k8s.core.access-mode
observations: PV accessMode: ReadWriteOnce (RWO — single node), ReadOnlyMany (ROX), ReadWriteMany (RWX), ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP — single pod). Many cloud disks are RWO.

name: k8s.core.volume
observations: Volume (in pod): Storage exposed to container at a path. Types: emptyDir (per-pod scratch), hostPath (host-fs), configMap, secret, persistentVolumeClaim, downwardAPI, projected.

name: k8s.core.empty-dir
observations: emptyDir volume: Per-pod scratch storage. Created at pod-start, deleted at pod-delete. Backed by node disk OR memory (medium: Memory). Used for temp files, cache, sidecar communication.

name: k8s.core.host-path
observations: hostPath volume: Mount node-fs path into pod. Security risk — escapes per-pod isolation. Restricted by PodSecurityStandards. Use only for system-level pods (CNI, log shippers).

name: k8s.core.projected-volume
observations: projected volume: Combine multiple sources (configMap, secret, serviceAccountToken, downwardAPI) into a single volume mount. The mechanism behind /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/.

name: k8s.core.downward-api
observations: Downward API: Expose pod metadata to container via env vars or volume files. Fields: spec.nodeName, status.podIP, metadata.name/namespace/labels/annotations, resource limits/requests.

name: k8s.core.controller-event-loop
observations: Controller event loop: Watch API for resource changes (informer/cache); on event, queue work; reconcile (drive observed → desired). Built on shared informers + workqueues. The pattern operators implement.

name: k8s.core.api-watch
observations: API watch (server-side): Long-lived HTTP connection or HTTP/2 stream. Server pushes events as objects change. resourceVersion tracks position. The mechanism behind kubectl get -w and informers.

name: k8s.core.terminationGracePeriodSeconds
observations: terminationGracePeriodSeconds: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL. Default 30. Pod has this long to gracefully shut down. preStop lifecycle hook also runs in this window.

name: k8s.core.preStop-hook
observations: preStop lifecycle hook: Run command/HTTP-GET before SIGTERM. Used to drain connections, deregister from LB, save state. Counts toward grace period.

name: k8s.core.security-context
observations: securityContext: Per-pod or per-container security settings. runAsUser, runAsGroup, fsGroup, runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities (add/drop), seccompProfile, seLinuxOptions.

name: k8s.core.pod-security-standards
observations: Pod Security Standards (PSS): Three policy levels: privileged (none), baseline (prevent known escapes), restricted (heavily restricted, hardened). Applied via Pod Security Admission with labels (pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted).

name: k8s.core.kubeconfig
observations: kubeconfig: Client config file: clusters[], users[], contexts[]. Default ~/.kube/config. KUBECONFIG env var (colon-separated) for multiple. Current context = active cluster+namespace+user combo.

name: k8s.core.context
observations: kubectl context: Named combo of cluster + user + namespace. Switch via `kubectl config use-context X`. List with `kubectl config get-contexts`.

name: k8s.core.declarative-vs-imperative
observations: Declarative vs imperative: Imperative: kubectl create/delete/run/expose (do this once). Declarative: kubectl apply -f (manifest is desired state). Declarative is the recommended pattern; imperative for quick experiments.

name: k8s.core.manifest
observations: Manifest (YAML/JSON): Resource definition in YAML or JSON. apiVersion + kind + metadata + spec. Applied via kubectl apply. Version-controlled in Git → GitOps.

name: k8s.core.kustomize
observations: Kustomize: Built into kubectl (kubectl apply -k DIR). Layered resource customization: base + overlays (per env). Patches, replacements, label/annotation propagation, secret/configMap generation.

name: k8s.core.helm
observations: Helm (cross-ref): Package manager (charts). Templating + values + release management. Outside this corpus's primary scope but ubiquitous. helm.sh.

name: k8s.core.gitops
observations: GitOps: Pattern: Git is source of truth; controller (ArgoCD, FluxCD) reconciles cluster to match repo. Pull-based deployment, audit trail, rollback via git revert.

name: k8s.core.api-deprecation
observations: API deprecation policy: alpha → beta → stable lifecycle. Deprecated APIs removed after 12mo or 3 releases (whichever later). Migration: `kubectl convert` (legacy), or rewrite manifests.

name: k8s.core.admission-controller
observations: Admission controller: Plugins running on API server BEFORE persisting object. Mutating (modify) and Validating (allow/reject). Built-in: NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger, PodSecurity, ResourceQuota. Custom via webhooks.

name: k8s.core.finalizer
observations: Finalizer: Pre-deletion hook. Object stays in 'Terminating' until finalizers cleared by their owners. Use for cleanup before object disappears (release cloud resource, delete dependent objects).

name: k8s.core.owner-reference
observations: Owner reference: metadata.ownerReferences links child to parent. Garbage Collector deletes child when parent gone (per propagationPolicy: Foreground/Background/Orphan).

name: k8s.core.cordon
observations: kubectl cordon / drain: cordon: mark node Unschedulable (no new pods). drain: cordon + evict existing pods (respect PDB). uncordon: remove. Used for node maintenance.

name: k8s.core.pdb
observations: PodDisruptionBudget (PDB): Bounds voluntary disruption: minAvailable / maxUnavailable. Drain respects PDB; can't violate.

name: k8s.networking.service
observations: Service (network abstraction): Stable virtual IP+port for accessing pods. Selects pods by labels. Implementations: kube-proxy iptables/IPVS/eBPF rules on each node. Types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName.

name: k8s.networking.cluster-ip
observations: ClusterIP service: Default. Allocated from cluster service-cidr. Reachable only from inside cluster. DNS: <name>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local.

name: k8s.networking.nodeport
observations: NodePort service: Exposes service on every node's IP at a static port (default 30000-32767). Routes to backend pods (kube-proxy iptables). Useful for bare-metal where no LB available.

name: k8s.networking.loadbalancer
observations: LoadBalancer service: Provisions cloud LB (ELB, Azure LB, GCP LB) via cloud-controller-manager. LB targets NodePort which targets pods. External IP visible in status.loadBalancer.ingress[].

name: k8s.networking.externalname
observations: ExternalName service: DNS CNAME pointing to external host. No proxying. Used to give external service a cluster-internal DNS name.

name: k8s.networking.endpoints
observations: Endpoints / EndpointSlice: Lists pod IPs+ports backing a Service. Endpoints (legacy, single object) → EndpointSlice (modern, partitioned for scale). Filtered by pod readiness.

name: k8s.networking.kube-proxy-iptables
observations: kube-proxy iptables mode: Default. iptables NAT rules per Service+endpoint. O(N) lookup per packet. Fine up to ~5k services.

name: k8s.networking.kube-proxy-ipvs
observations: kube-proxy IPVS mode: Hash-table based load balancing in kernel. O(1) lookup. Better at scale (>10k services). LB algorithms: rr, lc, dh, sh, sed, nq.

name: k8s.networking.kube-proxy-nftables
observations: kube-proxy nftables mode: Modern (1.29+) replacement for iptables mode. Better performance, cleaner rule structure. Same semantics.

name: k8s.networking.kube-proxy-ebpf-cilium
observations: eBPF (Cilium-style replacement): Cilium / kpng / Calico eBPF dataplane. Bypass kube-proxy entirely. Faster, supports sockets-level policy, observable via Hubble.

name: k8s.networking.ingress
observations: Ingress: L7 routing rules (HTTP/HTTPS) mapping hostnames + paths to services. Implemented by ingress-controller (nginx-ingress, Traefik, HAProxy, AWS ALB, Istio gateway).

name: k8s.networking.ingress-controller
observations: Ingress controller: Watches Ingress resources, configures the actual L7 proxy. nginx-ingress is most common (ingress-nginx project). Takes the controller's ingressClass annotation.

name: k8s.networking.gateway-api
observations: Gateway API: Successor to Ingress. More expressive: GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, TCPRoute, GRPCRoute, ReferenceGrant. Multi-team-ownership friendly. Stable since 1.31.

name: k8s.networking.network-policy
observations: NetworkPolicy: Per-namespace, label-selector-based ingress/egress allow rules. CNI plugin must implement (not all do). Default: allow all if no policy applies; deny all if any policy applies + selects pod.

name: k8s.networking.cni
observations: CNI (Container Network Interface): Plugin spec for pod networking. Kubelet calls CNI binary on pod create (ADD) and delete (DEL). Plugin sets up veth, IP, routes per cluster's pod CIDR. Major plugins: Calico, Cilium, Flannel, Weave, AWS VPC CNI, Azure CNI.

name: k8s.networking.cni-plugin
observations: CNI plugin (binary): Located at /opt/cni/bin/. Config at /etc/cni/net.d/*.conflist. Multiple plugins can chain (e.g. main + meta-plugins for bandwidth, port-mapping).

name: k8s.networking.pod-cidr
observations: Pod CIDR: IP range allocated to each node for pod IPs. Set by kube-controller-manager (--allocate-node-cidrs) or by CNI. Cluster-wide CIDR (--cluster-cidr) divided into per-node CIDRs.

name: k8s.networking.service-cidr
observations: Service CIDR: IP range for ClusterIPs. Configured at kube-apiserver (--service-cluster-ip-range). Distinct from pod CIDR.

name: k8s.networking.coredns
observations: CoreDNS: Default cluster DNS. Runs as Deployment in kube-system. Handles <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local lookups. Configurable via Corefile in coredns ConfigMap.

name: k8s.networking.cluster-dns
observations: Cluster DNS: Pods get /etc/resolv.conf with cluster DNS as nameserver, search list (<ns>.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local), ndots:5 default.

name: k8s.networking.dns-policy-clusterfirst
observations: DNS policy: ClusterFirst: Default. Cluster DNS first, fallback to upstream for non-cluster names.

name: k8s.networking.dns-policy-default
observations: DNS policy: Default: Inherit kubelet host's resolv.conf. NOT cluster DNS. Useful when pod doesn't need cluster DNS.

name: k8s.networking.dns-policy-none
observations: DNS policy: None: Use spec.dnsConfig field exclusively.

name: k8s.networking.dns-search-suffix
observations: DNS search suffix expansion: With ndots:5 and search [ns.svc.cluster.local, svc.cluster.local, cluster.local]: any name with <5 dots tried with each suffix first. 'github.com' (1 dot) = 4 cluster lookups before external. The Kubernetes DNS-overhead surprise.

name: k8s.networking.headless-service
observations: Headless Service (clusterIP=None): DNS returns each backing pod's IP directly (vs single VIP). Required for StatefulSet stable per-pod DNS. <pod-name>.<svc-name>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local.

name: k8s.networking.session-affinity
observations: sessionAffinity: ClientIP = sticky session by source IP. None = round-robin (default). 5xx-tier services don't usually want.

name: k8s.networking.external-traffic-policy-local
observations: externalTrafficPolicy: Local: Preserve client source IP. NodePort/LB only routes to pods on SAME node (no cross-node hop, no SNAT). Drops if no local pod. Use with healthCheckNodePort to drain.

name: k8s.networking.external-traffic-policy-cluster
observations: externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster: Default. SNATs source IP to node IP, may cross node hop. Even traffic distribution but loses client IP.

name: k8s.networking.internal-traffic-policy
observations: internalTrafficPolicy: Local: In-cluster traffic only routed to pods on SAME node. Useful for node-local caches/agents.

name: k8s.networking.dual-stack
observations: Dual-stack networking: IPv4+IPv6 simultaneously. Service.spec.ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack|PreferDualStack|RequireDualStack. ipFamilies: [IPv4, IPv6] order.

name: k8s.networking.ingress-class
observations: IngressClass: Selects which controller handles an Ingress (matched via Ingress.spec.ingressClassName). Allows multiple ingress controllers in same cluster.

name: k8s.networking.tls
observations: TLS termination: Ingress.spec.tls[] references a Secret of type kubernetes.io/tls (tls.crt + tls.key). Controller terminates TLS at the proxy.

name: k8s.networking.ip-allocation
observations: Pod IP allocation: Pod IP assigned at scheduling time, persists for pod lifetime. On restart in-place (not eviction), IP keeps. New pod = new IP.

name: k8s.networking.network-policy-default-deny
observations: Default-deny pattern: NetworkPolicy with empty podSelector + no ingress/egress rules = deny all to/from all pods in namespace. The starting point of zero-trust policies.

name: k8s.networking.network-policy-pod-selector
observations: NetworkPolicy podSelector: Selects pods to which the policy applies. Empty = all pods in namespace. Combined with namespace selector for cross-namespace rules.

name: k8s.networking.network-policy-ingress
observations: NetworkPolicy ingress rule: from: list of {podSelector, namespaceSelector, ipBlock}. ports: list of allowed ports.

name: k8s.networking.network-policy-egress
observations: NetworkPolicy egress rule: to: list of selectors. Limits where pods can connect outbound.

name: k8s.networking.podip-vs-clusterip
observations: PodIP vs ClusterIP: PodIP = ephemeral, per-pod (changes if pod recreated). ClusterIP = stable, per-Service. Use ClusterIP for client connections; never hardcode PodIP.

name: k8s.networking.svc-dns-name
observations: Service DNS name format: <svc>.<ns>.svc.<cluster-domain> (default cluster-domain = cluster.local). Search suffixes mean within same ns, just '<svc>' resolves.

name: k8s.networking.coredns-corefile
observations: CoreDNS Corefile: Configuration. Plugins: kubernetes (auto-discovery), forward (upstream resolver), cache, reload, errors, health, ready, prometheus, loop. Modify via kubectl edit cm/coredns -n kube-system.

name: k8s.networking.kube-proxy-mode
observations: kube-proxy --proxy-mode: iptables (default), ipvs, nftables (1.29+), kernelspace (Windows). Set via kube-proxy ConfigMap mode field.

name: k8s.networking.cluster-network-plugin
observations: Cluster network model: Each pod has unique cluster-routable IP (no NAT between pods). Each node has cluster-routable IP. Pods on same node communicate without NAT. Implemented by CNI.

name: k8s.networking.cilium
observations: Cilium: eBPF-based CNI + service mesh. Replaces kube-proxy with eBPF dataplane. Hubble for observability. NetworkPolicy with L7 rules (HTTP, gRPC, Kafka).

name: k8s.networking.calico
observations: Calico: BGP/IP-routing or VXLAN-overlay CNI. Strong NetworkPolicy support. Tigera enterprise tier.

name: k8s.networking.flannel
observations: Flannel: Simple overlay-network CNI. VXLAN backend most common. No NetworkPolicy enforcement (use Calico chained behind).

name: k8s.networking.weavenet
observations: Weave Net: Older overlay CNI. Mesh-routing without etcd. Project archived 2024.

name: k8s.networking.aws-vpc-cni
observations: AWS VPC CNI: Each pod gets a real ENI/secondary-IP from VPC. No overlay. AWS-native; pods reach AWS resources directly. Limit per node based on instance type ENIs.

name: k8s.networking.azure-cni
observations: Azure CNI: Similar to AWS VPC CNI for Azure VNet.

name: k8s.networking.gke-vpc-native
observations: GKE VPC-native: GKE pod IPs come from a secondary GCP VPC range. Pods routable from VPC.

name: k8s.networking.service-mesh
observations: Service mesh (Istio/Linkerd): L7 traffic management via sidecar proxies (Envoy/linkerd-proxy) injected into pods. mTLS, retry, circuit-break, traffic-shift, observability. Out-of-tree but ubiquitous.

name: k8s.networking.cluster-networking-doc
observations: Cluster Networking concepts doc: kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/networking — the canonical 'how does pod networking work' overview.

name: k8s.networking.endpointslice-mirroring
