observations: EndpointSlice mirroring: Endpoints API auto-mirrored to EndpointSlice. Backwards compat — old controllers still work but get sliced data.

name: k8s.networking.endpoint-slice-controller
observations: EndpointSlice controller: Watches Service+Pod, generates per-service EndpointSlice objects. Sliced for scale (instead of one massive Endpoints object).

name: k8s.networking.headless-statefulset-dns
observations: StatefulSet pod DNS: With headless Service named <sts>: pod-N.<sts>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local resolves to that pod's IP. Stable identity for clustering apps (Cassandra, Kafka).

name: k8s.networking.dns-pod-search
observations: Pod's resolv.conf search list: Generated per-pod: <pod-namespace>.svc.<cluster-domain> svc.<cluster-domain> <cluster-domain>. Plus host's search if dnsPolicy=Default. ndots:5 default expands lookups.

name: k8s.networking.gateway-resource
observations: Gateway resource (Gateway API): Defines listener (port, protocol, hostname, TLS). Bound by GatewayClass. Routes (HTTPRoute) attach to it.

name: k8s.networking.httproute
observations: HTTPRoute (Gateway API): L7 routing rules. matches, filters (header rewrite, redirect), backendRefs (services). Attaches to Gateway via parentRefs.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-describe-events
observations: kubectl describe events block: Per-resource events shown in `kubectl describe`. Most-useful section for triage. Format: Type Reason Age From Message. e.g. Warning FailedScheduling 30s default-scheduler 0/3 nodes available: insufficient memory.

name: k8s.debugging.event-resource
observations: Event resource: Cluster-wide log of significant changes. Defaults to events.k8s.io/v1 (newer) or v1 (legacy). TTL'd (default 1h). Visible via `kubectl get events`.

name: k8s.debugging.event-type-normal
observations: Event Type: Normal: Informational events: Created, Started, Pulled, Killing, Scheduled, SuccessfulCreate.

name: k8s.debugging.event-type-warning
observations: Event Type: Warning: Problem events: Failed, FailedScheduling, FailedMount, BackOff, Unhealthy, FailedKillPod. The triage focus.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-failed-scheduling
observations: Event Reason: FailedScheduling: Pod can't be scheduled. Message details fitness failure: 'insufficient cpu', 'didn't have free ports', 'node(s) had taint X', 'didn't match Pod's node affinity', 'persistentvolumeclaim X not found'.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-failed-mount
observations: Event Reason: FailedMount: Volume couldn't be mounted. PVC not bound, secret/configmap not found, NFS server unreachable, csi driver crashed.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-failed-pull
observations: Event Reason: Failed (image pull): Image pull failed. Often combined with reason 'ErrImagePull' or 'ImagePullBackOff' on container.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-backoff
observations: Event Reason: BackOff: Container repeatedly crashing; kubelet backing off restart attempts.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-unhealthy
observations: Event Reason: Unhealthy: Probe failed. Message: 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503'.

name: k8s.debugging.event-reason-failed-killpod
observations: Event Reason: FailedKillPod: Kubelet couldn't kill pod. Often runtime hung or container in D state.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-debug-feature
observations: kubectl debug command: Three modes: ephemeral container in existing pod, copy-pod-with-modifications, node-debug (privileged pod with hostPath rootfs).

name: k8s.debugging.ephemeral-debug-pattern
observations: Ephemeral container debug pattern: `kubectl debug -it pod/X --image=nicolaka/netshoot --target=app` adds netshoot container sharing PID+network namespace with 'app'. Inspect from inside without modifying pod spec.

name: k8s.debugging.copy-pod-debug-pattern
observations: Copy-pod debug pattern: `kubectl debug pod/X --copy-to=X-debug --container=app --image=busybox` clones the pod with image swapped on a container. Don't kill the original; experiment in copy.

name: k8s.debugging.node-debug-pattern
observations: Node debug pattern: `kubectl debug node/X -it --image=busybox` schedules a privileged pod on node with hostPath / mount. Then `chroot /host` to act as host root. Risky — avoids needing SSH.

name: k8s.debugging.crictl
observations: crictl: CRI-direct CLI. Bypasses kubelet+API server. Talks straight to containerd/CRI-O via /run/containerd/containerd.sock. For node-level debug when API unavailable.

name: k8s.debugging.kubelet-logs
observations: Kubelet logs: Per-node kubelet logs. systemd: `journalctl -u kubelet -f`. Verbose: --v=4. Source for: pod admission, runtime errors, volume mounts, garbage collection, eviction decisions.

name: k8s.debugging.api-server-logs
observations: API server logs: `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-NODE`. Audit log if enabled. Source for: auth failures, admission rejections, etcd errors.

name: k8s.debugging.scheduler-logs
observations: Scheduler logs: `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-scheduler-NODE`. Source for: why pods aren't scheduling. Verbose `--v=10` shows per-pod scheduling decisions.

name: k8s.debugging.controller-manager-logs
observations: Controller-manager logs: `kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-controller-manager-NODE`. Source for: deployment rollout decisions, garbage collection, node lifecycle.

name: k8s.debugging.etcd-logs
observations: etcd logs: `kubectl logs -n kube-system etcd-NODE`. Source for: storage errors, leader changes, slow operations (>100ms warnings).

name: k8s.debugging.pod-log-rotation
observations: Pod log rotation: Kubelet rotates per-container logs at /var/log/pods/<ns>_<pod>_<uid>/<container>/N.log. ContainerLogMaxSize, ContainerLogMaxFiles in kubelet config. Old rotated logs available via --previous in `kubectl logs`.

name: k8s.debugging.metrics-server
observations: metrics-server: Cluster-internal monitoring source for `kubectl top`. Polls kubelet's resource-metrics endpoint (/metrics/resource). Required for HPA. NOT a long-term metrics store.

name: k8s.debugging.metrics-resource-api
observations: Resource Metrics API: metrics.k8s.io group. Aggregated API served by metrics-server. Provides PodMetrics, NodeMetrics. Consumers: kubectl top, HPA.

name: k8s.debugging.custom-metrics-api
observations: Custom Metrics API: custom.metrics.k8s.io. For HPA scaling on app-defined metrics (queue depth, etc.). Implementations: prometheus-adapter, KEDA.

name: k8s.debugging.external-metrics-api
observations: External Metrics API: external.metrics.k8s.io. For metrics not associated with K8s objects (e.g. SQS queue length, GCP Pub/Sub backlog). KEDA implements.

name: k8s.debugging.logging-architecture-doc
observations: K8s logging architecture: App writes to stdout/stderr → container runtime captures → kubelet exposes → /var/log/pods/ on node. Cluster-level: log shipper (Fluent Bit, Vector, Filebeat) DaemonSet → backend (Loki, ELK, Datadog).

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-events-cmd
observations: kubectl events (modern): 1.23+ replacement for `kubectl get events`. Better filtering, --for=TYPE/NAME scoping.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-get-events
observations: kubectl get events (legacy): Standard event listing. --sort-by=.lastTimestamp for chrono. -A for cluster-wide.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-top-feature
observations: kubectl top: Resource usage. Requires metrics-server. Pods or nodes scope. Sort by cpu/memory.

name: k8s.debugging.cluster-info
observations: kubectl cluster-info: Quick check: control-plane reachable + addon endpoints. dump variant: full cluster state to dir for offline analysis.

name: k8s.debugging.cluster-info-dump
observations: kubectl cluster-info dump: Dump full cluster state (nodes, pods, events, services) to dir. For support tickets / postmortems. --output-directory=DIR.

name: k8s.debugging.must-gather
observations: must-gather (OpenShift) / sosreport: Bundled diagnostic collection. OpenShift: `oc adm must-gather`. K8s: cluster-info dump + per-distro tooling (KIND has its own).

name: k8s.debugging.troubleshoot-init-pattern
observations: Troubleshoot init containers: Init containers run sequentially. Pod stuck Initializing means an init container failed/hung. `kubectl logs POD -c <init-container-name>` (no --previous since they don't restart in default policy).

name: k8s.debugging.debug-services-doc
observations: Debug Services workflow: K8s docs canonical Service-debug procedure: confirm Service exists, has endpoints, kube-proxy programmed iptables, network reachable from a debug pod. Each step: a kubectl command.

name: k8s.debugging.debug-running-pod-doc
observations: Debug Running Pods workflow: K8s docs procedure: get pod status, describe events, logs (current + --previous), exec for in-pod inspection, ephemeral debug container if needed.

name: k8s.debugging.terminating-stuck
observations: Pod stuck Terminating: Pod won't disappear. Usually finalizer or volume detach failure. Diagnose: `kubectl get pod X -o yaml` look at finalizers + deletionTimestamp + status. Force: `--grace-period=0 --force` (last resort).

name: k8s.debugging.pending-stuck
observations: Pod stuck Pending: Schedulable causes (FailedScheduling event), volume binding failure, init-container failure, image-pull-back-off. `kubectl describe` events tell you which.

name: k8s.debugging.crashloop-debug-pattern
observations: CrashLoopBackOff debug pattern: Container crashing+restarting. Sequence: `kubectl logs POD --previous` (last instance's logs), `kubectl describe POD` (events + restart count), exec into a sleeping copy via kubectl debug --copy-to.

name: k8s.debugging.oomkilled-debug-pattern
observations: OOMKilled debug pattern: Memory exceeded. `kubectl describe pod` shows reason: OOMKilled, exit 137. Diagnose: actual memory use via `kubectl top pod` (live) or container memory.events from cgroup. Fix: raise limits or fix leak.

name: k8s.debugging.imagepull-debug-pattern
observations: ImagePullBackOff debug pattern: Image can't be pulled. Causes: typo in image name, missing imagePullSecrets, registry rate limit, registry auth expired, private registry network unreachable. Events show registry response.

name: k8s.debugging.dns-resolution-debug
observations: DNS resolution debug: Run `nslookup` from a debug pod with same DNS config as failing pod. Check /etc/resolv.conf. Verify CoreDNS pods running and Service `kube-dns` has endpoints. Test cluster.local + external resolution.

name: k8s.debugging.api-throttle
observations: API server throttling: kube-apiserver responds 429 (Too Many Requests) when client exceeds rate limit (Priority+Fairness). Visible in client logs. Increase priority class or batch requests.

name: k8s.debugging.etcd-slow-watch
observations: etcd slow watch: etcd warnings: 'apply request took too long'. Caused by disk latency, large objects, watch cache miss. Look at etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds metric.

name: k8s.debugging.csi-debug
observations: CSI driver debug: Volume mount issues: check csi driver pods (DaemonSet) running, `kubectl describe pvc` for binding, `journalctl -u kubelet` on the node for mount logs.

name: k8s.debugging.prometheus-cross-ref
observations: Prometheus + Grafana (cross-ref): Standard observability stack. ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor CRDs (prometheus-operator) for scrape config. Out of this corpus's scope.

name: k8s.debugging.profiling-pprof
observations: pprof profiling: Go components (apiserver, kubelet, controller-manager, scheduler) expose pprof at /debug/pprof. `go tool pprof http://NODE:10250/debug/pprof/profile`. Restricted by RBAC.

name: k8s.debugging.audit-logging
observations: Audit logging: kube-apiserver --audit-policy-file. Records every API request: who, what, when, response. Levels: None, Metadata, Request, RequestResponse. Crucial for security forensics.

name: k8s.debugging.kubernetes-dashboard
observations: Kubernetes Dashboard: Web UI. Useful for visualizing resource state, but `kubectl describe` covers same info faster. Auth: token + RBAC.

name: k8s.debugging.lens-k9s
observations: Lens / k9s (clients): Third-party kubectl frontends. Lens = GUI; k9s = TUI. Productivity-boosters; same auth/authz as kubectl.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-debug-profile-netadmin
observations: kubectl debug --profile=netadmin: Pre-defined profile granting CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW for network debugging. Combined with image=netshoot.

name: k8s.debugging.kubectl-debug-profile-sysadmin
observations: kubectl debug --profile=sysadmin: Profile with CAP_SYS_ADMIN + privileged for system-level debug. Use sparingly.

name: k8s.debugging.events-vs-conditions
observations: Events vs Conditions: Events = transient log of changes (TTL'd). Conditions = current status fields (PodScheduled, Initialized, Ready). Both useful — conditions for live state; events for history.

name: k8s.debugging.kubeadm-troubleshoot
observations: kubeadm troubleshoot: For self-managed clusters: `kubeadm init/join phase ... --dry-run`, kubelet logs (journalctl -u kubelet), kubelet config /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml.

name: k8s.debugging.cluster-component-debug
observations: Component debug procedure: For control-plane issues: SSH to node → check kubelet → check container runtime (crictl ps) → check static pod manifests at /etc/kubernetes/manifests/.

name: k8s.runtime.cri
observations: CRI (Container Runtime Interface): gRPC API between kubelet and runtime. Two services: RuntimeService (sandbox + container lifecycle, exec, attach) + ImageService (pull, list, remove). Unix-socket transport.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-runtime-service
observations: CRI RuntimeService: Methods: RunPodSandbox, StopPodSandbox, RemovePodSandbox, ListPodSandbox; CreateContainer, StartContainer, StopContainer, RemoveContainer, ListContainers, ContainerStats; ExecSync, Exec, Attach, PortForward.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-image-service
observations: CRI ImageService: Methods: ListImages, ImageStatus, PullImage, RemoveImage, ImageFsInfo.

name: k8s.runtime.pod-sandbox
observations: Pod sandbox: CRI primitive representing a pod's shared environment (network namespace, IPC namespace, optionally UTS+PID). Container runtime creates sandbox first, then containers attached to it. 'pause' container historically held the sandbox.

name: k8s.runtime.pause-container
observations: pause container: Tiny container per-pod holding namespaces alive. ALWAYS first to start, last to stop. Bare-minimum image (~700KB). Image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.x. The 'invisible' container in every pod.

name: k8s.runtime.containerd
observations: containerd (in K8s): Default since K8s 1.24 dropped Docker shim. Multi-tenant, OCI-conformant, lightweight. Configured via /etc/containerd/config.toml. Plugin: io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-o
observations: CRI-O: Alternative runtime. K8s-only scope (no docker-style API). Smaller surface than containerd. Default on RHEL/OpenShift.

name: k8s.runtime.runc
observations: runc: Default OCI runtime under containerd/CRI-O. Sets up Linux namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, mounts; execs container init. Exit code 137 = SIGKILL (OOM).

name: k8s.runtime.crun
observations: crun: runc-compatible alternative in C. Faster startup, lower memory. Default in podman, available as drop-in for containerd.

name: k8s.runtime.kata-runtime
observations: Kata Containers: VM-isolated container runtime. Each pod = lightweight VM. Stronger isolation than namespace-only. Uses RuntimeClass to opt-in pods.

name: k8s.runtime.gvisor
observations: gVisor (runsc): Userspace kernel — intercepts container syscalls, executes in sandboxed Sentry. Strong isolation, ~10% perf cost. Used by GKE Sandbox, Cloud Run.

name: k8s.runtime.runtime-class
observations: RuntimeClass: Cluster-scoped resource selecting which runtime to use. spec.handler matches containerd/CRI-O config-defined runtime name. Pod refs via spec.runtimeClassName.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet
observations: kubelet: Per-node agent. Watches Pods scheduled to node, calls CRI to start, runs probes, reports status, manages volume mounts, cgroup setup. The bridge between K8s control plane and container runtime.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-static-pods
observations: Static pods: Pods defined directly in kubelet config (--pod-manifest-path /etc/kubernetes/manifests/). NOT created via API. Used for control-plane bootstrap (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, etcd self-hosting). Mirror Pod created in API.

name: k8s.runtime.mirror-pod
observations: Mirror Pod: API-server-visible representation of a static pod. Created automatically by kubelet so users see static pods via kubectl. Cannot edit via API.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-config
observations: Kubelet config (KubeletConfiguration): YAML at /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml. Controls all kubelet behavior: cgroup driver, evictions, log rotation, feature gates, eviction thresholds, image GC.

name: k8s.runtime.cgroup-v1
observations: cgroup v1 (in K8s): Multi-hierarchy. Per-controller mounts. Many K8s features (PodOverhead, PSI metrics, swap support) are v2-only. Migration to v2 is the modern recommendation.

name: k8s.runtime.cgroup-v2
observations: cgroup v2 (in K8s): Unified hierarchy. Required for: MemoryQoS, swap support (1.30+), per-pod PSI, modern resource controls. Set host's systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 + kubelet's cgroupDriver=systemd.

name: k8s.runtime.cgroup-driver-systemd
observations: cgroup driver: systemd: Recommended. Kubelet + container runtime both delegate cgroup creation to systemd. Avoids dual-management conflicts. Set in kubelet config: cgroupDriver: systemd. Same in containerd config: SystemdCgroup = true.

name: k8s.runtime.cgroup-driver-cgroupfs
observations: cgroup driver: cgroupfs: Direct write to /sys/fs/cgroup. Older default. Conflicts with systemd-managed cgroups. Migrate to 'systemd' on systemd hosts.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-pod-cgroup
observations: Kubelet pod-cgroup hierarchy: kubepods.slice → kubepods-pod<UID>.slice (per-pod) → cri-containerd-<containerID>.scope (per-container). Visible via systemd-cgls or /sys/fs/cgroup/kubepods.slice/.

name: k8s.runtime.qos-cgroup
observations: QoS cgroups: kubepods-besteffort.slice, kubepods-burstable.slice, kubepods.slice (Guaranteed). Hierarchical caps so BestEffort can't starve Guaranteed.

name: k8s.runtime.kube-proxy
observations: kube-proxy: Per-node networking agent. Reads Service+EndpointSlice via API, programs iptables/IPVS/nftables for VIP→pod-IP mapping.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-spec
observations: CRI spec versions: CRI v1 stable. Older runtimes used v1alpha2. Compatibility matrix in K8s docs. Check via crictl version.

name: k8s.runtime.containerd-config
observations: containerd config.toml: /etc/containerd/config.toml. Sections: [plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri"] for CRI; [plugins."...cri".containerd.runtimes.runc] for runc settings; SystemdCgroup = true for cgroup-driver.

name: k8s.runtime.containerd-runtime-handler
observations: Containerd runtime handler: Named runtime in config.toml (e.g. runc, crun, gvisor, kata). RuntimeClass.spec.handler refers to this name.

name: k8s.runtime.image-pull-credentials
observations: Image pull credentials: Sources: pod's imagePullSecrets, ServiceAccount's imagePullSecrets, kubelet's --image-credential-provider-config (cloud auth helpers like ECR/GCR), node's /var/lib/kubelet/config.json or /root/.docker/config.json.

name: k8s.runtime.image-credential-provider
observations: Image credential provider: Plugin executable kubelet calls for image-pull auth. Cloud providers ship: ecr-credential-provider (AWS), gcr-credential-provider (GCP). Avoids storing static creds.

name: k8s.runtime.pod-overhead
observations: Pod Overhead: RuntimeClass.spec.overhead — extra CPU/memory accounted for the runtime itself (e.g. Kata VM has 200Mi memory + 250m CPU overhead). Scheduler reserves; cgroups apply to the pod cgroup.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-volume-plugins
observations: Kubelet volume plugins: In-tree (legacy) + CSI (modern) volume drivers. Mount/unmount on pod start/delete. Volume manager loop tracks attach/detach state.

name: k8s.runtime.csi
observations: CSI (Container Storage Interface): Standard volume plugin API. Out-of-tree drivers (ebs, azure-disk, gce-pd, ceph, nfs). Provisioner CSI controller + per-node CSI driver. Replaces in-tree volume plugins.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-cni-call
observations: Kubelet calls CNI: During RunPodSandbox, runtime invokes CNI to set up pod's network namespace. CNI binary at /opt/cni/bin, config at /etc/cni/net.d/. Returns IP allocation back to runtime + kubelet.

name: k8s.runtime.image-fs
observations: Image filesystem: Where container images stored. containerd: /var/lib/containerd/. CRI-O: /var/lib/containers/. Sometimes separate from rootfs (--image-service-endpoint). evictionHard imagefs.available signals on this FS.

name: k8s.runtime.container-rootfs
observations: Container rootfs: Per-container writable layer + image's read-only layers via overlayfs. Lives under /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-pleg
observations: PLEG (Pod Lifecycle Event Generator): Kubelet subsystem polling CRI for container state changes. Generates events to drive sync loops. PLEG-relisting-too-slow warnings = runtime under stress.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-graceful-node-shutdown
observations: Graceful node shutdown: Kubelet listens to systemd-logind for shutdown signal. Drains pods (per priority class) before shutdown. shutdownGracePeriod, shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods kubelet config.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-summary-api
observations: Kubelet Summary API: /stats/summary endpoint returning resource use per node + pod + container + system-container. Source for metrics-server and kubelet's own eviction decisions.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-stream
observations: CRI streaming server: Separate HTTP server in containerd/CRI-O for exec/attach/port-forward. URL returned by Exec/Attach/PortForward calls; kubelet redirects clients to it.

name: k8s.runtime.dockershim-removal
observations: Dockershim removal (1.24): K8s 1.24 dropped the in-kubelet Docker shim. Migrating: switch container runtime to containerd or CRI-O. Docker Engine itself doesn't go away on the host (you can still use docker for non-K8s) — but kubelet no longer talks to it.

name: k8s.runtime.swap-support
observations: Swap support (alpha→beta): K8s 1.22+ alpha, 1.30+ beta. Allows pods to swap. Requires cgroup v2 + kubelet failSwapOn=false + featureGates: NodeSwap=true. Modes: LimitedSwap (default), UnlimitedSwap (deprecated).

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-cpumanager
observations: CPU manager: Per-pod CPU pinning. Policies: none (default, CFS quota only), static (pin Guaranteed-pods with integer CPU requests to dedicated CPUs). Useful for latency-sensitive workloads.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-memorymanager
observations: Memory manager: NUMA-aware memory pinning. Beta. Polices: None (default), Static (pin Guaranteed pods to NUMA nodes).

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-topology-manager
observations: Topology manager: Coordinates CPU manager, Memory manager, Device manager (GPUs) for NUMA-aligned allocation. Policies: none, best-effort, restricted, single-numa-node.

name: k8s.runtime.device-plugin
observations: Device plugin: gRPC service kubelet talks to for special hardware (GPU, FPGA, RDMA, SR-IOV NIC). Registers via /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/. Reports devices kubelet exposes as 'extended resources' (e.g. nvidia.com/gpu).

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-port
observations: kubelet port (10250): Default HTTPS port. API for kubectl exec/logs forwards, metrics, /stats. Authn via TokenReview; authz via SubjectAccessReview.

name: k8s.runtime.read-only-port
observations: kubelet read-only port (10255): Insecure HTTP port. Disabled by default since 1.10. Reads node/pod stats. Major security risk; ensure --read-only-port=0.

name: k8s.runtime.kube-proxy-port
observations: kube-proxy port (10256): Health check endpoint. /healthz returns last sync error.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-tls
observations: Kubelet TLS bootstrap: Kubelet auto-generates CSR signed by kube-controller-manager (or cloud-controller). Replaces manual cert management. --bootstrap-kubeconfig + RBAC for system:bootstrappers.

name: k8s.runtime.kubelet-config-drift
observations: Kubelet config drift: Multiple sources for kubelet config: command-line flags, /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, Node.spec.configSource (deprecated). Mismatches cause hard-to-debug behavior.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-debug-via-crictl
observations: crictl debug pattern: When kubectl can't reach API but you have node access: crictl ps, crictl inspect, crictl logs to debug containers. Bypasses kubelet+API.

name: k8s.runtime.runtime-handler-name-conflict
observations: Runtime handler name conflict: RuntimeClass.spec.handler must match a name in containerd config. Mismatch = pods stuck Pending with 'no runtime for ...'.

name: k8s.runtime.cri-version-mismatch
observations: CRI version mismatch: Old runtime + newer kubelet (or vice versa). Symptoms: weird gRPC errors in kubelet logs about unknown methods. Check crictl version + kubelet version compat.

name: k8s.runtime.eviction-pod-priority
observations: Eviction-by-pod-priority: Under node pressure, kubelet evicts pods. Order: BestEffort (first), Burstable exceeding requests, Guaranteed (last). Within tier: lower priorityClass first.

name: k8s.runtime.systemd-cgroup-path
observations: systemd cgroup path encoding: systemd-managed cgroups: /sys/fs/cgroup/kubepods.slice/kubepods-burstable.slice/kubepods-burstable-pod<UID>.slice/cri-containerd-<CID>.scope/. Versus cgroupfs driver's flat structure.

name: k8s.runtime.image-gc-state
observations: Image GC state: When imagefs > imageGCHighThresholdPercent, kubelet GC's unused images down to imageGCLowThresholdPercent. Aggressive GC = repeated pulls = traffic to registry.

name: k8s.runtime.runtime-handler-default
observations: Default runtime handler: In containerd config: [plugins."...cri".containerd] default_runtime_name = "runc". Pods without RuntimeClass get this.

name: devin.devbox.devbox
observations: DevBox: Devin's per-session execution environment — a Linux-based VM workspace with the customer's repos cloned, tools installed, dependencies resolved, and configuration applied. Functionally equivalent to a developer's laptop: OS, terminal, toolchain, cloned repos. Each session boots a fresh copy from the active snapshot; in-session changes are discarded at session end. Also branded in admin contexts as 'Devin's Machine' or 'Devin's Workspace'.

name: devin.devbox.microvm
observations: microVM: Hypervisor-managed VM per agent session, providing dedicated kernel + isolated storage / networking / compute. Cognition's microVM implementation took over a year of hypervisor engineering. Side benefit: agents can use full browser, desktop apps, and arbitrary tool stacks. The fundamental isolation unit underneath every Devin session.

name: devin.devbox.hypervisor
observations: Hypervisor: The Cognition-built virtualization layer that manages microVMs, performs snapshot/restore at the level of memory + process trees + filesystem, and shuts down compute while agents idle. Allows sessions to survive async gaps (CI waits, code review delays, follow-up commits) lasting minutes to days without burning compute to stay alive.

name: devin.devbox.snapshot
observations: Snapshot: A frozen, bootable image of a Devin environment — VM image with tools, repos, dependencies pre-installed. Each org has ONE active snapshot. Every session boots from a fresh copy. In-session changes don't persist back. Direct analogue to a Docker image, except produced by a build that runs the org's blueprint(s).

name: devin.devbox.session
observations: Session: A single agent run. Boots a fresh copy of the active snapshot. At session start: latest code is pulled for the relevant repos; maintenance commands are surfaced to the agent (NOT auto-executed); per-repo knowledge entries are loaded into Devin's context. Knowledge is per-repo — Devin only sees knowledge for the repo it's working on.

name: devin.devbox.snapshot-machine-state
observations: Machine-state snapshot: Hypervisor-level snapshot of a session's full machine state — memory, process trees, filesystem. Lets compute shut down while the agent is idle and resume exactly where it left off when a CI result or review comment arrives. Working reliably across thousands of concurrent sessions with different repos / dependencies / runtime envs took longer than any other piece of Cognition infra.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint
observations: Blueprint: YAML configuration describing what to install and how to set up Devin's environment. Direct analogue to a Dockerfile. Authored / edited in the Settings UI. Has three sections: initialize, maintenance, knowledge. Saved blueprints trigger automatic builds. Multi-document YAML supported via `---` separator.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-section-initialize
observations: Blueprint `initialize` section: Blueprint section for things that only need to happen ONCE: language runtimes, system packages, global CLI tools. Runs during builds only; results persist in the snapshot.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-section-maintenance
observations: Blueprint `maintenance` section: Blueprint section for dependency installs that should stay current. Runs during builds AND surfaced to the agent at session start (NOT auto-executed). Should be fast and incremental — `npm install`, not `npm ci`. The agent may re-run if it detects dependencies changed since the last build.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-section-knowledge
observations: Blueprint `knowledge` section: Reference info loaded into Devin's context at session start — NOT executed. Tells Devin the correct lint / test / build commands. Distinct from the standalone Knowledge product feature, which holds architecture docs, conventions, and team workflows. Per-repo: Devin only sees the entries for the repo it's working on.

name: devin.devbox.build
observations: Build: The process that runs your blueprint(s), clones repos, and produces a snapshot. Direct analogue to `docker build`. Builds are additive across tiers (enterprise → org → repo) — lower tiers cannot override what a higher tier set up. Builds typically take 5–15 minutes; individual steps time out after 1 hour.

name: devin.devbox.build-status
observations: Build status: One of: Success (all steps completed, snapshot ready), Partial (some repo-level steps failed but snapshot is usable — succeeded repos work, failed repos need blueprint fixes), Failed (critical failure at org or enterprise tier — snapshot not usable), Cancelled (superseded or manually cancelled).

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-tier-enterprise
observations: Enterprise blueprint tier: Highest tier in the additive 3-tier blueprint hierarchy. Applies across all organizations under an enterprise account. Sets baseline tools that org and repo blueprints can build on top of.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-tier-organization
observations: Organization (Org-wide) blueprint tier: Mid tier in the additive 3-tier hierarchy. Configured at Settings > Environment > Blueprints > Org-wide setup. Holds tools shared across all repos: language runtimes, package managers, Docker auth.

name: devin.devbox.blueprint-tier-repository
observations: Repository blueprint tier: Lowest tier in the additive 3-tier hierarchy. One per configured repo, at Settings > Environment > Blueprints > [repo name]. Holds project-specific setup: `npm install`, lint/test/build commands. A repo's `maintenance` can use tools installed by the org's `initialize`.

name: devin.devbox.repository-state
observations: Repository state: One of: Configured (has a blueprint with initialize/maintenance/knowledge — fully set up in the snapshot), Included (cloned into the snapshot but no custom blueprint — Devin can read the code), Available (connected to the org but not added to the environment — not cloned).

name: devin.devbox.snapshot-pinning
observations: Snapshot pinning: Locks the org to a specific build's snapshot. Useful when a new build introduces a regression, or to freeze the environment for a batch of sessions. While pinned: periodic refreshes are skipped; UI shows 'Auto-updates paused'. Pinnable builds must be Success or Partial and < 7 days old. Unpinning ('Resume auto-updates') switches back to the latest successful build.

name: devin.devbox.machine-version-history
observations: Machine Version History: Tab under Settings > Devin's Machine that lets you revert to a previous environment snapshot. Used after accidentally introducing a breaking change in setup. Restored snapshots replace the active snapshot.

name: devin.devbox.periodic-refresh
observations: Periodic snapshot refresh: Automatic build trigger that runs roughly every 24 hours to keep dependencies fresh. Skipped while a snapshot is pinned. Saving a new blueprint cancels any queued/in-progress build and starts a new one.

name: devin.devbox.build-trigger
observations: Build trigger: Events that initiate a new build: saving a blueprint (create/update/delete), adding/removing a repository, adding a repository secret, manual 'Build snapshot' click, periodic refresh (~24h), or a Devin in-session blueprint suggestion that gets approved.

name: devin.devbox.classic-configuration
observations: Classic configuration: Legacy environment-setup mode using an interactive wizard (8 steps: Git Pull, Configure Secrets, Install Dependencies, Maintain Dependencies, Set up Lint, Set up Tests, Run Local App, browser login) inside an embedded VS Code terminal. Superseded by declarative blueprints. Migration path documented; Devin can handle most of the migration automatically.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-git-pull
observations: Repo Setup — Git Pull step: Classic-config step 1. Command Devin runs at the start of each session to pull latest changes. Default usually fine. Devin must have access to submodules.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-configure-secrets
observations: Repo Setup — Configure Secrets step: Classic-config step 2. Set up secrets / env vars Devin needs to work with the repo. Reference via `$VARIABLE_NAME` in shell commands; manage via the Secrets dashboard.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-install-deps
observations: Repo Setup — Install Dependencies step: Classic-config step 3. Initial dependency install. Runs once during setup to prepare Devin's environment for the repo.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-maintain-deps
observations: Repo Setup — Maintain Dependencies step: Classic-config step 4. Commands run after `git pull` during session startup in case new dependencies were added — typically the same install command (`npm install`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-lint
observations: Repo Setup — Set up Lint step: Classic-config step 5. Lint commands; Devin checks output before committing changes.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-test
observations: Repo Setup — Set up Tests step: Classic-config step 6. Test commands; Devin checks output before committing changes.

name: devin.devbox.repo-setup-step-run-local
observations: Repo Setup — Run Local App step: Classic-config step 7. How Devin runs your code locally — useful when Devin must execute the app to test/debug. Browser tab can be used to log in to websites; cookies persist across sessions.

name: devin.devbox.setup-agent
observations: Devin AI Setup Agent: AI assistant that proposes setup commands per step based on codebase analysis. Surfaces suggestion cards in the timeline; user approves/rejects each. Used during repo setup and during 'Let Devin do it' blueprint generation.

name: devin.devbox.embedded-vscode
observations: Embedded VS Code: VS Code instance running inside DevBox; the primary terminal/editor surface for environment setup and live debugging. Drag-and-drop file uploads route to a known directory (`.files/`). Used to run blueprint commands manually, inspect filesystem, and edit files directly.

name: devin.devbox.cdp-endpoint
observations: Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint: DevBox's Chrome browser exposes a CDP endpoint at `http://localhost:29229` that Playwright can connect to. Used for browser-based authentication flows (SSO, OAuth) and systematic data entry — Devin can write and run Playwright scripts against its own running browser.

name: devin.devbox.direnv
observations: direnv: Pre-installed in DevBox; hook is already configured in `~/.bashrc`. Manages per-repo environment variables via `.envrc` files. After creating `.envrc` in a repo root, run `direnv allow` to load. Recommended pattern for managing repo-scoped env vars.

name: devin.devbox.nvm
observations: nvm (Node Version Manager): Pre-installed in Linux DevBox. Used to install/select Node versions per repo (e.g., `nvm install 18`, `nvm use 18`). Combine with `~/.bashrc` edits to auto-select per repo.

name: devin.devbox.bashrc
observations: ~/.bashrc: User shell init file inside DevBox. Edit via `devin ~/.bashrc` (which opens it in VS Code). Common edits: PATH manipulation, per-repo env auto-selection (cd-hooks calling `nvm use`), direnv hook (already configured by default).

name: devin.devbox.envrc
observations: .envrc: direnv config file at a repo's root. Holds repo-scoped env var assignments. Loaded automatically when entering the directory after `direnv allow` is run once.

name: devin.devbox.agents-md
observations: AGENTS.md: Open standard (https://agents.md) — a 'README for agents' file at the project root. Devin reads it before starting work. Typical sections: Setup Commands, Code Style, Testing Guidelines, Project Structure, Development Workflow. Vendor-neutral; complementary to Devin's blueprint configuration.

name: devin.devbox.windows-support
observations: Windows DevBox support: DevBox available on Windows on a limited basis (contact sales for access). Uses Git Bash (same shell as Linux), so most blueprint commands work cross-platform. Different file system layout (`/c/Users/Administrator` vs `/home/ubuntu`) and package manager (`choco` / `winget` instead of `apt-get`).

name: devin.devbox.runs-on-field
observations: Blueprint `runs-on` field: Top-level blueprint field selecting platform: `default` / `linux` / `windows`. Accepts a string OR a list (e.g., `[default, windows]`) — list runs identical commands on each platform, producing one snapshot per platform. For platform-specific commands, use the multi-block YAML format with one block per platform.

name: devin.devbox.multi-platform-blueprint
observations: Multi-platform (multi-block) blueprint: Multi-document YAML blueprint where each `---`-separated block declares its own `runs-on` label. Each block produces a separate snapshot build for its platform. The pattern for platform-specific commands (apt-get vs choco).

name: devin.devbox.large-performant-vm
observations: Large Performant VM (Beta): Updated VM-infra tier introduced in Jan 2025 to address Docker storage/perf issues on Devin's machine. Default for new teams. Existing teams enable via Settings > Devin's Workspace > Danger Zone > switch to 'Large Performant (Beta)' (requires resetting machine setup); experimental auto-migration available via support.

name: devin.devbox.acu
observations: Agent Compute Unit (ACU): Billing unit for Devin Enterprise (and the underlying metric for self-serve usage). Customers receive a monthly ACU capacity; usage above capacity bills as additional usage. Cognition recommends keeping sessions under 10 ACUs because Devin's performance degrades in long sessions.

name: devin.devbox.usage-budget
observations: Usage budget / Additional usage budget: Pay-as-you-go cap. Once monthly ACU capacity is consumed, sessions continue charging up to this budget. Billed at end of cycle OR when usage exceeds $2,000 (whichever comes first). Set in Settings > Plans > Manage Plan Limits or Settings > Usage and Limits > Manage Additional Usage Budget. Introduced January 9, 2025.

name: devin.devbox.devin-for-terminal
observations: Devin for Terminal: Local CLI agent with full access to the user's codebase, tools, and environment. Installed via `curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash`. Lets the user choose any frontier model (Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, SWE-1.6). Supports local-to-cloud handoff: hand the same session to a cloud DevBox when work outgrows the laptop. Custom Rust terminal renderer.

name: devin.devbox.blockdiff
observations: BlockDiff: Cognition open-source Apache-2.0 tool (https://github.com/CognitionAI/blockdiff). Computes block-level diffs of files (especially VM disk images) using CoW filesystem metadata. Supports two modes: (1) creating a diff between a base image and a target, (2) compactifying a sparse file (sparse 100GB → compact 10GB blockdiff). The DevBox snapshot infra primitive — explains how Cognition snapshots VM disks efficiently at scale.

name: devin.devbox.repository-indexing
observations: Repository indexing: Build of a search/understanding index over a repo's contents. Distinct from environment configuration. Enables Ask Devin and DeepWiki. Triggered via Settings > Repositories > Index repo on a per-repo, per-branch basis. Multiple branches per repo can be indexed via 'Manage' > 'Add branch'.

name: devin.devbox.deepwiki
observations: DeepWiki: AI-generated documentation surface for any repo (https://github.com/CognitionAI/deepwiki). Depends on repository indexing. Surfaces architecture / module / function-level summaries that Devin can reference during sessions.

name: devin.devbox.ask-devin
observations: Ask Devin: Codebase-question-answering feature. Depends on repository indexing. Used inside the Devin product to query 'where is X defined?', 'who calls Y?', etc.

name: devin.devbox.knowledge-feature
observations: Knowledge (product feature): Standalone product feature for persisting architecture docs, conventions, and team workflows that Devin should know. Distinct from blueprint `knowledge` section (which holds short command refs). Per-repo: Devin only sees knowledge for the repo it's working on. Configured at Settings > Devin's Settings > Knowledge.

name: devin.devbox.secrets-reference
observations: Secret reference (`$VARIABLE_NAME`): Bash-syntax reference to a secret stored in Devin's Secrets dashboard. Available inside blueprint commands (initialize/maintenance) and inside live sessions. Materialized into the snapshot if used in `initialize` (value persists), or refreshed on every periodic build if used in `maintenance` (recommended for credentials that rotate).

name: devin.devbox.file-attachments-dir
observations: File attachments directory (`.files/`): Directory inside DevBox where uploaded files are written. Linux: `/home/ubuntu/.files/`. Windows: `/c/Users/Administrator/.files/`. Source of truth for files dragged into the embedded VS Code instance.

name: devin.devbox.repos-directory
observations: Repos directory (`~/repos/<repo-name>`): Per-repo working-tree location inside DevBox. Linux: `/home/ubuntu/repos/<repo-name>`. Windows: `/c/Users/Administrator/repos/<repo-name>`. Each configured repo lives in its own subdirectory; dependencies are installed independently.

name: devin.devbox.vpn-openvpn
observations: OpenVPN client (pre-installed): VPN client pre-installed in DevBox's workspace. Configured by uploading a `config.ovpn` file and creating a systemd service unit at `/etc/systemd/system/openvpn.service`. The default VPN solution for accessing customer-internal resources (internal package registries, staging services, self-hosted services).

name: devin.devbox.vpn-alternatives
observations: Alternative VPN clients (Fortinet, Palo Alto GlobalProtect): Non-OpenVPN clients can be installed in DevBox. Publicly-available clients (Fortinet) install via package manager during setup. Private clients requiring binary install (Palo Alto GlobalProtect) are uploaded to the workspace and installed manually. All configured to start at session boot.

name: devin.devbox.outbound-ip-allowlist
observations: Devin outbound IP allowlist: Set of public IPs from which Devin's services originate outbound traffic. Customers must allowlist these on their side (corporate firewalls, SCM IP allowlists, internal services) for Devin to reach internal endpoints. Documented IPs as of P1: 100.20.50.251, 44.238.19.62, 52.10.84.81, 52.183.72.253, 20.172.46.235, 52.159.232.99, 4.204.199.103.

name: devin.devbox.async-gap-survival
observations: Async-gap survival: DevBox's defining capability over containerized agents: surviving the minutes / hours / days waits between session steps (CI runs, code reviews, follow-up commits). Containers can't snapshot state then shut down compute reliably. Hypervisor-level snapshots solve this — compute shuts down while idle, restores when a CI result or review comment arrives.

name: devin.devbox.warm-vm-pool
observations: Warm VM pool: Pre-provisioned pool of VMs kept ready for incoming sessions. The orchestration layer predicts demand and keeps the pool sized appropriately, so session-start latency is bounded. Built and maintained by a dedicated Cognition team. Sized to thousands of concurrent VMs.

name: devin.devbox.identity-chaining
observations: Identity chaining: Mechanism by which each session inherits the dispatching engineer's permissions across every system it touches (SCM, CI, package registries, ticketing). Every action recorded in a tamper-evident audit trail. Enterprise governance plumbing built and maintained at scale.

name: devin.devbox.audit-trail
observations: Tamper-evident audit trail: Append-only log of every action a session takes across SCM / CI / package-registry / docs / ticketing systems. Tamper-evident at the data plane — required by enterprise customers for security and compliance.

name: devin.devbox.aws-deployment
observations: AWS production deployment: Devin's cloud environment runs in AWS. Access granted on as-required basis based on business roles; only a small number of employees / contractors have direct production access. All transmission encrypted in transit and at rest. Production monitored via logging, error handling, live metrics dashboards; unusual states (high error rates, slowness, failures) trigger alerts.

name: devin.devbox.soc2-type-ii
observations: SOC 2 Type II certification: Certification Cognition obtained in March 2024. Auditors reviewed all security policies / procedures / internal and third-party controls related to data security, privacy, processing integrity, confidentiality, availability. Public Trust Center at https://trust.cognition.ai/.

name: devin.devbox.data-controls-opt-in
observations: Data Controls — opt-in to model training: By default Cognition does NOT use customer data for model training. Opt-in toggle on the Data Controls settings page. Enterprise customers are NEVER trained on (regardless of toggle).

name: devin.devbox.status-page
observations: Devin status page: Public status surface at https://www.devinstatus.com/. Tracks 6 components: Web Client, Agent, Integrations, Enterprise, Web Client (Enterprise), Agent (Enterprise). Subscribable via email, SMS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, webhook. Powers a JSON incidents archive at /api/v2/incidents.json (T0 corpus source — primary live capture).

name: devin.devbox.incident-record
observations: Status incident record: Single resolved-incident entry from the status JSON API. Carries timestamps (created/updated/resolved), affected components, status (investigating/identified/monitoring/resolved), and a human-readable narrative. ~47 records archived as of 2026-05-02 — gold layer for Phase 4 failure-modes mining.

name: devin.devbox.subshell-monorepo-pattern
observations: Monorepo subshell pattern: For monorepos, blueprint commands use subshells `(cd <subdir> && <command>)` so the working directory resets between steps. Required because each blueprint step otherwise inherits the previous step's `cd`.

name: devin.integrations.github-app
observations: GitHub App integration: App-based connection between Devin and a GitHub organization. Installed via Settings > Integrations > GitHub > Add Connection. Supports All-repositories or Select-repositories scope. Inherits permissions at the organization level (NOT individual user level). Required for Devin to create PRs, respond to PR comments, set commit statuses, and contribute to discussions/issues.

name: devin.integrations.github-enterprise-server
observations: GitHub Enterprise Server integration: Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server connection using personal access tokens (rather than the GitHub App flow). Setup documented at /enterprise/integrations/github-enterprise-server. Required for customers running on-prem GitHub.

name: devin.integrations.gitlab
observations: GitLab integration: Connection to GitLab.com or GitLab Self-Hosted (Enterprise plan only). Setup via Settings > Integrations > Gitlab > Connect (with optional Self-Hosted dropdown). Recommended pattern: dedicated GitLab account for Devin. Devin sees/responds to MR comments only when explicitly asked — does not auto-wake on new comments.

name: devin.integrations.bitbucket-cloud
observations: Bitbucket Cloud integration: OAuth-based connection to Bitbucket Cloud. Setup via Settings > Integrations > Bitbucket > Connect. Recommended: dedicated Bitbucket account for Devin (e.g., devin@yourcompany.com). Devin sees/responds to PR comments only when explicitly asked.

name: devin.integrations.bitbucket-data-center
observations: Bitbucket Data Center integration: Self-hosted Bitbucket connection. Setup via Settings > Integrations > Bitbucket > 'Bitbucket Data Center'. Requires the Bitbucket DC URL and service-account credentials. The service account needs project + repository permissions.

name: devin.integrations.azure-devops
observations: Azure DevOps integration: Connection to Azure DevOps repositories and pipelines. Listed in the integrations overview alongside GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket. Sub-page (`/integrations/azure-devops`) deferred from Phase 1 — content not yet ingested.

name: devin.integrations.slack
observations: Slack integration: Slack app for triggering and managing Devin runs from Slack. Triggered by `@Devin` mention in any channel. Supports inline keywords (!ask, !deep, mute, unmute, sleep, archive, EXIT, !dana). Optional dedicated #devin-runs channel pattern. Each user must link their individual account so Slack identity → Devin user. Slack-app-container (sidebar) requires a paid Slack plan; everything else works on free workspaces.

name: devin.integrations.microsoft-teams
observations: Microsoft Teams integration: Microsoft Teams app for triggering Devin runs. Triggered by @Devin mention in a Team channel or chat. Same inline keywords as Slack (!ask, !deep, mute, unmute, sleep, archive, EXIT, help). Each user must link their account so Teams identity → Devin user.

name: devin.integrations.jira
observations: Jira integration: Atlassian Jira connection for triggering Devin from tickets. Four trigger paths: assign to Devin (uses default playbook), playbook-label macro (e.g., !plan, !implement, !triage), generic 'devin' label (default playbook), or @mention Devin in a comment (no playbook, uses comment as task). Word-boundary matching is case-insensitive.

name: devin.integrations.linear
observations: Linear integration: Linear connection for triggering Devin from tickets. Three trigger paths: assign to Devin (default playbook), synced playbook label (e.g., !plan), @mention Devin in a comment. Includes native MCP tooling — when connected, Linear MCP is automatically available without separate marketplace setup. Default playbook for new connections is `!plan`.

name: devin.integrations.self-hosted-scm
observations: Self-hosted SCM connection: Pattern for connecting Devin to self-hosted GitLab / Bitbucket DC / etc. Two setup options: (1) Direct IP whitelisting at firewall — simplest, recommended; (2) Centralized Application Load Balancer or Network Load Balancer fronting multiple services. Enterprise-plan-only.

name: devin.integrations.self-hosted-artifacts
observations: Self-hosted artifact repository connection: Pattern for connecting Devin to self-hosted Artifactory / Nexus. Same options as SCM (direct whitelisting OR load balancer). When fronted by an Application Load Balancer (Layer 7), source IPs are NAT'd — must configure IP allowlist on the artifact repo itself, not just the ALB. NLB (Layer 4) preserves source IPs, so allowlisting at the LB is sufficient.

name: devin.integrations.network-load-balancer
observations: Network Load Balancer (NLB) — Layer 4: TCP-level load balancer that preserves original source IP addresses. Backend services see Devin's actual source IPs, so IP allowlisting at the load balancer is sufficient. Requires manual security group configuration for each Devin IP. Suitable for IP-whitelisting-driven setups.

name: devin.integrations.application-load-balancer
observations: Application Load Balancer (ALB) — Layer 7: HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with advanced routing capabilities. Traffic is NAT'd — backends see the ALB's internal IPs, NOT Devin's source IPs. Recommended for most use cases when paired with AWS WAF for IP filtering. For artifact repos behind an ALB, IP allowlisting MUST be configured on the artifact repo (Artifactory/Nexus) itself.

name: devin.integrations.aws-waf
observations: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall): AWS service used to enforce IP allowlists at the ALB level. The recommended pattern for IP-filtering Layer-7 load balancers fronting Devin-accessible services.

name: devin.integrations.aws-kms
observations: AWS KMS (Key Management Service): Cognition's encryption-key store. Manages and periodically rotates the keys used by Devin. Surfaced in the GitHub integration FAQ.

name: devin.integrations.pr-template
observations: PR Template (GitHub-style): Devin uses GitHub-style pull request templates when generating or regenerating PR descriptions. Searches a fixed set of repository locations and uses the first match. Falls back to a built-in default with sections for Summary / Review & Testing Checklist / (Optional) Mermaid diagram / Notes when no file matches.

name: devin.integrations.devin-pr-template
observations: devin_pr_template.md (Devin-specific PR template): Optional Devin-specific PR template that overrides the standard human-facing template only for Devin's PRs. Filename `devin_pr_template.md` (case-insensitive — both DEVIN_PR_TEMPLATE.md and devin_pr_template.md are supported). Searched at six paths in priority order before falling back to the standard pull_request_template.md locations.

name: devin.integrations.commit-signing-gpg
observations: GPG commit signing: Configuration that signs Devin's commits with a GPG key. Must be set up at the org-wide (or enterprise) blueprint layer because each session boots a fresh machine — keys generated mid-session are lost. Requires a dedicated GitHub user account, a GPG key with that account's email as UID, the public key uploaded to that account's GitHub keys, and the base64-encoded private key + GIT_USER_NAME / GIT_USER_EMAIL stored as Devin secrets.

name: devin.integrations.branch-protection
observations: Branch protection: GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repo setting that requires checks to pass before a branch can be merged. Cognition recommends enabling on main/master to gate Devin's merges (and human-authored merges) on CI passing.

name: devin.integrations.dedicated-service-account
observations: Dedicated service account (per integration): Recommended pattern across SCM and ticketing integrations: create an integration-specific user account (devin@yourcompany.com or similar) rather than using a personal account. Cleaner audit trails, separate permission management, easier rotation. Surfaces in GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Bitbucket DC, Jira, and self-hosted SCM docs.

name: devin.integrations.jira-playbook-label
observations: Jira playbook label: Jira label whose name matches a Devin playbook macro (e.g., `!plan`, `!implement`, `!triage`). Adding the label to a ticket triggers Devin with that specific playbook. Labels must be created manually in the Jira project — copy the name from Devin's integration settings.

name: devin.integrations.jira-devin-label
observations: Jira `devin` label (generic trigger): Jira label whose name contains 'devin' as a standalone word (case-insensitive, word-boundary matching). Adding it triggers Devin with the default playbook. Examples that trigger: `devin`, `Devin`, `devin-workshop`, `devin-task`. Examples that DON'T: `devinworkshop`, `devin_workshop`.

name: devin.integrations.linear-synced-playbook-label
observations: Linear synced playbook label: Linear label automatically synced from Devin's integration settings into the 'Devin Playbooks' label group in Linear. Adding the label to a ticket triggers Devin with the specific playbook. Default playbook for new connections is `!plan`.

name: devin.integrations.default-playbook
observations: Default playbook (per integration): Per-integration setting designating which playbook Devin uses when triggered without a specific playbook label (assignment, generic 'devin' label, etc.). Configurable in Jira and Linear integration settings.

name: devin.integrations.automation-trigger
observations: Automation trigger (Jira / Linear): Auto-start condition: Devin starts a session when a ticket transitions to a state matching configured filters (project/team, labels, status, optional playbook). Uses EDGE detection — fires on transition INTO matching state, not for tickets already matching.

name: devin.integrations.session-mode-direct
observations: Session mode — Direct session creation (Jira): Default Jira session-mode toggle. Devin creates a full session and works on the issue, posting updates back to Jira (PR links, session links, follow-up replies).

name: devin.integrations.session-mode-scoping
observations: Session mode — Scoping only (Jira): Alternative Jira session-mode. Devin only analyzes the ticket and posts a scoping comment with summary + implementation plan + confidence estimate. The user clicks a link to start a session manually.

name: devin.integrations.enterprise-jira-project-mapping
observations: Enterprise Jira project mapping: Enterprise-only configuration mapping each Jira project to a specific Devin organization. Required for the Jira integration to work in enterprise setups with multiple Devin orgs.

name: devin.integrations.enterprise-linear-team-mapping
observations: Enterprise Linear team mapping: Enterprise-only configuration mapping each Linear team to a specific Devin organization. Required for the Linear integration to work in enterprise setups.

name: devin.integrations.linear-agent-session-ui
observations: Linear agent session UI: Linear's native agent-session interface. Devin posts real-time activity feed (commands run, files edited, progress summaries), syncs its todo list to Linear's plan UI, accepts follow-up messages in the session thread, and supports a stop-signal that puts Devin to sleep on the current task.

name: devin.integrations.jira-oauth-service-account
observations: Jira OAuth 2.0 service account: Optional dedicated Jira identity for Devin's comments. Created via Atlassian admin > OAuth 2.0 service account with Classic scopes: read:me, read:jira-user, read:jira-work, write:jira-work. Connected by entering client ID and client secret in Devin's Jira integration settings. Makes Devin's comments appear under a bot identity instead of the connecting user's personal account.

name: devin.integrations.teams-rsc-permissions
observations: Microsoft Teams Resource-Specific Consent (RSC): Teams permission model granting per-Team/Chat scopes only where the bot is installed. Used by Devin to limit message access to specific surfaces. Includes ChannelMessage.Read.Group, ChannelMessage.Send.Group, Member.Read.Group, TeamSettings.Read.Group, ChatMember.Read.Chat, ChatMessage.Read.Chat, ChatMessage.Send.Chat, ChatSettings.Read.Chat. Removing the app from a Team/Chat revokes RSC for that resource.

name: devin.integrations.teams-graph-app-permissions
observations: Microsoft Graph Application permissions (Teams): Tenant-wide Graph permissions Devin's Teams integration requires; granted via Admin Consent in Entra ID. Includes Organization.Read.All, User.ReadBasic.All, AppCatalog.Read.All, TeamsAppInstallation.ReadWriteAndConsentSelfForTeam.All. Used only for discovery + installation orchestration — NOT for reading message content (that flows through RSC).

name: devin.integrations.teams-x509-cert-auth
observations: Microsoft Teams X.509 certificate authentication: Service-to-service authentication mechanism Devin's Teams integration uses (rather than client secrets). X.509 client assertion. Applies to Microsoft Graph calls, bot communications with the Bot Framework adapter, and any app-only API calls.

name: devin.integrations.dedicated-runs-channel
observations: Dedicated #devin-runs channel pattern: Recommended Slack workspace pattern: a single #devin-runs channel where all Devin conversations live. Improves team-level visibility, lets engineers learn from each other's runs.

name: devin.integrations.session-keyword-set
observations: Inline session-keyword set: Set of inline keywords supported across Slack and Teams: `!ask`, `!deep`, `mute`, `unmute`, `(aside)`, `!aside`, `sleep`, `archive`, `EXIT`, `help`. Slack also supports `!dana`, `!fast`, `![macro_name]` for slash-style invocations.

name: devin.integrations.user-account-link
observations: Per-user identity link: Required step where each individual user links their integration identity (Slack email / Teams identity / Linear account) to their Devin user. Without it Devin can't attribute a session to the correct user. Slack uses email matching (Slack email must equal Devin email).

name: devin.integrations.repo-permissions-enterprise
observations: Enterprise Repository Permissions: Enterprise-admin-only setting at Enterprise Settings > Repository Permissions. Maps each connected SCM repository to one or more Devin organizations under the enterprise. Orgs cannot see/use repos until explicitly granted access.

name: devin.integrations.dependabot-alerts
observations: Dependabot alerts (read access): GitHub permission Devin requires (read). Lets Devin resolve dependabot alerts on the customer's behalf — i.e., bumping dependency versions in PRs.

name: devin.integrations.commit-statuses-write
observations: Commit statuses (read+write): GitHub permission Devin requires (read+write). Lets Devin set commit statuses indicating CI pass/fail, mirroring its understanding of check results.

name: devin.integrations.checks-write
observations: Checks (read+write): GitHub permission Devin requires (read+write). Lets Devin view and report check results, communicating CI pass/fail back to the user.

name: devin.integrations.workflows-write
observations: Workflows (read+write): GitHub permission Devin requires (read+write). Lets Devin set up new GitHub Actions workflows — used during repo onboarding to configure CI/CD.

name: devin.integrations.no-repo-creation
observations: No repository-creation permission: Explicit security boundary: Devin's GitHub App permissions do NOT include repository creation. Devin cannot create new repositories in the customer's GitHub account.

name: devin.integrations.org-level-permissions
observations: Organization-level permissions (NOT user-level): Devin uses the permissions granted at the GitHub organization level, NOT the permissions of the individual user running a session. All users with access to both the GitHub and Devin organizations share the same Devin integration permissions.

name: devin.integrations.async-pr-comment-policy
observations: Async PR/MR comment policy: On GitLab and Bitbucket, Devin can SEE/RESPOND to PR/MR comments only when explicitly asked — Devin does NOT auto-wake to respond to new comments. (GitHub integration handles auto-responses; this is a behavior gap noted in GitLab + Bitbucket docs.)

name: devin.integrations.support-channel-slack-connect
observations: Slack Connect support channel: Customer can request a dedicated Slack Connect channel with the Cognition team via app.devin.ai/settings/support. Used for SCM/integration setup escalation, especially self-hosted onboarding.

name: devin.integrations.dns-record-for-load-balancer
observations: DNS record for self-hosted load balancer: Required step in the self-hosted-SCM/artifacts onboarding: after configuring the LB and IP allowlist, publish a DNS record (e.g., gitlab.yourcompany.com) that Devin uses to reach the service. Often configured via dns-change.json in AWS Route 53.

name: devin.integrations.tls-https-required
observations: HTTPS / valid SSL required: All self-hosted SCM/artifact endpoints exposed to Devin must use HTTPS with valid trusted SSL certificates. Plain HTTP is not supported.

name: devin.mcp.mcp-protocol
observations: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Open standard (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) enabling AI applications to securely connect to data sources and tools. 'A USB-C port for AI applications.' Devin uses MCP to mount tool servers into agent sessions — both Anthropic-shipped and customer-built.

name: devin.mcp.transport-stdio
observations: STDIO transport: Local MCP transport. Server runs as a local process; stdin/stdout exchange JSON-RPC messages. Required fields: command, args, env vars. Best for local CLI-based servers (npx, uvx, docker). Stdout MUST contain only valid JSON-RPC — any logging/debug output to stdout breaks the protocol.

name: devin.mcp.transport-sse
observations: SSE transport (Server-Sent Events): Remote MCP transport over Server-Sent Events. Required fields: server URL, headers. Legacy / being deprecated in favor of Streamable HTTP. Devin still supports it for legacy server compatibility.

name: devin.mcp.transport-http
observations: Streamable HTTP transport: Remote MCP transport over Streamable HTTP. Required fields: server URL, headers. Recommended for new integrations — more reliable across clients (Cloudflare, OpenAI, Claude). Endpoint convention: `<server-base>/mcp`.

name: devin.mcp.tools-list
observations: MCP `tools/list` method: Standard MCP RPC method that returns the server's available tools. Devin's 'Test listing tools' button invokes this against a freshly-spun-up isolated environment. Servers that connect but expose no tools have typically not implemented this method or have failed to register tools (often due to missing env vars).

name: devin.mcp.marketplace
observations: MCP Marketplace: Curated catalog of vetted MCP servers, browsable in Settings > MCP Marketplace. Many MCPs are 1-click enable; others require credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens, headers). 'Add Your Own' surface for custom servers.

name: devin.mcp.add-your-own
observations: Add Your Own (custom MCP server): MCP-Marketplace surface for adding any custom MCP server. Form-driven: server name, optional icon, short description, transport type (STDIO/SSE/HTTP), transport-specific config. JSON schema is shown for clarity but not edited directly.

name: devin.mcp.test-listing-tools
observations: Test listing tools (button): MCP-Marketplace UI action that spins up an isolated environment, connects to the configured server, and attempts tool discovery via tools/list. Disabled until the server config is saved. Validation failures categorize as: connectivity, authentication, or timeout.

name: devin.mcp.devin-mcp-server
observations: Devin MCP server: Cognition-hosted MCP server providing programmatic access to Devin's platform — sessions, playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations — plus repository documentation/search. Base URL https://mcp.devin.ai/. Authenticated; requires a Devin API key. Supports public + private repository access (unlike the free DeepWiki MCP).

name: devin.mcp.deepwiki-mcp-server
observations: DeepWiki MCP server: Free, no-auth Cognition-hosted MCP server providing access to PUBLIC repository documentation/search via DeepWiki. Base URL https://mcp.deepwiki.com/. Three tools: read_wiki_structure, read_wiki_contents, ask_question. The light-weight public counterpart of Devin MCP.

name: devin.mcp.tool.read-wiki-structure
observations: Tool: read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a GitHub repository. Available on both DeepWiki MCP (public repos) and Devin MCP (public + private with auth).

name: devin.mcp.tool.read-wiki-contents
observations: Tool: read_wiki_contents: View full documentation for a GitHub repository. Available on DeepWiki MCP (public) and Devin MCP (public + private).

name: devin.mcp.tool.ask-question
observations: Tool: ask_question: Ask any question about one or more repositories (up to 10 on Devin MCP) and get an AI-powered, context-grounded response. Available on DeepWiki MCP (public) and Devin MCP (public + private).

name: devin.mcp.tool.list-available-repos
observations: Tool: list_available_repos: List all repositories available to query with the authenticated Devin account. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-session-create
observations: Tool: devin_session_create: Create one or more Devin sessions. Each session can have a prompt, title, playbook, tags, and ACU limit. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-session-search
observations: Tool: devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions by tags, playbook, origin, schedule, user, creation/update time. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-session-interact
observations: Tool: devin_session_interact: Interact with a Devin session. Sub-actions: get status, send messages, sleep, terminate, archive, read messages and attachments, manage tags. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-session-events
observations: Tool: devin_session_events: Inspect events within a session — list summaries, fetch full event details, search event contents by text. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-session-gather
observations: Tool: devin_session_gather: Wait for multiple Devin sessions to reach a settled state (finished, errored, sleeping, or waiting) before returning. Useful after creating parallel sessions instead of polling in a loop. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-playbook-manage
observations: Tool: devin_playbook_manage: Full CRUD for playbooks. List, get, create, update, delete. Supports automation macros (e.g., `!my_macro`). Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-knowledge-manage
observations: Tool: devin_knowledge_manage: Full CRUD for knowledge notes — list, get, create, update, delete, browse folder structure. Also manages knowledge SUGGESTIONS — list, view, dismiss pending. Filters: repo, folder, search query. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.devin-schedule-manage
observations: Tool: devin_schedule_manage: Full CRUD for schedules. Supports cron expressions (recurring), one-time scheduling, notification preferences, agent selection. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.tool.list-integrations
observations: Tool: list_integrations: List native integrations (GitHub, Jira, Slack) and MCP servers with install status + settings URLs. Filter: installed | not-installed | all. Devin MCP only.

name: devin.mcp.x-org-id-header
observations: X-Org-Id header (enterprise auth): HTTP header that enterprise service-user keys and PATs MUST send to specify which Devin organization to target. The MCP tools operate on org-level resources (sessions/playbooks/knowledge); the org_id is otherwise auto-resolved from org-scoped service-user keys.

name: devin.mcp.api-key-cog-prefix
observations: Devin API key (`cog_` prefix): Auth token for Devin MCP server. Three flavors: org-scoped service user key (auto-resolves org), enterprise service user key (requires X-Org-Id), personal access token (requires X-Org-Id). All three use `cog_` prefix. Legacy `apk_`/`apk_user_` prefixes are NOT supported.

name: devin.mcp.database-toolbox
observations: Database Toolbox (CognitionAI): Apache-2.0 production-ready Docker images that connect AI agents to 22+ database systems through MCP. Built on Google's Database Toolbox base. Universal interface across SQL/NoSQL/graph/analytics platforms. Universal image: `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/database-toolbox/toolbox/toolbox:latest`.

name: devin.mcp.database-toolbox-prebuilt
observations: Database Toolbox `--prebuilt` mode: Database Toolbox CLI flag `--prebuilt <db-id>` for databases with built-in support. 12 prebuilt: AlloyDB, BigQuery, Cloud SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQL Server), Dataplex, Firestore, Looker, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Spanner, SQL Server. Most common configuration mode.

name: devin.mcp.database-toolbox-tools-file
observations: Database Toolbox `--tools-file` mode: Database Toolbox CLI flag `--tools-file <path.yaml>` for databases requiring custom configuration YAML files. ~10 databases use this mode: Bigtable, Couchbase, Dgraph, MongoDB, Neo4j, Redis, Redshift, Snowflake, SQLite, TiDB, Valkey.

name: devin.mcp.metabase-mcp-server
observations: Metabase MCP server (CognitionAI): MIT-licensed Cognition-built MCP server for Metabase analytics platform. 81+ tools spanning Dashboard Management (23), Card/Question Management (21), Database Management (13), Table Management (16), additional tools (9). Tool-loading flags: --essential (default), --all, --write, --read. Auth: API key (preferred) or username/password (fallback).

name: devin.mcp.metabase-tool-loading-flags
observations: Metabase MCP tool-loading flags: Metabase MCP server CLI flags controlling which subset of tools to load: --essential (default — minimal set), --all (load all 80+ tools), --write (write/modification tools only), --read (read-only tools only).

name: devin.mcp.read-only-connection
observations: Read-only connection (production DB pattern): Recommended pattern for connecting Devin to production databases via MCP: use a read-only connection string OR a database user with restricted permissions. Devin executes queries based on user instructions; scoping access prevents accidental writes.

name: devin.mcp.oauth-flow
observations: MCP server OAuth flow: First-time auth path for OAuth-based MCP servers. Devin prompts the user (during their first session OR when they click 'Test listing tools') to visit a URL and complete OAuth in a browser. Devin waits for the callback. ONLY org admins can authenticate OAuth-based MCP servers.

name: devin.mcp.service-account-recommendation
observations: OAuth service-account recommendation: Strong recommendation: use a SERVICE ACCOUNT (not a personal account) when authenticating OAuth-based MCP servers. Access is shared across the organization; all members' sessions use the same authenticated connection.

name: devin.mcp.cataloged-marketplace-mcps
observations: Cataloged marketplace MCPs (one-click): Many marketplace MCPs require no configuration — just click 'Enable'. The user is prompted to connect a service account during their first session or via 'Test listing tools'. Includes: AlloyDB, Asana, Atlassian, BigQuery, Cloud SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQL Server), Cloudflare, Cortex, Dataplex, Fireflies, Firestore, Jam, Linear, Looker, Metabase, MySQL, Neon, Notion, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Sentry, Spanner, SQL Server, Vercel.

name: devin.mcp.linear-native-tools
observations: Linear native MCP tools (auto-mounted): When the Linear integration is connected, Devin already has native Linear tools using the integration's authentication. Linear MCP does NOT need to be configured separately from the marketplace.

name: devin.mcp.snyk-mcp-pattern
observations: Snyk MCP pattern (custom env + CLI install): Snyk MCP requires three steps: (1) configure the MCP server with custom env var (not in default docs), (2) install Snyk CLI on Devin's machine, (3) trust folder. Some scans require an `unmanaged: true` flag (e.g., C++) which can be set in knowledge or during a session.

name: devin.mcp.devin-as-data-analyst
observations: Devin as data analyst (in Slack via DB MCPs): Use case: connect Devin to database MCPs (Postgres, BigQuery, etc.) and trigger from Slack with !ask. Devin acts as a data analyst answering ad-hoc questions over the data. Step-by-step guide on the marketplace docs page.

name: devin.mcp.session-logs-debugging
observations: Session logs debugging (MCP failures): When an MCP server fails during a session, Devin logs the error in session output. Look for MCP-related messages — connection errors, tool-call timeouts, schema mismatches. The first stop for debugging custom MCP server issues.

name: devin.mcp.universal-toolbox-image
observations: Universal Database Toolbox Docker image: Single Docker image at `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/database-toolbox/toolbox/toolbox:latest` that powers all 22+ Database Toolbox configurations. SBOM, provenance attestation, multi-arch support. Pulled once; runs configured per database via flags + env vars.

name: devin.mcp.metabase-81-tools
observations: Metabase MCP — 81+ tools coverage: Metabase MCP server's tool surface: 23 dashboard-management, 21 card/question-management, 13 database-management, 16 table-management, 9 additional (collections/search/users/activity/playground-links). Effectively complete Metabase API coverage.

name: devin.mcp.metabase-auth-api-key
observations: Metabase MCP — API key auth (preferred): Preferred Metabase MCP authentication via METABASE_API_KEY env var. Server logs 'Using Metabase API Key' when active. Alternative fallback: username/password (METABASE_USERNAME + METABASE_PASSWORD).

name: devin.mcp.legacy-api-key-not-supported
observations: Legacy API key prefix not supported: Devin MCP server does NOT accept legacy `apk_` / `apk_user_` prefix API keys. Customers using legacy keys must rotate to a service-user API key (`cog_` prefix) before connecting MCP clients.

name: devin.mcp.deepwiki-mcp-no-auth
observations: DeepWiki MCP — no-auth, public-only: DeepWiki MCP server is a free, no-authentication-required service. Public repositories ONLY. For private-repo access, use the authenticated Devin MCP server (mcp.devin.ai) instead.

name: devin.api.principal-token-model
observations: Principal + Token authentication model: Devin API authentication model. PRINCIPAL is who you are (identity); TOKEN is how you prove it (credential). Two principal types: Service User (non-human) and User (human). Two corresponding token types: Service User API Key and Personal Access Token (PAT). Both share the `cog_` prefix and the same Authorization header format.

name: devin.api.service-user
observations: Service User (non-human principal): Non-human principal designed for API integrations and CI/CD. RBAC role-controlled. Created via Settings > Service users (org) or Enterprise settings > Service users. Recommended over PATs for production automation.

name: devin.api.personal-access-token
observations: Personal Access Token (PAT): Token authenticating as the human user who created it — user's identity, permissions, and org memberships apply. Currently in CLOSED BETA, feature-flagged. NOT available for SSO/enterprise accounts. `cog_` prefix.

name: devin.api.service-user-api-key
observations: Service User API Key: API key tied to a service user. `cog_` prefix; shown only once at creation time. Used in `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header. Recommended for automation, CI/CD, production workflows.

name: devin.api.legacy-personal-api-key
observations: Legacy Personal API Key: Deprecated. Tied to a user account. Prefix `apk_user_`. Used with v1 and v2 APIs. Inherits user permissions; no RBAC. Continues to work during deprecation period; not accepted by Devin MCP server.

name: devin.api.legacy-service-api-key
observations: Legacy Service API Key: Deprecated. Organization-scoped service key. Prefix `apk_`. Used with v1 API. No RBAC.

name: devin.api.api-version-v1
