name: firecracker.kvm.exit-fail-entry
observations: KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY: VMX/SVM entry into the guest failed at the hardware-virt level. kvm_run.fail_entry carries hardware_entry_failure_reason and cpu (vCPU number). Common on nested-virt setups (firecracker-microvm/firecracker#668), corrupted vmcs state after botched snapshot restore, or unsupported CPU features.

name: firecracker.kvm.exit-internal-error
observations: KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR: KVM detected an unrecoverable internal inconsistency — emulation impossible, simul exception delivery, unexpected delivery_event. kvm_run.internal carries suberror code and ndata extra registers. Should never happen; if it does, the microVM is unsalvageable.

name: firecracker.kvm.exit-hlt
observations: KVM_EXIT_HLT: Guest executed HLT in a state where it would block. KVM returns to userspace so it can decide what to do (typically Firecracker's vCPU thread blocks on a futex waiting for an interrupt).

name: firecracker.kvm.exit-irq-window-open
observations: KVM_EXIT_IRQ_WINDOW_OPEN: Guest interrupt-window is open and userspace had previously requested notification (kvm_run.request_interrupt_window=1). Firecracker uses this to deliver pending IRQs that couldn't be injected synchronously.

name: firecracker.kvm.exit-system-event
observations: KVM_EXIT_SYSTEM_EVENT: Guest requested a system-level event — SHUTDOWN, RESET, CRASH, S2RAM, SEV_TERM, WAKEUP. kvm_run.system_event.type identifies which. Firecracker handles RESET (warm reset) and SHUTDOWN (terminal).

name: firecracker.kvm.exit-debug
observations: KVM_EXIT_DEBUG: Guest hit a debug exception — single-step or hardware breakpoint set via KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG. Used by `firecracker --gdb-socket` flow for in-guest debugging (see fc-docs-gdb-debugging).

name: firecracker.kvm.user-memory-region
observations: User Memory Region: KVM's mechanism for mapping host userspace memory into guest physical address space. Each region: slot ID (max KVM_USER_MEM_SLOTS), guest_phys_addr, memory_size, userspace_addr, flags (KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES | KVM_MEM_READONLY | KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD). Set via KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION (or _REGION2 for guest_memfd). Firecracker registers one large region for guest RAM at boot; snapshots replay the same regions on restore.

name: firecracker.kvm.dirty-log
observations: Dirty Page Logging: Per-region bitmap of pages written by the guest since last query. Enabled by KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on a memory region; queried via KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG. Backbone of incremental snapshots — Firecracker enables this when taking a diff snapshot to capture only modified pages since the last full.

name: firecracker.kvm.in-kernel-irqchip
observations: In-kernel IRQchip: KVM emulates the IRQ controllers (PIC/IOAPIC on x86, GIC on ARM) inside the kernel rather than in userspace. Created via KVM_CREATE_IRQCHIP (x86) or KVM_CREATE_DEVICE with KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3 (ARM). Firecracker requires this for low-latency interrupt delivery; switching to userspace irqchip would dramatically increase VM-exit count.

name: firecracker.kvm.gsi-routing
observations: GSI Routing Table: Maps Global System Interrupts (GSIs) to in-kernel IRQ-line / MSI / hypercall destinations. Set via KVM_SET_GSI_ROUTING; entries are KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_IRQCHIP / _MSI / _HV_SINT. Firecracker programs MSI routes for VirtIO devices to deliver interrupts directly to vCPUs without userspace involvement.

name: firecracker.kvm.irqfd
observations: irqfd: eventfd registered with KVM_IRQFD that, when written, raises a guest IRQ on a configured GSI. Lets userspace devices signal interrupts without the cost of a vCPU ioctl per event. Firecracker uses irqfd extensively for VirtIO ring-event-to-IRQ delivery.

name: firecracker.kvm.ioeventfd
observations: ioeventfd: eventfd registered with KVM_IOEVENTFD that signals when the guest writes a specific value to a specific I/O port or MMIO address. Lets KVM short-circuit notification of VirtIO doorbell writes — the guest write is consumed in-kernel and the eventfd is signaled, bypassing userspace until the device thread is ready.

name: firecracker.kvm.cpuid-control
observations: Guest CPUID control: KVM_SET_CPUID2 lets userspace specify the CPUID leaves the guest sees. Firecracker uses CPU templates (T2, T2A, T2CL, T2S, etc.) to mask features for live-migration-safety across host CPU generations. Mismatched CPUID between snapshot-source and -target hosts causes restore to fail.

name: firecracker.kvm.msr-control
observations: Guest MSR control: KVM_GET_MSRS / KVM_SET_MSRS save and restore the guest's Model-Specific Registers. Snapshot/restore uses these to checkpoint per-vCPU state. KVM_GET_MSR_INDEX_LIST enumerates which MSRs the host KVM supports — Firecracker filters out unsupported MSRs to make CPU-template snapshots portable.

name: firecracker.kvm.xsave-state
observations: XSAVE state: Extended state (FPU, SSE, AVX, AVX-512, etc.) saved via KVM_GET_XSAVE2 (or KVM_GET_XSAVE for legacy fixed-size). Per-vCPU; included in snapshots. Size depends on enabled XCRs and supported features — KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION(KVM_CAP_XSAVE2) returns the dynamic size.

name: firecracker.kvm.lapic-state
observations: LAPIC state: Per-vCPU Local APIC register file (1 KiB), saved via KVM_GET_LAPIC and restored via KVM_SET_LAPIC. Required for snapshot consistency — pending interrupts and timer state live here.

name: firecracker.kvm.mp-state
observations: vCPU MP State: Multiprocessing state of a vCPU: RUNNABLE, UNINITIALIZED, INIT_RECEIVED, HALTED, SIPI_RECEIVED, STOPPED, CHECK_STOP, OPERATING, LOAD. Set/get via KVM_SET_MP_STATE / KVM_GET_MP_STATE. Snapshots restore this so a halted vCPU stays halted on resume.

name: firecracker.kvm.kvm-clock
observations: kvm-clock: Paravirtualized clock source the guest sees as kvm-clock. Backed by host monotonic clock; survives vCPU migration between host CPUs. Default for Linux guests <5.10; ≥5.10 prefers TSC if stable.

name: firecracker.kvm.tsc-control
observations: TSC control + KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL: Lets userspace set the guest's TSC frequency and offset. Required for snapshot restore on a host with a different TSC frequency. KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL must be present; KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ and KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ are the ioctls.

name: firecracker.kvm.virtio-mmio
observations: VirtIO over MMIO: VirtIO transport that uses memory-mapped I/O (vs PCI). Firecracker uses VirtIO-MMIO for all its emulated devices (block, net, vsock, balloon) — keeps the device model minimal vs the PCI alternative. Each device occupies a 4KiB MMIO region; doorbell writes trigger ioeventfds; interrupts via configured GSI/MSI.

name: firecracker.api.firecracker-api
observations: Firecracker REST API: RESTful HTTP API exposed by the Firecracker process. Transport is a Unix Domain Socket (default `/tmp/firecracker.socket`); requests carry JSON. Used for all VMM control plane: configuring devices, vCPU count, memory, then triggering InstanceStart, then runtime management (snapshot, balloon update, network rate-limit changes).

name: firecracker.api.unix-domain-socket-transport
observations: API Unix Domain Socket transport: Firecracker accepts API requests only over a UDS, never TCP. The socket path is given via `firecracker --api-sock <path>` or auto-named under the jailer chroot. Per-VM isolation: each Firecracker process owns one socket; orchestrators talk to N sockets for N microVMs.

name: firecracker.api.api-thread
observations: API thread: One of three Firecracker threads (API + VMM + vCPU). Owns the HTTP server and routes incoming requests to the VMM thread via a channel. Never on the fast path of guest execution. Failure of this thread is non-fatal to running guests but loses control-plane access.

name: firecracker.api.pre-boot-vs-runtime
observations: Pre-boot vs runtime API states: Most resource-creation endpoints (drives, network interfaces, vsock, machine-config, boot-source, cpu-config) only accept PUT before InstanceStart. After boot, only a small set are mutable: PATCH machine-config (pre-boot only — only PATCH on drive/network for rate-limiter at runtime), balloon, mmds, metrics target, snapshot create/load. Calling a pre-boot-only endpoint after boot returns 400.

name: firecracker.api.put-vs-patch-semantics
observations: PUT vs PATCH idempotency: PUT replaces the entire resource (e.g., putBalloon overwrites all fields). PATCH applies partial updates (patchBalloon updates only the fields supplied). PATCH is the only legal mutation path post-boot for most resources.

name: firecracker.api.boot-source
observations: Boot source: The kernel image + boot args + (optional) initrd path that the microVM boots. Set via PUT /boot-source pre-boot. Firecracker does not provide a kernel — user must supply an uncompressed ELF/PE Linux kernel built per fc-docs-rootfs-kernel.md.

name: firecracker.api.machine-config
observations: Machine configuration: Aggregate compute config: vcpu_count, mem_size_mib, smt (Intel hyperthreading), track_dirty_pages, huge_pages, cpu_template (deprecated — use /cpu-config). PUT replaces; PATCH applies a delta. Required before InstanceStart.

name: firecracker.api.cpu-config-resource
observations: CPU configuration (custom CPU templates): PUT /cpu-config supplies a custom CPU template — JSON list of CPUID modifiers + MSR modifiers + Aarch64 register modifiers. Replaces the deprecated machine_config.cpu_template static templates. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.drive-resource
observations: Drive (block device): VirtIO/block device backed by a host file. PUT /drives/{id} attaches; supports is_root_device, is_read_only, cache_type (Unsafe/Writeback), io_engine (Sync/Async), rate_limiter, socket (vhost-user). PATCH at runtime can only update path_on_host (drive swap) and rate limiters.

name: firecracker.api.network-interface-resource
observations: Network interface: VirtIO/net device backed by a host TAP. PUT /network-interfaces/{id} attaches; required: iface_id, host_dev_name. Optional: guest_mac, rx_rate_limiter, tx_rate_limiter. PATCH at runtime updates rate limiters only.

name: firecracker.api.vsock-resource
observations: Vsock device: Single-instance VirtIO/vsock device. PUT /vsock; required: vsock_id, guest_cid, uds_path (host-side Unix socket). Pre-boot only. Removing a vsock requires VM destroy/recreate.

name: firecracker.api.balloon-resource
observations: Balloon device: VirtIO/balloon for guest-cooperative memory reclaim. PUT pre-boot to attach; amount_mib, deflate_on_oom, stats_polling_interval_s. PATCH at runtime to inflate/deflate.

name: firecracker.api.entropy-device-resource
observations: Entropy device: VirtIO/rng exposing /dev/urandom from host to guest. PUT /entropy pre-boot; optional rate_limiter. Highly recommended for cryptographic workloads — without it, guest startup may stall on entropy.

name: firecracker.api.mmds-microvm-metadata-service
observations: MMDS (MicroVM Metadata Service): In-process metadata store accessible from the guest via a configurable IP/MAC on a network interface. PUT /mmds-config sets ipv4_address + version (V1|V2) + network_interfaces; PUT/PATCH /mmds writes the metadata; the guest reads via 169.254.169.254 by default (mimics EC2 IMDS).

name: firecracker.api.logger-resource
observations: Logger: PUT /logger configures a named-pipe (FIFO) logging sink. Required before any meaningful logging. Fields: log_path, level (Error|Warn|Info|Debug|Trace), show_level, show_log_origin, module (filter).

name: firecracker.api.metrics-resource
observations: Metrics: PUT /metrics configures a named-pipe metrics sink. Firecracker emits a JSON metrics blob on instance start, every 60s while running, and on panic. Use PUT a second time at runtime to flush metrics on demand.

name: firecracker.api.snapshot-create
observations: Snapshot create: PUT /snapshot/create — write VM state (memory + device state + vCPU state) to host files. Body specifies snapshot_type (Full|Diff), snapshot_path, mem_file_path, version. VM must be paused first via PATCH /vm{state=Paused}.

name: firecracker.api.snapshot-load
observations: Snapshot load: PUT /snapshot/load — restore VM state into a fresh Firecracker process. Body: snapshot_path, mem_backend (File|Uffd), enable_diff_snapshots, resume_vm. After load, VM is Paused unless resume_vm=true; otherwise PATCH /vm{state=Resumed}.

name: firecracker.api.vm-state-resource
observations: VM state (Paused/Resumed): PATCH /vm sets state — Paused (stop vCPU threads, no I/O) or Resumed. Required transition before snapshot create. Independent of InstanceStart action.

name: firecracker.api.actions-resource
observations: InstanceActions: PUT /actions triggers synchronous actions: InstanceStart (boot the configured machine), SendCtrlAltDel (graceful guest shutdown via PS/2 keyboard reset signal). Body is {"action_type": <enum>}.

name: firecracker.api.error-response-shape
observations: Error response shape: All non-2xx responses return JSON `{"fault_message": "<reason>"}` with HTTP 400 (bad input) or default (Internal Server Error). The fault_message is human-readable; orchestrators often regex it to classify failures (`vCPU count must be greater than 0`, `Block device backing file ... does not exist`, etc.).

name: firecracker.api.idempotent-204
observations: 204 No Content on success: Most mutation endpoints return 204 with empty body on success — orchestrators must check status code, not body. Only GET endpoints return 200 with payload. Confusing 204 vs 200 is a common integration bug.

name: firecracker.api.api-version-deprecation-policy
observations: API versioning policy: Firecracker maintains backward compatibility on a best-effort basis within a minor-version line. Breaking changes between minor versions are rare but documented in CHANGELOG. The /version GET returns the running Firecracker semver — orchestrators should check before issuing version-sensitive calls.

name: firecracker.api.swagger-spec-canonical-source
observations: Swagger spec is the canonical contract: src/firecracker/swagger/firecracker.yaml in the upstream repo is the single source of truth for the API. The Rust API server is generated from it. Orchestrators should pin to a specific version of the spec, not the docs site.

name: firecracker.api.serial-device-resource
observations: Serial device (custom): PUT /serial — attach a non-default serial device backend. Default behavior writes serial output to stdout (development) or discards it (production). Custom backend lets orchestrators capture guest console output.

name: firecracker.vmm.firecracker-vmm
observations: Firecracker VMM: Open-source Virtual Machine Monitor (VMM) written in Rust. Built by AWS for Lambda + Fargate. Forked from Google's crosvm; today crosvm and Firecracker have diverged. Provides minimal-overhead microVMs (≈125 ms boot, ≈5 MiB memory footprint) targeting serverless and container isolation.

name: firecracker.vmm.process-model
observations: Process model (3-thread): Each Firecracker process owns exactly one microVM and runs three thread classes: (1) API thread — HTTP control plane, never on the fast path; (2) VMM thread — device emulation (VirtIO net/block/vsock/balloon, MMDS, serial, i8042) and rate-limiting; (3) vCPU threads — one per guest core, running the KVM_RUN main loop. Fault domains: VMM crash kills the microVM; API thread loss only loses control plane.

name: firecracker.vmm.minimal-device-model
observations: Minimal device model (6 devices): Firecracker exposes only 6 emulated devices to the guest: virtio-net, virtio-block, virtio-vsock, virtio-balloon, serial console (ttyS0), and a partial i8042 keyboard controller (used only to signal microVM reset). No PCI bus, no USB, no graphics, no sound. Reduces attack surface and boot time vs QEMU's hundreds of device models.

name: firecracker.vmm.threat-containment
observations: Threat containment trust zones: Concentric trust zones from least-trusted to most-trusted: (1) guest vCPU threads (assumed running malicious code); (2) Firecracker VMM thread (handles device emulation and copies guest data to host fds); (3) jailer (chroot/cgroup/uid sandbox); (4) host kernel. Each barrier enforces specific security properties — e.g., I/O rate limiting is applied at the VMM-thread/host-fd boundary.

name: firecracker.vmm.token-bucket-rate-limiter
observations: Token-bucket rate limiter: Two-bucket implementation: one for ops/sec, one for bandwidth (bytes/sec). Each bucket: size (capacity), refill_time (ms), one_time_burst (optional one-shot extra). Applied per VirtIO/net interface and per VirtIO/block drive — both directions where applicable. Allows tunable burst behavior.

name: firecracker.vmm.startup-budget
observations: Startup budget (≈125ms / ≈5 MiB): Design-target startup characteristics: ≈125 ms from process start to guest jiffies (with serial console DISABLED — turning it on adds significant time), ≈5 MiB memory overhead per microVM. Per-host steady-state mutation rate: ≈5 microVMs per host core per second (e.g., 180 microVMs/s on 36 cores).

name: firecracker.vmm.kvm-clock
observations: Guest clocksources: Firecracker exposes the following clocksources: x86_64 — kvm-clock (paravirt) and tsc (Linux ≥5.10 picks tsc by default if stable); aarch64 — arch_sys_counter. KVM PTP (CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM=y in guest) is the recommended NTP source at scale to avoid network NTP traffic.

name: firecracker.vmm.cpu-template-mechanism
observations: CPU template mechanism: Per-vCPU CPUID + MSR + (Aarch64) register modifiers applied via KVM_SET_CPUID2 / KVM_SET_MSRS / KVM_SET_ONE_REG. Static templates: T2, T2A, T2CL, T2S, V1N1, C3 (Intel/AMD-specific). Custom templates: PUT /cpu-config supplies a JSON manifest. Snapshot portability requires identical templates between save and restore hosts.

name: firecracker.vmm.architecture-support
observations: Architecture support: Intel x86_64 (VMX), AMD x86_64 (SVM), 64-bit ARM (EL2). Firecracker is processor-agnostic at the VMM layer but guests must be built for the same arch as the host — no cross-arch emulation.

name: firecracker.vmm.kernel-support-policy
observations: Host kernel support policy: Firecracker pins host-kernel and guest-kernel version requirements per release. See docs/kernel-policy.md for the current matrix. Running outside the policy may work but is unsupported. Mismatched policies are a frequent cause of boot failures (e.g., GH issue #4881 kernel 6.1 panic).

name: firecracker.vmm.ctrl-alt-del-shutdown
observations: SendCtrlAltDel guest shutdown: Firecracker doesn't support guest reboot. Graceful guest shutdown on x86: PUT /actions{action_type=SendCtrlAltDel} injects a Ctrl+Alt+Del keyboard sequence; with `reboot=k` in boot_args, the i8042 reset line terminates the Firecracker process. ARM: `poweroff` inside the guest works directly via KVM PSCI emulation.

name: firecracker.vmm.eventfd-heavy-fd-usage
observations: Heavy eventfd usage (~20 FDs per microVM): Each Firecracker process holds 20+ file descriptors as a normal-state property — not a leak. eventfd backs every doorbell-to-device-thread wakeup (KVM_IOEVENTFD) and every VirtIO ring-event-to-IRQ delivery (KVM_IRQFD). Orchestrators must size host fd ulimits accordingly: 100 microVMs ≈ 2000 fds.

name: firecracker.vmm.config-file-mode
observations: --config-file startup mode: Alternative to API-driven configuration: pass a JSON file via `firecracker --config-file <path>`. The file contains the same shape as the resources you'd PUT (boot-source, drives, machine-config, network-interfaces, vsock, mmds-config, etc.). The microVM auto-starts after parsing. Useful for orchestrators that want zero round-trips to start a VM.

name: firecracker.vmm.host-integration-tap-files
observations: Host integration: TAP + files: Firecracker delegates persistent state to the host: emulated network is backed by TAP devices (orchestrator creates), block devices are backed by host files (orchestrator pre-formats). This keeps Firecracker stateless beyond the microVM lifecycle and lets orchestrators decouple storage/networking from the VMM.

name: firecracker.vmm.mmds-imdsv2
observations: MMDS — V1 vs V2: MMDS V1: unauthenticated GET — guest reads metadata via simple HTTP. Vulnerable to SSRF (any guest workload that proxies arbitrary URLs can leak metadata). V2: PUT to obtain a session token, then GET with the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header — same model as EC2 IMDSv2. Always use V2 for multi-tenant workloads.

name: firecracker.vmm.serial-console-overhead
observations: Serial console overhead: Default Firecracker behavior leaves serial console DISABLED in boot args for performance — booting with the console enabled adds significant time (every kernel printk causes a VM exit). Enable only for debugging via `console=ttyS0` in boot_args. Production: leave off; capture logs via PUT /serial to a host file or rely on guest-side logging.

name: firecracker.vmm.crosvm-lineage
observations: Lineage from crosvm: Firecracker forked from Chromium OS's crosvm (Rust VMM for ChromeOS Crostini). The two have since diverged — crosvm targets Chromebook desktop-VM use cases; Firecracker targets serverless. Shared Rust virtualization components live in the rust-vmm community (github.com/rust-vmm).

name: firecracker.vmm.no-arch-emulation
observations: No cross-arch emulation: Firecracker does NOT emulate a different guest CPU architecture than the host. Running an x86_64 guest on an aarch64 host (or vice versa) is unsupported. Use QEMU-TCG for cross-arch.

name: firecracker.vmm.no-guest-reboot
observations: No guest reboot — termination model: Firecracker has no concept of guest reboot. A guest reset terminates the Firecracker process. Reboot, in orchestrator terms, means: capture state (snapshot or scratch), tear down the process, start a fresh process, restore state (or boot fresh). This decision keeps the device model minimal.

name: firecracker.vmm.metrics-emission-cadence
observations: Metrics emission cadence: Firecracker emits a JSON metrics blob to the configured /metrics FIFO at three points: (1) instance start, (2) every 60 seconds while running, (3) on panic. PUT /metrics a second time at runtime forces an immediate flush. Counters cover device events, KVM exits, API errors, snapshot timing, etc.

name: firecracker.vmm.log-named-pipe-fifo
observations: Logger writes to FIFO (line-flushed): Logger backend is a host-side named pipe (FIFO) — orchestrators must create it before PUT /logger. Logs are flushed line-by-line, so a downstream reader sees lines as Firecracker emits them. If the FIFO has no reader, Firecracker blocks on write — common cause of mysterious VMM hangs.

name: firecracker.vmm.no-acpi-pm
observations: No ACPI power management: x86 Firecracker does not virtualize ACPI PM. Consequence: a guest `poweroff` will halt the OS but leave the Firecracker process alive. Use `reboot` (with reboot=k) or SendCtrlAltDel to terminate the process.

name: firecracker.vmm.uffd-snapshot-backend
observations: userfaultfd (UFFD) snapshot backend: On snapshot load, mem_backend.backend_type=Uffd uses Linux userfaultfd to lazy-load guest pages from the snapshot mem file on first access. Reduces RSS spike on restore vs File-backend (which pre-faults all pages). Requires a host process to handle the UFFD events — orchestrator implements this.

name: firecracker.vmm.dev-kvm-exclusive
observations: Exclusive /dev/kvm acquisition: Other hypervisors (VMware Workstation, VirtualBox) lock /dev/kvm exclusively. Firecracker fails to start with 'Resource busy' (EBUSY) when another hypervisor is loaded. Workaround: unload the conflicting kernel module (`modprobe -r vboxdrv`) before starting Firecracker.

name: firecracker.vmm.minimum-microvm-memory
observations: Minimum microVM memory (128 MiB default): If machine-config doesn't specify mem_size_mib, Firecracker defaults to 128 MiB. Process exits with code 12 ('Out of memory') if the host can't allocate that. Always set explicitly to avoid surprise.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshotting
observations: MicroVM snapshotting: Mechanism to serialize a running microVM (guest memory + emulated HW state including KVM state) to host files and later restore it in a different Firecracker process. The Cognition-cited 'hypervisor-level snapshotting' pattern that Devin sessions plausibly use. Original guest sees only the latency of the create operation; resumed guest may see network/vsock packet loss.

name: firecracker.snapshots.full-snapshot
observations: Full snapshot: Captures the complete microVM state — all guest memory, all device state, all vCPU state. mem_file_path is the size of guest RAM. Slower to create than diff but self-contained — restore needs only this snapshot, no chain.

name: firecracker.snapshots.diff-snapshot
observations: Diff snapshot: Captures only memory pages dirtied since the last snapshot (full or diff). Requires machine-config.track_dirty_pages=true on the original boot (enables KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES). mem_file_path holds only changed pages; restore needs the full chain. Currently in developer-preview while guest_memfd integration is being designed.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-files
observations: Snapshot file set: A snapshot is composed of multiple files: (1) microVM state file (KVM + emulated-HW state + 64-bit CRC), (2) memory file (guest RAM contents), (3) zero or more disk files (managed by the user — not produced by Firecracker). Restore needs all three sets. The state file CRC is the only integrity check Firecracker does — corruption beyond CRC scope is the user's problem.

name: firecracker.snapshots.map-private-on-restore
observations: MAP_PRIVATE memory restore strategy (File backend): On snapshot load with mem_backend=File, Firecracker mmaps the memory file as MAP_PRIVATE. Pages are demand-loaded into anonymous memory on first access; writes go to copy-on-write anonymous pages. Result: very fast restore but the memory file must remain on the host for the lifetime of the resumed microVM (it's the page-fault backing store).

name: firecracker.snapshots.uffd-backend
observations: Userfaultfd (UFFD) memory restore backend: Alternative to File backend. Firecracker registers guest memory with userfaultfd; an orchestrator-supplied UFFD handler process services page faults (e.g., fetch from a remote page server, decompress, etc.). Enables creative restore strategies — remote memory, deduplicated memory, just-in-time decompression. Higher first-fault latency than File backend.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-versioning
observations: Snapshot versioning: Snapshot files are versioned. Cross-version restore is supported within a stability window. The `version` field in PUT /snapshot/create lets orchestrators target an older format for backward compat with older Firecracker readers.

name: firecracker.snapshots.pause-resume-cycle
observations: Pause → snapshot → resume cycle: Snapshot creation requires the VM to be Paused first: PATCH /vm{state=Paused} → PUT /snapshot/create → PATCH /vm{state=Resumed}. The pause is a clean stopping point — vCPU threads exit KVM_RUN, no devices are mid-transaction. Skipping the pause leads to inconsistent device state.

name: firecracker.snapshots.network-disruption-on-restore
observations: Network disruption on resume: Open TCP connections, in-flight packets, and ARP-cache state of the guest are not guaranteed to survive resume. Workaround patterns documented in fc-docs-snapshot-network-clones: re-IP the guest after resume, clear ARP cache, use connection-resilient protocols. For 'clones' (multiple resumes from one snapshot) the host TAP must be re-uniqued per clone.

name: firecracker.snapshots.vsock-reset-on-restore
observations: Vsock device reset on resume: Open vsock connections are CLOSED across snapshot/restore. Listen sockets in the guest remain active and can accept new connections after resume. Orchestrators must design their host↔guest control plane to tolerate connection resets at restore time.

name: firecracker.snapshots.dirty-page-protocol
observations: Dirty-page tracking protocol: Two-phase protocol: (1) PATCH /vm{state=Paused} freezes vCPUs; (2) Firecracker calls KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG (or KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG with KVM_CAP_MANUAL_DIRTY_LOG_PROTECT2) per memory region; (3) only the marked pages are written to the diff mem file. Background: KVM marks pages dirty on every guest write via the page-fault path with KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES set on the region.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-clone
observations: Snapshot clone: Multiple Firecracker processes restore from the SAME snapshot file set, producing N independent microVMs (clones). Standard pattern for AI-agent sandboxes (one snapshot = warm template; each user session is a clone). Requires per-clone host configuration: unique TAP, unique vsock socket, unique mmds payload, regenerated VMGenID.

name: firecracker.snapshots.vmgenid-device
observations: VMGenID device: Virtual Machine Generation ID — a 16-byte value the guest reads to detect 'I have been cloned/restored'. Crypto and DRBG state inside the guest should be re-seeded when VMGenID changes. Firecracker emits a NEW VMGenID on every restore. Caveat: snapshots taken before the guest kernel finishes booting may not have a stable VMGenID device — restore from very early boot can crash the guest.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-trust-model
observations: Snapshot trust model: Firecracker's threat model trusts the host, the host↔API channel, and snapshot files. Firecracker only verifies the state file's CRC — disk files and memory file are NOT cryptographically verified. Orchestrators must implement their own authentication + encryption when storing/transporting snapshots across trust boundaries.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-portability
observations: Snapshot portability across hosts: Snapshot save and restore hosts must agree on: same CPU architecture (no x86↔ARM); same KVM capabilities; same CPU template (KVM_SET_CPUID2 + MSRs must match); on ARM, same GIC version (v2 vs v3 cannot cross). Without a CPU template, MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL overwrites are NOT preserved across restore.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cgroupv1-restore-latency
observations: cgroups v1 restore-latency tax: Snapshot restore is significantly slower under cgroups v1 vs v2 — see GH issue firecracker-microvm/firecracker#2129. Production deployments should use cgroups v2 (default on most modern distros).

name: firecracker.snapshots.userspace-restore-notify
observations: Userspace notifications of snapshot load: After restore, Firecracker can notify orchestrator/userspace processes that a snapshot was loaded — useful for refreshing crypto state, reseeding RNGs, re-establishing connections. Pattern: orchestrator passes a control fd or vsock channel that fires post-restore.

name: firecracker.snapshots.network-for-clones
observations: Network setup for clones (TAP per clone): Each restored clone needs its own host TAP device with a unique IP/MAC — the snapshot encodes the original guest's IP/MAC, but multiple guests sharing the same MAC on the same bridge causes connectivity loss. Workflow: pre-create N TAPs, restore N clones each pointing at a different TAP, optionally re-IP the guest post-restore via init script.

name: firecracker.snapshots.snapshot-where-can-resume
observations: Restore-host eligibility matrix: Eligibility constraints summarized: same arch; KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL must be available if TSC frequency differs; CPU template intersection must be non-empty; same GIC version on ARM. The fc-docs-snapshot-support 'Where can I resume my snapshots?' section is the canonical reference.

name: firecracker.jailer.jailer
observations: Firecracker Jailer: Privileged setup binary that wraps Firecracker. Sets up cgroups, chroot, network namespace, and resource limits, drops privileges to a low uid/gid, then exec()s into the Firecracker binary. Production-deployment-mandatory wrapper — design.md states 'Firecracker should only run constrained at the process level' achieved via the jailer.

name: firecracker.jailer.statically-linked-pairing
observations: Statically linked Firecracker pairing: Each jailer binary must be paired with a STATICALLY linked Firecracker (default musl toolchain) of the SAME version. Mixing dynamically-linked Firecracker (experimental gnu builds) is unsupported — symbol resolution inside the chroot may fail because libraries aren't copied in.

name: firecracker.jailer.chroot-jail
observations: Chroot jail layout: Jailer creates `<chroot_base>/<exec_file_name>/<id>/root` (default chroot_base=/srv/jailer). Copies the Firecracker binary into the chroot (so each microVM has its own non-shared mapping). Switches mount namespace via unshare() + pivot_root() + chroot(). The microVM's API socket, log/metrics FIFOs, and snapshot files all live INSIDE this chroot.

name: firecracker.jailer.uid-gid-drop
observations: Privilege drop (uid/gid): Jailer setuid/setgid to a non-privileged uid/gid before exec()ing Firecracker. Once dropped, Firecracker can only access resources granted to that uid (e.g., chroot tree, /dev/kvm if kvm-group has access). Critical defense-in-depth: KVM compromise is constrained to the jailed uid's reach.

name: firecracker.jailer.cgroup-setup
observations: Cgroup setup (v1 + v2): Jailer creates a cgroup `<cgroup_base>/<parent_cgroup>/<id>` and writes the Firecracker pid to its tasks file. Supports both cgroup-v1 (--cgroup-version=1, default) and v2. Caller specifies cgroup values via repeated --cgroup flag (e.g. cpuset.cpus=0,cpu.shares=512). Lets orchestrators bound CPU/memory/IO without separate root operations.

name: firecracker.jailer.cgroup-v2-subtree-control-trap
observations: cgroup-v2 subtree-control trap: If using --cgroup-version=2 with --parent-cgroup pointing at an existing cgroup, the jailer attempts to MOVE the process there. If that cgroup has domain controllers (e.g., memory) enabled in cgroup.subtree_control, the move fails with 'no internal process constraint' — exit error. Workaround: leave subtree_control empty or move to a leaf cgroup.

name: firecracker.jailer.netns-handling
observations: Network namespace join (--netns): When --netns <path> is given, jailer setns()s into the network namespace at that path before exec()ing Firecracker. Combined with TAP devices created INSIDE that netns, this gives each microVM its own network stack — no leakage between sandboxes.

name: firecracker.jailer.resource-limits
observations: Resource limits (setrlimit): --resource-limit fsize=<N> or no-file=<N> applies setrlimit() on the Firecracker process before exec. fsize bounds max file size (use to prevent runaway snapshot files); no-file bounds max FD count. Default no-file is 2048 if unspecified — sufficient for moderate microVM device counts but may need raising for vsock-heavy or VirtIO-MMIO-heavy guests.

name: firecracker.jailer.daemonize-flag
observations: --daemonize flag: Jailer calls setsid() and redirects stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null. Detaches from controlling terminal. Useful when launching Firecracker from a non-systemd orchestrator that doesn't handle daemonization itself.

name: firecracker.jailer.new-pid-ns-flag
observations: --new-pid-ns flag (PID namespace): Spawns Firecracker into a fresh PID namespace via clone(CLONE_NEWPID). Inside the jail, the Firecracker process appears as PID 1 with no visibility into other host processes. The host-side PID is recorded in `<chroot_dir>/<exec_file_name>.pid` for the orchestrator to track.

name: firecracker.jailer.fd-cleanup
observations: FD + env cleanup before exec: Jailer closes ALL open fds except 0/1/2 (per /proc/<jailer-pid>/fd) and clears all environment variables before pivoting to the chroot and exec()ing Firecracker. Prevents leaking parent-process state — orchestrator-side fds, secrets in env vars, etc. — into the sandbox.

name: firecracker.jailer.dev-mknod-passthrough
observations: /dev passthrough via mknod: Inside the chroot, jailer mknod()s `/dev/net/tun` and `/dev/kvm` so Firecracker can open them. These are the ONLY two devices the jail exposes — minimum surface for VirtIO-net (TAP) and KVM (the hypervisor itself). No other /dev entries.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.e2b
observations: e2b (E2B Dev): Open-source infrastructure for AI code interpreting and agent sandboxes. Provides SDKs (Python, JavaScript) + CLI for starting/managing sandbox environments. Hundreds of millions of sandboxes launched in production. Architecturally adjacent to Devin DevBox: per-session isolated execution environments with secure file/process APIs from a thin orchestration layer over a low-level VMM.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.e2b-firecracker-substrate
observations: e2b's Firecracker substrate (e2b-dev/infra): github.com/e2b-dev/infra is the Firecracker-based execution engine that powers E2B. Self-hostable via Terraform. Cloud-provider matrix: GCP (available), AWS (Beta), Azure (not yet), generic Linux (not yet). The closest public proxy to Devin DevBox internals, by reasoned analogy from Cognition's microVM-pattern blog post.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.e2b-sandbox-primitive
observations: Sandbox primitive (E2B's atomic unit): E2B's core abstraction is a 'Sandbox': start a fresh isolated environment, execute code/commands inside, read/write files, then dispose. Lifetime measured in seconds-to-minutes. Per-session isolation is the security boundary. Pattern: SDK call → orchestrator allocates a Firecracker microVM → guest workload runs → snapshot or destroy on completion.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.e2b-llms-txt-pattern
observations: llms.txt index pattern: E2B publishes a complete documentation index at https://e2b.mintlify.app/llms.txt for LLM-driven documentation discovery. Mirrors Devin's own docs.devin.ai/llms.txt convention — both target AI-agent consumers as first-class doc readers. Adoption signal: Mintlify-rendered docs sites are converging on this pattern.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.devin-devbox-likely-pattern
observations: Devin DevBox likely architectural pattern (inferred): By reasoned analogy from (1) Cognition's blog explicitly describing 'microVM isolation' and 'hypervisor-level snapshotting' for Devin sessions and (2) E2B's published Firecracker-based architecture serving the same problem domain, Devin DevBox plausibly runs each session in a Firecracker microVM with snapshot-based fast-start. STRONG-HINT, NOT DEFINITIVE — Cognition has not publicly named Firecracker. Useful as an interview-prep reasoning anchor: 'if the substrate is Firecracker-class, then the failure modes you'd debug are X, Y, Z.'

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.sandbox-fan-out-pattern
observations: Snapshot fan-out (warm-template) pattern: Pattern shared across AI-agent sandbox systems (E2B, Devin-likely, Modal, etc.): take a snapshot of a fully-booted, dependencies-installed microVM, then fan out N clones from it for incoming user sessions. Each clone gets unique TAP/vsock/MMDS but shares the warm template's memory image (MAP_PRIVATE COW). Achieves <100ms session start vs cold-boot's ~125ms+kernel+app init.

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.sdk-over-sandbox-api
observations: SDK-over-sandbox-API abstraction layer: User-facing SDK (Python/JS for E2B) abstracts away the underlying VMM control plane. SDK call sandbox.run('ls /') translates to: orchestrator picks a warm clone → opens vsock channel → dispatches command → returns stdout. Devin's tool API is plausibly the same shape — the user/agent doesn't see Firecracker, they see Sandbox.method().

name: firecracker.comparable-systems.cve-2026-31431-copy-fail
observations: CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail) — case study in why microVM isolation matters: Recent (Apr 2026) CVE that affected container-isolated sandboxes. E2B published a blog post explaining their Firecracker-based sandboxes weren't affected — direct evidence that microVM isolation provides defense-in-depth that container runtimes don't. Useful interview-prep talking point: 'why does Devin run in a microVM and not just a Docker container?'

name: firecracker.security.seccomp-boundary
observations: Seccomp boundary: Seccomp BPF filters limit the host syscalls Firecracker can issue. Loaded per-thread immediately before that thread runs guest code (VMM thread before vCPU dispatch; vCPU threads before KVM_RUN; API thread before HTTP server start). The primary defense-in-depth between guest-controlled code and the host kernel — assumes the guest has rooted the VMM and tries to expand to the host.

name: firecracker.security.default-seccomp-filter
observations: Default seccomp filter (embedded): Firecracker embeds compiled seccomp BPF filters at build time. Source JSON lives at resources/seccomp/<arch>_musl.json in the repo. The build step uses seccompiler-bin to compile JSON → bitcode → embed in the binary. Production deployments use these defaults — overriding is for experimental targets or quick mitigations only.

name: firecracker.security.custom-seccomp-filter
observations: Custom seccomp filter (--seccomp-filter): Override the embedded default with a custom seccompiler-bin-compiled file via --seccomp-filter <path>. Use cases: GNU libc experimental builds, debug builds that need extra syscalls (fcntl F_GETFD), emergency mitigation of an unallowed syscall in production. CAUTION: misconfiguration can disable the boundary entirely.

name: firecracker.security.no-seccomp-flag
observations: --no-seccomp (development only): Disables ALL seccomp filtering. Marked NOT FOR PRODUCTION. Useful for quickly prototyping Firecracker changes that use new syscalls. Often paired with --gdb-socket since GDB-required syscalls are blocked by default filter.

name: firecracker.security.seccomp-debug-binary-gap
observations: Debug-binary seccomp gap: Debug binaries and experimental GNU targets ship WITHOUT default seccomp filters installed — the build process skips embedding them since they're not for production. Implication: never run debug builds in untrusted environments. Verify with `firecracker --version` (release vs debug suffix).

name: firecracker.security.seccompiler-bin
observations: Seccompiler-bin: Compiles seccomp filter JSON into serialized BPF bitcode consumed by Firecracker. CLI: `seccompiler-bin --target-arch <arch> --input-file <json> --output-file <bin>`. Library API also exposed for in-process compilation. Filters use a custom JSON schema with thread-name-keyed objects, each containing default-action + filter rules (syscall-name + arg conditions).

name: firecracker.security.seccomp-thread-key
observations: Thread-keyed seccomp filter structure: JSON filter file is keyed by thread-name string (vmm, api, vcpu) — Firecracker installs the matching policy per thread before that thread starts running. Lets the API thread allow HTTP-server syscalls (accept, recvfrom) that vCPU threads must NOT have.

name: firecracker.security.bpf-filter-bitcode-format
observations: BPF bitcode serialization format: Compiled filters are stored as bitcode (not raw BPF instructions). Firecracker deserializes the bitcode at startup and installs via prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER, ...). Bitcode format isolates the BPF compiler from runtime — Firecracker doesn't need a BPF assembler embedded.

name: firecracker.security.kernel-support-policy
observations: Kernel support policy: Each Firecracker release commits to supporting specific HOST and GUEST kernel versions for a minimum of 2 years. ≥2 major versions of each kept simultaneously. New version added → oldest deprecated and removed in the next release after its end-of-support date. Going outside the matrix may work but is not validated by CI — frequent source of obscure boot/runtime failures.

name: firecracker.security.host-kernel-matrix
observations: Host kernel matrix: Currently supported host kernels: v5.10 (since v1.0.0, end-of-support 2024-01-31) and v6.1 (since v1.5.0, end-of-support 2025-10-12). 4K page size only. Other kernels may run but are unvalidated.

name: firecracker.security.guest-kernel-matrix
observations: Guest kernel matrix: Currently supported guest kernels: v5.10 (since v1.0.0, EOS 2024-01-31) and v6.1 (since v1.9.0, EOS 2026-09-02). Validation guest configs at resources/guest_configs/ in the repo. Microvm-specific kernels are vended by Amazon Linux at github.com/amazonlinux/linux under microvm-kernel-* tags.

name: firecracker.security.minimal-boot-config
observations: Minimal guest boot Kconfig set: Smallest guest-kernel CONFIG flags needed to boot. Initrd boot: CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD=y + (aarch64 CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO=y | x86_64 CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y). Block-device boot: CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK=y + (x86_64: CONFIG_ACPI=y, CONFIG_PCI=y, CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y). Optional console: CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE=y + CONFIG_PRINTK=y.

name: firecracker.security.acpi-vs-mptable-boot
observations: ACPI vs MPTable boot transition: x86_64 only. Firecracker historically used MPTable + virtio-mmio.cmdline kernel-param hack to enumerate devices. Modern path: ACPI (CONFIG_ACPI=y, CONFIG_PCI=y in guest) supersedes both. Firecracker still supports legacy mode for back-compat — but if the guest kernel has BOTH enabled, devices are enumerated TWICE and the second init fails (harmless dmesg warnings; devices still work).

name: firecracker.security.pci-transport-option
observations: VirtIO over PCI (--enable-pci): x86_64 optional. --enable-pci flag at firecracker startup switches all VirtIO devices to PCI transport (vs default MMIO). Higher throughput + lower latency per device. Requires PCI-enabled guest kernel + REMOVING `pci=off` from boot_args (Firecracker auto-adds it when PCI is disabled).

name: firecracker.security.default-boot-args
observations: Default kernel boot args: Default boot_args: `reboot=k panic=1 nomodule 8250.nr_uarts=0 i8042.noaux i8042.nomux i8042.dumbkbd swiotlb=noforce`. Each flag tuned for fast boot or for the i8042-driven shutdown path. + `pci=off` appended unless --enable-pci. User can override entirely via /boot-source.boot_args.

name: firecracker.security.snapshot-cross-kernel
observations: Snapshot compatibility across kernel versions: Snapshot save and restore hosts must agree on enough kernel features for the snapshot's encoded device/CPU state to be replayable. Cross-kernel-version restore is best-effort — see fc-docs-snapshot-support 'Snapshot compatibility across kernel versions' section. Plan production deployments to use the same host kernel.

name: firecracker.security.security-md-disclosure
observations: SECURITY.md disclosure policy: Firecracker's responsible-disclosure policy. Vulnerability reports go to firecracker-security@amazon.com (NOT public GitHub issues). Disclosure timeline aligns with AWS-wide policy. Reproducers and CVE assignment handled by the maintainer team.

name: firecracker.networking.tap-backend
observations: TAP-device backend: Firecracker's only network backend is a Linux TUN/TAP device — no multi-queue support. Each VirtIO/net device requires a corresponding TAP on the host (created by orchestrator before PUT /network-interfaces). Firecracker reads/writes ethernet frames directly on the TAP fd. The TAP IP and the guest IP must NOT be in the same subnet as the host.

name: firecracker.networking.no-multi-queue
observations: No TAP multi-queue support: Firecracker uses single-queue TAP only. For high-throughput workloads, this is a per-microVM bottleneck — multi-queue (IFF_MULTI_QUEUE) is not implemented. Workaround for fan-out: more microVMs vs more queues per microVM.

name: firecracker.networking.nat-routing-pattern
observations: NAT-based routing pattern: Default network setup: host masquerades guest packets via nftables/iptables-nft. Simple, but the microVM is invisible to the LAN. Required: ip_forward=1 on host, masquerade rule on POSTROUTING chain (oifname eth0 ip saddr <guest-IP>), forward-accept rule from tap0 to eth0. Suitable for outbound-only workloads.

name: firecracker.networking.bridge-routing-pattern
observations: Bridge-based routing pattern: Alternative: attach TAPs to a Linux bridge that's slaved to the physical NIC. MicroVMs become visible on the LAN with their own IPs. Higher overhead than NAT but allows inbound connections without DNAT rules. Documented in fc-docs-network-setup 'Advanced: Bridge-based routing'.

name: firecracker.networking.namespaced-nat-clones
observations: Namespaced NAT for clones: Each microVM (typically a snapshot clone) lives in its own network namespace with its own TAP and its own NAT rules. Sacrifices some performance vs flat NAT but lets multiple clones of the SAME snapshot run simultaneously without IP/MAC collision. Documented in fc-docs-snapshot-network-clones.

name: firecracker.networking.iface-id-internal
observations: iface_id is Firecracker-internal: The iface_id used in PUT /network-interfaces is for Firecracker management only. The guest names the interface itself (typically eth0, eth1...). Init order across multiple interfaces is not guaranteed by Firecracker, though most kernels/distros respect API-call order in practice.

name: firecracker.networking.guest-mac-deterministic-pattern
observations: Deterministic guest MAC pattern (06:00:AC:10:00:02): If using the default-rootfs getting-started flow, the last 4 bytes of guest_mac encode the guest IP — `06:00:AC:10:00:02` ↔ 172.16.0.2 (AC.10 = 172.16). Lets simple init scripts derive their IP from the assigned MAC. Optional convention; Firecracker generates a random MAC if guest_mac is omitted.

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-tightly-coupled-to-iface
observations: MMDS coupling to network interface(s): MMDS isn't a separate network device — it intercepts packets destined for its IP on a specific configured network interface. PUT /mmds/config requires a network_interfaces[] list naming the interfaces that may forward MMDS-destined packets. Without at least one configured interface, MMDS returns 400.

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-default-ip
observations: Default MMDS IPv4 (169.254.169.254): MMDS defaults to 169.254.169.254 — link-local — matching EC2 IMDS for cloud-init compatibility. Custom IPs supported via /mmds/config.ipv4_address. Guest must have a route: `ip route add 169.254.169.254 dev eth0`.

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-v1-vs-v2
observations: MMDS V1 (deprecated) vs V2: V1: simple GET; deprecated, will be removed in next major version. V2: session-token-required (PUT /latest/api/token to mint, then GET with X-metadata-token header). V2 mimics IMDSv2 — defends against SSRF where a guest workload proxies an attacker URL to MMDS. V1 still answers without token (with mmds.rx_invalid_token / mmds.rx_no_token metrics tracking migration readiness).

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-token-ttl
observations: MMDS V2 token TTL: V2 token TTL is set via X-metadata-token-ttl-seconds (or X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds) header. Range: 1..21600 (1 second to 6 hours). Token expires after the TTL — guest must mint a new one. PUT requests minting tokens cannot include X-Forwarded-For (defends against header-injection attacks).

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-snapshot-non-persist
observations: MMDS data store NOT persisted across snapshots: Intentional: the MMDS payload often contains VM-specific identifiers (instance-id, public keys) that should NOT cross to clones. Snapshot persists MMDS *configuration* (version, network_interfaces, ipv4_address) but not *data*. Orchestrator must reseed metadata after snapshot restore.

name: firecracker.networking.mmds-imds-compat-mode
observations: imds_compat output format: PUT /mmds/config with imds_compat=true forces all responses to use AWS IMDS plain-text format regardless of Accept header. Lets EC2-IMDS-targeted guest code (cloud-init, instance-metadata library) work unmodified against Firecracker MMDS. Without imds_compat, MMDS uses Accept header negotiation: application/json → JSON, plain/text or none → IMDS format.

name: firecracker.networking.token-bucket-rate-limit
observations: Per-direction token-bucket rate limiting: Each network interface supports independent rx_rate_limiter and tx_rate_limiter. Each is a token bucket: bandwidth bucket (bytes) + ops bucket (packets), each with size + refill_time + optional one_time_burst. PATCH at runtime updates limiters on a live interface. Defense against noisy-neighbor microVMs in shared-host deployments.

name: firecracker.networking.network-perf-considerations
observations: Network performance considerations: Per fc-docs-network-perf: VirtIO/net throughput limited by single-queue TAP, userspace packet copy from TAP fd to guest ring buffer (and vice versa), no zero-copy / no offload pass-through. Hot path: TAP read → epoll → VMM thread copy → VirtIO ring → KVM_IRQFD wakeup. Tunables: rate-limiter sizing, host TAP send queue length (txqueuelen), and choice of NAT vs bridge.

name: firecracker.vsock.virtio-vsock-device
observations: VirtIO/vsock device: Firecracker's emulated VirtIO-vsock device. Single-instance per microVM. Mediates between AF_UNIX sockets on the host and AF_VSOCK sockets in the guest. Bypasses vhost-vsock kernel code on the host (vhost-style I/O is implemented in the Firecracker userspace VMM, not the kernel) — but still requires vhost-vsock as a host kernel module (CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK=m).

name: firecracker.vsock.cid-port-addressing
observations: CID/port addressing: AF_VSOCK addresses guest endpoints by (CID, port). Reserved CIDs: 0=Hypervisor, 1=Local, 2=Host. Guest CID is configurable via PUT /vsock.guest_cid (must be ≥3). Ports are 32-bit; same conventions as TCP/UDP. Inside the guest, /dev/vsock exposes the standard Linux vsock API.

name: firecracker.vsock.uds-multiplexing
observations: UDS multiplexing pattern: All vsock traffic for a microVM funnels through a single host-side AF_UNIX socket (the configured uds_path). Per-port channels are multiplexed: host-initiated uses an in-band 'CONNECT <port>\n' command; guest-initiated maps to per-port AF_UNIX sockets at <uds_path>_<port>. Lets one Firecracker process expose unbounded vsock channels via a single socket.

name: firecracker.vsock.host-initiated-handshake
observations:
Host-initiated CONNECT/OK handshake: Sequence: host connects to UDS at uds_path → sends 'CONNECT <port>
' (port is decimal, 
 is ASCII 0x0A) → Firecracker forwards to the guest-side listener → on success replies 'OK <hostside-port>
'. If no guest listener, Firecracker terminates the host connection.

name: firecracker.vsock.guest-initiated-per-port-uds
observations: Guest-initiated per-port UDS pattern: Sequence: guest connects to (CID=2 host, port=N) → Firecracker tries to forward to a host-side AF_UNIX socket listening at <uds_path>_<N> → if exists, channel established; if not, VIRTIO_VSOCK_OP_RST sent back to guest (connection refused). Convention: host pre-creates listeners for each port the guest is expected to call.

name: firecracker.vsock.snapshot-reset
observations: Vsock connection reset on snapshot restore: All open vsock connections are closed across snapshot/restore. Listening sockets in the guest survive — they accept fresh connections post-resume. Orchestrators must design control-plane protocols to tolerate this (idempotent operations + reconnect logic).

name: firecracker.vsock.uds-path-override-on-restore
observations: vsock_override on snapshot restore: PUT /snapshot/load supports a vsock_override.uds_path field to remap the host UDS path on restore. Critical when running multiple clones of the same snapshot in environments without the jailer (where chroots would otherwise isolate paths) — avoids UDS-path collision between simultaneous clones.

name: firecracker.setup.production-checklist
observations: Production deployment checklist (high-level): Per fc-docs-prod-host-setup, defense-in-depth requires: regularly patched host+guest kernels and microcode (per ALAS or distro security advisories); jailer (always); seccomp default filters (never --no-seccomp in prod); SMT off; KSM off; swap off; Rowhammer-mitigated memory (DDR4 TRR + ECC); per-tenant Firecracker process isolation (one tenant per process).

name: firecracker.setup.unprivileged-uid-per-microvm
observations: Per-microVM unique uid/gid pattern: Recommended: each Firecracker microVM runs as its OWN uid/gid (not a shared 'firecracker' user). Adds a layer of cross-microVM filesystem-permission isolation in case one jail is broken out of. Orchestrator allocates uid/gid pool.

name: firecracker.setup.serial-device-prod-anti-pattern
observations: Serial device in production (anti-pattern): 8250 serial device is tied to Firecracker stdout (or non-daemonized jailer stdout). Guest controls writes — unbounded data can fill host storage. Recommendations: (a) use serial rate-limiter + bounded storage (logrotate, journald); (b) redirect to /dev/null; (c) DISABLE in guest kernel via `8250.nr_uarts=0` boot arg. Caveat: guest can re-enable the device at runtime even if disabled at boot.

name: firecracker.setup.signal-handler-deadlock-risk
observations: Custom signal handler deadlock (logging/metrics race): Firecracker's SIGSEGV/SIGSYS/etc. handlers log + flush metrics — these are NOT async-signal-safe (use locks). Rare race: handler intercepts signal on a thread already holding the log/metrics lock → deadlock → unresponsive thread. NO security impact. Mitigation: run an overwatcher process that periodically SIGKILLs unresponsive Firecracker processes.

name: firecracker.setup.kvm-pit-cpu-overhead
observations: kvm-pit kernel-thread CPU overhead (x86): x86 KVM-PIT (Programmable Interval Timer) kernel thread services guest timer interrupts. Spawned by KVM after guest start — is in the ROOT cgroup by default, so its CPU usage isn't accounted to the microVM. Mitigations: (1) external agent moves `kvm-pit/<fc-pid>` thread into the microVM's cgroup; (2) raise modprobe kvm min_timer_period_us to reduce timer event rate (also affects APIC timer — workload-test before deploying).

name: firecracker.setup.smt-off-side-channel
observations: Disable SMT for tenant separation: Simultaneous Multi-Threading (Hyperthreading) is a precondition for many speculation-class side channels (Spectre variants, MDS). For tenant-separation scenarios, disable SMT host-side via BIOS/UEFI or `nosmt` boot arg. Trades performance for isolation.

name: firecracker.setup.ksm-off-side-channel
observations: Disable Kernel Samepage Merging (KSM): KSM dedupes identical memory pages across processes — known precondition for memory-deduplication side channels. Disable via /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run=0. Mandatory for multi-tenant Firecracker hosts.

name: firecracker.setup.swap-off-data-remanence
observations: Disable swap (data remanence): Memory pressure → swap-out → guest memory contents written to host disk → data remanence risk on disk reuse. Recommendation: disable swap entirely OR use secure (encrypted) swap. Verify with `grep -q /dev /proc/swaps && echo bad || echo OK`.

name: firecracker.setup.rowhammer-trr-ecc-memory
observations: Use Rowhammer-mitigated memory: Rowhammer is a DRAM side channel. Recommended hardware: DDR4 with Target Row Refresh (TRR) AND error-correcting code (ECC). Pseudo-TRR for DDR3 is partial mitigation (perf cost). Hardware procurement decision — not configurable at runtime.

name: firecracker.setup.spectre-meltdown-checker
observations: spectre-meltdown-checker verification: Open-source script (github.com/speed47/spectre-meltdown-checker) that audits the host's protections against speculation side channels. Run as part of deployment validation; recheck after kernel/microcode updates.

name: firecracker.setup.arm-cntpct-counter-reset
observations: ARM CNTPCT counter reset on VM boot: ARM only. Firecracker resets the guest's physical timer counter on VM boot (prevents leaking host time). Requires KVM_CAP_COUNTER_OFFSET (kernel ≥6.4). Older kernels: counter passes through from host — minor info leak.

name: firecracker.setup.host-kernel-quiet-loglevel
observations: Host kernel: `quiet loglevel=1` recommendation: Recommended host kernel cmdline addition: `quiet loglevel=1`. Reduces messages to serial console — concrete example from docs: adding `console=ttyAMA0` to host kernel cmdline degraded snapshot restore time from 3ms → 8.5ms on aarch64 because TAP-creation generated host kernel logs that were slow to write.

name: firecracker.setup.rootfs-build-pattern
observations: Rootfs build pattern (ext4 image): Firecracker rootfs is a host file (typically ext4) presented to the guest as /dev/vda via VirtIO/block. Build steps (per fc-docs-rootfs-kernel): (1) dd a sparse ext4 image; (2) mkfs.ext4; (3) loopmount; (4) populate with debootstrap or alpine-make-rootfs or similar; (5) install init scripts; (6) umount. The image is the host's view; the guest sees a regular block device.

name: firecracker.setup.kernel-build-vmlinux
observations: Guest kernel build (vmlinux/vmlinuz): Guest kernel is built from upstream Linux (or Amazon Linux microvm-kernel) with Firecracker-relevant Kconfig set. Output: uncompressed ELF (x86_64) or PE (aarch64). Firecracker loads this directly — no bootloader. Reference Kconfigs at resources/guest_configs/ in the FC repo.

name: ecs.agent.amazon-ecs-agent
observations: Amazon ECS Container Agent: Open-source Go binary that runs on each EC2 container instance. Connects to the ECS service via the ACS (Agent Communication Service) protocol; receives task placement instructions; executes tasks via the local Docker daemon (or containerd); reports task state. Source: github.com/aws/amazon-ecs-agent (Apache 2.0).

name: ecs.agent.amazon-ecs-init
observations: amazon-ecs-init (RPM/systemd integration): RPM that supervises the ECS agent on Amazon Linux instances. Originally Upstart; now systemd. Reads /etc/ecs/ecs.config and passes its contents as env vars to the agent container. Logs at /var/log/ecs/ecs-init.log; agent logs at /var/log/ecs/ecs-agent.log. Source: github.com/aws/amazon-ecs-init.

name: ecs.agent.acs-protocol
observations: ACS (Agent Communication Service) protocol: WebSocket-based bidirectional protocol between the agent and the ECS service control plane. Agent maintains a persistent connection to receive RunTask / StopTask payloads and pushes state-change events (task started, container stopped, task transitioned). Disconnects trigger reconnect with backoff; prolonged disconnect is the most common 'agent disconnected' alert.

name: ecs.agent.introspection-api
observations: Agent Introspection API (port 51678): HTTP API the agent exposes on localhost:51678 for on-instance debugging. Endpoints: /v1/metadata (container instance ID, cluster, agent version), /v1/tasks (all tasks), /v1/tasks?taskarn=<arn> (specific task), /v1/tasks?dockerid=<id> (task by container ID), /license. Bound to localhost only by default; ecs-init's iptables rule blocks off-host access.

name: ecs.agent.task-metadata-endpoint
observations: Task Metadata Endpoint (v3/v4): Per-container HTTP API at $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI / $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 (env vars injected into each container). Replaces the older /v1 introspection-API for in-container metadata access. v4 adds task tags + container-stats endpoints. Combined with task-iam-role credentials endpoint at 169.254.170.2.

name: ecs.agent.iam-roles-for-tasks
observations: IAM Roles for Tasks (TaskRoleArn): Per-task IAM credentials served by the agent on 169.254.170.2/v2/credentials/<credential-id>. Each task gets short-lived AWS credentials scoped to the task's IAM role — separate from the container instance's role. Requires ECS_ENABLE_TASK_IAM_ROLE=true on the agent and a CredentialsId injected into the task via env. Pairs with awsvpc network mode for stronger isolation.

name: ecs.agent.container-instance-state-machine
observations: Container instance state machine (ACTIVE → DRAINING → INACTIVE): ACTIVE: instance accepts new task placements. DRAINING: stops accepting new tasks; replaces service-managed tasks; standalone tasks continue. INACTIVE: deregistered. DRAINING is the safe path for AMI updates / scale-in — combined with deployment-circuit-breaker on services, this gives zero-impact rotation.

name: ecs.agent.docker-vs-containerd
observations: Docker vs containerd backends: Agent historically required Docker daemon. Newer agent versions support containerd directly (no Docker shim). Backend selected via ECS_DOCKER_GRAPH_PATH and runtime-detection. ECS-Optimized AMI 2023+ ships containerd-capable agent. DOCKER_HOST env var (Linux: unix:///var/run/docker.sock; Windows: npipe).

name: ecs.agent.image-pull-behavior
observations: Image pull behavior policy: ECS_IMAGE_PULL_BEHAVIOR controls per-task image fetching. default: pull remote, fall back to cache on failure. always: pull remote, fail task if pull fails. once: pull only if not cached. prefer-cached: use cache if present, pull only if absent. The 'always' setting is critical for security but trades startup latency.

name: ecs.agent.image-cleanup
observations: Automated image cleanup: Agent reaps unused container images periodically. ECS_DISABLE_IMAGE_CLEANUP toggle; ECS_IMAGE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL period; ECS_IMAGE_MINIMUM_CLEANUP_AGE / NON_ECS_IMAGE_MINIMUM_CLEANUP_AGE thresholds; ECS_NUM_IMAGES_DELETE_PER_CYCLE per-cycle cap. Untracked-image cleanup gated by ECS_ENABLE_UNTRACKED_IMAGE_CLEANUP. Common foot-gun: aggressive cleanup races with task scheduler.

name: ecs.agent.task-cleanup-wait
observations: Task cleanup wait (ECS_ENGINE_TASK_CLEANUP_WAIT_DURATION): After a task stops, agent keeps the Docker containers around for this duration so logs and exit-code can be collected. Default 3h. Lower for high-churn instances; raise for log-collection workflows. JITTER variant adds randomization to avoid thundering-herd cleanup.

name: ecs.agent.checkpoint-state
observations: Agent state checkpointing: Agent persists task state to disk (ECS_DATADIR, default /data/) so it survives restarts. ECS_CHECKPOINT toggle. Bind-mounted from $ECS_HOST_DATA_DIR/data on the host into $ECS_DATADIR in the agent container. Loss of this state forces re-discovery of running tasks.

name: ecs.agent.spot-instance-draining
observations: Spot Instance draining: When ECS_ENABLE_SPOT_INSTANCE_DRAINING=true and the instance receives a Spot interruption notice (2-minute warning), agent automatically transitions the instance to DRAINING. Service-managed tasks get gracefully replaced on other capacity. Strongly recommended for any Spot-backed ECS cluster.

name: ecs.agent.task-iam-network-host
observations: Task IAM with host-mode networking: ECS_ENABLE_TASK_IAM_ROLE_NETWORK_HOST gates task-IAM-role injection for tasks using `host` network mode (where 169.254.170.2 routing requires special iptables rules). awsvpc-mode tasks get task-IAM by default; host-mode tasks need this opt-in.

name: ecs.agent.cni-plugins
observations: ECS CNI plugins: Agent invokes CNI plugins (vendored at ECS_CNI_PLUGINS_PATH, default /amazon-ecs-cni-plugins) to set up awsvpc-mode networking — attaches per-task ENI to the instance, configures veth pairs, programs routing. Failures here surface as 'CannotCreateContainerError: failed to setup task network'.

name: ecs.agent.high-density-eni
observations: High-density ENI (HDE): ECS_ENABLE_HIGH_DENSITY_ENI=true (default) lets the agent attach more tasks per instance than the EC2 ENI limit allows by using ENI trunking. Requires Nitro instance + IAM permission. Without HDE, awsvpc task density is capped at the per-instance ENI limit (e.g., 4 on m5.large).

name: ecs.agent.awsvpc-block-imds
observations: Block IMDS from awsvpc tasks: ECS_AWSVPC_BLOCK_IMDS=true makes awsvpc-mode tasks unable to reach 169.254.169.254 (instance metadata). Defends against SSRF-leak of the container instance role. Recommended for multi-tenant clusters; not enabled by default.

name: ecs.agent.container-metadata-file
observations: Container metadata file: ECS_ENABLE_CONTAINER_METADATA=true makes the agent write a per-container JSON metadata file inside each container; path injected as $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_FILE. Older alternative to the Task Metadata Endpoint (TMDS); kept for backward compat.

name: ecs.agent.task-cpu-mem-limit
observations: Task-level cgroup CPU+memory limit: ECS_ENABLE_TASK_CPU_MEM_LIMIT=true (default on Linux) creates a per-task cgroup that bounds total CPU+memory across the task's containers. Not just per-container — sum of containers can't exceed task-level cap. ECS_CGROUP_CPU_PERIOD tunes the CFS period.

name: ecs.agent.localhost-traffic-filter
observations: Localhost traffic filter (iptables): ecs-init installs an iptables rule that drops non-local packets to 127.0.0.0/8 not part of an existing forwarded connection. Defends against off-instance access to introspection (51678) + task-credentials endpoints. ECS_SKIP_LOCALHOST_TRAFFIC_FILTER=true disables (NOT recommended).

name: ecs.agent.offhost-introspection-block
observations: Off-host introspection block: ecs-init installs an iptables rule blocking the introspection port (51678) from off-host or from awsvpc-mode containers. Combined with task-credentials endpoint protection. Toggle via ECS_ALLOW_OFFHOST_INTROSPECTION_ACCESS=true (NOT recommended).

name: ecs.agent.pid-namespace-host
observations: Agent PID-namespace-host mode (SELinux): ECS_AGENT_PID_NAMESPACE_HOST=true makes ecs-init start the agent container with --pid=host instead of an isolated PID namespace. Required when SELinux enforcing + Docker SELinux policy enabled. Available in agent ≥1.94.0. Disables ECS Exec, EBS-attach, Service Connect, FireLens — significant feature loss.

name: ecs.agent.reserved-ports
observations: Reserved ports list: Ports the agent excludes from task placement. ECS_RESERVED_PORTS default Linux: [22, 2375, 2376, 51678, 51679] (SSH + Docker daemon + ECS introspection); Windows adds RDP + WinRM. ECS_RESERVED_PORTS_UDP for UDP ports (e.g. [53, 123]).

name: ecs.agent.metrics-poll-vs-stream
observations: Metrics poll vs stream: ECS_POLL_METRICS=true switches the agent from streaming docker stats to polling. Reduces dockerd/containerd CPU usage on dense instances at the cost of slightly stale metrics. ECS_POLLING_METRICS_WAIT_DURATION (5-20s, default 10s) tunes interval. Recommended <18s to avoid memory-reservation metric instability.

name: ecs.agent.engine-auth
observations: Engine auth (private registry credentials): ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_TYPE + ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA store Docker registry credentials on the instance for pulling private images. Two formats: 'docker' (raw username/password) or 'dockercfg' (matches ~/.docker/config.json shape). Cluster-wide alternative: use repositoryCredentials on the task definition with a Secrets Manager ARN.

name: ecs.task-defs.task-definition
observations: Task Definition: Versioned, immutable JSON manifest describing how a task is built. Identified by family + revision (e.g., my-app:7). Bundles container definitions, volumes, network mode, IAM roles, runtime platform, capacity requirements. RegisterTaskDefinition creates a new revision; previous revisions remain referenceable.

name: ecs.task-defs.task-family-revision
observations: Task family + revision: family is the logical name (a string); revision is an auto-incremented integer per family (1, 2, 3…). Services pin to either family:revision (immutable) or family alone (latest ACTIVE revision). Deregistered revisions enter INACTIVE but stay queryable.

name: ecs.task-defs.container-definition
observations: Container Definition: Per-container spec inside a task: name, image, resources, env, ports, mounts, logging, health, security. A task can have 1-10 container definitions; the first essential container's exit terminates the task.

name: ecs.task-defs.essential-flag
observations: essential flag (sidecar semantics): Per-container: essential=true means task stops when this container exits; essential=false (sidecar pattern) means container exit doesn't stop the task. At least one container must be essential. Common usage: app=essential, log-router/proxy=non-essential.

name: ecs.task-defs.network-modes
observations: Task network modes (awsvpc/bridge/host/none): awsvpc: per-task ENI with own IP+SG (Fargate REQUIRES this; EC2 supports). bridge: shared docker0 bridge (EC2 default; uses port-mappings). host: shares host network namespace (no isolation; highest perf). none: no networking. Choice constrains IAM-for-tasks behavior + service-discovery + port-conflict semantics.

name: ecs.task-defs.task-role-vs-execution-role
observations: taskRoleArn vs executionRoleArn: executionRoleArn: agent's perms to RUN the task (pull from ECR, write to CloudWatch Logs, fetch Secrets/SSM, attach EFS). taskRoleArn: container's runtime perms (the AWS APIs the app code calls). These MUST be separate — execution role is infrastructure; task role is application.

name: ecs.task-defs.requires-compatibilities
observations: requiresCompatibilities: Pre-flight validator: FARGATE, EC2, EXTERNAL (ECS Anywhere). Validates the task def against the launch type's restrictions (e.g., FARGATE forbids privileged containers, requires awsvpc). Caller exception if mismatch.

name: ecs.task-defs.fargate-cpu-memory-matrix
observations: Fargate CPU/memory matrix: Fargate restricts task-level cpu+memory to discrete combinations: 256/.25vCPU → 512MiB/1GB/2GB; 512 → 1-4GB; 1024 → 2-8GB; 2048 → 4-16GB (1GB steps); 4096 → 8-30GB; 8192 → 16-60GB (4GB steps, Linux platform 1.4.0+); 16384 → 32-120GB (8GB steps, Linux 1.4.0+). Mismatched combos fail at RegisterTaskDefinition.

name: ecs.task-defs.ephemeral-storage
observations: ephemeralStorage (Fargate): Fargate-only. Per-task scratch disk size in GiB, range 21-200 (default 20). Mounted into all containers. EC2 launch type uses host disk + dockerPathOnHost without this field.

name: ecs.task-defs.runtime-platform
observations: runtimePlatform (OS family + CPU arch): Combines operatingSystemFamily (LINUX, WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_FULL/CORE, WINDOWS_SERVER_2022_FULL/CORE, WINDOWS_SERVER_2025_FULL/CORE) + cpuArchitecture (X86_64, ARM64). Required on Fargate. Service.platformFamily must match for service-managed tasks.

name: ecs.task-defs.volumes-types
observations: Volume types (host, efsVolumeConfiguration, fsxWindowsFileServer, dockerVolumeConfiguration, configuredAtLaunch): Task-level volumes attached to one or more containers via mountPoints. Types: host (host bind-mount), dockerVolumeConfiguration (named Docker volume), efsVolumeConfiguration (EFS network mount), fsxWindowsFileServerVolumeConfiguration (FSx for Windows), configuredAtLaunch (EBS attach, Fargate platform 1.4+).

name: ecs.task-defs.mount-point
observations: mountPoint (volume → container binding): Per-container array of {sourceVolume, containerPath, readOnly}. Binds a task-level volume into a specific in-container path. sourceVolume must match a name in task-level volumes[].

name: ecs.task-defs.depends-on
observations: Container dependsOn (ordering): Per-container array of {containerName, condition}. Conditions: START (depended-on container started), COMPLETE (exited 0), SUCCESS (exited 0 — alias), HEALTHY (passed healthCheck). Lets you express init-container patterns + sidecar startup ordering.

name: ecs.task-defs.health-check
observations: Container healthCheck: Per-container Docker HEALTHCHECK semantics: command (CMD-SHELL or CMD list), interval (5-300s, default 30s), timeout (2-60s, default 5s), retries (1-10, default 3), startPeriod (0-300s, grace before failures count). Combined with dependsOn HEALTHY for inter-container ordering.

name: ecs.task-defs.log-configuration
observations: logConfiguration (drivers + options + secrets): Per-container logDriver (awslogs, awsfirelens, splunk, fluentd, gelf, journald, json-file, syslog) + options (driver-specific KV) + secretOptions (driver options sourced from Secrets Manager / SSM). Available drivers gated by ECS_AVAILABLE_LOGGING_DRIVERS on the agent.

name: ecs.task-defs.linux-parameters
observations: linuxParameters (capabilities, devices, tmpfs, sharedMemorySize, swappiness): Per-container Linux-specific overrides: capabilities.add[]/.drop[] (ALL, CHOWN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN, etc.), devices (host device passthrough), initProcessEnabled (tini PID 1), maxSwap, sharedMemorySize (MB), swappiness, tmpfs[].

name: ecs.task-defs.firelens-configuration
observations: firelensConfiguration (log routing): Per-container Fluent Bit / Fluentd-based log routing. type=fluentbit|fluentd; options={enable-ecs-log-metadata, config-file-type, config-file-value}. Enables flexible multi-destination log shipping (e.g., CloudWatch + Datadog + S3 from one container).

name: ecs.task-defs.service-definition
observations: Service Definition: Long-lived task-runner. Pins a task definition + desiredCount + launch type + load balancer + service discovery + capacity provider strategy + deployment configuration. Maintains desiredCount of running tasks via task-replacement on failure.

name: ecs.launch-types.cluster
observations: ECS Cluster: Logical grouping of tasks/services + the capacity infrastructure they run on. Default cluster auto-created; production usage typically per-environment (prod/staging/dev) or per-team. Cluster scopes IAM, capacity-provider strategies, and account-settings opt-ins.

name: ecs.launch-types.fargate
observations: Fargate launch type: Serverless — AWS owns the underlying compute. Pay per task vCPU+memory+ephemeralStorage per second. Networking REQUIRES awsvpc. Restrictions: no privileged containers, no host networking, restricted sysctls, restricted Linux capabilities, no host volumes (only EFS/FSx + ephemeralStorage). Per Cognition's NSDI-paper analog: each Fargate task runs in its own Firecracker microVM (cross-domain link).

name: ecs.launch-types.fargate-spot
observations: Fargate Spot: Spot-priced Fargate. ~70% discount vs on-demand. AWS may interrupt with a SIGTERM-then-2-minute-warning. Use via capacityProviderStrategy mixing FARGATE + FARGATE_SPOT (e.g. base=2 on FARGATE, weight 1:9 FARGATE:FARGATE_SPOT). Best for fault-tolerant async workloads.

name: ecs.launch-types.ec2-launch-type
observations: EC2 launch type: User manages container instances (EC2 instances running ECS-optimized AMI + amazon-ecs-agent). Required for: privileged containers, host network mode, custom AMIs, GPU/Inferentia/Trainium hardware, capacity reservations, .metal instances, ECS Anywhere. Pay for EC2 instances regardless of task density.

name: ecs.launch-types.external-launch-type
observations: External launch type (ECS Anywhere): ECS orchestration on customer-managed on-prem or other-cloud machines. Each external instance runs amazon-ecs-agent + SSM Agent + activation token. Limitations: no awsvpc network mode, no Service Connect, no Capacity Providers (manage capacity yourself).

name: ecs.launch-types.managed-instances
observations: ECS Managed Instances: AWS fully manages the underlying EC2 instances (provisioning, patching, scaling) while preserving more control than Fargate (e.g., GPU support, custom AMIs from a curated set). Newer (mid-2024) middle option between Fargate and EC2-launch-type. Promoted as the recommended option for most clusters.

name: ecs.launch-types.capacity-provider
observations: Capacity Provider: Decouples 'where do tasks run' from 'what launch type are they'. Built-in: FARGATE, FARGATE_SPOT. EC2: bind to an ASG (Auto Scaling Group) — managedScaling enables ECS to drive ASG up/down based on task demand. Cluster has a default strategy; services + run-task can override.

name: ecs.launch-types.managed-scaling
observations: Managed Scaling (CP-driven ASG): ECS publishes a CloudWatch metric (CapacityProviderReservation = active-tasks / target-capacity * 100) that the ASG's TargetTrackingScalingPolicy reacts to. targetCapacity (default 100%) lets the cluster keep slack for fast scale-out. instanceWarmupPeriod governs how long until a new instance counts as 'available'.

name: ecs.launch-types.cp-strategy-base-weight
