observations: Capacity Provider strategy (base + weight): {capacityProvider, weight, base}. base = first N tasks placed on this CP unconditionally. weight = ratio for tasks beyond base. e.g. [{cp:FARGATE,base:2,weight:1},{cp:FARGATE_SPOT,base:0,weight:9}] → first 2 tasks on FARGATE, then 1:9 split. Enables cost-tier mixing.

name: ecs.launch-types.ecs-optimized-ami-family
observations: ECS-optimized AMI family: AMI variants pre-loaded with Docker/containerd + amazon-ecs-agent + ecs-init. Variants: AL2023 (recommended; long-term-support through 2028), AL2 kernel 5.10 (EOL 2026-06-30), AL2023 arm64 (Graviton), AL2023 GPU (NVIDIA + Docker GPU runtime), AL2023 Neuron (Inferentia/Trainium). 30 GiB root volume default.

name: ecs.launch-types.ami-via-ssm-parameter
observations: AMI ID via SSM Parameter Store: Latest ECS-optimized AMI ID is published as an SSM parameter (/aws/service/ecs/optimized-ami/<variant>/recommended/image_id). CloudFormation references this dynamic parameter so each stack-update picks up the newest AMI without code change. Same pattern works in Terraform via aws_ssm_parameter.

name: ecs.launch-types.ami-deprecation-2yr
observations: AMI 2-year deprecation default: All ECS-Optimized AMIs are auto-marked deprecated 2 years after creation. EC2 DescribeImages returns the deprecation status. Pinning to an old AMI ID risks silent-deprecation; use the SSM parameter approach.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nitro-system
observations: AWS Nitro System: Hardware + software stack underpinning all modern EC2 instances. Components: Nitro Cards (offload network/storage I/O), local NVMe storage, Nitro Security Chip (motherboard-integrated, boot-firmware integrity), Nitro Hypervisor (lightweight KVM-derived hypervisor — only used on virtualized instance types). Bare-metal instance types skip the hypervisor while keeping all other Nitro components.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nitro-hypervisor
observations: Nitro Hypervisor: Lightweight hypervisor managing memory + CPU allocation on virtualized Nitro EC2 instances. AWS-internal; not user-accessible. Indistinguishable-from-bare-metal performance for most workloads. KVM-derived. Cross-domain link: AWS Fargate Linux tasks run in Firecracker microVMs that are SEPARATE from the Nitro Hypervisor — Firecracker is the inner-VMM, Nitro is the outer-VMM (when not bare-metal).

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.bare-metal-instance
observations: Bare-Metal EC2 instance: .metal-suffix instance types (i3.metal, m5.metal, m5d.metal, r5.metal, z1d.metal, c5.metal, m6i.metal, m7i.metal, etc.). EC2 instance types that expose the underlying hardware directly — no Nitro Hypervisor between guest and CPU. Boot is slower (up to 20 minutes initial verification of all hardware/firmware). Use cases: workloads requiring Intel VT (nested KVM, Firecracker host); license-bound software needing non-virtualized environment (Oracle, ESXi); custom hypervisors.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nitro-security-chip
observations: Nitro Security Chip: Motherboard-integrated chip that monitors firmware + hardware on every Nitro instance, including bare-metal. Continuously verifies that firmware hasn't been tampered with. Foundation of AWS's hardware-supply-chain integrity claim.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nitro-card
observations: Nitro Card: PCIe cards that offload network/storage I/O from the host CPU. Net Nitro Card handles ENA (Elastic Network Adapter) + EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter); Storage Nitro Card handles EBS + local NVMe.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nitro-version-matrix
observations: Nitro version matrix (v2-v6): Cumulative feature stack. v2: ENA enhanced networking + Traffic Mirroring. v3: 100 Gbps/card + encryption-in-transit. v4: 100/170 Gbps/card + ENA Express + RDMA read/write on select types. v5: 200 Gbps/card. v6: 400 Gbps/card + reduced default TCP idle timeout (432000s → 350s). New networking features added cumulatively.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.bare-metal-boot-time
observations: Bare-metal boot time (~20 min): Bare-metal launches go through full hardware/firmware verification — instance can take 20+ min from 'running' state to network-reachable. Plan AMI rotations + auto-scaling around this. Subsequent boots from cache may be faster.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.nested-kvm-on-bare-metal
observations: Nested KVM (Firecracker host): Bare-metal instances expose Intel VT-x / AMD-V to the guest, enabling nested virtualization. Critical for running KVM-based workloads (e.g., Firecracker as the inner-VMM). The C8i/M8i/R8i Nitro v6 instances ALSO support nested-virt without being bare-metal — but pay ~10% CPU overhead. Pure bare-metal has no nested-virt tax.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.use-case-licensing
observations: Bare-metal use case: licensing: Some commercial software (Oracle, Microsoft) prohibits or extra-charges for virtualized environments. Bare-metal EC2 lets enterprises run such software on AWS without licensing penalty.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.use-case-perf-sensitive
observations: Bare-metal use case: hardware-perf-sensitive: Workloads that need direct access to CPU performance counters (perf, PMU events), undisturbed cache + TLB, or specialized hardware features (Intel VT for nested-virt, SGX). Examples: HFT systems, perf-research, HPC, latency-sensitive databases.

name: ecs.networking.network-mode-bridge
observations: bridge network mode (EC2 default): Containers attached to the host's docker0 bridge. Each container gets a private IP within the bridge subnet. Inbound exposed via per-container hostPort (static or ephemeral 0). Multiple tasks of the same family on one instance need different hostPorts. Default for EC2 launch type.

name: ecs.networking.network-mode-host
observations: host network mode: Container shares the host's network namespace — uses host IP directly, no port translation. Highest perf (no veth-bridge hop). DOWNSIDE: only one task per containerPort per host (port conflicts if 2+ tasks try same port). Forbidden on Fargate.

name: ecs.networking.network-mode-awsvpc
observations: awsvpc network mode: Per-task ENI (Elastic Network Interface) with own IP, own security group(s), own routing. Required for Fargate. Recommended for EC2 in production. Enables: per-task IAM credentials over 169.254.170.2 endpoint, per-task SG isolation, full VPC integration. Limited by per-instance ENI quota — see HDE/trunking for relief.

name: ecs.networking.network-mode-none
observations: none network mode: No networking at all. Loopback only inside container. Used for batch jobs that don't need network (data-processing reading from a mounted volume).

name: ecs.networking.eni-trunking
observations: ENI trunking (HDE — High Density ENI): Bypasses the per-instance ENI quota by attaching a 'trunk' ENI that sub-divides into 'branch' ENIs (one per awsvpc task). Increases task density 5-20x depending on instance type. Requires: Nitro instance + IAM perm (ec2:CreateNetworkInterfacePermission) + ECS_ENABLE_HIGH_DENSITY_ENI=true + AwsvpcTrunking opt-in via PutAccountSetting.

name: ecs.networking.task-eni-attach-detach-flow
observations: Task ENI attach/detach flow: Per-task ENI lifecycle: 1) ECS service requests EC2 to attach an ENI to the instance. 2) Agent's CNI plugins move the ENI into the task's network namespace. 3) Routes + IP configured. 4) On task stop, agent unmounts; ECS detaches. Failures here surface as 'CannotCreateContainerError: failed to setup task network'.

name: ecs.networking.task-credentials-endpoint
observations: Task credentials endpoint (169.254.170.2): Link-local IP that resolves to the agent on every task instance. Serves task-IAM-role credentials at $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI. AWS SDKs auto-discover this. Only works on awsvpc + select bridge configurations; host mode requires ECS_ENABLE_TASK_IAM_ROLE_NETWORK_HOST + iptables setup.

name: ecs.networking.task-metadata-endpoint-v3-v4
observations: Task Metadata Endpoint (TMDS) v3/v4: Per-container HTTP endpoint serving task + container metadata + container stats. Path injected as $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI (v3) and $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 (v4). v4 adds /task/stats endpoint with cgroup-derived metrics. Use this from inside containers — avoid the agent's port 51678 (host-only) and the EC2 IMDS (different scope).

name: ecs.networking.security-group-per-task
observations: Per-task Security Groups: awsvpc mode lets each task have its own SG(s) — separate from the instance's SG. Enables fine-grained network policy per workload (e.g., db-client tasks allowed to reach RDS, log-shipper tasks blocked from RDS). Configured at run-task / service-create time via networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.securityGroups[].

name: ecs.networking.assign-public-ip
observations: assignPublicIp toggle: awsvpc tasks in public subnets can get a public IP (assignPublicIp=ENABLED) or stay private (DISABLED). Required ENABLED for tasks pulling from public-internet-only registries when no NAT is available. Default DISABLED.

name: ecs.networking.service-connect
observations: ECS Service Connect: AWS-managed service-mesh layer (Envoy-based) that gives services DNS-discoverable names + automatic mTLS + telemetry. Replaces older Service Discovery (Cloud Map alone). Requires per-task sidecar; works with awsvpc mode. Cluster-level configuration.

name: ecs.networking.service-discovery-cloud-map
observations: Service Discovery (AWS Cloud Map): Older service-discovery: ECS registers task IPs in a Cloud Map namespace (private DNS namespace in Route 53). Other services DNS-resolve <service>.<namespace>. Service Connect supersedes for new clusters but Cloud Map still useful for cross-service-type discovery (Lambda + ECS + EC2).

name: ecs.troubleshooting.task-stop-reason-classes
observations: Task stoppedReason classes: DescribeTasks returns stoppedReason as a free-form string but it follows recognizable patterns: 'Essential container in task exited' (app crash), 'CannotPullContainerError' (image fetch — auth/network/missing), 'ResourceInitializationError' (CNI/EFS/Secrets failed pre-launch), 'OutOfMemoryError' (cgroup OOM), 'Task failed ELB health checks' (LB-driven kill), 'Scaling activity initiated by deployment' (scheduler intentional), 'Spot capacity not available' (Fargate Spot interruption), 'Task stopped by user'.

name: ecs.troubleshooting.cannot-pull-container-error
observations: CannotPullContainerError taxonomy: Sub-classes: (a) auth — invalid ECR token, missing repositoryCredentials, executionRoleArn lacks ecr:GetAuthorizationToken; (b) network — task subnet has no NAT/internet egress, VPC endpoint missing for ECR; (c) image-not-found — wrong tag/sha, image deleted, wrong region; (d) rate-limited — Docker Hub anonymous-pull rate exceeded, ECR throttled. Surface: stoppedReason in DescribeTasks.

name: ecs.troubleshooting.resource-initialization-error
observations: ResourceInitializationError taxonomy: Pre-launch failures attaching task resources. Sub-classes: ENI attach timeout (subnet IP exhaustion, ENI quota, awsvpc-trunking not enabled), EFS mount failed (transit-encryption mismatch, SG blocking 2049, fileSystem ID typo), Secret resolution failed (executionRole lacks secretsmanager:GetSecretValue or kms:Decrypt; bad ARN), CNI plugin failed (agent log /var/log/ecs/ecs-agent.log shows 'plugin failed').

name: ecs.troubleshooting.task-placement-failure
observations: Task placement failure (RESOURCE:* + ATTRIBUTE): Returned synchronously from RunTask (in failures[]). Reasons: 'RESOURCE:CPU' (no instance has enough free CPU), 'RESOURCE:MEMORY', 'RESOURCE:PORTS' (host network port conflict), 'RESOURCE:ENI' (awsvpc ENI quota hit), 'RESOURCE:GPU', 'ATTRIBUTE:ecs.<x>' (no instance matches placementConstraints), 'AGENT' (agent disconnected from instance).

name: ecs.troubleshooting.service-event-log-deciphering
observations: Service event log deciphering: DescribeServices returns events[] (last 100). Patterns: 'service X has reached a steady state' (good), 'service X was unable to place a task' (placement failure — see task-placement-failure), 'service X has stopped 3 running tasks' (LB unhealthy → scheduler kill), 'service X is unable to consistently start tasks successfully' (deployment circuit breaker tripped). Time-correlate with task stoppedReason for full picture.

name: docker.fm.cannot-connect-daemon
observations: `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock` [class: daemon-unavailable]

name: docker.fm.exit-137-oomkilled
observations: Container exited with code 137; `docker inspect` shows OOMKilled=true [class: resource-limit]

name: docker.fm.published-port-not-reachable
observations: `docker run -p 8080:80` succeeds but client can't reach localhost:8080 [class: networking]

name: docker.fm.disk-full-but-df-shows-free
observations: `docker pull` or `docker run` fails 'no space left on device'; `df` shows host has space [class: storage]

name: docker.fm.docker-build-cache-not-hitting
observations: `docker build` re-runs RUN steps that should be cached [class: build-cache]

name: docker.fm.container-network-host-mode-permission
observations: `docker run --network=host` requires root or fails [class: capabilities]

name: docker.fm.exit-126-not-executable
observations: Container exit code 126 [class: image-build]

name: docker.fm.exit-127-command-not-found
observations: Container exit code 127 [class: image-build]

name: docker.fm.docker-network-create-conflict
observations: `docker network create` fails with `Pool overlaps with other one on this address space` [class: networking]

name: docker.fm.userns-remap-permissions
observations: With `userns-remap` enabled, container can't write to host bind-mount; permission denied [class: namespace-isolation]

name: docker.fm.dns-not-resolving-from-container
observations: Container can't resolve DNS — `getent hosts example.com` fails inside [class: dns]

name: docker.fm.live-restore-skipped-version
observations: Container died on docker daemon major-version upgrade despite live-restore=true [class: daemon-upgrade]

name: docker.fm.compose-volume-named-vs-anon
observations: After `docker compose down -v`, named volumes preserved unintentionally OR anonymous volumes leaking [class: volume-misconfig]

name: docker.fm.exit-125-daemon-error
observations: `docker run` exits 125 immediately [class: daemon-error]

name: docker.fm.healthcheck-flapping
observations: Container repeatedly transitions between healthy/unhealthy [class: app-health]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-secret-leaked
observations: Secret accidentally baked into image (visible in `docker history`) [class: build-security]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-cache-mount-id-collision
observations: Two parallel `docker buildx build` runs of different projects corrupt each other's `RUN --mount=type=cache` content [class: build-cache]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-multi-arch-emulation-slow
observations: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` is 10-50x slower than native; build hangs or OOMs in QEMU [class: build-perf]

name: docker.fm.copy-from-stage-not-found
observations: `COPY --from=builder /out/app /app` fails: 'invalid from flag value builder: stage not found' [class: image-build]

name: docker.fm.dockerignore-too-aggressive
observations: `docker build` fails 'COPY failed: file not found in build context' but the file exists on disk [class: build-context]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-registry-cache-no-credentials
observations: `--cache-from type=registry,ref=...` ignored; build always misses cache from registry [class: build-cache]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-frontend-version-pinning
observations: Dockerfile parser feature (heredoc `<<EOF`, `--mount=type=secret`) errors as 'unknown flag' on older builders [class: build-frontend]

name: docker.fm.buildkit-output-no-load
observations: `docker buildx build -t app .` succeeds but `docker images` doesn't list `app` [class: build-output]

name: docker.fm.containerd-shim-orphaned
observations: `ps aux | grep containerd-shim` shows shims with no parent containerd; `docker ps` doesn't list the corresponding container [class: runtime-orphan]

name: docker.fm.containerd-content-store-disk-fill
observations: `/var/lib/containerd` grows beyond expected size; `docker system df` shows much less [class: storage-leak]

name: docker.fm.compose-profile-not-applied
observations: `docker compose up` doesn't start a service that has `profiles: [debug]` even with `--profile debug` [class: compose-config]

name: docker.fm.compose-healthcheck-dep-timeout
observations: `docker compose up` exits before app starts: dependency 'service X' did not pass healthcheck within timeout [class: compose-orchestration]

name: docker.fm.compose-network-default-collision
observations: Two `docker compose` projects in different dirs collide because both default to network name 'default' [class: compose-networking]

name: docker.fm.compose-restart-unless-stopped-vs-always

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.kernel-6-1-vfs-cannot-open-root
observations: Guest kernel panic on boot with 'VFS: Cannot open root device vda or unknown-block(0,0)'. vmlinux size jumped from ~29MB to ~38MB after upgrading to a 6.1 build. [class: host-kernel-config]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.kvm-exit-fail-entry-nested-virt
observations: MicroVM crashes immediately on InstanceStart with KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY when running Firecracker inside another VM (Azure VM, GCP VM, nested KVM). [class: nested-virt-unsupported]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.amd-zen-msr-freeze
observations: VM hangs after 'random: crng init done' with no exception or message on AMD Zen processors (Zen, Zen+, Zen 2). [class: host-cpu-msr-quirk]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.error-creating-kvm-object-13
observations: Firecracker exits at startup with 'Error creating Kvm object: Error(13)' (errno 13 = EACCES, permission denied). [class: permission-denied-dev-kvm]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.dev-kvm-busy-vbox-vmware
observations: Firecracker fails to start with 'Resource busy' on /dev/kvm. Another hypervisor (VMware Workstation, VirtualBox) is loaded and holds /dev/kvm exclusively. [class: exclusive-dev-kvm-contention]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.page-allocation-failure-fragmentation
observations: Host dmesg shows 'fc_vmm: page allocation failure: order:6, mode:0x140c0c0' during high-rate microVM creation. KVM cannot allocate large contiguous pages because host memory is fragmented. [class: host-memory-fragmentation]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.exit-code-12-oom
observations: Firecracker process exits immediately with exit code 12 (Out of memory). Host cannot satisfy the requested guest memory size (default 128 MiB if /machine-config not set). [class: host-oom]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.oom-despite-available-memory
observations: Guest with 16 GiB allocation OOM-killed despite host showing 9 GiB RSS / 64 GiB total. Memory accounting or page cache accumulation during heavy compilation workloads. [class: memory-accounting-or-page-cache-pressure]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.kvm-exit-shutdown-seccomp-shutdown
observations: Occasional KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN with 'bad system call (14)' (rt_sigprocmask) during VM shutdown — ~0-3 failures per 100 VMs. [class: seccomp-policy-gap]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.signal-handler-seccomp-sigaction
observations: Firecracker process exits with seccomp violation when receiving SIGSEGV/SIGBUS — Rust signal handler calls unwhitelisted sigaction syscall. [class: seccomp-policy-gap]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.panic-handler-seccomp-mremap
observations: Firecracker panic produces a secondary seccomp violation — the panic handler calls mremap (Rust unwinding) which isn't in the default filter. Original panic info is lost. [class: seccomp-policy-gap-during-panic]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.signal-handler-deadlock-on-log-lock
observations: Firecracker thread becomes unresponsive after receiving a signal (SIGSEGV/SIGSYS). Custom signal handlers write logs and flush metrics — these use locks for synchronization but are NOT async-signal-safe. Handler intercepts signal on a thread already holding the lock → deadlock. [class: signal-handler-not-async-signal-safe]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.x86-poweroff-leaves-process-alive
observations: Guest `poweroff` shuts down the OS but the Firecracker process stays alive — no ACPI PM means there's no way for the guest to signal poweroff to the VMM. [class: no-acpi-pm]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.reboot-without-reboot-k-hangs
observations: Guest `reboot` doesn't terminate the Firecracker process. Guest enters reboot loop — kernel restarts but Firecracker keeps running because i8042 reset signal isn't issued. [class: missing-reboot-k-bootarg]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.serial-console-enabled-slow-boot
observations: MicroVM boot takes 500+ ms instead of expected ≤125 ms. Serial console is enabled — every kernel printk causes a VM exit. [class: perf-misconfiguration-serial-console]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.missing-virtio-blk-cannot-mount-root
observations: Guest panics at boot with 'Cannot open root device vda' even though /drives is configured correctly. Guest kernel lacks CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK. [class: guest-kernel-config-missing]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.missing-acpi-on-x86-acpi-boot
observations: x86_64 guest kernel built with CONFIG_ACPI=n fails to enumerate VirtIO devices when Firecracker uses ACPI boot path. Devices appear missing in dmesg. [class: guest-kernel-config-missing]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.cross-arch-guest-on-host
observations: Firecracker fails to boot when guest kernel is built for a different architecture than the host (e.g., aarch64 guest on x86_64 host). [class: arch-mismatch]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.pci-off-when-pci-enabled
observations: Started Firecracker with --enable-pci but boot_args still contains pci=off. Guest disables PCI scanning and never sees the VirtIO/PCI devices Firecracker exposes. [class: config-mismatch-pci]

name: firecracker.vmm.fm.kvm-internal-error-unsalvageable
observations: vCPU thread returns KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. KVM detected an unrecoverable inconsistency (emulation impossible, simul exception delivery, unexpected delivery_event). MicroVM is unsalvageable. [class: kvm-bug-or-unrecoverable-state]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.crc-mismatch-corrupt-state-file
observations: PUT /snapshot/load fails with CRC validation error. Snapshot state file is corrupted (interrupted write, disk corruption, transport error). [class: snapshot-corruption]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.gic-version-cross-restore-fails
observations: ARM snapshot restore fails when GIC version differs between save host (e.g., GICv2) and restore host (e.g., GICv3). Device-state mismatch. [class: host-hardware-mismatch-arm-gic]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.tsx-msr-not-preserved-no-template
observations: After snapshot restore, MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL value differs from pre-snapshot. Workload that overwrote this MSR sees the host default after restore. Only happens when no CPU template is in use. [class: missing-cpu-template]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.tsc-frequency-mismatch-no-cap
observations: Snapshot restore fails (or guest time runs at wrong rate) when source and destination hosts have different TSC frequencies and KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL is unavailable. [class: host-tsc-frequency-divergence]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.cpuid-divergence-restore-fails
observations: Snapshot restore fails because CPUID exposed at save time references features unavailable on the restore host (e.g., AVX-512 absent on target). [class: host-cpu-feature-mismatch]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.virtio-block-flush-not-syncing
observations: virtio-block VIRTIO_BLK_T_FLUSH command issued by guest doesn't reach the host kernel block layer. Risk of data loss on host crash even though guest believes data is durable. [class: virtio-block-flush-propagation-bug]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.vmgenid-early-boot-restore-crash
observations: Restoring a snapshot taken during early guest kernel boot causes the resumed guest to crash. VMGenID device wasn't fully initialized when snapshot was taken. [class: snapshot-taken-too-early]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.diff-snapshot-without-track-dirty
observations: PUT /snapshot/create with snapshot_type=Diff returns 400. machine-config.track_dirty_pages was not set to true at boot, so KVM has no dirty bitmap to query. [class: missing-pre-boot-config]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.mem-file-deleted-while-vm-running
observations: Guest crashes mysteriously after restore — page faults can't be served. The MAP_PRIVATE-backed memory file was deleted from the host while the resumed VM was still running. [class: snapshot-mem-file-lifecycle-bug]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.uffd-handler-crash-leaves-vm-stuck
observations: Restored VM hangs on cold-page access. The userfaultfd handler process crashed or blocked, so page faults from KVM never get serviced. [class: uffd-handler-failure]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.network-disrupt-after-resume
observations: After snapshot restore, in-flight TCP connections to the guest break. ARP cache is stale, switches haven't seen the new MAC's frames yet. [class: expected-network-disruption-on-resume]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.virtio-net-no-nack-lro
observations: FreeBSD (or other guest) disables Large Receive Offload (LRO), but Firecracker keeps sending 1536+ byte segments anyway. Guest virtio-net device hangs. [class: virtio-feature-negotiation-bug]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.tap-cap-net-admin-required
observations: Firecracker fails to attach a TAP device with EPERM. Running uid lacks CAP_NET_ADMIN. [class: missing-capability]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.ip-forward-disabled
observations: Guest can't reach the internet through the host. Packets from the TAP never make it to the egress interface. Host has IPv4 forwarding disabled. [class: host-routing-disabled]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.nat-masquerade-rule-missing
observations: Guest packets reach the host's egress interface but have non-routable source IPs. NAT masquerade rule isn't installed. [class: missing-nat-rule]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.mmds-unreachable-no-route
observations: Guest gets connection-refused or no-route when trying to fetch from MMDS at 169.254.169.254 (or configured IP). Guest hasn't added a route for the MMDS IP. [class: guest-routing-missing]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.mmds-v1-ssrf-vulnerability
observations: Untrusted guest workload (e.g., AI agent fetching arbitrary URLs) reads sensitive metadata from MMDS via SSRF. MMDS V1 has no token requirement. [class: mmds-v1-deprecated-no-auth]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.mmds-data-lost-on-snapshot
observations: After snapshot restore, MMDS GETs return empty/old data. The MMDS data store is intentionally not persisted across snapshots. [class: intentional-non-persistence]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.single-queue-tap-throughput-cap
observations: VirtIO/net throughput per microVM caps at ~10-15 Gbps despite faster host NIC. TAP backend is single-queue; no IFF_MULTI_QUEUE. [class: design-constraint]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.rate-limit-req-size-exceeds-bucket
observations: Network requests larger than the rate-limiter bucket size are silently never permitted — bucket can't accumulate enough tokens for one request. [class: rate-limiter-misconfiguration]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.vsock-connect-before-guest-init
observations: Host initiates vsock CONNECT immediately after InstanceStart but Firecracker closes the host-side socket before the guest agent finishes booting and starts listening. [class: lifecycle-race]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.vsock-stream-read-error-mid-flight
observations: Active vsock connection terminates mid-flight with a stream read error — Firecracker fails to read from the backing AF_UNIX stream, possibly because the host peer closed it abruptly. [class: stream-cleanup-race]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.uds-path-collision-clones
observations: Two restored clones of the same snapshot collide on the same vsock UDS path. Second restore fails (or worse: succeeds and steps on the first clone's UDS). [class: snapshot-clone-uds-collision]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.missing-virtio-vsockets-config
observations: Guest doesn't see /dev/vsock. PUT /vsock attached the device on Firecracker side but guest kernel lacks CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS. [class: guest-kernel-config-missing]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.vhost-vsock-host-module-missing
observations: PUT /vsock fails with ENOENT or ENODEV. Host kernel lacks CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK module — even though Firecracker bypasses vhost code, the module needs to be loaded. [class: host-kernel-module-missing]

name: firecracker.networking.fm.guest-initiated-vsock-no-host-listener
observations: Guest tries to vsock-connect to host CID=2 port N but receives VIRTIO_VSOCK_OP_RST. No process is listening on the host UDS at <uds_path>_<N>. [class: missing-host-listener]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.kvm-pit-cpu-overhead-untracked
observations: Host CPU usage spikes from kvm-pit kernel threads but the cost isn't accounted to any microVM cgroup. Schedulers undercount per-tenant CPU; noisy-neighbor effects. [class: kernel-thread-not-in-microvm-cgroup]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.smt-enabled-side-channel-risk
observations: Multi-tenant Firecracker host has SMT (Hyperthreading) enabled. Speculation-class side channels (Spectre, MDS) become exploitable across tenants. [class: host-hardening-missing]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.ksm-enabled-side-channel-risk
observations: Multi-tenant host has KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging) enabled. Page-deduplication side channels exploitable — one tenant can detect another's memory contents. [class: host-hardening-missing]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.swap-enabled-data-remanence
observations: Host has swap enabled. Under memory pressure, guest memory contents get written to disk → data remanence on disk reuse. [class: host-hardening-missing]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.fd-ulimit-too-low
observations: Firecracker fails with EMFILE (Too many open files) when starting many devices or under vsock-heavy workload. Each microVM uses 20+ FDs baseline. [class: fd-limit-exhaustion]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.no-seccomp-in-production
observations: Production Firecracker is started with --no-seccomp (or with a custom filter that whitelists too many syscalls). Defense-in-depth boundary disabled. [class: operator-error-security-disabled]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.debug-binary-in-production
observations: Production deployment is using a debug-built Firecracker binary. Default seccomp filters are not embedded in debug builds — process runs unsandboxed at the syscall layer. [class: wrong-build-artifact]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.drive-unsafe-cache-data-loss
observations: Host crashes; on reboot, guest filesystem is corrupted or 'recently committed' data is missing. Drive was attached with cache_type=Unsafe — guest fsync()s were dropped. [class: drive-cache-misconfiguration]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.drive-backing-file-missing
observations: PUT /drives returns 400 with 'Block device backing file does not exist' or InstanceStart fails reading the disk. [class: missing-host-file]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.pre-boot-only-call-after-boot
observations: API call returns 400 with 'cannot be modified after machine startup' or similar. Trying to PUT a pre-boot-only resource (drive, network-interface, vsock, machine-config, boot-source, mmds-config) after InstanceStart. [class: lifecycle-misuse]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.jailer-cgroup-v2-subtree-control-trap
observations: Jailer fails with 'no internal process constraint' when launched with --cgroup-version=2 + --parent-cgroup pointing at an existing cgroup that has domain controllers in subtree_control. [class: cgroup-v2-subtree-control-misconfiguration]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.jailer-chroot-base-permission-denied
observations: Jailer exits with EACCES creating <chroot_base>/<exec>/<id>/root. The chroot base directory or its parents have wrong permissions. [class: filesystem-permissions]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.balloon-overcommit-thrashing
observations: MicroVM with VirtIO balloon overcommitted memory thrashes — guest's effective RAM drops to a tiny fraction (e.g., 8 GiB → 1.4 GiB) causing massive page churn. [class: balloon-overcommit]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.e2b-uffd-firecracker-process-killing-race
observations: Orchestrator (e2b-style) tries to kill a Firecracker process while UFFD handler is mid-fault-service. Process kill races with handler cleanup → orphaned UFFD state, leaked fds, hung handlers. [class: lifecycle-race-uffd]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.e2b-client-restart-cascades-to-sandboxes
observations: Orchestrator (e2b-style) client process restarts → all live Firecracker sandboxes crash. UFFD handler closure on client exit cascades to FCs that depend on it. [class: orchestrator-lifecycle-coupling]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.e2b-guest-clock-drift-on-startup
observations: Guest clock drifts by ~100-500ms on startup. KVM PTP not configured in guest; guest relies on its initial RTC read which lags. [class: guest-time-source]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.e2b-orchestrator-cascade-restart
observations: Orchestrator-level health-check failure (Nomad/Consul) triggers a cascade of Firecracker process restarts. The actual fault wasn't with FC. [class: orchestrator-health-check-misconfig]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.virtio-net-tx-scatter-gather-perf
observations: VirtIO/net TX throughput is lower than expected. Packets get copied twice — descriptor → intermediate buffer → kernel — instead of using scatter-gather. [class: design-perf-issue-fixed]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.dirty-page-tracking-overhead
observations: VM with track_dirty_pages=true sees noticeable per-write overhead (small but measurable on write-heavy workloads). KVM page-walk for dirty bits adds cost. [class: intentional-tradeoff]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.hugepages-not-reserved
observations: PUT /machine-config with huge_pages='2M' fails or microVM creates fail under load. Host hasn't reserved enough hugepages. [class: host-resource-not-reserved]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.hyperthreading-exposed-via-machine-config-smt-true
observations: machine-config.smt is true on a multi-tenant host. Guest sees hyperthreaded siblings via CPUID — speculation side-channel attack surface increases. [class: config-misuse-multi-tenant]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.api-on-tcp-not-uds-attempt
observations: Operator attempts to bind the Firecracker API to a TCP port. Firecracker only accepts UDS transport. [class: fundamental-design-misunderstanding]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.action-without-prerequisites
observations: PUT /actions {action_type: InstanceStart} returns 400. Required pre-boot resources aren't all configured. [class: missing-pre-boot-config]

name: firecracker.setup.fm.host-kernel-logs-slow-snapshot-restore
observations: Snapshot restore time degrades inexplicably (e.g., 3ms → 8.5ms on aarch64) after host kernel cmdline change. Host kernel logging hot during TAP create — synchronous console writes hold up the FC main thread. [class: host-console-blocking-fc-syscalls]

name: firecracker.snapshots.fm.cgroupv1-restore-latency-tax
observations: Snapshot restore on cgroup-v1 hosts is significantly slower than v2 — restore times of 100ms+ vs 5-15ms on v2. [class: host-cgroup-version]

name: ecs.agent.fm.agent-disconnected-from-ecs-service
observations: Container instance shows status=ACTIVE but agentConnected=false. New tasks aren't placed; running tasks continue but state-changes aren't reported. ECS event log: 'service X has stopped Y running tasks: Task failed ELB health checks'. [class: acs-protocol-disconnect]

name: ecs.agent.fm.agent-oom-on-dense-instance
observations: Agent process killed by OOM killer on instance running many high-density tasks. dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process <pid> (agent)'. Tasks orphaned (still running but no agent control). [class: agent-memory-budget-exceeded]

name: ecs.agent.fm.cgroupv2-task-launch-failure
observations: Tasks fail to launch on cgroup v2 instances; CannotCreateContainerError mentions cgroup-v2 mount or hierarchy issues. Particularly with older agent versions. [class: agent-cgroup-version-mismatch]

name: ecs.agent.fm.draining-stuck-services-not-replacing
observations: Container instance set to DRAINING but tasks aren't being replaced. Tasks stuck in RUNNING on the draining instance. Service event log shows no new task placements. [class: no-capacity-for-replacement]

name: ecs.agent.fm.dev-kvm-not-needed-but-docker-failing
observations: agent log: 'failed to dial docker: Get "http://%2Fvar%2Frun%2Fdocker.sock": EOF'. Docker daemon isn't reachable. [class: docker-daemon-unhealthy]

name: ecs.agent.fm.image-cleanup-races-task-launch
observations: Task fails with CannotPullContainerError 'image not found' RIGHT after a previous task using the same image successfully completed and was cleaned up. Image was deleted by agent's cleanup right as the new task tried to use it. [class: image-cleanup-too-aggressive]

name: ecs.agent.fm.iam-role-propagation-race
observations: Task fails immediately with 'Unable to assume the role' or 'access denied' on first call to AWS API, even though task IAM role exists. Race: task starts before IAM role's trust relationship has propagated. [class: iam-eventual-consistency]

name: ecs.agent.fm.spot-interruption-no-draining
observations: Spot-backed instance terminated mid-task. Tasks were running but no draining happened; service has to scramble to replace them. Disrupts in-flight work. [class: ecs-enable-spot-instance-draining-not-set]

name: ecs.agent.fm.checkpoint-state-loss
observations: Agent restart re-discovers running tasks but takes a long time. agent log: 'state file not found'. Symptom: brief task-status flapping in console. [class: agent-data-dir-not-persisted]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.cannot-pull-container-error-auth
observations: Task stops with stoppedReason 'CannotPullContainerError: pull access denied for <repo>, repository does not exist or may require authorization'. Image is in private ECR (or Docker Hub private repo) and authn is missing. [class: registry-auth-missing]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.cannot-pull-container-error-network
observations: stoppedReason 'CannotPullContainerError: net/http: TLS handshake timeout' or 'no such host'. Task subnet has no path to the registry. [class: registry-network-unreachable]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.cannot-pull-container-error-rate-limited
observations: stoppedReason 'CannotPullContainerError: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit. You may increase the limit by authenticating'.  Anonymous Docker Hub pull rate limit hit. [class: registry-rate-limit]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.resource-initialization-secret-fetch-failed
observations: Task fails with stoppedReason 'ResourceInitializationError: unable to pull secrets or registry auth: ... AccessDeniedException'. Execution role can't fetch from Secrets Manager / SSM. [class: execution-role-missing-secret-perms]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.resource-initialization-eni-attach-timeout
observations: Task fails with stoppedReason 'ResourceInitializationError: failed to setup task network: ... ENI attach timeout'. Subnet IP exhaustion or ENI quota hit. [class: subnet-eni-exhaustion]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.placement-failure-resource-cpu-memory
observations: RunTask fails synchronously with failures[].reason 'RESOURCE:CPU' or 'RESOURCE:MEMORY' — no instance has enough free capacity. [class: cluster-capacity-exhausted]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.placement-failure-attribute
observations: Placement fails with reason 'ATTRIBUTE:ecs.<x>'. No instance matches the task's placementConstraints expression. [class: placement-constraint-no-match]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.essential-container-exited-app-crash
observations: Task stops with stoppedReason 'Essential container in task exited' and container exitCode != 0. App crashed; ECS terminated the whole task. [class: app-crash]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.health-check-grace-too-short
observations: ELB-fronted service constantly killing tasks. Service event: 'service X has stopped Y running tasks: Task failed ELB health checks'. Tasks are healthy app-internally but slow to start. [class: health-check-grace-too-short]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.deployment-circuit-breaker-trip
observations: Deployment fails; service event: 'service X is unable to consistently start tasks successfully'. Circuit breaker tripped after multiple task failures; rolled back automatically. [class: deployment-broken]

name: ecs.networking.fm.awsvpc-eni-quota-exhaustion
observations: Tasks fail to launch with 'ENI attach timeout'. Per-instance ENI limit hit (e.g., 4 on m5.large) before HDE/trunking enabled. [class: per-instance-eni-quota]

name: ecs.networking.fm.awsvpc-subnet-ip-exhaustion
observations: Task ENI attach fails with 'InsufficientFreeAddressesInSubnet'. Subnet IP space exhausted by accumulated ENIs. [class: subnet-ip-exhaustion]

name: ecs.networking.fm.security-group-blocks-task-traffic
observations: Task ENI security group denies egress (or ingress). App can't reach RDS, can't be reached by ALB targets, etc. [class: security-group-misconfig]

name: ecs.networking.fm.host-mode-port-conflict
observations: Second task in host network mode fails to start: 'port already allocated'. Two tasks on same instance try to bind same containerPort. [class: host-network-port-conflict]

name: ecs.networking.fm.task-iam-not-working-host-mode
observations: App in host-network-mode task gets 'no credentials available'. AWS SDK can't reach 169.254.170.2/credentials. [class: task-iam-host-mode-not-enabled]

name: ecs.networking.fm.alb-health-check-cascading-failures
observations: ALB target group constantly killing tasks. Cascading failures: tasks killed → service launches replacements → new tasks also fail health check. [class: alb-health-check-misconfig]

name: ecs.networking.fm.awsvpc-cant-pull-from-ecr-no-vpce
observations: awsvpc tasks in private subnets can't reach ECR. CannotPullContainerError net-timeout. No VPC endpoints + no NAT. [class: no-private-egress-to-aws-services]

name: ecs.networking.fm.imds-leak-from-task
observations: Untrusted task code accesses 169.254.169.254 (EC2 instance metadata) and exfiltrates the container instance role's credentials. SSRF in app code → metadata leak. [class: missing-awsvpc-imds-block]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.task-stopped-by-asg-scale-in
observations: Tasks stopped without app fault. ASG scaled in and terminated the underlying instance. Service event: 'service X has stopped Y running tasks'. [class: asg-scale-in-without-protection]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.fargate-spot-interruption
observations: Fargate Spot tasks stopped with stoppedReason 'Spot capacity not available' or 'TerminationNotice'. AWS reclaimed Spot capacity. [class: spot-capacity-reclaimed]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.containerinsights-missing-metrics
observations: CloudWatch Container Insights dashboard shows no data for an ECS cluster. Or partial data missing (e.g., per-container memory). [class: container-insights-not-enabled]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.bare-metal-boot-time-exceeded-asg-warmup
observations: Bare-metal instance launched by ASG never becomes available. 20+ minute boot time exceeds ASG instanceWarmupPeriod / managed-scaling expectations. [class: warmup-too-short-for-bare-metal]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.containerinsights-on-but-no-data-iam
observations: Container Insights enabled but no data flows. Cluster IAM role missing CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy / metrics:PutMetricData. [class: iam-missing-cloudwatch-perms]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.scheduled-task-eventbridge-rule-misfire
observations: Scheduled task (EventBridge rule with ECS target) doesn't fire. Cron expression valid but no tasks launched. [class: eventbridge-iam-missing]

name: ecs.troubleshooting.fm.amazon-linux-2-eol-2026-06-30
observations: Cluster running ECS-Optimized AL2 AMI past 2026-06-30. No more security updates from upstream Amazon Linux 2. [class: ami-eol]

name: ecs.agent.fm.efs-mount-failed-transit-encryption
observations: Task fails ResourceInitializationError 'failed to mount EFS volume: ... transit encryption mismatch'. Task-def says transitEncryption=ENABLED but EFS mount-target SG doesn't allow port 2049 from task SG, OR EFS access point requires IAM and task lacks perms. [class: efs-mount-misconfig]

name: ecs.agent.fm.awslogs-missing-log-group
observations: Task fails ResourceInitializationError 'failed to create container: failed to initialize logging driver: awslogs: log group does not exist'. awslogs-create-group not set + group doesn't exist. [class: awslogs-create-group-not-set]

name: ecs.agent.fm.firelens-config-fluentbit-syntax-error
observations: FireLens log-router container exits immediately. Task stops with 'essential container exited' for the firelens container; app logs lost. Fluent Bit parsed config-file-value with syntax error. [class: firelens-config-syntax]

name: ecs.agent.fm.ephemeral-storage-exhausted-fargate
observations: Fargate task fills its scratch disk; container crashes with 'no space left on device'. Default ephemeralStorage is 20 GiB; bigger images / scratch usage exceeds. [class: ephemeral-storage-too-small]

name: ecs.agent.fm.codedeploy-blue-green-rollback-stuck
observations: CodeDeploy blue/green ECS deployment fails to roll back. Old (blue) target group still receiving 0 traffic; service stuck. Manual ALB intervention needed. [class: codedeploy-iam-or-hook-failed]

name: ecs.agent.fm.cross-account-ecr-pull-denied
observations: Task in account A pulls from ECR in account B; CannotPullContainerError. Cross-account ECR repo policy doesn't allow account A's executionRole. [class: ecr-cross-account-policy-missing]

name: ecs.agent.fm.ecs-anywhere-ssm-activation-expired
observations: External instance fails to register. ecs-init log: 'ssm activation expired or invalid'. SSM activation token has 30-day max TTL. [class: ssm-activation-ttl-expired]

name: ecs.agent.fm.exec-command-ssm-session-failed
observations: aws ecs execute-command fails: 'The execute command failed because execute command was not enabled when the Task was run'. [class: exec-command-not-opted-in]

name: ecs.agent.fm.task-def-volume-name-collision
observations: Task fails to start: 'volume name X already exists'. Two task-def volumes with the same name; OR mountPoint references a volume name that doesn't exist in volumes[]. [class: task-def-volume-misconfig]

name: ecs.agent.fm.task-stuck-in-stopping
observations: Task transitions to STOPPING but never reaches STOPPED. Held there for many minutes. Container won't respond to SIGTERM. [class: container-ignoring-sigterm]

name: ecs.agent.fm.account-setting-arn-format-required
observations: API calls return 'enable the new ARN format with account-setting before using this feature'. Tagging-aware features need new ARN format. [class: old-arn-format]

name: ecs.agent.fm.environment-file-s3-not-found
observations: Task fails ResourceInitializationError 'environment file s3://bucket/file not accessible'. Bucket/key missing or executionRole lacks s3:GetObject. [class: environment-file-fetch-failed]

name: ecs.agent.fm.fargate-platform-version-pin-stale
observations: Fargate service pinned to platformVersion=1.3.0 hits behavior bugs that 1.4+ fixes. Or pin to LATEST and behavior changes broke an integration. [class: platform-version-mismatch]

name: ecs.agent.fm.fargate-restricted-syscall-or-cap
observations: Fargate task fails to launch: 'unsupported parameter: privileged' or 'sysctl X not allowed'. Fargate restricts privileged + many sysctls + capabilities. [class: fargate-restriction]

name: ecs.agent.fm.bare-metal-host-misuse-firecracker
observations: Bare-metal EC2 instance hosting Firecracker-based workloads exhibits performance degradation. Investigation shows Firecracker not configured per fc-docs-prod-host-setup recommendations on the host. [class: host-not-firecracker-tuned]

name: ecs.task-defs.fm.task-oom-killed
observations: Task stops with stoppedReason 'OutOfMemoryError: Container killed due to memory usage'. Container hit its hard memory limit. [class: container-cgroup-oom]

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-stop
observations: docker container stop [OPTIONS] CONTAINER [CONTAINER...] — Send SIGTERM (or configured stop-signal), wait for grace period, then SIGKILL. Aliases: `docker stop`. Exit semantics: clean if app handles signal; otherwise 137 (128+9). The 10-second-then-SIGKILL pattern is responsible for many 'docker stop hangs' tickets.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-logs
observations: docker container logs [OPTIONS] CONTAINER — Fetch logs from a container. Aliases: `docker logs`. Works only with `json-file`, `local`, and `journald` log drivers; with `fluentd`/`syslog`/etc., the daemon doesn't keep a local cache and `docker logs` returns nothing.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-start
observations: docker container start [OPTIONS] CONTAINER [CONTAINER...] — Start one or more stopped containers. Aliases: `docker start`. Reuses the previous run-config (env, mounts, port publish) — no re-spec. Useful after `docker stop` and after host reboot if `--restart` policy isn't set.

name: docker.engine.cmd.volume-prune
observations: docker volume prune [OPTIONS] — Remove all volumes not used by at least one container. Volumes are NEVER auto-removed (could destroy data); explicit prune required.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-inspect
observations: docker container inspect [OPTIONS] CONTAINER [CONTAINER...] — Display detailed JSON for one or more containers (config, state, mounts, networks, log config, restart-policy). The single most useful debugging command: every field of `docker inspect` is queryable via `--format`.

name: docker.engine.cmd.dockerd
observations: dockerd [OPTIONS] — The Docker daemon process itself. Self-sufficient runtime for containers; reads /etc/docker/daemon.json by default. Most flags map 1:1 to daemon.json keys (catalogued in docker.engine.cfg.daemon.json). Failure-modes: 'unable to configure the Docker daemon with file /etc/docker/daemon.json: invalid character …' on bad JSON; 'the following directives are specified both as a flag and in the configuration file' on dual-spec.

name: docker.engine.cmd.image-prune
observations: docker image prune [OPTIONS] — Remove dangling (no tag, not referenced) images by default; with -a, remove all images not used by an existing container. Most aggressive disk-reclaim.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-exec
observations: docker container exec [OPTIONS] CONTAINER COMMAND [ARG...] — Execute a command in a RUNNING container. Aliases: `docker exec`. Fails on paused/stopped containers. The command isn't restarted with the container; chained commands need explicit `sh -c`.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-prune
observations: docker container prune [OPTIONS] — Remove all stopped containers. Their writable layers are freed; named volumes preserved.

name: docker.engine.cmd.network-prune
observations: docker network prune [OPTIONS] — Remove networks not used by any containers. Cleans up iptables/bridge/route entries left behind.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-rm
observations: docker container rm [OPTIONS] CONTAINER [CONTAINER...] — Remove one or more containers. Aliases: `docker rm`. Fails on running containers unless `-f`. Removing frees the writable layer; named volumes attached are NOT removed (use `-v` for anonymous volumes).

name: docker.engine.cmd.system-df
observations: docker system df [OPTIONS] — Show Docker disk usage broken down by Images, Containers, Local Volumes, Build Cache. Active vs reclaimable. Resource-intensive — traverses every image/container/volume filesystem; avoid in latency-critical contexts. Drives the 'where did my disk go' diagnosis.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-run
observations: docker container run [OPTIONS] IMAGE [COMMAND] [ARG...] — Create and run a new container from an image. Pulls the image if missing (controlled by --pull). Aliases: `docker run`. The most commonly invoked Docker subcommand; surface area is enormous (~115 flags). Failure paths: image not found, port conflict, mount source missing, OOM-kill, exit-code 125 (daemon error before runtime), 126 (entrypoint not executable), 127 (not found).

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-kill
observations: docker container kill [OPTIONS] CONTAINER [CONTAINER...] — Send a signal (default SIGKILL) to the container's pid 1. Aliases: `docker kill`. With shell-form ENTRYPOINT/CMD, signals go to /bin/sh -c not the real binary — root cause of 'docker kill -s SIGUSR1 doesn't reach my app'. Fix: exec-form or `--init`.

name: docker.engine.cmd.container-ls
observations: docker container ls [OPTIONS] — List containers. Aliases: `docker ps`, `docker container list`, `docker container ps`. By default shows running only. Filter expressions are the meat — `--filter status=exited`, `--filter health=unhealthy`, `--filter exited=137` are interview-day staples.

name: docker.engine.cmd.system-prune
observations: docker system prune [OPTIONS] — Remove unused data: stopped containers, unused networks, dangling images, unused build cache. Volumes NOT pruned by default — must add --volumes. Reclaims disk fast; prompts before deleting.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.ctr
observations: ctr [global-flags] <subcommand> [subcommand-flags] — containerd's bundled debug CLI. Native API (NOT CRI). Subcommands grouped by service: images (pull/push/ls/rm/import/export), containers (create/ls/info/rm), tasks (start/ls/kill/exec/pause/resume), namespaces, content, snapshots, events, version, plugins. 'For debugging only' per the official docs — use nerdctl for general purpose.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-delete
observations: runc delete [--force] <container-id> — Delete resources held by a container. Container must be in `stopped` state unless `--force`. Deletes only what runc created — pre-existing resources are left alone.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-spec
observations: runc spec [options] — Generate a starter `config.json` in the bundle dir. ALWAYS needs editing afterwards (default sets process.args=["sh"], which fails on most images). Pair with `jq` to mutate.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.crictl-pods
observations: crictl pods [flags] — List pod sandboxes via the CRI grpc API. Connects to `unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock` (or kubelet-configured socket). Used to debug k8s nodes when kubectl can't reach the node.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.crictl-exec
observations: crictl exec [flags] <container-id> <command> [args...] — Run a command inside a running container via the CRI. Useful for debugging from a node when `kubectl exec` can't reach the API server. Mirrors `kubectl exec` but at the kubelet/CRI level.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-state
observations: runc state <container-id> — Output current state of a container as JSON: ociVersion, id, status (creating|created|running|stopped), pid, bundle, annotations.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-kill
observations: runc kill <container-id> [signal] — Send signal to container's pid 1. Default SIGTERM. No grace period at this layer — that's containerd / dockerd. Errors if state is not `created` or `running`.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-create
observations: runc create [options] <container-id> — Create an instance of a container from an OCI bundle (config.json + rootfs). All config.json properties EXCEPT process.args are applied; user process is not started until `runc start`. Container appears in `runc list` with state `created`.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-exec
observations: runc exec [options] <container-id> [--] <command> [args...]   |   runc exec -p <process.json> <container-id> — Execute a new process inside a running container. Two forms: command-line + flags, or full process spec from a JSON file. Exits with the command's exit status (255 on internal error).

name: docker.runtime.cmd.containerd
observations: containerd [global-flags] — The containerd daemon. Default config at /etc/containerd/config.toml. State at /var/lib/containerd; runtime sockets under /run/containerd. Built-in CRI plugin lets kubelet talk to it directly.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.runc-run
observations: runc run [options] <container-id> — Shortcut for `create` + `start` — creates and starts a container in one go. Most common for one-off / interactive use. Default attached; `--detach` for backgrounded.

name: docker.runtime.cmd.crictl-ps
observations: crictl ps [flags] — List containers via the CRI grpc API (the in-pod containers, distinct from the pod sandbox listed by `crictl pods`).

name: docker.networking.cmd.image-push
observations: docker image push [OPTIONS] NAME[:TAG] — Upload an image to a registry. Aliases: `docker push`. Daemon-level concurrency from `max-concurrent-uploads`. Compresses layers before upload (progress bar shows uncompressed size). Killing the CLI terminates the push cleanly.

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-prune
observations: docker network prune [OPTIONS] — Remove networks not used by any containers. Cleans up iptables/bridge/route entries left behind by stale networks. (Domain-level prune is also catalogued under `docker.engine.cmd.network-prune`; networking-leaf row gives the network-debugging context.)

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-inspect
observations: docker network inspect [OPTIONS] NETWORK [NETWORK...] — JSON dump of network metadata: driver, scope, IPAM config, attached containers (with their endpoints, IPs, MACs), driver-specific options, swarm Peers (overlay), Services (overlay+swarm verbose).

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-ls
observations: docker network ls [OPTIONS] — List Docker networks. Aliases: `docker network list`. Default columns: NETWORK ID, NAME, DRIVER, SCOPE.

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-disconnect
observations: docker network disconnect [OPTIONS] NETWORK CONTAINER — Detach a container from a network. Removes its endpoint, frees the IP.

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-connect
observations: docker network connect [OPTIONS] NETWORK CONTAINER — Attach a running container to an additional network. Adds a new endpoint with its own IP+MAC. The container can have static IP/alias on the new network.

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-rm
observations: docker network rm NETWORK [NETWORK...] — Remove one or more networks. Network must have no attached containers; disconnect them first.

name: docker.networking.cmd.image-pull
observations: docker image pull [OPTIONS] NAME[:TAG|@DIGEST] — Download an image from a registry. Aliases: `docker pull`. Default tag = `latest`. Pulling by digest pins to immutable bytes; pulling by tag may yield different bytes over time. Daemon-level concurrency from `max-concurrent-downloads`.

name: docker.networking.cmd.network-create
observations: docker network create [OPTIONS] NETWORK — Create a Docker network. Default driver is `bridge`. For multi-host: `--driver overlay` (Swarm required). Driver-specific options via `--opt key=val` (repeatable).

name: docker.networking.cmd.port
observations: docker port CONTAINER [PRIVATE_PORT[/PROTO]] — Show port bindings for a container — `<container-port>/<proto> -> <host-ip>:<host-port>`. Especially useful with `-P` (random ephemeral host port) where you don't know the binding ahead of time.

name: docker.compose.cmd.down
observations: docker compose down [SERVICE...] — Stop and remove containers, networks. Volumes preserved by default (use `-v` to also remove). Reverse-order shutdown of `depends_on` graph.

name: docker.compose.cmd.logs
observations: docker compose logs [SERVICE...] — Fetch + stream logs from project services. Multi-service streams are interleaved with a `<service> | ` prefix. Subset of services via positional args.

name: docker.compose.cmd.build
observations: docker compose build [SERVICE...] — Build images for services that have a `build` block. Reuses BuildKit. Subset by service name(s).

name: docker.compose.cmd.ps
observations: docker compose ps [SERVICE...] — List containers in the project. Default columns: NAME, IMAGE, COMMAND, SERVICE, CREATED, STATUS, PORTS. Filterable by service name.

name: docker.compose.cmd.run
observations: docker compose run [OPTIONS] SERVICE [COMMAND] [ARG...] — Run a one-off container against a service definition. Doesn't reuse the service's running container — creates a new one each time. By default, also brings up its `depends_on` graph (so DB is up before the migration runs).

name: docker.compose.cmd.exec
observations: docker compose exec [OPTIONS] SERVICE COMMAND [ARG...] — Execute a command in a RUNNING service container. Mirrors `docker exec`. Picks the first replica if multiple.

name: docker.compose.cmd.restart
observations: docker compose restart [SERVICE...] — Restart service containers. Doesn't recreate — same container, just stop+start. For config changes that took effect on restart, use `up` instead (or with `--force-recreate`).

name: docker.compose.cmd.up
observations: docker compose up [SERVICE...] — Build, (re)create, start, and attach to containers for the project's services. The most-used compose subcommand. Builds images for services with a `build` block (unless `--pull always`). Brings up `depends_on` graph in topological order; honors `condition: service_healthy`. By default streams logs to stdout; `-d` for detached.

name: docker.security.cmd.trust-inspect
observations: docker trust inspect [OPTIONS] IMAGE[:TAG] — Display Notary trust data for a tag or repository: signers, signed tags, key IDs, signing thresholds. JSON-formatted by default; `--pretty` for human output.

name: docker.security.cmd.trust-key-load
observations: docker trust key {generate|load} [OPTIONS] [KEY_FILE] --name NAME — Manage delegation keys in the local trust store. `generate` creates a new keypair (private under `~/.docker/trust/private/`, public to cwd); `load` imports an existing private key. Both prompt for a passphrase to encrypt the on-disk key. The companion to `docker trust signer add` which uploads the public side to Notary.

name: docker.security.cmd.trust-revoke
observations: docker trust revoke [OPTIONS] IMAGE:TAG — Remove trust data for a specific tag (or all tags via `--yes` on a repo). After revocation, pulls with `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1` reject the tag. Cannot be undone without re-signing.

name: docker.security.cmd.trust-sign
observations: docker trust sign [OPTIONS] IMAGE:TAG — Sign and push a tagged image's trust data via Notary. Requires a delegation key in the local trust store (`~/.docker/trust/private/`) and the public-key counterpart already added to the Notary server for the GUN. Overwrites remote trust metadata. Equivalent to `docker push` with `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildx-build
observations: docker buildx build [OPTIONS] PATH | URL | - — Same surface as `docker build` (since 23.0 they're aliases) but explicitly invokes the buildx CLI. Use directly when you want to be sure you're getting the buildx behavior, or when running a non-default builder via `--builder`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildx-bake
observations: docker buildx bake [OPTIONS] [TARGET...] — Build a matrix of targets defined in HCL/JSON/Compose files. Each target is a separate image. Variables, groups, and target overrides supported. The CI driver for monorepo / multi-image builds.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildx-imagetools-create
observations: docker buildx imagetools create [OPTIONS] [SOURCE...] — Create or modify an image manifest list (multi-arch image) on a registry from existing single-arch images. Doesn't rebuild — just stitches. Companion: `imagetools inspect <ref>` to view a manifest list.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildctl
observations: buildctl [global-flags] <subcommand> [subcommand-flags] — Native BuildKit CLI. Works against the buildkitd daemon directly via gRPC. For debugging buildkitd, running standalone BuildKit (without docker), or driving builds with non-Dockerfile frontends. Subcommands: build, debug, prune, du.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildkitd
observations: buildkitd [global-flags] — BuildKit daemon. gRPC server on `/run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock` by default. Two worker backends: OCI (runc; default) and containerd. Reads `/etc/buildkit/buildkitd.toml`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildx-use
observations: docker buildx use [OPTIONS] NAME — Switch the active builder. Persists across shell sessions (per `docker context`).

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.build
observations: docker build [OPTIONS] PATH | URL | - — Build an image from a Dockerfile + context. Since Docker Engine 23.0, `docker build` uses Buildx + BuildKit by default (was the legacy builder). Aliases: `docker image build`. Source PATH (local), URL (git), `-` (stdin Dockerfile).

name: docker.build-buildkit.cmd.buildx-create
observations: docker buildx create [OPTIONS] [CONTEXT|ENDPOINT] — Create a buildx builder instance. Combined with `--use`, it becomes the active builder for subsequent `docker build` / `docker buildx build` commands.

name: linux.primitives.cmd.unshare
observations: unshare [options] [program [arguments]] — Run a program in newly created namespaces. The userspace front-end to the unshare(2) syscall family. The 'create a fresh container-like environment without a runtime' tool — sysadmins use it to debug namespace behavior, mount/unmount inside an isolated mountns, or test a program's response to fresh PID/network namespaces. Without --fork, the new PID namespace's pid 1 is unshare itself; with --fork, unshare clones a child to be pid 1 (almost always what you want for --pid). util-linux package; ships with every modern distro.

name: linux.primitives.cmd.nsenter
observations: nsenter [options] [program [arguments]] — Enter one or more namespaces of an existing process and run a command inside. The userspace front-end to setns(2). The fundamental 'attach to a running container's namespaces' tool — `docker exec` and `kubectl exec` are layered atop this primitive (via the runtime). Without --target, can take individual --<ns>=<file> options pointing to /proc/<pid>/ns/* magic links or persisted bind-mounts.

name: linux.primitives.cmd.pivot-root
observations: pivot_root new_root put_old — Move the current root filesystem to put_old and make new_root the new root. Userspace front-end to pivot_root(2). The 'switch the rootfs cleanly inside a mount namespace' tool — what container runtimes do during container start (after preparing new_root with the image's rootfs). Safer than chroot because once the old root is unmounted, escape via reusing chroot is impossible.

name: linux.networking.cmd.ip
observations: ip [OPTIONS] OBJECT { COMMAND | help } — The Swiss-army knife for Linux networking config — replaces ifconfig, route, arp, netstat link table. Talks to kernel via NETLINK_ROUTE. OBJECT is one of: address, link, route, neighbour, rule, netns, tunnel, addrlabel, l2tp, fou, macsec, monitor, mptcp, mroute, mrule, sr, vrf, xfrm. Most subcommands have their own man page (ip-address, ip-link, ip-route, ip-neighbour, etc). For the JSON-friendly machine-readable output, add `-j` (often `-j -p` for pretty-printed).

name: linux.networking.cmd.ip-link
observations: ip link { add | delete | set | show | help } [DEV] [TYPE] — Manage L2 network devices — physical NICs, virtual interfaces (veth, bridge, vlan, vxlan, tun, tap, bond, dummy, gre, ipip, sit, geneve, wireguard). Where you bring interfaces up/down, set MAC, MTU, state, attach to bridges, configure namespaces.

name: linux.networking.cmd.ip-address
observations: ip address { add | del | flush | show } [DEV] — Manage IPv4/IPv6 addresses on interfaces. Add/remove/list addresses, peer addresses, broadcasts, scopes, lifetimes (for DHCP/SLAAC).

name: linux.networking.cmd.ip-route
observations: ip route { add | del | replace | get | show | flush } [DEST] — Manage routing-table entries. Add/remove/inspect routes, evaluate which route a packet would take, manipulate the multiple routing tables, set per-route metric/MTU/source.

name: linux.networking.cmd.ip-neighbour
observations: ip neighbour { add | del | change | replace | show | flush } [ADDR] — Manage the ARP/NDP cache (kernel's IP→MAC mapping). 'ip neigh' = synonym. Replaces the legacy `arp` command.

name: linux.networking.cmd.bridge
observations: bridge [OPTIONS] OBJECT { COMMAND | help } — Configure Linux bridges beyond what `ip link` exposes — STP, per-port flags, FDB (forwarding database = MAC table), MDB (multicast), VLAN filtering, group_fwd_mask. The detailed-bridge-config CLI.

name: linux.networking.cmd.iptables
observations: iptables [-t TABLE] {-A|-I|-D|-R|-L|-F|-N|-X|-P|-Z} CHAIN [RULE] [-j TARGET] — Configure netfilter rules (legacy front-end). Tables: filter (default), nat, mangle, raw, security. Chains: INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD, PREROUTING, POSTROUTING, plus user-defined. Operates on rules within chains; first match wins (unless target returns).

name: linux.networking.cmd.nft
observations: nft [OPTIONS] CMD — Modern netfilter front-end. Single CLI for IPv4/IPv6/ARP/bridge/netdev rules. Atomic ruleset replace, sets/maps, named chains, easier syntax than iptables. Default on RHEL 8+, Debian 11+.

name: linux.networking.cmd.tcpdump
observations: tcpdump [OPTIONS] [FILTER] — Capture and display packets on an interface using libpcap. The Swiss-army knife for network debugging. FILTER is a libpcap BPF expression. Requires CAP_NET_RAW (or root). Outputs human-readable summary by default; `-w FILE` saves a pcap.

name: linux.networking.cmd.ss
observations: ss [OPTIONS] [FILTER] — Socket statistics. Replaces netstat. Reads /proc/net via NETLINK; faster than netstat at scale. Default lists established TCP. Filters: state, src/dst address+port, owning UID/process, protocol.

name: linux.networking.cmd.dig
observations: dig [@SERVER] [TYPE] [NAME] [+OPTION...] — DNS lookup tool, the gold-standard debugging interface. Defaults: query default resolver for A record. Verbose output includes question/answer/authority/additional sections, query time, server, flags. Plus-options control behavior (+short, +trace, +dnssec, +tcp, etc.).

name: linux.networking.cmd.getent
observations: getent [OPTIONS] DATABASE [KEY...] — Query system databases via the NSS (name service switch) layer. Goes through nsswitch.conf — exactly the same path getaddrinfo() and friends take. Useful for testing NSS configuration without writing C.

name: linux.networking.cmd.conntrack
observations: conntrack [-L | -G | -D | -I | -U | -E | -F | -C] [OPTIONS] — Inspect/manipulate the kernel connection tracking table. Lists tracked flows, kills entries, watches events in real time, dumps stats. The diagnostic for stateful firewall and NAT issues.

name: linux.networking.cmd.nmap
observations: nmap [SCAN-TYPES] [OPTIONS] TARGETS — Network discovery and security scanner. Port scan, service/version detection, OS fingerprint, scriptable via NSE. Outbound-traffic intensive; use with permission.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.strace
observations: strace [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS] | strace -p PID — Trace system calls and signals via ptrace(2). Output: each syscall with arg decoding + return value/errno. The 'why is my program failing' tool of last resort. Slows tracee dramatically (5-50x).

name: linux.debugging.cmd.ltrace
observations: ltrace [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS] | ltrace -p PID — Library call tracer — like strace but for shared-library function calls (and optionally syscalls with -S). Useful when bug is at the library API layer (malloc, libssl, libc string functions) rather than syscall.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.lsof
observations: lsof [OPTIONS] [NAMES] — List all open files in the system: regular files, dirs, sockets, pipes, devices, deleted-but-still-open. Reads /proc/<pid>/fd. The 'who has X open' tool. Slow on busy systems.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.htop
observations: htop [OPTIONS] — Interactive curses-based process monitor. Color-coded CPU/mem bars per CPU, tree view, filter, sort, kill, renice — all keyboard-driven. Replaces top for interactive use.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.pidstat
observations: pidstat [OPTIONS] [INTERVAL [COUNT]] — Per-process resource statistics. From sysstat. Shows CPU/memory/IO/context-switches/page-faults at INTERVAL.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.vmstat
observations: vmstat [OPTIONS] [DELAY [COUNT]] — System-wide virtual memory + processes + I/O + CPU stats sampled at interval. Quick triage tool: high si/so = swapping, high wa = IO bound, high cs = context-switch storm.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.iostat
observations: iostat [OPTIONS] [INTERVAL [COUNT]] — Per-device disk I/O statistics from /proc/diskstats. tps/throughput; -x for await/svctm/%util — the saturation indicator.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.iotop
observations: iotop [OPTIONS] — Per-process I/O monitor. Like top but showing disk I/O bandwidth per process. Reads /proc/<pid>/io. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN — typically root.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.blktrace
observations: blktrace [OPTIONS] DEVICES | blktrace -d DEVICE -o - | blkparse -i - — Trace block-layer events (every IO request: queue, merge, dispatch, complete). Output → blkparse for human-readable, btt for latency analysis. Diagnoses block-layer / IO scheduler / device latency at the kernel level.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.gdb
observations: gdb [OPTIONS] [PROGRAM [COREFILE | PID]] — GNU debugger. Source-level debugging for C/C++/Rust/Go (and many others). Breakpoints, watchpoints, single-step, backtrace, register/memory inspection, multi-thread, multi-process, remote via gdbserver, postmortem from core dump. Most useful with -g compiled binaries.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.dmesg
observations: dmesg [OPTIONS] — Read kernel ring buffer. First place to look on weird kernel symptoms: OOM killer, segfaults, hardware errors, driver messages, USB events, network device flapping.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.kexec
observations: kexec [OPTIONS] -l KERNEL [-i INITRD] [--command-line='...'] — Load a kernel for the next reboot via syscall (no firmware reboot). Used by kdump (capture kernel pre-loaded; on panic, kexec invoked from panic context to switch to it). Also for live kernel updates.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.crash
observations: crash [OPTIONS] [VMLINUX] [VMCORE] — Postmortem kernel debugger. Reads vmcore (kdump output) + vmlinux (debug symbols). Interactive shell with kernel-aware commands: bt, kmem, files, mount, log, irq, runq, rd, sym, dis, ps, sig.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.makedumpfile
observations: makedumpfile [OPTIONS] VMCORE DUMPFILE — Compress kernel crash dumps by stripping zero/free/cache pages. A 16 GB raw vmcore can shrink to <1 GB. Companion to crash(8); reduces disk footprint of kdump output.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.auditctl
observations: auditctl [OPTIONS] [-a|-d|-w] RULE — Configure kernel audit subsystem. Add/delete/list rules; control daemon enabled/locked state; configure failure mode and rate limits.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.ausearch
observations: ausearch [OPTIONS] — Query audit log. Filters by key, message type, time range, file, syscall, UID, success/failure. Default reads /var/log/audit/audit.log.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.numastat
observations: numastat [OPTIONS] [PID|PATTERN] — Per-NUMA-node memory statistics. Hits, misses, foreign allocations, local allocations. Diagnoses NUMA-affinity issues on multi-socket boxes.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.trace-cmd
observations: trace-cmd CMD [OPTIONS] — User-friendly ftrace front-end. Manages /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/ for you. Subcommands: record, report, reset, start, stop, extract, list, snapshot, hist.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.bpftrace
observations: bpftrace [-e PROGRAM | FILE] [OPTIONS] — DTrace-inspired high-level eBPF front-end. Compiles short DSL programs to BPF, attaches probes, prints output. The fastest way to write ad-hoc tracing scripts.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-stat
observations: perf stat [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND [ARGS] | perf stat [OPTIONS] -p PID — Run COMMAND (or attach to PID) and print PMU + software event counter values. Default counters: task-clock, context-switches, page-faults, cycles, instructions, branches, branch-misses. Also CPI (cycles-per-instruction) — branch-misses/inst.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-record
observations: perf record [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND | perf record [OPTIONS] -p PID — Sample events into a perf.data file for later analysis with perf report/script. Default samples cycles event at ~4000 Hz with kernel+user stacks. The capture half of CPU profiling.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-report
observations: perf report [OPTIONS] — Read perf.data and display profile (default: TUI tree view). Sort by overhead, sample count, etc. Drill into call graphs.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-top
observations: perf top [OPTIONS] — Real-time top-style profiler. Shows hottest functions live, refreshing per second. Like `top` but sorted by perf samples (vs CPU%).

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-trace
observations: perf trace [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND | perf trace [OPTIONS] -p PID — Live syscall tracer (like strace, but uses tracepoints + ring buffer — much faster, much less overhead). Combines well with -e for filtering.

name: linux.debugging.cmd.perf-script
observations: perf script [OPTIONS] — Process perf.data records. Default: print every sample as a line (timestamp, comm, pid, event, stack). Pipe to flamegraph.pl, custom analyzers, or built-in scripts (--list-script).

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemctl
observations: systemctl [OPTIONS] COMMAND [UNIT...] — Control the systemd service manager. The primary interface for managing units (start, stop, enable, disable, status, list) and the system (reboot, poweroff, isolate). Talks to PID 1 via D-Bus.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.journalctl
observations: journalctl [OPTIONS] [MATCHES...] — Query systemd journal logs. The replacement for grep'ing /var/log/syslog. Filter by unit, priority, time, fields. Tail with -f.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemd-analyze
observations: systemd-analyze [OPTIONS] COMMAND — Inspect boot performance, unit-file correctness, sandboxing posture. The performance + correctness toolbox.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemd-run
observations: systemd-run [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND [ARGS] — Run a command as a transient unit (service, scope, or timer). Lets you apply systemd resource controls + sandboxing to ad-hoc invocations.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemd-cgls
observations: systemd-cgls [OPTIONS] [CGROUP|UNIT|PID] — Tree view of cgroups + processes within. Shows the slice/service hierarchy.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemd-cgtop
observations: systemd-cgtop [OPTIONS] — Top-style live view of cgroup CPU/memory/IO/task counts. Real-time per-unit resource usage.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.loginctl
observations: loginctl [OPTIONS] COMMAND — Inspect + control logind sessions, users, seats. Where session data + suspend inhibitors live.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.coredumpctl
observations: coredumpctl [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] — Query + extract core dumps captured by systemd-coredump.

name: linux.systemd.cmd.systemd-tmpfiles
observations: systemd-tmpfiles [OPTIONS] {--create | --clean | --remove} [CONFIG_FILES...] — Apply tmpfiles.d rules: create, clean (delete old per Age field), or remove specific paths.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.mount
observations: mount [-t TYPE] [-o OPTIONS] DEVICE MOUNTPOINT — Attach a filesystem. Without args, lists current mounts (read /proc/mounts). With one arg, mounts per /etc/fstab entry.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.umount
observations: umount [OPTIONS] {DEVICE | MOUNTPOINT} — Detach a filesystem. Returns EBUSY if files open / processes have CWD inside.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.lsblk
observations: lsblk [OPTIONS] [DEVICES] — Tree view of block devices: disks → partitions → LVs → filesystems. Shows MAJ:MIN, SIZE, RO, TYPE, MOUNTPOINTS.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.blkid
