observations: blkid [OPTIONS] [DEVICE...] — Print block device attributes: UUID, LABEL, TYPE. Reads superblock signatures. Used by udev rules and /etc/fstab UUID resolution.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.losetup
observations: losetup [OPTIONS] {-l | -d LOOP | -f [-P] FILE | LOOP FILE} — Manage loop devices. Set up a /dev/loopN backed by a regular file (disk image, encrypted container, etc.).

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.mkfs-ext4
observations: mkfs.ext4 [OPTIONS] DEVICE — Create ext4 filesystem.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.tune2fs
observations: tune2fs [OPTIONS] DEVICE — Adjust ext2/3/4 filesystem parameters. Most operations require the FS unmounted.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.mkfs-xfs
observations: mkfs.xfs [OPTIONS] DEVICE — Create XFS filesystem. Modern XFS is the default for RHEL 7+ rootfs.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.mkfs-btrfs
observations: mkfs.btrfs [OPTIONS] DEVICES... — Create Btrfs filesystem. Multi-device aware: pass multiple DEVICES for built-in RAID.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.lvm
observations: lvm [COMMAND] — LVM2 main entry — interactive shell or CLI. In practice, individual binaries (pvcreate, vgcreate, lvcreate, etc.) are invoked. lvm itself rarely run directly.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.pvcreate
observations: pvcreate [OPTIONS] DEVICE... — Initialize disk/partition as LVM Physical Volume.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.vgcreate
observations: vgcreate [OPTIONS] VG_NAME DEVICE... — Create a Volume Group from one or more PVs.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.lvcreate
observations: lvcreate [OPTIONS] -L SIZE -n LV_NAME VG_NAME — Create a Logical Volume.

name: linux.filesystem.cmd.cryptsetup
observations: cryptsetup [OPTIONS] COMMAND — Manage LUKS-encrypted block devices.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl
observations: kubectl [COMMAND] [TYPE/NAME] [FLAGS] — The Kubernetes CLI. Talks to API server. Resource-oriented commands (get/describe/edit/apply/delete) + functional (logs/exec/port-forward/cp). Reads ~/.kube/config; --context overrides.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-get
observations: kubectl get [TYPE[/NAME]] [FLAGS] — List or display resources. Default brief table; -o yaml for full spec; -o jsonpath for scripting.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-describe
observations: kubectl describe TYPE/NAME — Human-readable per-resource detail INCLUDING events. The first command for 'why isn't this working?' triage.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-logs
observations: kubectl logs POD [-c CONTAINER] [FLAGS] — Container logs (stdout+stderr). For multi-container pods, -c CONTAINER required (or default). Reads from kubelet, which reads from container runtime, which writes to /var/log/pods/.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-exec
observations: kubectl exec POD [-c CONTAINER] [-it] -- COMMAND — Exec command inside running container. Like docker exec.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-debug
observations: kubectl debug POD [-c CONTAINER] [--image=IMAGE] [--target=CONTAINER] [-it] — Add an ephemeral debug container to a running pod (or copy pod with modifications). For debugging distroless containers without shell, or replicating a pod with debug tools.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-apply
observations: kubectl apply -f FILE_OR_DIR [FLAGS] — Declarative create-or-update. Reads manifest(s); diffs against live state via last-applied-configuration annotation; applies changes. The standard deployment command.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-delete
observations: kubectl delete TYPE/NAME [FLAGS] — Delete resources. Triggers finalizers; respects ownerReferences (cascading delete).

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-rollout
observations: kubectl rollout SUBCOMMAND DEPLOYMENT/NAME — Manage Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet rollouts.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-port-forward
observations: kubectl port-forward TYPE/NAME LOCAL:REMOTE — Tunnel from local machine to pod (or service). Local connections forwarded over kubectl→apiserver→kubelet→container.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-cp
observations: kubectl cp [POD:]SRC [POD:]DST [FLAGS] — Copy files in/out of containers. Implemented via tar piped over exec.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-config
observations: kubectl config SUBCOMMAND — Manage kubeconfig.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-explain
observations: kubectl explain TYPE[.FIELD] — Show field documentation for a resource type. Built from API schema. Indispensable for 'what fields does X have' without leaving terminal.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-top
observations: kubectl top {nodes|pods} [FLAGS] — Resource usage. Requires metrics-server installed in cluster (provides Resource Metrics API).

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-events
observations: kubectl events [-n NS] [--for=TYPE/NAME] [--watch] — Cluster events. Modern (1.23+) replacement for `kubectl get events`. Better formatting and filtering.

name: k8s.core.cmd.kubectl-drain
observations: kubectl drain NODE [FLAGS] — Cordon node + evict pods. For node maintenance. Respects PDBs.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-expose
observations: kubectl expose RESOURCE NAME [FLAGS] — Imperatively create a Service exposing a Pod/Deployment/ReplicaSet/Service. Quick way to make a workload reachable.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-get-endpoints
observations: kubectl get endpoints [NAME] | kubectl get endpointslices — List Service backing pods. Empty endpoints = no pods match selector or no pods Ready. EndpointSlices is the modern partitioned version.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-port-forward-svc
observations: kubectl port-forward svc/NAME LOCAL:REMOTE — Tunnel from local to a Service (picks one backing pod). Useful for accessing in-cluster services without exposing externally.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-create-ingress
observations: kubectl create ingress NAME --rule=HOST/PATH=SERVICE:PORT — Imperatively create an Ingress.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-get-svc
observations: kubectl get svc [-o wide] — List Services with type, ClusterIP, ExternalIP, Ports, Age.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-get-ingress
observations: kubectl get ingress — List Ingress resources with hosts, addresses, ports.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-get-netpol
observations: kubectl get networkpolicy / netpol — List NetworkPolicies. Default deny patterns visible here.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.dig-cluster-dns
observations: kubectl run dnsutils --image=tutum/dnsutils --rm -it -- dig SVC.NS.svc.cluster.local — Diagnostic: resolve cluster DNS from inside cluster.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.iptables-save-kube-proxy
observations: iptables-save -t nat | grep KUBE — Inspect kube-proxy's iptables rules on a node. The actual DNAT rules implementing Service VIPs.

name: k8s.networking.cmd.kubectl-get-eps-watch
observations: kubectl get endpoints --watch — Watch endpoints change as pods become ready/unready. Useful for debugging readiness probes / pod recycling.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.crictl
observations: crictl SUBCOMMAND [FLAGS] — CRI-direct CLI on node. Bypasses kubelet+API. For low-level container/sandbox/image debugging when kubectl isn't usable.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-cluster-info
observations: kubectl cluster-info [dump] — Quick check of cluster reachability; dump for full state collection.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-events-debug
observations: kubectl events [--for=TYPE/NAME] [--watch] — Modern event listing. Better filtering than `kubectl get events`.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-debug-node
observations: kubectl debug node/NODE -it --image=IMAGE — Schedule privileged debug pod on node with hostPath rootfs. `chroot /host` to act as host root.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-rollout-status-debug
observations: kubectl rollout status deploy/NAME --watch — Watch a rollout to see if it completes or stalls. Diagnoses progressDeadlineSeconds-style stalls.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-get-pod-yaml-status
observations: kubectl get pod NAME -o yaml — Full pod state including containerStatuses (waiting/running/terminated reasons), conditions, hostIP/podIP, qosClass.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-get-pdb
observations: kubectl get pdb [NAME] — List PodDisruptionBudgets. Required to understand drain blocking.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.journalctl-kubelet
observations: journalctl -u kubelet -f [-n N] — Kubelet logs on the node. Required for: pod admission rejections, mount errors, runtime issues, eviction decisions.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-api-resources
observations: kubectl api-resources [-o wide] — List all API resources known to cluster. Includes CRDs. Useful for 'what kinds exist'.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-api-versions
observations: kubectl api-versions — List enabled API versions in cluster.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-get-leases
observations: kubectl get lease -n kube-node-lease — Per-node heartbeat leases. Stale lease = node potentially down.

name: k8s.debugging.cmd.kubectl-auth-can-i
observations: kubectl auth can-i VERB RESOURCE [--as=USER] — RBAC permission check. 'Can I create deployments?'

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.kubelet
observations: kubelet [FLAGS] — Per-node K8s agent. Started by systemd: `systemctl status kubelet`. Most config now in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml (KubeletConfiguration); fewer command-line flags.

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.kube-proxy
observations: kube-proxy [FLAGS] — Per-node networking agent. Programs iptables/IPVS/nftables for Service VIP→pod-IP mapping.

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.containerd
observations: containerd [FLAGS] | ctr [FLAGS] SUBCOMMAND — containerd daemon + ctr (low-level CLI for containerd). Note: ctr is for direct containerd ops; for K8s use crictl (which goes through CRI).

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.runc
observations: runc SUBCOMMAND [FLAGS] — OCI runtime CLI. Containerd invokes runc to actually create containers. Direct invocation rare; useful for low-level reproductions.

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.systemd-cgls-k8s
observations: systemd-cgls /kubepods.slice — Visualize kubelet's cgroup hierarchy. See per-pod, per-QoS-class, per-container slicing.

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.cgroup-inspect-pod
observations: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/kubepods.slice/.../cri-containerd-CID.scope/{memory.max,cpu.max,memory.current,cpu.stat} — Read cgroup v2 control files for a pod's container directly.

name: k8s.runtime.cmd.kubectl-get-runtimeclass
observations: kubectl get runtimeclass — List RuntimeClasses (gvisor, kata, runc, etc.).

name: devin.devbox.cmd.install-devin-cli
observations: curl -fsSL https://cli.devin.ai/install.sh | bash — Install Devin for Terminal (the local CLI agent). One-shot installer that fetches and runs the install script over HTTPS. Minimum ~1 minute time-to-prompt after install.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.devin-edit-bashrc
observations: devin ~/.bashrc — Open a file inside DevBox in the embedded VS Code instance. Used during repo setup to edit the user shell init file (PATH, per-repo nvm-use hooks, direnv). Equivalent of `code <file>` in VS Code's CLI.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.direnv-allow
observations: direnv allow — Authorize direnv to load the current directory's `.envrc` file. Required once per repo after creating or modifying `.envrc` — direnv refuses to load unauthorized files for security.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.nvm-install
observations: nvm install <version> — Install a specific Node.js version via the pre-installed nvm in DevBox. Combine with `nvm use` to select it for the current shell.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.nvm-use
observations: nvm use <version> — Activate a specific Node.js version in the current shell. Typically called from a ~/.bashrc cd-hook so it auto-runs when entering a repo directory.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.choco-install
observations: choco install <package> [-y] [--version=<v>] — Install a package via Chocolatey on Windows DevBox. The default Windows package manager option in DevBox blueprints.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.winget-install
observations: winget install --id <package-id> --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements — Install a package via winget on Windows DevBox. Alternative to Chocolatey; preferred for Microsoft-published SDKs.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.blockdiff-create
observations: blockdiff create <output.bdiff> <target.img> [--base <base.img>] — Create a block-level diff (.bdiff) of `target.img` against `base.img`, or compactify `target.img` if --base is omitted. The DevBox snapshot infra primitive — fast block-level VM disk diffs using CoW filesystem metadata.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.blockdiff-apply
observations: blockdiff apply <input.bdiff> <target.img> [--base <base.img>] — Apply a .bdiff to produce a target image. With --base, reconstructs target from base + diff. Without --base, materializes a sparse target image from a compactified diff.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.subshell-cd
observations: (cd <subdir> && <command>) — Run a blueprint or shell command in a subshell with a temporary working directory change. The canonical monorepo pattern in DevBox blueprints — working directory resets after the subshell exits, so the next blueprint step starts fresh.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.openvpn-systemctl-enable
observations: systemctl enable openvpn && systemctl start openvpn — Enable and start the OpenVPN systemd service inside DevBox. Used after creating /etc/systemd/system/openvpn.service to bring up the VPN connection at session boot.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.uv-install
observations: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh — Install uv (Astral's Python package/project manager) in DevBox. Surfaced in the Linux blueprint examples as a fast alternative to pip+venv.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.uv-sync
observations: uv sync — Resolve and install Python dependencies into the project venv per the uv-managed lockfile. Cross-platform (works on Linux and Windows DevBox).

name: devin.devbox.cmd.dotnet-restore
observations: dotnet restore — .NET project dependency restore. Used in Windows blueprints for .NET repositories.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.msbuild-restore
observations: msbuild /t:Restore <Solution.sln> — Restore a Visual Studio C++ solution's NuGet packages via MSBuild. Used in C++ Windows blueprints.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.msbuild-build
observations: msbuild <Solution.sln> /p:Configuration=Release — Build a VS C++ solution in Release configuration via MSBuild.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.vstest-console
observations: vstest.console.exe <TestDll> — Run unit tests via the Visual Studio test runner. Used as the test command in Windows C++ blueprints.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.dotnet-format-check
observations: dotnet format --verify-no-changes — Verify that .NET code is already formatted (no changes would be made). Suitable as a lint command — exits non-zero if the source needs formatting.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.npm-install
observations: npm install — Install Node.js dependencies. Surfaced as the canonical `maintenance` example in Devin's docs because it's fast and incremental (does not enforce package-lock.json strictly the way `npm ci` does).

name: devin.devbox.cmd.pip-install-r
observations: pip install -r requirements.txt — Install Python dependencies from a requirements file. Surfaced as a canonical Maintenance example in repo-setup docs.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.npm-script
observations: npm run <script> — Run an npm script defined in package.json. Used in blueprint `knowledge` entries to wire up lint / test / build commands.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-build-snapshot
observations: [UI] Settings > Environment > Snapshots > Build snapshot — Manually trigger a new build of the active blueprint(s). Equivalent to a user-initiated build trigger; the periodic refresh and blueprint-save triggers cover most cases automatically.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-pin-snapshot
observations: [UI] Settings > Environment > Snapshots > Pin — Pin the org to a specific snapshot. Pinnable builds must be Success or Partial and < 7 days old. While pinned: periodic refreshes are skipped; UI shows 'Auto-updates paused'.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-resume-auto-updates
observations: [UI] Settings > Environment > Snapshots > Resume auto-updates — Unpin the snapshot, returning to the latest successful build and re-enabling periodic refreshes.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-restore-snapshot
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's Machine > Version History > Restore — Roll back to a previous snapshot from version history. Used when a setup change accidentally broke the environment.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-add-repository
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's Machine > Add repository — Add a repository to Devin's environment. Triggers entry into the repo-setup wizard (classic) or blueprint editor (declarative). Only one classic-mode setup can be in progress at a time.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-index-repo
observations: [UI] Settings > Repositories > Index repo — Build a search/understanding index over a repo. Required for Ask Devin and DeepWiki. Distinct from environment configuration.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-large-performant-toggle
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's Workspace > Danger Zone > switch to Large Performant (Beta) — Migrate an existing team's DevBox to the Large Performant VM tier (improved Docker storage / perf). Default for new teams. Requires resetting machine setup; experimental auto-migration available via support@cognition.ai.

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-set-usage-budget
observations: [UI] Settings > Plans > Manage Plan Limits (or Usage and Limits > Manage Additional Usage Budget) — Set the additional usage budget cap for pay-as-you-go ACU billing. Sessions stop after monthly capacity + this budget is exhausted; billed at end of cycle or when usage exceeds $2,000 (whichever comes first).

name: devin.devbox.cmd.ui-disconnect-integration
observations: [UI] Settings > Integrations > [GitHub|Slack] > Disconnect — Disconnect an integration that's blocking a new connection (because another Devin org/enterprise already holds it). Required when migrating an org's GitHub or Slack integration to a different Devin account.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.mention-devin-slack
observations: @Devin <message> — Trigger a Devin session in Slack from any channel by tagging @Devin. Devin responds in-thread; users continue the conversation in the thread. Attachments supported.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.mention-devin-teams
observations: @Devin <message> — Trigger a Devin session from a Microsoft Teams channel or chat. Devin responds in-thread.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.ask
observations: !ask <question> — Get a quick codebase answer without spinning up a full agent session. Available in Slack and Teams. Lower-cost alternative to a full session for read-only questions.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.deep
observations: !deep <question> — Deeper research answer using advanced search. Higher-effort variant of !ask. Available in Slack and Teams.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.mute
observations: mute (or @Devin mute) — Prevent Devin from seeing further messages in the current thread. Useful when humans need to confer without Devin reacting.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.unmute
observations: unmute (or @Devin unmute) — Re-enable Devin's processing of thread messages after a `mute`.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.aside
observations: (aside) <message>  OR  !aside <message> — Cause Devin to ignore a single message (useful for commenting on Devin's run directly in-thread without affecting Devin's behavior).

name: devin.integrations.cmd.sleep
observations: sleep — Put Devin to sleep on the current task. Send any message in the thread to wake Devin back up.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.archive
observations: archive (or @Devin archive) — Put Devin to sleep AND archive the session. Cleaner than `sleep` for sessions you're done with.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.exit
observations: EXIT — End the current Devin session immediately.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.help
observations: help — Show the available inline keywords and functions. Available in Microsoft Teams.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.dana-slack
observations: !dana <message> — Slack-only: launch a Dana session (Cognition's data-analyst agent variant). Equivalent to `!dana` triggers in the Slack inline-keyword set.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.macro-slack
observations: ![macro_name] <message> — Slack-only: invoke a named playbook macro at session start. Examples include user-defined `![ship-it]`, `![investigate]`, etc.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.fast-slack
observations: !fast <message> — Slack-only: launch a fast-mode Devin session. Trades off depth for speed.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.jira-assign-to-devin
observations: [Jira] Assign ticket to Devin — Trigger a Devin session from Jira by assigning the ticket to Devin's service account. Uses the default playbook configured in the Jira integration settings.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.jira-add-playbook-label
observations: [Jira] Add playbook-macro label — Trigger Devin with a specific playbook by adding a label whose name matches the macro (e.g., `!plan`, `!implement`, `!triage`).

name: devin.integrations.cmd.jira-add-devin-label
observations: [Jira] Add `devin` label (or any label containing 'devin' as a standalone word) — Trigger Devin using the default playbook by adding a generic devin-label. Word-boundary matching, case-insensitive: `devin`, `Devin`, `devin-workshop`, `devin-task` all match. `devinworkshop` and `devin_workshop` do NOT.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.jira-mention-comment
observations: [Jira] @Devin <instructions> (in ticket comment) — Trigger Devin from a Jira ticket comment. Devin uses the comment text as the task instruction (no playbook applied). If a session already exists for the ticket, the comment is forwarded to that session.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.linear-assign-to-devin
observations: [Linear] Assign ticket to Devin — Trigger Devin from Linear via assignment. Uses the default playbook (`!plan` for new connections).

name: devin.integrations.cmd.linear-add-playbook-label
observations: [Linear] Add synced playbook label — Trigger Devin with a specific playbook by adding a label from the 'Devin Playbooks' label group.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.linear-mention-comment
observations: [Linear] @Devin <instructions> (in ticket comment) — Trigger Devin from a Linear ticket comment with custom instructions. No playbook applied.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.ui-disconnect-github
observations: [GitHub] github.com/settings/installations > Devin.ai Integration > Configure > Danger zone > Uninstall — Remove Devin's GitHub App installation from a GitHub organization — required when migrating an org's Devin integration to a different Devin account.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.ui-rename-slack-bot
observations: [Slack] Workspace Admin > Configure apps > Installed Apps > Devin > App Details > Configuration tab > Bot User > rename — Rename Devin in a Slack workspace (the bot's display name).

name: devin.integrations.cmd.ui-enable-slack-notifications
observations: [Devin run UI] menu > Enable Slack notifications — Enable per-run private Slack notifications. Devin DMs the user on status updates for that session.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.aws-create-nlb
observations: [AWS] Create Network Load Balancer with security groups for Devin egress IPs — Stand up an NLB to front a self-hosted SCM/artifact endpoint, configured with security-group rules per Devin egress IP. Required for the manual-security-groups self-hosted setup pattern (NLB preserves source IPs).

name: devin.integrations.cmd.aws-create-alb-with-waf
observations: [AWS] Create Application Load Balancer + WAF with IP-allowlist rule — Stand up an ALB fronting a self-hosted endpoint, with AWS WAF enforcing IP allowlist. Recommended for most use cases. NOTE: ALB NATs source IPs — for artifact repos, IP allowlisting must ALSO be configured at the artifact repo itself.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.aws-route53-dns-change
observations: [AWS] aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id <id> --change-batch file://dns-change.json — Publish a DNS record pointing at the load balancer that fronts the self-hosted endpoint, so Devin can reach it via a stable domain name.

name: devin.integrations.cmd.email-enterprise-support
observations: Email enterprise@cognition.ai with self-hosted SCM URL + artifact repo URL + auth requirements — Hand off self-hosted-SCM/artifacts integration to Cognition support after the network plumbing is ready. Cognition completes the connection from their side.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.docker-pull-toolbox
observations: docker pull us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/database-toolbox/toolbox/toolbox:latest — Pull the universal Database Toolbox Docker image. One image powers all 22+ database integrations; pulled once before configuring per-database.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.docker-run-toolbox-prebuilt-postgres
observations: docker run --rm -i ... us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/database-toolbox/toolbox/toolbox:latest --prebuilt postgres --stdio — Run the Database Toolbox Docker image as an MCP server in STDIO mode against PostgreSQL using the prebuilt config. Requires POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_DATABASE, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD env vars.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.docker-run-toolbox-tools-file
observations: docker run --rm -i ... -v <yaml>:/config/<db>.yaml ... toolbox:latest --tools-file /config/<db>.yaml --stdio — Run the Database Toolbox in STDIO mode against a database that requires a custom tools-file YAML (Bigtable, Couchbase, Dgraph, MongoDB, Neo4j, Redis, Redshift, Snowflake, SQLite, TiDB, Valkey).

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npx-metabase-default
observations: npx @cognitionai/metabase-mcp-server — Run the Metabase MCP server in default (essential-tools) mode. Loads the smaller, curated tool set.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npx-metabase-all
observations: npx @cognitionai/metabase-mcp-server --all — Run the Metabase MCP server with ALL 80+ tools loaded. Use when you need the full Metabase API surface.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npx-metabase-read
observations: npx @cognitionai/metabase-mcp-server --read — Run the Metabase MCP server with read-only tools only. Recommended for production-data scenarios where Devin should not modify Metabase state.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npx-metabase-write
observations: npx @cognitionai/metabase-mcp-server --write — Run the Metabase MCP server with write/modification tools only. Used in dedicated write-path workflows.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npm-install-metabase
observations: npm install -g @cognitionai/metabase-mcp-server && metabase-mcp-server — Globally install the Metabase MCP server and run via the binary directly. Alternative to npx.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.docker-run-metabase
observations: docker run -it --rm -e METABASE_URL=... -e METABASE_API_KEY=... ghcr.io/CognitionAI/metabase-mcp-server — Run the Metabase MCP server from the prebuilt Docker image hosted on ghcr.io.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.curl-slack-auth-test
observations: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-<token>" https://slack.com/api/auth.test — Probe Slack to retrieve the team_id (required for the Slack MCP marketplace integration). Returns the workspace-team identifier under which the bot token was issued.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.curl-slack-conversations-list
observations: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-<token>" https://slack.com/api/conversations.list — List Slack channel IDs visible to the bot. Used to map channel names to IDs for the Slack MCP marketplace integration. Requires bot scopes channels:read, groups:read, mpim:read, im:read.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.ui-mcp-marketplace-enable
observations: [UI] Settings > MCP Marketplace > <server> > Enable — Enable a marketplace MCP server for the org. For 1-click servers, just click Enable. For configured servers, provide credentials/headers in the form first.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.ui-add-your-own-mcp
observations: [UI] Settings > MCP Marketplace > Add Your Own — Configure a custom MCP server. Form-driven: name, optional icon, description, transport (STDIO/SSE/HTTP), transport-specific config. Save, then click 'Test listing tools' to verify connectivity.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.ui-test-listing-tools
observations: [UI] Settings > MCP Marketplace > <server> > Test listing tools — Spin up an isolated test environment, connect to the MCP server, and discover tools via tools/list. Disabled until the config is saved. Failures categorize as connectivity / authentication / timeout.

name: devin.mcp.cmd.npx-uvx-stdio-server
observations: STDIO server: command=npx|uvx|docker, args=[...], env={...} — Generic shape for a custom STDIO MCP server. The 'command' is a launcher (npx/uvx/docker); 'args' is the command-line arg list; 'env' carries the secrets/config the server reads.

name: devin.api.cmd.curl-self
observations: GET /v3/self — Verify credentials and identify the authenticated principal. Returns principal_type ('service_user'|'user'), service_user_id, service_user_name, org_id (null for enterprise-scoped). The first call in any auth-debug flow.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-enterprise-organizations
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/organizations — List organizations under the enterprise. For enterprise service users to enumerate orgs they can act on.

name: devin.api.cmd.create-session-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions — Create a Devin session. Body fields: prompt (required), title (optional), playbook (optional), tags (optional), ACU limit (optional), create_as_user_id (optional, requires ImpersonateOrgSessions).

name: devin.api.cmd.get-session-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id} — Retrieve session status, prompt, output, and metadata. Used to poll lifecycle (`status` in {'running','exit','error','suspended'}).

name: devin.api.cmd.list-session-messages-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/messages — List all messages exchanged with a session. Used for follow-up monitoring or transcript export.

name: devin.api.cmd.send-session-message-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/messages — Send a follow-up message to a session. Continues the agent conversation.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-sessions-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions — List sessions in an org. Cursor-paginated. Filterable on creation/update time, tags, playbook, schedule, etc.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-sessions-insights-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/insights — List sessions with their AI-generated insights attached. Insights summarize session behavior post-hoc.

name: devin.api.cmd.get-session-insights-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/insights — Retrieve AI-generated insights for a single session.

name: devin.api.cmd.generate-session-insights-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/insights/generate — Trigger generation of insights for a session. Returns the new/updated insights record.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-session-attachments-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/attachments — List attachments produced/uploaded during a session. Each item has attachment_id, name, and url to download.

name: devin.api.cmd.get-session-tags-v3
observations: GET /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Retrieve the tags currently set on a session.

name: devin.api.cmd.append-session-tags-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Append tags to a session without removing existing ones.

name: devin.api.cmd.replace-session-tags-v3
observations: PUT /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Replace the full tag set on a session (idempotent set semantics).

name: devin.api.cmd.archive-session-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id}/archive — Archive a completed session (sleep + archive). Removes from active list.

name: devin.api.cmd.terminate-session-v3
observations: DELETE /v3/organizations/{org_id}/sessions/{session_id} — Terminate (and delete) a session. Permanent.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-enterprise-sessions-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions — Cross-org list of sessions for the entire enterprise account. Read-only by default.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-enterprise-sessions-insights-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/insights — Enterprise sessions with insights attached.

name: devin.api.cmd.get-enterprise-session-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id} — Get enterprise-scoped session detail (cross-org).

name: devin.api.cmd.list-enterprise-session-attachments-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/attachments — Enterprise-scoped session attachments list.

name: devin.api.cmd.list-enterprise-session-messages-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/messages — Enterprise-scoped session message list.

name: devin.api.cmd.send-enterprise-session-message-v3
observations: POST /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/messages — Send a message to a session from the enterprise scope.

name: devin.api.cmd.get-enterprise-session-tags-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Enterprise-scoped tag retrieval.

name: devin.api.cmd.append-enterprise-session-tags-v3
observations: POST /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Enterprise-scoped append tags.

name: devin.api.cmd.replace-enterprise-session-tags-v3
observations: PUT /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/tags — Enterprise-scoped replace tags.

name: devin.api.cmd.get-enterprise-session-insights-v3
observations: GET /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/insights — Enterprise-scoped session insights.

name: devin.api.cmd.generate-enterprise-session-insights-v3
observations: POST /v3/enterprise/sessions/{session_id}/insights/generate — Enterprise-scoped insights generation.

name: devin.api.cmd.upload-attachment-v3
observations: POST /v3/organizations/{org_id}/attachments — Upload a file as an attachment for sessions to use.

name: devin.api.cmd.download-attachment-v3

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-rollout-mode
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Rollout > Rollout mode dropdown — Set the enterprise-wide rollout mode for declarative environments (Not enabled / Testing / Available / Enabled by default). Switches between Testing and Available are reversible; Enabled-by-default is permanent (requires Cognition admin to undo).

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-per-org-override-in
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Rollout > per-org table > opt org IN to blueprints — Switch a specific organization to declarative blueprints (Testing/Available mode). Overrides the enterprise default for that org.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-per-org-override-out
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Rollout > per-org table > opt org OUT (back to classic) — Roll an org back to classic setup from blueprints. Configurations are preserved; takes effect on next session. Active sessions unaffected.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-base-environment-edit
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's base environment > edit blueprint — Edit the enterprise-tier blueprint (initialize/maintenance/knowledge sections). Saved changes trigger an enterprise-wide rebuild across all orgs.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-base-environment-secrets
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's base environment > Secrets tab — Manage enterprise-wide secrets. Available across all orgs/sessions. Requires ManageAccountResources permission.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-create-custom-role
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Roles > Create a custom role — Create a custom org-level or account-level role with selected permissions. Requires Manage Account Membership permission. Both Organization-level and Enterprise-level role types supported.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-assign-account-role
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Enterprise members > Assign account-level role — Assign an account-level (enterprise-wide) role to a user. Account-level roles inherit corresponding org-level permissions in every org. Requires Manage Account Membership.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-assign-org-role
observations: [UI] Org Settings > Organization members > Assign organization-level role — Assign an org-level role within a specific organization. Requires Manage Organization Membership permission.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-idp-group-mapping
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Members > Configure IdP group mappings — Map IdP group names to Devin roles for SSO auto-assignment. SSO provider must send `groups` array in the assertion.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-rollout-filter
observations: [UI] Enterprise Settings > Rollout > per-org table > filter dropdown — Filter the per-org table by All / Blueprints / Classic / Overrides. Used to find unmigrated orgs during phased rollout.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.ui-trigger-enterprise-rebuild
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's base environment > trigger enterprise-wide rebuild — Cascade a fresh build across ALL organizations. Used after enterprise-blueprint update or enterprise-secret rotation.

name: devin.enterprise.cmd.email-enterprise-sales
observations: Email enterprise@cognition.ai for Customer Dedicated Deployment setup — Initiate Customer Dedicated Deployment setup. Cognition Enterprise Sales handles networking discussion (PrivateLink vs IPSec, customer VPC topology).

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-devin-review-open
observations: [UI] Open Devin Review at app.devin.ai/review — Land on the Devin Review surface — your open PRs organized by category. Entry point for code review workflow.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-review-merge-pr
observations: [UI] Devin Review > PR detail > Merge — Merge a PR directly from Devin Review without leaving the page.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-review-toggle-auto-merge
observations: [UI] Devin Review > PR detail > Toggle auto-merge — Toggle GitHub auto-merge on/off from inside Devin Review.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-review-chat-edit
observations: [UI] Devin Review > chat > 'Make this change' > Apply as commit — Ask the chat agent for code edits, review the suggestions, and apply as a commit to the PR branch from inside Devin Review.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-add-knowledge
observations: [UI] Settings > Devin's Settings > Knowledge > Add knowledge — Add product-Knowledge-feature entries (architecture docs, conventions, team workflows) used by Devin across sessions in a repo.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-create-playbook
observations: [UI] Settings > Playbooks > Create playbook — Create a reusable instruction set with optional macro identifier. Macros (e.g., `!plan`, `!review`) become triggers in Slack/Teams/Jira/Linear.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-create-schedule
observations: [UI] Settings > Schedules > Create schedule — Create a recurring or one-time scheduled session.

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-add-secret

name: devin.product.cmd.ui-session-insights-open
observations: [UI] Open session > Session Insights tab — View per-session ACU usage, timeline, and AI-generated summary.

name: devin.product.cmd.cli-install-devin

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cmd.ui-add-knowledge

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cmd.ui-add-secret

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cmd.api-knowledge-manage
observations: MCP tool: devin_knowledge_manage — Programmatic full CRUD on knowledge notes + suggestions via the Devin MCP server. Filterable by repo/folder/search.

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.uprobe
observations: bpftrace -e 'uprobe:<binary>:<symbol> { ... }' — User-space dynamic tracing — attach to any function in any binary at runtime. Higher overhead than kprobes due to user/kernel boundary crossing.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.biolatency
observations: biolatency — Block-device I/O latency as a power-of-2 histogram. Reveals tail latency and bimodal distributions that mean-latency hides.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.gethostlatency
observations: gethostlatency — Trace getaddrinfo/gethostbyname (DNS lookup) latency at the libresolver level. Identifies slow DNS as an application-latency cause.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.tpoint
observations: tpoint — ftrace-based tracepoint tracer with optional filter and stack-trace capture.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.probe
observations: perf probe — Add or remove dynamic tracepoints (kprobes/uprobes) at runtime. Lets you observe arbitrary kernel or user-space functions with arguments — without recompiling.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.ext4slower
observations: ext4slower — Trace ext4 file-system operations slower than a configurable threshold. Surfaces filesystem-level slow paths without flooding output. (bcc has matching tools for btrfs, xfs, zfs.)

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.funcslower
observations: funcslower — ftrace-based: trace kernel functions that ran slower than a threshold. Filters out the noise of non-slow calls.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.c2c
observations: perf c2c — Cache-line contention analysis (Linux 4.10+). Records and reports cache-line transfers between CPUs — the key signal for false-sharing and NUMA hot spots.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.killsnoop
observations: killsnoop — Trace kill() signals with sender process, target PID, and signal number. Surfaces unexpected SIGKILLs and OOM-killer activity.

name: methodology.cmd.flamegraph.flamegraph
observations: flamegraph.pl — Render a folded-stack file as an interactive SVG FlameGraph. The original implementation; 100+ alternatives now exist (d3-flame-graph, speedscope, etc.).

name: methodology.cmd.perf.stat
observations: perf stat — Count events without recording each one — the lowest-overhead perf mode. Default counts a basic CPU set; -e specifies events; -a is system-wide; -p targets a PID.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.record
observations: perf record — Sample CPU stacks or trace specific events to a perf.data file for later analysis (perf report / perf script / FlameGraph generation). The workhorse for CPU profiling and tracepoint capture.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.syscount
observations: syscount — Count syscalls by syscall name or by process. Quick top-N syscall summary.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.tcpaccept
observations: tcpaccept — Trace TCP accept() syscalls — passive (inbound) connections with PID, source IP, port.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.tcpretrans
observations: tcpretrans — Trace TCP retransmits with addresses, ports, and TCP state. Surfaces network reliability issues without per-packet overhead — retransmits are normally <<1% of traffic.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.trace
observations: trace — Quick per-event tracer for kernel/user functions. Lets you print arguments without writing a bcc script. Format: 'p::FUNC "FMT", expr1, expr2'.

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.profile-time
observations: bpftrace -e 'profile:hz:99 { @[ustack, kstack] = count(); }' — All-CPU mixed kernel/user stack profile via timed sampling — bpftrace's one-liner equivalent of perf record + folded output.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.list
observations: perf list — List events available to perf_events on this kernel — tracepoints, PMC events, software events. The first command to run when planning a perf session.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.top
observations: perf top — Live top-N functions by sample count, refreshed continuously. Like top(1) but for code-paths instead of processes.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.tcplife
observations: tcplife — Trace TCP connection lifetimes — for each completed (closed) connection: PID, comm, addresses, ports, bytes, duration.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.argdist
observations: argdist — One-shot frequency count or histogram of function arguments. Useful for quick distribution analysis without writing a full bpftrace program.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.funclatency
observations: funclatency — Latency (function duration) histogram for kernel/user functions.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.iolatency
observations: iolatency — ftrace-based block I/O latency histogram for older Linux kernels.

name: methodology.cmd.flamegraph.stackcollapse
observations: stackcollapse-perf.pl — Convert perf script output into folded-stack format — one line per unique stack with a leading count. The standard input shape for flamegraph.pl.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.execsnoop
observations: execsnoop — Trace new process creation via the exec() syscall. Prints PID, parent PID, comm, and full argv as each exec() fires. Essential for catching short-lived processes invisible to top/ps.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.iosnoop
observations: iosnoop — ftrace-based per-event block I/O tracer for kernels too old for bcc/eBPF. Disk I/O details with latency.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.trace
observations: perf trace — strace-like tool built on perf_events — much lower overhead than strace because it uses perf's in-kernel buffer instead of ptrace.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.tcpconnect
observations: tcpconnect — Trace TCP connect() syscalls with PID, IP, and port. Captures outbound connection attempts that aren't visible via netstat-style snapshots.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.funccount
observations: funccount — Count kernel (or user) function calls matching a pattern. Discovery tool: which paths fired? -i provides interval-based output.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.functrace
observations: functrace — ftrace dynamic tracer of kernel function calls matching a pattern.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.funcgraph
observations: funcgraph — ftrace function-call graph with timing — shows children and durations of a kernel function.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.bashreadline
observations: bashreadline — Trace commands as they're typed at any bash prompt on the system (uprobe on bash's readline).

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.opensnoop
observations: opensnoop — Trace open() syscalls system-wide, printing process and full file path as files are opened.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.script
observations: perf script — Dump every event from perf.data as text, one line per event with timestamp, comm, PID, stack. The raw form needed for custom post-processing (flame graphs, sequence analysis).

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.kprobe
observations: bpftrace -e 'kprobe:<func> { ... }' — Attach a kprobe to a kernel function and run a BPF action block. The most common bpftrace shape for kernel-side dynamic tracing.

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.profile
observations: bpftrace -e 'profile:hz:99 { ... }' — Timed sampling — fire on every CPU at the specified rate. Equivalent to perf record -F for sampling + bpftrace's expressive aggregations.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.biosnoop
observations: biosnoop — Per-event block I/O trace — comm, PID, disk, R/W, sector, bytes, latency for every I/O. The drill-down companion to biolatency's histogram.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.profile
observations: profile — Timed CPU stack-trace sampling using eBPF (not perf record) — far more efficient on Linux 4.9+ because it summarizes in kernel context.

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.tracepoint
observations: bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:<category>:<name> { ... }' — Attach to a stable kernel tracepoint (more durable across kernel versions than kprobes). Discoverable via bpftrace -l 'tracepoint:*'.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.cachestat
observations: cachestat — Linux page-cache hit/miss/dirty stats summarized per second. Surfaces page-cache effectiveness; low hit rates suggest working-set > RAM or anti-pattern access.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.cpudist
observations: cpudist — Histogram of on-CPU or off-CPU run lengths per task. -O switches from on-CPU to off-CPU mode.

name: methodology.cmd.bpftrace.list
observations: bpftrace -l — List available probes matching a glob — discovery before attaching.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.kprobe
observations: perf-tools/kprobe — ftrace-based wrapper to dynamically trace any kernel function call or its return with variables. Simpler interface than 'perf probe' for one-off investigation.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.runqlat
observations: runqlat — Run-queue latency histogram — time threads spent waiting on the CPU run queue before being scheduled. Direct measurement of CPU saturation in USE-method terms.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.offcputime
observations: offcputime — Aggregate per-stack off-CPU time using kernel context-switch tracing. The canonical off-CPU analysis tool for Linux. Output is folded-stack-format suitable for FlameGraph.

name: methodology.cmd.bcc.stackcount
observations: stackcount — Count stack traces leading to a given function or tracepoint. Answers 'who calls X?' across the kernel — find which code paths trigger an event.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.report
observations: perf report — Display a perf.data file as a hierarchical (tree) summary with percentages. Default UI is the ncurses TUI; --stdio for text output. The default consumer of perf.data after perf record.

name: methodology.cmd.perf.annotate
observations: perf annotate — Disassemble hot functions and overlay percentages from perf.data on each instruction. Shows precisely which line is hot inside a function.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.bitesize
observations: bitesize — Histogram of disk I/O sizes by process — power-of-2 buckets. Reveals whether I/O is small-random vs large-sequential.

name: methodology.cmd.perftools.uprobe
observations: perf-tools/uprobe — ftrace-based wrapper for user-level dynamic tracing — counterpart to perf-tools/kprobe but for user functions.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-api-version
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_GET_API_VERSION) — Returns the stable KVM API version (always 12 since the API stabilized). Firecracker calls this at init and aborts if the value differs — earlier (2.6.20/2.6.21) versions are unsupported.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-check-extension
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd_or_vm_fd, KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION, capability) — Probe whether the host KVM supports a given KVM_CAP_*. System-fd form returns the global default; VM-fd form may return a per-VM value (e.g. KVM_CAP_NR_VCPUS). Firecracker probes capabilities at init and refuses to start if a required one is missing.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-create-vm
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_CREATE_VM, machine_type) — Create a new VM. Returns a VM fd. machine_type identifier is 0 for default; on aarch64 encodes IPA size with KVM_VM_TYPE_ARM_IPA_SIZE().

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-create-vcpu
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_CREATE_VCPU, vcpu_id) — Create a vCPU. Returns a vCPU fd. vcpu_id starts at 0 and must be < KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS. Firecracker creates one vCPU thread per ID; each thread runs KVM_RUN in a loop.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-vcpu-mmap-size
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE) — Returns the size (in bytes) of the kvm_run struct that userspace must mmap on each vCPU fd. Firecracker calls this once and reuses the size for every vCPU.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-user-memory-region
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION, &region) — Map a host userspace memory range into the guest physical address space. Slot ID identifies the region; size 0 deletes a slot. Firecracker registers one large region for guest RAM; snapshot restore replays the same regions.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-user-memory-region2
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION2, &region) — Like KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION but supports guest_memfd-backed regions (KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD flag) for confidential-VM cases. Available when KVM_CAP_USER_MEMORY2 is supported.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-dirty-log
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG, &log) — Atomically copy + clear the dirty-page bitmap for a memory region. Backbone of incremental snapshots — Firecracker calls this per region during a diff snapshot.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-clear-dirty-log
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG, &log) — Clear specific bits of the dirty bitmap without copying. Used with KVM_DIRTY_LOG_MANUAL_PROTECT_ENABLE / KVM_DIRTY_LOG_INITIALLY_SET to decouple read and clear (lets userspace read first, then selectively clear after persisting).

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-run
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_RUN) — Enter the guest. Returns when the vCPU exits; userspace inspects kvm_run.exit_reason, handles the exit (MMIO/PIO/SHUTDOWN/etc.), and re-enters. The entire CPU-virt fast path. ALL guest execution happens between calls to this ioctl.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-interrupt
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_INTERRUPT, &irq) — Inject a synchronous interrupt vector into the guest. Used when Firecracker has a userspace-emulated PIC (rarely — Firecracker prefers in-kernel irqchip). Asserting an in-kernel-PIC IRQ uses KVM_IRQ_LINE instead.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-irq-line
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_IRQ_LINE, &irq_level) — Assert or deassert an in-kernel-irqchip IRQ. Faster than KVM_INTERRUPT because it doesn't context-switch the vCPU. Firecracker uses this for serial-console TX-ready and other userspace-driven IRQs.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-create-irqchip
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_CREATE_IRQCHIP) — Instantiate the in-kernel PIC + IOAPIC + LAPIC (x86) or pre-bind preparation for ARM GIC creation via KVM_CREATE_DEVICE. Must be called BEFORE creating any vCPU. Firecracker always creates the in-kernel irqchip — userspace-irqchip mode is too slow.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-gsi-routing
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_GSI_ROUTING, &routing) — Install or replace the GSI routing table — maps GSIs to in-kernel IRQchip pin / MSI / HV SINT. Firecracker programs this so MSIs from VirtIO devices land directly on the right vCPU.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-signal-msi
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SIGNAL_MSI, &msi) — Inject an MSI directly without going through the routing table. Useful for one-shot interrupts (e.g. VirtIO config-change) that don't have a stable GSI binding.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-irqfd
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_IRQFD, &irqfd) — Bind an eventfd to a GSI. When userspace writes to the eventfd, KVM raises the IRQ on the configured GSI without involving the writing thread further. Backbone of low-latency device-event IRQ delivery.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-ioeventfd
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_IOEVENTFD, &ioev) — Bind an eventfd to be signaled when the guest writes a specific value (or any value) to a specific MMIO/PIO address. Lets the kernel short-circuit doorbell writes — no exit to userspace, just signal the device thread.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-regs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_REGS, &regs) — Set the general-purpose register file (RAX..R15, RIP, RFLAGS) for the vCPU. Used at boot to set up the entry point and during snapshot restore.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-regs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_REGS, &regs) — Read the GPR register file. Used by snapshots to checkpoint vCPU state and by the GDB debug stub.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-sregs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_SREGS, &sregs) — Set special registers — segment selectors, control registers (CR0..CR4, CR8), GDTR/IDTR, EFER, APIC base. Used at boot to set up protected/long mode and during snapshot restore.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-sregs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_SREGS, &sregs) — Read special registers. Pairs with KVM_SET_SREGS for snapshot save.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-msrs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_MSRS, &msrs) — Bulk-write MSRs. Variable-length kvm_msrs struct: nmsrs followed by entries[]. Returns the count actually written; entries past the failure point are skipped.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-msrs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_MSRS, &msrs) — Bulk-read MSRs. Pre-fill entries with the MSR indices to read; KVM populates the .data fields.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-msr-index-list
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_GET_MSR_INDEX_LIST, &list) — Enumerate MSRs the host KVM knows about. Variable-length result. Firecracker uses this to build the snapshot MSR set, intersected with CPU-template-allowed MSRs.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-cpuid2
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_CPUID2, &cpuid) — Define the CPUID leaves the guest sees. Variable-length: nent + entries[] (function/index/flags/eax/ebx/ecx/edx). Firecracker computes this from the chosen CPU template and the host's KVM_GET_SUPPORTED_CPUID intersection.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-supported-cpuid
observations: ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_GET_SUPPORTED_CPUID, &cpuid) — Enumerate CPUID features KVM knows it can virtualize on this host. Firecracker uses the result as the universe from which CPU templates pick.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-fpu
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_FPU, &fpu) — Set legacy FPU/SSE state (fxsave-format). Snapshots use this on hosts without XSAVE2 support.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-fpu
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_FPU, &fpu) — Read legacy FPU/SSE state.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-xsave2
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_XSAVE2, &xsave) — Set extended-state (XSAVE) area. Variable-size — query KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION(KVM_CAP_XSAVE2) for the size on this host. Required for AVX/AVX-512 state.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-xsave2
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_XSAVE2, &xsave) — Read extended-state area. Buffer size from KVM_CAP_XSAVE2 query.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-xcrs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_XCRS, &xcrs) — Set the extended control registers (XCR0). Determines which XSAVE features are enabled. Restored as part of snapshot.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-xcrs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_XCRS, &xcrs) — Read extended control registers.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-lapic
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_LAPIC, &state) — Restore Local APIC register file (1 KiB). Required for snapshot consistency — preserves pending interrupts and timer state.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-lapic
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_LAPIC, &state) — Read Local APIC register file.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-mp-state
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_MP_STATE, &mp_state) — Set vCPU MP state (RUNNABLE / HALTED / etc.). Snapshot restore uses this so a halted vCPU stays halted on resume.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-mp-state
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_MP_STATE, &mp_state) — Read vCPU MP state.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-vcpu-events
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS, &events) — Restore pending exceptions, interrupts, NMIs, and SMI state. Critical for snapshot consistency — without this, an in-flight exception is lost on resume.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-vcpu-events
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_VCPU_EVENTS, &events) — Read pending exception/interrupt/NMI/SMI state.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-debugregs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_DEBUGREGS, &dregs) — Set debug registers DR0..DR7. Used by snapshot restore and by the GDB stub for hardware breakpoints.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-debugregs
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_DEBUGREGS, &dregs) — Read debug registers.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-guest-debug
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG, &dbg) — Configure guest debug — single-step, software breakpoints, hardware breakpoints. When set, the vCPU returns KVM_EXIT_DEBUG to userspace on debug events. Powers `firecracker --gdb-socket` mode.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-tsc-khz
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ, khz) — Set the guest's TSC frequency. Required for snapshot restore on a host with a different TSC frequency. KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL must be supported.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-tsc-khz
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ) — Read the guest's TSC frequency in kHz.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-arm-vcpu-init
observations: ioctl(vcpu_fd, KVM_ARM_VCPU_INIT, &init) — ARM-only. Configure the vCPU's target processor and feature flags before first KVM_RUN. Firecracker calls this for each ARM vCPU during init.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-arm-preferred-target
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_ARM_PREFERRED_TARGET, &init) — ARM-only. Returns the preferred CPU target for this host (used as input to KVM_ARM_VCPU_INIT).

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-create-device
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_CREATE_DEVICE, &dev) — Create an in-kernel device. On ARM, used for the GIC (KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3) and PMU. Firecracker uses this only on ARM.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-device-attr
observations: ioctl(dev_fd, KVM_SET_DEVICE_ATTR, &attr) — Configure an in-kernel device. ARM GIC distributor base address, redistributor regions, etc., are set this way.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-tss-addr
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR, addr) — x86 Intel-only. Set the address of a 3-page region used by Intel VT-x for guest-state save (TSS area). Must be set before first KVM_RUN. Firecracker hardcodes this to 0xfffbd000 (matches QEMU convention).

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-identity-map-addr
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_IDENTITY_MAP_ADDR, &addr) — x86 Intel-only. Set the address of a 1-page identity map for guest paging during early boot. Firecracker sets this to 0xfffbc000 (page below TSS area).

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-pit-enable
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_CREATE_PIT2, &cfg) — Create the in-kernel Programmable Interval Timer (8254). Firecracker uses this for legacy timer interrupts; the alternative (userspace PIT) would generate excessive vCPU exits.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-set-clock
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_SET_CLOCK, &clock) — Set the kvmclock value. Used during snapshot restore to maintain monotonic guest time across pause/resume.

name: firecracker.kvm.cmd.kvm-get-clock
observations: ioctl(vm_fd, KVM_GET_CLOCK, &clock) — Read the current kvmclock value. Snapshot save records this.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.describe-instance
observations: GET / — Returns instance information: id, state (Not started|Running|Paused), vmm_version, app_name. The minimum-impact health check.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.create-sync-action
observations: PUT /actions — Trigger a synchronous action: InstanceStart (boot the configured machine), SendCtrlAltDel (graceful guest shutdown via keyboard reset).

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-guest-boot-source
observations: PUT /boot-source — Set kernel image, boot args, and (optional) initrd path. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-machine-config
observations: PUT /machine-config — Set vCPU count, memory size, hyperthreading, dirty-page tracking. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-machine-config
observations: PATCH /machine-config — Update a subset of machine-config fields. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.get-machine-config
observations: GET /machine-config — Return the current machine configuration.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-cpu-configuration
observations: PUT /cpu-config — Apply a custom CPU template — explicit CPUID/MSR/Aarch64-register modifiers. Replaces the legacy machine_config.cpu_template enum. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-guest-drive-by-id
observations: PUT /drives/{drive_id} — Attach or replace a block device. Pre-boot for full PUT; runtime PATCH only updates a subset.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-guest-drive-by-id
observations: PATCH /drives/{drive_id} — Update a drive at runtime — swap backing file (path_on_host) or change rate limiters. Other fields are immutable post-boot.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-guest-network-interface-by-id
observations: PUT /network-interfaces/{iface_id} — Attach a VirtIO/net device backed by a host TAP. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-guest-network-interface-by-id
observations: PATCH /network-interfaces/{iface_id} — Update RX/TX rate limiters at runtime. Other fields immutable post-boot.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-guest-vsock
observations: PUT /vsock — Attach the (single) VirtIO/vsock device. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-balloon
observations: PUT /balloon — Attach the VirtIO/balloon device. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-balloon
observations: PATCH /balloon — Inflate or deflate the balloon at runtime.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.describe-balloon-config
observations: GET /balloon — Return the current balloon device configuration.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.describe-balloon-stats
observations: GET /balloon/statistics — Return latest balloon stats — only available if stats_polling_interval_s > 0 was set pre-boot.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-balloon-stats-interval
observations: PATCH /balloon/statistics — Update the balloon-stats polling interval at runtime.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-entropy-device
observations: PUT /entropy — Attach VirtIO/rng (entropy device). Pre-boot only. Strongly recommended for crypto workloads.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-logger
observations: PUT /logger — Configure logging to a named pipe (FIFO).

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-metrics
observations: PUT /metrics — Configure metrics-emission FIFO. Re-PUT at runtime to flush metrics on demand.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-mmds
observations: PUT /mmds — Replace the entire MMDS payload with a new JSON object.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-mmds
observations: PATCH /mmds — Apply a JSON-merge-patch to the MMDS payload.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.get-mmds
observations: GET /mmds — Return the current MMDS payload.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-mmds-config
observations: PUT /mmds/config — Configure MMDS network exposure: which network interface(s) to attach to, IPv4 address, version (V1|V2). Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-serial-device
observations: PUT /serial — Configure a custom serial device backend (e.g., write console output to a host file).

name: firecracker.api.cmd.create-snapshot
observations: PUT /snapshot/create — Persist VM state to disk. VM must be Paused (PATCH /vm{state=Paused}) first.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.load-snapshot
observations: PUT /snapshot/load — Restore VM state into a fresh Firecracker process. Must be the first API call after process start (no prior PUT /machine-config etc.).

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-vm
observations: PATCH /vm — Set VM state — Paused or Resumed.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.get-firecracker-version
observations: GET /version — Return the running Firecracker version (semver).

name: firecracker.api.cmd.get-export-vm-config
observations: GET /vm/config — Export the full current VM configuration as a JSON document — useful for snapshotting the configuration alongside the VM-state binary.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.start-balloon-hinting
observations: PATCH /balloon/hinting/start — Trigger a free-page-hinting run on the balloon device — the guest reports unused pages so the host can drop them.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.describe-balloon-hinting
observations: GET /balloon/hinting/status — Return the current free-page-hinting statistics.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.stop-balloon-hinting
observations: PATCH /balloon/hinting/stop — Stop an in-progress free-page-hinting run.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-guest-pmem-by-id
observations: PUT /pmem/{pmem_id} — Attach a virtio-pmem device backed by a host file. Persistent-memory semantics in the guest. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-guest-pmem-by-id
observations: PATCH /pmem/{pmem_id} — Update a pmem device at runtime — limited fields.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.put-memory-hotplug
observations: PUT /memory-hotplug — Configure virtio-mem for runtime memory resizing. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.patch-memory-hotplug
observations: PATCH /memory-hotplug — Hot-plug or hot-unplug memory at runtime via virtio-mem.

name: firecracker.api.cmd.get-memory-hotplug
observations: GET /memory-hotplug — Return the current memory-hotplug configuration.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.firecracker
observations: firecracker — The Firecracker VMM binary. Started by orchestrator (typically via the jailer). Reads API requests from a Unix socket and runs one microVM per process.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.curl-api-status
observations: curl --unix-socket <path> http://localhost/ — Probe a running Firecracker via its API socket. Returns instance state (Not started|Running|Paused) and version.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.dmesg-check-page-alloc-failure
observations: dmesg | grep 'page allocation failure' — Diagnose host-side OOM during Firecracker startup. fc_vmm: page allocation failure messages indicate the host can't satisfy a high-order allocation (KVM needs contiguous pages for the guest).

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.tune-vm-min-free-kbytes
observations: sysctl -w vm.min_free_kbytes=<value> — Raise the kernel's minimum-free-memory watermark to combat memory fragmentation that causes Firecracker page allocation failures.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.modprobe-r-vboxdrv
observations: modprobe -r vboxdrv — Unload VirtualBox kernel module that holds /dev/kvm exclusively, freeing it for Firecracker. Needed when Firecracker fails with 'Resource busy'.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.lsmod-check-kvm
observations: lsmod | grep kvm — Verify the KVM kernel modules are loaded (kvm + kvm_intel or kvm_amd). Without these, Firecracker can't open /dev/kvm.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.access-dev-kvm
observations: [ -r /dev/kvm ] && [ -w /dev/kvm ] — Verify the calling user has read+write access to /dev/kvm. Typically requires being in the 'kvm' group; jailer drops to a lower uid that must also have access.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.curl-put-machine-config
observations: curl -X PUT --unix-socket <sock> http://localhost/machine-config -d '<json>' — Configure vCPU + memory for the microVM. Pre-boot only.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.curl-put-instance-start
observations: curl -X PUT --unix-socket <sock> http://localhost/actions -d '{"action_type":"InstanceStart"}' — Boot the configured microVM. Synchronous: returns 204 once vCPUs are running.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.send-ctrl-alt-del
observations: curl -X PUT --unix-socket <sock> http://localhost/actions -d '{"action_type":"SendCtrlAltDel"}' — Inject Ctrl+Alt+Del into the guest. With reboot=k in boot_args, terminates the Firecracker process gracefully (x86 only).

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.curl-put-flush-metrics
observations: curl -X PUT --unix-socket <sock> http://localhost/actions -d '{"action_type":"FlushMetrics"}' — Force an immediate metrics emission to the configured /metrics FIFO without waiting for the 60-second cadence.

name: firecracker.vmm.cmd.mkfifo-log-pipe
observations: mkfifo <path> — Create the named pipe Firecracker requires for /logger and /metrics endpoints. Must exist before PUT /logger or PUT /metrics.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.create-snapshot-full
observations: PUT /snapshot/create (snapshot_type=Full) — Persist full microVM state to host files. VM must be Paused first.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.create-snapshot-diff
observations: PUT /snapshot/create (snapshot_type=Diff) — Persist only pages dirtied since the last snapshot. Requires machine-config.track_dirty_pages=true.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.load-snapshot-file-backend
observations: PUT /snapshot/load (mem_backend=File) — Restore from snapshot using MAP_PRIVATE on the memory file. Must be the FIRST API call in the restoring Firecracker process.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.load-snapshot-uffd-backend
observations: PUT /snapshot/load (mem_backend=Uffd) — Restore using userfaultfd — orchestrator-supplied page-fault handler services memory access. Useful for remote-memory or compressed-memory backends.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.patch-vm-pause
observations: PATCH /vm {"state":"Paused"} — Pause the microVM (vCPU threads exit KVM_RUN; no I/O). Required before snapshot create.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.patch-vm-resume
observations: PATCH /vm {"state":"Resumed"} — Resume the microVM after pause or after a restore that didn't auto-resume.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.fallocate-mem-file
observations: fallocate -l <size> <mem_file_path> — Pre-allocate the snapshot memory file space on the host before snapshot create. Avoids ENOSPC mid-snapshot.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cmd.cgroup-v2-check
observations: stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup — Confirm the host is using cgroups v2 (cgroup2fs filesystem). cgroups v1 imposes high restore-latency tax; v2 recommended for production snapshots.

name: firecracker.jailer.cmd.jailer
observations: jailer — Privileged setup wrapper. Sets up cgroups, chroot, network namespace, resource limits, drops privileges, and exec()s the statically-linked Firecracker binary.

name: firecracker.jailer.cmd.ip-netns-add
observations: ip netns add <name> — Create a network namespace for the jailer to attach via --netns. Combine with TAP creation inside the netns to give the microVM an isolated network stack.

name: firecracker.jailer.cmd.cgcreate-prep
observations: cgcreate -g <controllers>:<group> — Pre-create a cgroup hierarchy for the jailer to use (alternative to letting jailer create it inline via --cgroup). Useful when the orchestrator is non-privileged.

name: firecracker.jailer.cmd.find-jail-pid
observations: cat <chroot_dir>/<exec_file_name>.pid — Read the host-side PID of the jailed Firecracker process. Recorded by jailer when --new-pid-ns is used (since the jail-internal PID is meaningless to the host).

name: firecracker.jailer.cmd.curl-via-jailed-socket
observations: curl --unix-socket <chroot>/run/firecracker/api.sock http://localhost/... — Communicate with a jailed Firecracker — the API socket lives INSIDE the chroot tree. Orchestrator must use the absolute host path to the socket.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.ip-tuntap-add-tap
observations: ip tuntap add <name> mode tap — Create a Linux TAP device for Firecracker to attach to. The TAP must exist on the host before PUT /network-interfaces references it.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.enable-ip-forward
observations: echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward — Enable IPv4 forwarding on the host. Required for any NAT-based or bridge-based microVM routing.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.nft-masquerade-rule
observations: nft add rule <table> postrouting ip saddr <guest-ip> oifname <host-iface> counter masquerade — Create the NAT masquerade rule that rewrites guest packets' source IP to the host's egress interface IP. The kernel's outbound side of the NAT-routing pattern.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.iptables-nft-masquerade
observations: iptables-nft -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o <host-iface> -s <guest-ip> -j MASQUERADE — Equivalent to the nft masquerade rule via the iptables-nft compat layer. Use only if your tooling/familiarity prefers iptables syntax (nft is recommended for production).

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.guest-ip-route-add-default
observations: ip route add default via <tap-ip> dev eth0 (in guest) — Inside the guest, configure the default route through the TAP IP. Combined with `ip addr add <guest-ip>/30 dev eth0` and `ip link set eth0 up`, gives the guest egress.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.curl-mmds-token-mint
observations: curl -X PUT http://<mmds-ip>/latest/api/token -H 'X-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: <N>' — From INSIDE the guest, mint an MMDS V2 session token. TTL between 1 and 21600 seconds. Returns the token as plaintext body.

name: firecracker.networking.cmd.curl-mmds-get
observations: curl -H 'X-metadata-token: <token>' http://<mmds-ip>/<path> — From INSIDE the guest, fetch an MMDS resource. Path is a JSON Pointer into the MMDS data store.

name: firecracker.vsock.cmd.socat-host-connect
observations: socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<uds_path> — From the host, connect to the vsock UDS. After connection, send 'CONNECT <port>\n' to forward to a guest-side listener. The first 'OK <hostside-port>\n' line is Firecracker's acknowledgement.

name: firecracker.vsock.cmd.socat-guest-listen
observations: socat VSOCK-LISTEN:<port>,fork - (in guest) — Inside the guest, listen on a vsock port for incoming host-initiated connections. ,fork forks per-connection.

name: firecracker.vsock.cmd.socat-guest-connect-host
observations: socat - VSOCK-CONNECT:2:<port> (in guest) — From inside the guest, open an AF_VSOCK connection to the host (CID=2) on <port>. Firecracker forwards to <uds_path>_<port> on the host.

name: firecracker.setup.cmd.modprobe-kvm-min-timer-period
observations: modprobe kvm min_timer_period_us=<value> — Raise the KVM minimum timer period. Reduces kvm-pit kernel-thread CPU overhead on x86. Caveat: same setting also affects APIC timer events — workload-test before deploying.

name: firecracker.setup.cmd.disable-ksm
observations: echo 0 > /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run — Disable Kernel Samepage Merging — required for multi-tenant Firecracker hosts to mitigate page-deduplication side channels.

name: firecracker.setup.cmd.swapoff-all
observations: swapoff -a — Disable all swap to prevent guest memory contents from being written to disk (data remanence). Make persistent by removing swap entries from /etc/fstab.

name: firecracker.setup.cmd.spectre-meltdown-checker
observations: spectre-meltdown-checker.sh — Audit host's protections against speculation side channels (Spectre, Meltdown, MDS, etc.). Run as part of deployment validation; rerun after any kernel/microcode update.

name: firecracker.setup.cmd.mkfs-rootfs-ext4
observations: mkfs.ext4 -L rootfs <image> — Format a sparse host file as ext4 to use as a Firecracker rootfs (PUT /drives is_root_device=true).

name: ecs.agent.cmd.curl-introspection-metadata
observations: curl -s http://localhost:51678/v1/metadata — Read container instance metadata via the agent introspection API. Returns Cluster name, ContainerInstanceArn, agent Version. Health-check + identity probe; first command to run when SSH'd into a container instance.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.curl-introspection-tasks
observations: curl -s http://localhost:51678/v1/tasks — List all tasks running on this container instance. Shows Arn, DesiredStatus, KnownStatus, Family, Version, Containers[]. Diagnose 'why isn't my task running' from the agent's view.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.systemctl-restart-ecs
observations: sudo systemctl restart ecs — Restart the ECS agent via ecs-init systemd unit. Required after editing /etc/ecs/ecs.config to pick up env-var changes. The agent container is destroyed + recreated; running tasks survive (managed by Docker daemon).

name: ecs.agent.cmd.tail-agent-logs
observations: tail -F /var/log/ecs/ecs-agent.log — Stream live agent logs. Format depends on ECS_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT (logfmt or json) and ECS_LOG_ROLLOVER_TYPE (size or hourly). Look for ACS connection state + task-state-change events.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.docker-inspect-agent
observations: docker inspect ecs-agent — Inspect the running ECS agent container. Shows env vars, mounts, network, restart policy. Most useful field: .Config.Env — confirms which ECS_* vars made it through ecs-init.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.ecs-init-reload-cache
observations: sudo /usr/libexec/amazon-ecs-init reload-cache — Force ecs-init to reload its cached agent container image. Used during agent-update rollback or when /var/cache/ecs/ecs-agent.tar is stale.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.curl-task-credentials
observations: curl -s http://169.254.170.2$AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI — From INSIDE a task container, fetch the task's IAM-role credentials. The agent serves this endpoint; AWS SDKs auto-discover via the AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI env var injected into the container.

name: ecs.agent.cmd.aws-ecs-update-container-instances-state-draining
observations: aws ecs update-container-instances-state --cluster <name> --container-instances <arn> --status DRAINING — Transition a container instance to DRAINING — stops accepting new task placements; service-managed tasks are gradually replaced on other capacity. Standard pre-AMI-update / pre-scale-in workflow.

name: ecs.task-defs.cmd.aws-ecs-register-task-definition
observations: aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://td.json — Register a new revision of a task definition. Returns the new revision number. Idempotent only if the JSON differs — same content → still creates a new revision (no dedup).

name: ecs.task-defs.cmd.aws-ecs-run-task
