observations: cache-export-import-attr.compression: Layer compression.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.cache-export-import-attr.gha-scope
observations: cache-export-import-attr.scope (gha): GitHub Actions cache scope. Different scopes don't share cache.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.bake-hcl-toml-json.group.targets
observations: bake-hcl-toml-json.group.<name>.targets: Logical group of targets. `docker buildx bake <group>` builds all members.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.dockerfile-instruction-keyword.SHELL
observations: dockerfile-instruction-keyword.SHELL ["executable", "arg"]: Override shell for shell-form RUN/CMD/ENTRYPOINT. Use `["powershell","-Command"]` on Windows for PowerShell builds.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.dockerfile-instruction-keyword.COPY-chown
observations: dockerfile-instruction-keyword.COPY --chown=<user>[:<group>]: Set ownership on the copied files.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.dockerfile-parser-directive.case-insensitive
observations: dockerfile-parser-directive.directive names case-insensitive: `# Syntax=`, `# SYNTAX=`, `# syntax=` all valid. Convention: lowercase.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.buildkitd-toml.worker-oci.enabled
observations: buildkitd-toml.[worker.oci].enabled: Enable OCI worker (runc-based).

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.buildkitd-toml.registry-mirrors
observations: buildkitd-toml.[registry."<host>"].mirrors: Mirror endpoints for a registry. e.g. `[registry."docker.io"].mirrors = ["yourmirror.local:5000"]`.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.build-flag.cpu-quota
observations: build-flag.--cpu-quota: CFS quota during build.

name: docker.build-buildkit.cfg.bake-hcl-toml-json.target.tags
observations: bake-hcl-toml-json.target.<name>.tags: Image tags for the target.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-audit-control
observations: cap-flag.CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL: Enable/disable kernel auditing; change auditing filter rules; retrieve auditing status and filter rules. Required for `auditctl -e 1` and rule manipulation.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-audit-write
observations: cap-flag.CAP_AUDIT_WRITE: Write records to kernel auditing log. Granted to PAM-driven login programs that need to log session-start records.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-block-suspend
observations: cap-flag.CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND: Employ features that can block system suspend (epoll EPOLLWAKEUP, /proc/sys/wake_lock writes).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-bpf
observations: cap-flag.CAP_BPF: Use most BPF facilities (load programs, create maps). Split out from CAP_SYS_ADMIN in 5.8 to enable least-privilege BPF tooling. Note: tracing-class BPF still needs CAP_PERFMON; networking-class needs CAP_NET_ADMIN.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-checkpoint-restore
observations: cap-flag.CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE: Read /proc/<pid>/{maps,statm,smaps,stack,syscall} of any process; bypass /proc/sys/kernel/{ns_last_pid,nstgid_last,etc.} restrictions; needed by CRIU. Split out from CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-chown
observations: cap-flag.CAP_CHOWN: Make arbitrary changes to file UIDs/GIDs (without it, only owner can chown to own group). Container `chown` inside images requires this; Docker grants by default.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-dac-override
observations: cap-flag.CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE: Bypass file read/write/execute permission checks (DAC = discretionary access control). Effectively 'I am root for file access regardless of mode bits.'

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-dac-read-search
observations: cap-flag.CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH: Bypass file read and directory read+execute (search) permission checks. Weaker than CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE — read/list-only, no write.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-fowner
observations: cap-flag.CAP_FOWNER: Operations that normally require the file's UID to match the process EUID — chmod, chown of group, utimes on others' files, sticky-bit unlink override.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-fsetid
observations: cap-flag.CAP_FSETID: Don't clear setuid/setgid bits when modifying a file you don't own. Without it, write/chown of a setuid file as a non-owner clears the bit.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-ipc-lock
observations: cap-flag.CAP_IPC_LOCK: Lock memory (mlock, mlockall, mmap MAP_LOCKED, shmctl SHM_LOCK). Required by some real-time / crypto / DB workloads to keep secrets out of swap.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-ipc-owner
observations: cap-flag.CAP_IPC_OWNER: Bypass permission checks for System V IPC objects.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-kill
observations: cap-flag.CAP_KILL: Bypass permission checks for sending signals (kill any process). Without it, only same-EUID/RUID and a few signals to children.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-mac-admin
observations: cap-flag.CAP_MAC_ADMIN: LSM-specific: SELinux/AppArmor admin operations (load policy, change enforcing mode).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-mac-override
observations: cap-flag.CAP_MAC_OVERRIDE: Override MAC (mandatory access control) policy. Effective only on Smack LSM (and a few others); SELinux/AppArmor have their own bypass mechanisms.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-mknod
observations: cap-flag.CAP_MKNOD: Create special files (mknod for char/block devices). Container runtimes drop this by default — root inside a container can't create new device nodes.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-net-admin
observations: cap-flag.CAP_NET_ADMIN: Network admin: interface config, routing, firewall (iptables/nftables), netfilter, multicast, packet socket bind. Required to manipulate routes inside a container.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-net-bind-service
observations: cap-flag.CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE: Bind a socket to privileged ports (<1024). The lowest-privilege way to run a non-root webserver on port 80/443.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-net-broadcast
observations: cap-flag.CAP_NET_BROADCAST: Make socket broadcasts and listen to multicasts. Rarely needed; mostly historical.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-net-raw
observations: cap-flag.CAP_NET_RAW: Use RAW and PACKET sockets; bind to any address for transparent proxying. Required for ping (without setuid), tcpdump, traceroute. Container runtimes typically drop this.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-perfmon
observations: cap-flag.CAP_PERFMON: Use performance monitoring (perf_event_open, full BPF tracing). Split from CAP_SYS_ADMIN in 5.8.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-setgid
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SETGID: Make arbitrary GID manipulations (setgid, setresgid, setgroups). Forge GID in unix-domain socket credentials.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-setfcap
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SETFCAP: Set arbitrary file capabilities on files (extended attributes 'security.capability'). Required to install setcap-style bestowal.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-setpcap
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SETPCAP: Drop any capability from any process's bounding set; raise inheritable caps not in the calling thread's permitted set.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-setuid
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SETUID: Make arbitrary UID manipulations (setuid, setreuid, setresuid, setfsuid). Forge UID in unix socket credentials.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-admin
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_ADMIN: The 'kitchen sink' capability — mount, swapon/swapoff, sethostname, namespace setup, BPF (pre-5.8), keyctl, ioperm/iopl, vm86, and many more. Often called 'the new root' because dropping it disables most container-relevant operations.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-boot
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_BOOT: Use reboot(2) and kexec_load(2). Reboot the system.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-chroot
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_CHROOT: chroot(2) the calling process and change mount namespaces via setns(2)+CLONE_NEWNS.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-module
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_MODULE: Load and unload kernel modules. Container runtimes always drop — letting a container load modules = compromised host.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-nice
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_NICE: Raise nice value, change scheduling policy/priority of any process, set IO scheduling class/priority, set CPU affinity beyond own.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-pacct
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_PACCT: Use acct(2) — process accounting on/off.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-ptrace
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_PTRACE: Trace any process (ptrace, /proc/<pid>/mem, perf_event_open with PERF_SAMPLE_REGS_USER, etc.). Required for gdb/strace on non-children. Yama LSM /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope=2 restricts further.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-rawio
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_RAWIO: Perform IO port operations (iopl, ioperm); access /proc/kcore, /dev/mem, /dev/kmem; raw block-device IO (e.g. SG_IO ioctls).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-resource
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_RESOURCE: Override resource limits — set RLIMIT_NPROC > current, override fs reserved-block disk-quota, override max user inotify watches, etc.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-time
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_TIME: Set system clock (settimeofday, stime, adjtimex), set realtime hardware clock.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-syslog
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYSLOG: Read kernel logs (klogctl); change console log level. Required for `dmesg` when /proc/sys/kernel/dmesg_restrict=1.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-wake-alarm
observations: cap-flag.CAP_WAKE_ALARM: Trigger system wake from suspend (CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM, CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM timers).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-linux-immutable
observations: cap-flag.CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE: Set FS_APPEND_FL and FS_IMMUTABLE_FL inode flags via chattr.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-lease
observations: cap-flag.CAP_LEASE: Establish leases on arbitrary files via fcntl F_SETLEASE.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cap-flag.cap-sys-tty-config
observations: cap-flag.CAP_SYS_TTY_CONFIG: Use vhangup(2). TTY config tweaks like KDFONTOP ioctl.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newuser
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWUSER: Create new user namespace. Initially: child has full caps inside, no caps outside. Allows unprivileged container creation.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newpid
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWPID: Create new PID namespace. First process becomes pid 1 of the namespace.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newns
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWNS: Create new mount namespace (named NEWNS for historical 'new namespace' meaning, when there was only one type).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newipc
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWIPC: Create new IPC namespace (System V IPC, POSIX message queues).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newuts
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWUTS: Create new UTS namespace (hostname, domainname).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newnet
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWNET: Create new network namespace.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newcgroup
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWCGROUP: Create new cgroup namespace. Virtualizes /proc/self/cgroup view.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-newtime
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_NEWTIME: Create new time namespace (CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_BOOTTIME offsets). Kernel 5.6+. NOTE: Cannot be passed to unshare(2)/clone(2) — set via /proc/<pid>/ns/time_for_children + setns.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-vm
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_VM: Share virtual memory with parent. Used by pthread_create. Without CLONE_VM, fork-style copy-on-write.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-fs
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_FS: Share filesystem state (root, cwd, umask). Required by pthreads.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-files
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_FILES: Share file descriptor table. Used by pthreads (so threads share open FDs).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-sighand
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_SIGHAND: Share signal handlers. Required when CLONE_THREAD is set.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-thread
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_THREAD: Place child in same thread group as parent. Requires CLONE_SIGHAND. Requires CLONE_VM in modern kernels. Foundation of pthread_create.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-parent
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_PARENT: Make parent of new child the same as parent of caller (sibling instead of child). SIGCHLD goes to grandparent.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-pidfd
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_PIDFD: Return a pidfd referring to the child via the parent_tidptr arg. Race-free signaling via pidfd_send_signal.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-io
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_IO: Share IO context with parent (CFQ scheduler grouping).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-detached
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_DETACHED: Historical flag; ignored in modern kernels. Documented for completeness.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-untraced
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_UNTRACED: Tracer cannot force CLONE_PTRACE on this clone. Used by kernel threads.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-parent-settid
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_PARENT_SETTID: Store child TID in parent_tidptr in the parent's memory.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-child-settid
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_CHILD_SETTID: Store child TID in child_tidptr in the child's memory.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.clone-flag.clone-child-cleartid
observations: clone-flag.CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID: Clear child_tidptr on child exit and futex-wake any waiter — the mechanism behind pthread_join.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-max
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.max: Hard memory ceiling for the cgroup. Allocations beyond trigger reclaim then OOM kill (within cgroup). The systemd `MemoryMax=` directive writes here.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-high
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.high: Throttle threshold — kernel aggressively reclaims when usage exceeds. No OOM (unlike .max). systemd `MemoryHigh=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-low
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.low: Soft protection — usage below this is preferred over reclaim from sibling cgroups. Best-effort. systemd `MemoryLow=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-min
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.min: Hard protection — kernel will not reclaim below this. Stronger guarantee than memory.low. systemd `MemoryMin=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-current
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.current: Current memory usage of the cgroup including all descendants.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-events
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.events: Lines: low, high, max, oom, oom_kill counts. Watching this is how systemd-oomd reacts before global OOM.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-swap-max
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.swap.max: Swap ceiling for the cgroup. 0 disables swap usage by this cgroup. systemd `MemorySwapMax=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-pressure
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.pressure: PSI metric for memory contention. Lines: 'some avg10=… avg60=… avg300=… total=…' and 'full ...'. The data behind oomd.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu-max
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu.max: CFS quota+period for the cgroup. e.g. '50000 100000' = 50% of one CPU. systemd `CPUQuota=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu-weight
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu.weight: Relative CPU share weight under contention. Higher = more CPU. systemd `CPUWeight=` (mapped from a 1-10000 scale; default 100).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu-stat
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu.stat: Per-cgroup CPU accounting: usage_usec, user_usec, system_usec, nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_usec. Throttling diagnostic.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu-pressure
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpu.pressure: PSI for CPU contention.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.io-max
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.io.max: Per-device IO bandwidth/IOPS ceiling. e.g. '8:0 rbps=1048576 wbps=1048576 riops=100 wiops=100'. systemd `IOMax*=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.io-weight
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.io.weight: Relative IO share. systemd `IOWeight=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.io-stat
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.io.stat: Per-device 'rbytes wbytes rios wios dbytes dios'. Block-layer IO; doesn't include pagecache hits.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.io-pressure
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.io.pressure: PSI for IO contention.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.pids-max
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.pids.max: Hard ceiling on number of processes/threads in the cgroup. Hitting it causes fork()/clone() to fail with EAGAIN. systemd `TasksMax=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.pids-current
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.pids.current: Current process count in cgroup including descendants.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-procs
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.procs: Members of the cgroup. Write a PID to add a process (and all its threads); read to enumerate. The way to move a process between cgroups.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-threads
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.threads: Per-thread membership (only in 'threaded' cgroups).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-controllers
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.controllers: Controllers available in this cgroup (filtered by parent's subtree_control).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-subtree-control
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.subtree_control: Controllers enabled for direct child cgroups. Write '+memory' / '-cpu' to add/remove. Cannot enable a controller in a cgroup that has processes (no-internal-procs rule).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-events
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.events: populated (1 if any descendant has procs), frozen (1 if cgroup.freeze took effect). poll/epoll friendly.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-freeze
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.freeze: Write 1 to freeze every process in cgroup atomically; 0 to thaw.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-kill
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.kill: Write 1 to SIGKILL every process in cgroup. v5.14+. Cleaner alternative to walking cgroup.procs.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup-type
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cgroup.type: Cgroup type. 'domain' = standard process-grouping. 'threaded' = thread-grouping mode for fine-grained scheduling.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpuset-cpus
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpuset.cpus: CPUs the cgroup may run on. Hard pin. systemd `AllowedCPUs=`.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.cpuset-mems
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.cpuset.mems: Memory NUMA nodes allowed.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v2-control-file.memory-oom-group
observations: cgroup-v2-control-file.memory.oom.group: If 1, OOM kill in this cgroup kills every process in it atomically (vs single-victim default).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpuset-cpus
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpuset.cpus: v1 cpuset controller — CPUs the cgroup runs on.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpuset-mems
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpuset.mems: v1 cpuset — NUMA memory nodes allowed.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.memory-limit
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.memory.limit_in_bytes: v1 memory hard limit.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.memory-soft-limit
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.memory.soft_limit_in_bytes: v1 memory soft limit (best-effort).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.memory-swappiness
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.memory.swappiness: v1 per-cgroup swappiness override.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.memory-oom-control
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.memory.oom_control: v1 OOM control: write 'oom_kill_disable 1' to suspend processes instead of killing on OOM.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpu-shares
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpu.shares: v1 relative CPU weight. v2 equivalent: cpu.weight.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpu-cfs-quota
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpu.cfs_quota_us: v1 CFS quota per period.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpu-cfs-period
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpu.cfs_period_us: v1 CFS period.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.cpu-rt-runtime
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.cpu.rt_runtime_us: v1 RT scheduling runtime per period.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.blkio-weight
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.blkio.weight: v1 block IO relative weight.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.blkio-throttle-read
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.blkio.throttle.read_bps_device: v1 read bandwidth ceiling per device.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.blkio-throttle-write
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.blkio.throttle.write_bps_device: v1 write bandwidth ceiling per device.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.devices-allow
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.devices.allow: v1 device allowlist entry. Type a/b/c (any/block/char). e.g. 'c 1:3 rmw' = char dev 1:3 read/mknod/write.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.devices-deny
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.devices.deny: v1 device denylist entry. Same format as devices.allow.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.freezer-state
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.freezer.state: v1 freezer controller state. Replaced by cgroup.freeze in v2.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.cgroup-v1-controller.pids-max
observations: cgroup-v1-controller.pids.max: v1 pids controller — process count ceiling.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-kill-process
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS: Kill the process (entire thread group). The 'never recover' verdict.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-kill-thread
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_KILL_THREAD: Kill only the offending thread. Older 'KILL' alias maps here.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-trap
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_TRAP: Send SIGSYS to the thread; siginfo.si_call_addr/si_syscall set.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-errno
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO: Return the configured errno value to userspace without executing the syscall.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-user-notif
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF: Suspend the thread and forward the syscall to a userspace supervisor over a notification FD.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-trace
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_TRACE: If a ptracer is attached, notify it (PTRACE_EVENT_SECCOMP). Otherwise return ENOSYS.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-log
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_LOG: Allow the syscall but log it (audit).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.seccomp-action.ret-allow
observations: seccomp-action.SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW: Allow the syscall (the default for unmatched).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-name
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_NAME: Set the calling thread's name (max 16 chars). Visible in /proc/<pid>/comm and ps -L.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-pdeathsig
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_PDEATHSIG: Set signal to receive when parent dies. Cleared on setuid execve.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-no-new-privs
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS: Set the per-thread no_new_privs bit (one-way; cleared only by exit/exec). Required for unprivileged seccomp filter installation.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-seccomp
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_SECCOMP: Set seccomp mode (1=strict, 2=filter). For filter mode, requires no_new_privs OR CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-keepcaps
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_KEEPCAPS: Preserve permitted capabilities across UID 0→nonzero transitions. Cleared on execve.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.capbset-drop
observations: prctl-option.PR_CAPBSET_DROP: Drop a capability from the bounding set. One-way.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.capbset-read
observations: prctl-option.PR_CAPBSET_READ: Test if a capability is in the bounding set.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.cap-ambient
observations: prctl-option.PR_CAP_AMBIENT: Manipulate ambient capability set: PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE / LOWER / IS_SET / CLEAR_ALL sub-ops.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-child-subreaper
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER: Mark calling thread as subreaper for orphaned descendants.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-securebits
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_SECUREBITS: Set securebits flags (NOROOT, NO_SETUID_FIXUP, KEEP_CAPS, plus *_LOCKED counterparts).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.prctl-option.set-dumpable
observations: prctl-option.PR_SET_DUMPABLE: Control whether the process is dumpable (core dump allowed; ptrace attach allowed). Reset on setuid execve to 'suid_dumpable' value.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-restart
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_RESTART: Auto-restart certain blocking syscalls interrupted by signal (instead of returning EINTR). Doesn't help all syscalls — read/write/wait yes; sleep/poll no.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-siginfo
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_SIGINFO: Use 3-arg sa_sigaction handler (signo, siginfo_t*, ucontext_t*) instead of legacy sa_handler. Required to access fault address, sender PID, etc.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-nocldstop
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_NOCLDSTOP: For SIGCHLD: don't deliver when child is stopped/continued (only on exit).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-nocldwait
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_NOCLDWAIT: For SIGCHLD: auto-reap children — they don't become zombies. The 'lazy' alternative to wait().

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-nodefer
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_NODEFER: Don't add this signal to the mask while handler runs (allows reentry).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-resethand
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_RESETHAND: Reset disposition to SIG_DFL after first delivery (System V signal() semantics).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.sigaction-flag.sa-onstack
observations: sigaction-flag.SA_ONSTACK: Run handler on alternate signal stack (set up via sigaltstack(2)). Useful for SIGSEGV handlers when main stack overflows.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-rdonly
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_RDONLY: Read-only mount. Equivalent to mount -o ro.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-nosuid
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_NOSUID: setuid/setgid bits ignored on this mount. Common on /home, /tmp, container rootfs to limit privilege escalation surface.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-nodev
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_NODEV: Disallow access to device special files. Container runtimes apply on every non-/dev mount.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-noexec
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_NOEXEC: Disallow executing programs from this mount. Hardening for /tmp, /var.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-bind
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_BIND: Bind-mount: make the source visible at a second mountpoint. mount --bind. The volume primitive every container runtime uses.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-rec
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_REC: Apply operation recursively to all submounts. Combine with MS_BIND for rbind.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-private
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_PRIVATE: Set propagation type to private (no event propagation).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-shared
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_SHARED: Set propagation type to shared (bidirectional events with peers).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-slave
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_SLAVE: Set propagation type to slave (receives from master, doesn't send).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-unbindable
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_UNBINDABLE: Cannot be source of a bind-mount.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-noatime
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_NOATIME: Don't update file access time on read. Common perf tweak.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.mount-flag.ms-remount
observations: mount-flag-MS_*.MS_REMOUNT: Remount existing mount with new flags (e.g., remount,rw).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.vm-overcommit-memory
observations: proc-sys-file.vm.overcommit_memory: 0 = heuristic, 1 = always allow, 2 = strict (commit ≤ overcommit_ratio% of RAM+swap). The ENOMEM-from-malloc-vs-OOM-on-touch fork.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.vm-overcommit-ratio
observations: proc-sys-file.vm.overcommit_ratio: With overcommit_memory=2, percentage of RAM that can be committed (plus all of swap).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.vm-swappiness
observations: proc-sys-file.vm.swappiness: How aggressively kernel swaps. 0 = avoid unless OOM imminent. 100 = swap freely. Servers commonly set 1-10.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.vm-drop-caches
observations: proc-sys-file.vm.drop_caches: 1 = pagecache, 2 = dentries+inodes, 3 = both. Diagnostic tool; releases reclaimable memory.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.vm-max-map-count
observations: proc-sys-file.vm.max_map_count: Per-process VMA count ceiling. Elasticsearch / databases often need raised to 262144.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-pid-max
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.pid_max: Maximum PID number. PIDs wrap around at this value.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-threads-max
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.threads-max: System-wide thread count ceiling. Hitting it: clone() returns EAGAIN.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-shmmax
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.shmmax: Max single SysV SHM segment size.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-shmall
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.shmall: System-wide SysV SHM total in pages.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-dmesg-restrict
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.dmesg_restrict: 1 = require CAP_SYSLOG to read /dev/kmsg / dmesg. Container hardening.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-yama-ptrace-scope
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.yama.ptrace_scope: 0 = anyone with same uid; 1 = only descendants; 2 = CAP_SYS_PTRACE only; 3 = no ptrace ever (unrecoverable until reboot).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-core-pattern
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.core_pattern: Filename template for core dumps. '|<program>' pipes to a handler — what systemd-coredump installs as '|/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-coredump %P %u %g %s %t %c %h'.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-core-uses-pid
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.core_uses_pid: Append .PID to core dump filename. Largely superseded by %p in core_pattern.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.kernel-sysrq
observations: proc-sys-file.kernel.sysrq: SysRq trigger enabled features. 0 = disabled, 1 = all, otherwise bitmask. echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger reboots immediately.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.fs-file-max
observations: proc-sys-file.fs.file-max: System-wide max open file count.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.fs-nr-open
observations: proc-sys-file.fs.nr_open: Per-process max FDs ceiling (RLIMIT_NOFILE cannot exceed).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.fs-inotify-max-user-watches
observations: proc-sys-file.fs.inotify.max_user_watches: Per-user inotify watch count. IDEs/file watchers commonly need raised to 524288.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.fs-inotify-max-queued-events
observations: proc-sys-file.fs.inotify.max_queued_events: Per-instance inotify queue depth.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.proc-sys-file.user-max-user-namespaces
observations: proc-sys-file.user.max_user_namespaces: Per-user max nested user namespaces. 0 effectively disables unprivileged userns.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.ns-pid
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/ns/pid: PID namespace identifier. Target is 'pid:[<inode>]'. setns(2) takes an FD opened on this.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.ns-user
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/ns/user: User namespace identifier.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.ns-mnt
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/ns/mnt: Mount namespace identifier.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.ns-net
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/ns/net: Network namespace identifier.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.uid-map
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/uid_map: User-namespace UID translation table. Format: 'inside_uid host_uid count' lines. Writable by privileged caller in parent namespace, OR (unprivileged) only a 1:1 mapping for the calling user unless setgroups=deny written first (and gid_map after).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.gid-map
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/gid_map: User-namespace GID translation table. Companion to uid_map.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.namespace-proc-file.setgroups
observations: namespace-proc-file./proc/<pid>/setgroups: Gates setgroups(2) inside the userns. Must be 'deny' before unprivileged gid_map write.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.init
observations: kernel-cmdline.init=: Override the user-space init binary the kernel execs after rootfs mount.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.root
observations: kernel-cmdline.root=: Root filesystem device. Specifier forms: /dev/sda1, UUID=..., LABEL=..., PARTUUID=...

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.ro
observations: kernel-cmdline.ro: Mount root filesystem read-only at boot (init usually remounts rw later).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.rw
observations: kernel-cmdline.rw: Mount root read-write at boot.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.quiet
observations: kernel-cmdline.quiet: Suppress most boot messages on console.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.splash
observations: kernel-cmdline.splash: Show graphical boot splash (plymouth integration).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.loglevel
observations: kernel-cmdline.loglevel=: Kernel printk minimum log level for console (0=emerg .. 7=debug).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.console
observations: kernel-cmdline.console=: Console device for kernel messages (and optionally early-userspace). e.g. console=ttyS0,115200.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.panic
observations: kernel-cmdline.panic=: Auto-reboot delay after kernel panic. 0 = never reboot.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.mem
observations: kernel-cmdline.mem=: Force kernel to use only N bytes/MB/GB of RAM (e.g. mem=4G).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.crashkernel
observations: kernel-cmdline.crashkernel=: Reserve memory for kdump capture kernel. e.g. crashkernel=256M.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.nokaslr
observations: kernel-cmdline.nokaslr: Disable kernel address-space layout randomization. Useful for kernel debugging.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.mitigations
observations: kernel-cmdline.mitigations=: CPU vulnerability mitigations (Spectre/Meltdown family). off = max performance, no protection.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.intel-iommu
observations: kernel-cmdline.intel_iommu=: Enable Intel IOMMU (VT-d) for DMA remapping. Required for VFIO PCI passthrough.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.iommu
observations: kernel-cmdline.iommu=: Generic IOMMU mode. 'pt' = passthrough mode for the host kernel.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.intel-pstate
observations: kernel-cmdline.intel_pstate=: Intel P-state CPU frequency driver mode.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.cgroup-no-v1
observations: kernel-cmdline.cgroup_no_v1=: Disable v1 hierarchies for the listed controllers. e.g. cgroup_no_v1=all to enforce v2-only.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.systemd-unified-cgroup
observations: kernel-cmdline.systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy: systemd's preference for cgroup v2 unified hierarchy. 1 = pure v2; 0 = legacy v1.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.transparent-hugepage
observations: kernel-cmdline.transparent_hugepage=: THP allocation policy. 'never' often recommended for DBs (Mongo, Redis) due to defrag latency.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.hugepagesz
observations: kernel-cmdline.hugepagesz=: Huge page size to allocate at boot (combine with hugepages=).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.hugepages
observations: kernel-cmdline.hugepages=: Number of huge pages to reserve at boot (size from hugepagesz=).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.ipv6-disable
observations: kernel-cmdline.ipv6.disable=: Disable IPv6 entirely at kernel level.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.audit
observations: kernel-cmdline.audit=: Enable kernel audit subsystem at boot.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.lsm
observations: kernel-cmdline.lsm=: Order in which LSMs initialize. Stackable LSMs evaluated in this order.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.selinux
observations: kernel-cmdline.selinux=: Enable/disable SELinux at boot. Combines with enforcing= for mode.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.kernel-cmdline.enforcing
observations: kernel-cmdline.enforcing=: SELinux enforcing/permissive at boot.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.in-flight
observations: iostat-field.in_flight: /proc/diskstats field: number of IOs currently in progress on the device.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.io-ticks
observations: iostat-field.io_ticks: /proc/diskstats field: total time spent doing IOs (saturation indicator).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.read-ios
observations: iostat-field.read_ios: Total reads completed.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.read-merges
observations: iostat-field.read_merges: Reads merged before queueing (block layer optimization indicator).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.read-sectors
observations: iostat-field.read_sectors: Sectors read (sector = 512 bytes traditionally).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.write-ios
observations: iostat-field.write_ios: Total writes completed.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.write-merges
observations: iostat-field.write_merges: Writes merged before queueing.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.iostat-field.write-sectors
observations: iostat-field.write_sectors: Sectors written.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.credential-flag.secbit-noroot
observations: credential-flag.SECBIT_NOROOT: If set, UID 0 does NOT confer root capabilities (no auto-grant of full P set on UID 0).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.credential-flag.secbit-no-setuid-fixup
observations: credential-flag.SECBIT_NO_SETUID_FIXUP: If set, capability sets are NOT recalculated on UID 0↔nonzero transitions.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.credential-flag.secbit-keep-caps
observations: credential-flag.SECBIT_KEEP_CAPS: If set, capabilities are preserved when UID 0 changes to nonzero (vs being cleared). Same as PR_SET_KEEPCAPS.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.credential-flag.secbit-noroot-locked
observations: credential-flag.SECBIT_NOROOT_LOCKED: Locks SECBIT_NOROOT — cannot be cleared after setting.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.get-keyring-id
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_GET_KEYRING_ID: Get the ID of a special keyring (thread, process, session, user, etc.) — possibly creating it.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.join-session-keyring
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING: Replace the session keyring with a new (named or anonymous) one.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.revoke
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_REVOKE: Mark a key revoked — subsequent ops on it return EKEYREVOKED.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.link
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_LINK: Add a key to a keyring.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.unlink
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_UNLINK: Remove a key from a keyring.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.search
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_SEARCH: Search a keyring (and subkeyrings) for a key matching type+description.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.keyring-operation.read
observations: keyring-operation.KEYCTL_READ: Read the payload of a key (if read permission granted).

name: linux.primitives.cfg.pthread-attr.detachstate
observations: pthread-attr.detachstate: Whether thread is joinable (default) or starts detached.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.pthread-attr.stacksize
observations: pthread-attr.stacksize: Initial stack size for new thread. Honor RLIMIT_STACK by default.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.pthread-attr.scope
observations: pthread-attr.scope: Contention scope. SYSTEM (Linux NPTL only supports this) = compete with all system threads.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.pthread-attr.schedpolicy
observations: pthread-attr.schedpolicy: Scheduling policy for the new thread.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.signal-safety-rule.async-safe-functions
observations: signal-safety-rule.async-signal-safe-set: signal-safety(7) lists ~80 functions safe to call from a signal handler. Includes _exit, abort, accept, alarm, chdir, close, dup, execve, fork, fstat, kill, listen, lseek, open, pipe, raise, read, recv, send, setpgid, setsid, sigaction, sigprocmask, write — but NOT printf, malloc, fprintf, syslog.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.signal-safety-rule.no-malloc-in-handler
observations: signal-safety-rule.no-malloc-in-handler: malloc/free are NOT async-signal-safe (they take internal locks). Calling them from a signal handler can deadlock if the interrupted code held the same lock.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.signal-safety-rule.no-stdio-in-handler
observations: signal-safety-rule.no-stdio-in-handler: stdio (printf, fprintf, fopen) is NOT async-signal-safe — locks per-FILE. Use write(2) directly to STDERR_FILENO if you must log from a handler.

name: linux.primitives.cfg.signal-safety-rule.errno-save-restore
observations: signal-safety-rule.errno-save-restore: Signal handler MUST save+restore errno around any syscall that might modify it; otherwise the interrupted code sees a corrupted errno.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.ip-forward
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.ip_forward: Enable IPv4 packet forwarding (router/NAT functionality). Required for `iptables -j MASQUERADE` to work, and what `docker -p` requires on the host. Disabled = host won't route packets between interfaces.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-syncookies
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies: Enable SYN cookie protection against SYN floods. 1 = engage when SYN queue overflows; 2 = always. Default 1 — almost always leave on.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-fin-timeout
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout: Time held in FIN_WAIT_2 before forced cleanup. Lowering helps clear orphaned half-closed sockets faster (high-load proxies sometimes set 30).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-tw-reuse
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse: Allow reuse of TIME_WAIT sockets for new outbound connections (only safe with timestamps option). 2 = loopback only (safer default since 4.12).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-max-syn-backlog
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog: Max half-open connections (SYN_RECV) per listening socket before SYN cookies kick in. Raise on heavy connection-rate servers.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-max-tw-buckets
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_max_tw_buckets: Cap on TIME_WAIT sockets system-wide. Beyond this, TIME_WAIT entries are dropped immediately — risky with delayed-segment scenarios.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.ip-local-port-range
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range: Ephemeral port range for outbound connections. Widen on hosts opening many concurrent outbound conns to a single dest:port (e.g. proxy to backend). Format: low high.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-fastopen
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen: TFO mode bitmask. 1 = client, 2 = server, 3 = both, 4-9 = various with-cookie modes. Default 1 (client only).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-keepalive-time
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time: Idle time before keepalive probes start. Per-socket override via TCP_KEEPIDLE.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-keepalive-intvl
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl: Interval between keepalive probes. Per-socket: TCP_KEEPINTVL.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-keepalive-probes
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes: Number of failed probes before connection is reset. Per-socket: TCP_KEEPCNT.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-rmem
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_rmem: TCP receive buffer auto-tune: min default max bytes. SO_RCVBUF setsockopt overrides (and disables auto-tune for that socket).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-wmem
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_wmem: TCP send buffer auto-tune: min default max bytes.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-congestion-control
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control: System-wide default. Available algorithms in net.ipv4.tcp_available_congestion_control. Common: cubic (default), bbr, reno, dctcp.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-mtu-probing
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing: Enable PMTU probing fallback (when ICMP needed-fragment is blocked). 1 = enable on PMTUD blackhole detection; 2 = always enable.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-window-scaling
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_window_scaling: RFC 1323 window scaling. Disable only if a buggy middlebox strips the option.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-timestamps
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps: RFC 1323 timestamps. Required for tcp_tw_reuse, PAWS protection, accurate RTT.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-sack
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_sack: Selective ACK (RFC 2018). Improves recovery from multiple-segment losses.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-syn-retries
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_syn_retries: SYN retransmissions before connect() gives up. With default ~127s total timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-retries2
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_retries2: Retries on established connection before giving up. Default ~15min total.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-orphan-retries
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_orphan_retries: Retries on connection that the local end has closed. 0 = use system default 8.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-no-metrics-save
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_no_metrics_save: 0 = save TCP metrics (cwnd, ssthresh) per-destination; 1 = disable. Saved metrics speed connection ramp-up to known-good destinations.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-slow-start-after-idle
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle: Reset cwnd to initial after RTO-equivalent idle. Disable for keepalive-using long-lived connections.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-rfc1337
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_rfc1337: Reject RST in TIME_WAIT (avoids the rare race in RFC 1337).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.icmp-echo-ignore-all
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_all: 1 = stop responding to ICMP echo (ping). Hardening for hosts that don't want to be pingable.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.icmp-echo-ignore-broadcasts
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts: 1 = ignore broadcast ping (Smurf attack mitigation).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-rp-filter
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter: Reverse path filter. 1 = strict (drop packets if return path doesn't match arrival interface — RFC 3704). 2 = loose. 0 = off. Container/VM hosts often need 2 or 0 for asymmetric routing.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-accept-redirects
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects: Accept ICMP redirects (router can tell host of better next-hop). 0 = ignore (security hardening; routers/NAT boxes always 0).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-send-redirects
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects: Send ICMP redirects when this host routes a packet that would have been better sent direct. 0 = silent (most non-router hosts).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-arp-ignore
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_ignore: Reply to ARP requests for any local IP (0) vs only if target IP is on the receiving interface (1). Important for multi-homed hosts to avoid wrong-interface-replies.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-arp-announce
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.arp_announce: Source IP selection for outgoing ARP requests. 2 = always use the IP on the announcing interface (avoids leaking other-interface IPs).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.conf-all-proxy-arp
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.conf.all.proxy_arp: Respond to ARP for IPs on other interfaces. Used in some bridging/routing setups.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.ip-no-pmtu-disc
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc: 1 = disable Path MTU Discovery system-wide (don't set DF bit). Workaround for broken intermediate ICMP filtering.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.ip-default-ttl
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.ip_default_ttl: Default TTL for outgoing IPv4 packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-available-congestion-control
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_available_congestion_control: List of compiled-in congestion control algorithms.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-allowed-congestion-control
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_allowed_congestion_control: Algorithms unprivileged users can select per-socket via TCP_CONGESTION.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-notsent-lowat
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_notsent_lowat: Limit unsent bytes in send queue when EPOLLOUT triggers. Helps app-layer paced sending. Per-socket: TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-ecn
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_ecn: Explicit Congestion Notification. 0=off, 1=on, 2=passive (advertise but don't initiate).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv4.tcp-low-latency
observations: sysctl-net.ipv4.net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency: Hint to kernel to favor latency over throughput in scheduling decisions.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-disable-ipv6
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6: 1 = disable IPv6 on all interfaces. Persistent disable: also set in sysctl.d. Better to set per-interface if some need IPv6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-forwarding
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding: Enable IPv6 forwarding (router functionality).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-accept-ra
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra: Accept Router Advertisement. 2 = accept even with forwarding=1 (otherwise RAs ignored on routers).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-autoconf
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.autoconf: SLAAC (stateless autoconfig) on/off.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-use-tempaddr
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.use_tempaddr: RFC 4941 privacy temp addresses. 0 = off, 1 = generate but don't prefer, 2 = generate and prefer.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.conf-all-accept-source-route
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route: Accept source-routed packets. 0 = drop (security default).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.bindv6only
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.bindv6only: 0 = AF_INET6 socket also accepts v4 (mapped). 1 = v6-only by default. Per-socket override IPV6_V6ONLY.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.icmp-ratelimit
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.icmp.ratelimit: Min ms between ICMPv6 error messages (rate limit).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-ipv6.route-max-size
observations: sysctl-net.ipv6.net.ipv6.route.max_size: Max IPv6 routing cache entries.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.somaxconn
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.somaxconn: Hard ceiling on listen() backlog. App requests min(app, somaxconn). Raise on heavy connection-rate servers.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.netdev-max-backlog
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.netdev_max_backlog: Per-CPU max packets queued from NIC to softnet (between IRQ and IP stack). Drops here visible in /proc/net/softnet_stat. Raise on 10G+ NICs.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.rmem-max
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.rmem_max: Max value SO_RCVBUF can be set to. Raise to allow apps to set larger buffers (typical: 16777216).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.wmem-max
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.wmem_max: Max value SO_SNDBUF can be set to.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.rmem-default
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.rmem_default: Default SO_RCVBUF for new sockets (non-TCP — TCP uses tcp_rmem auto-tune).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.wmem-default
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.wmem_default: Default SO_SNDBUF.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.optmem-max
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.optmem_max: Max ancillary buffer per socket (for SCM_RIGHTS, IP_PKTINFO, etc.).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.bpf-jit-enable
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.bpf_jit_enable: BPF JIT compilation. 1 = on, 2 = on + log to kernel ring buffer.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.bpf-jit-harden
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.bpf_jit_harden: BPF JIT hardening (constant blinding) against spectre-style attacks. 1 = unprivileged users only, 2 = all.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.busy-poll
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.busy_poll: Poll-mode socket recv (low latency at cost of CPU). Per-socket: SO_BUSY_POLL.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.busy-read
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.busy_read: Same as busy_poll but for socket read.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-core.default-qdisc
observations: sysctl-net.core.net.core.default_qdisc: Default queueing discipline assigned to new interfaces. fq_codel is bufferbloat-resistant; bbr congestion control wants fq.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-max
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max: Max connection-tracking entries. Hitting it = `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` in dmesg, new conns drop. Raise on busy NAT/firewall hosts.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-buckets
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets: Conntrack hash table bucket count. Set to nf_conntrack_max/4 typically. Boot-time only on some kernels.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-tcp-timeout-established
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established: How long ESTABLISHED entries persist without traffic. Long-lived TCP through stateful FW must use TCP keepalive shorter than this OR firewall will silently lose state, killing the conn on next packet.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-tcp-timeout-time-wait
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait: TIME_WAIT timeout in conntrack.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-tcp-timeout-close-wait
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait: CLOSE_WAIT timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-tcp-timeout-fin-wait
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_fin_wait: FIN_WAIT timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-tcp-timeout-syn-sent
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_syn_sent: SYN_SENT timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-udp-timeout
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout: UDP unidirectional timeout (seen one direction only).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-udp-timeout-stream
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout_stream: UDP bidirectional (assumed stream) timeout. e.g. DNS round-trip.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-icmp-timeout
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_icmp_timeout: ICMP timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-generic-timeout
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_generic_timeout: Catch-all for protocols without specific timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-checksum
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_checksum: Verify packet checksum before tracking.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-helper
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_helper: Auto-load conntrack ALG helpers (FTP, SIP, TFTP, IRC). 0 = require explicit loading (security default since 4.7).

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-acct
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_acct: Per-flow byte/packet counters. Doubles conntrack entry size.

name: linux.networking.cfg.sysctl-net-netfilter.nf-conntrack-log-invalid
observations: sysctl-net.netfilter.net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_log_invalid: Log packets that fail conntrack validation. 6 = TCP, 17 = UDP, 1 = ICMP, 255 = all.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-reuseaddr
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_REUSEADDR: Allow bind() to address still in TIME_WAIT, or to wildcard when specific is bound (and vice versa).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-reuseport
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_REUSEPORT: Allow MULTIPLE listeners on same address+port; kernel hashes incoming connections across them. The way to scale accept() across CPU cores.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-keepalive
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_KEEPALIVE: Enable TCP keepalive on this socket. Defaults from net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_*.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-linger
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_LINGER: On close(), if linger.l_onoff && data queued: block up to l_linger seconds. l_linger=0 → RST instead of FIN (immediate close, no TIME_WAIT — useful for short-lived clients but discards in-flight data).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-rcvbuf
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_RCVBUF: Receive buffer size. Setting disables TCP auto-tuning. Cap by net.core.rmem_max.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-sndbuf
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_SNDBUF: Send buffer size.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-rcvtimeo
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_RCVTIMEO: Per-socket recv timeout. recv() returns EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK after this elapses.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-sndtimeo
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_SNDTIMEO: Per-socket send timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-broadcast
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_BROADCAST: Allow sendto() to broadcast addresses (UDP only). Required for DHCP clients, etc.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-error
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_ERROR: Pending socket-level error. Reading clears it. Used after non-blocking connect() to retrieve actual error.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-type
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_TYPE: Socket type (SOCK_STREAM/DGRAM/SEQPACKET/RAW). Useful for libraries given a generic FD.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-bindtodevice
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_BINDTODEVICE: Bind socket to specific interface. Requires CAP_NET_RAW. Used by VPN clients to send out a tunnel.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-mark
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_MARK: Set fwmark on outgoing packets. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN. Used by policy routing.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-passcred
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_PASSCRED: Receive SCM_CREDENTIALS ancillary data with each message (PID/UID/GID of sender). AF_UNIX only.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-peercred
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_PEERCRED: Get credentials of peer process at connect time. AF_UNIX. The mechanism systemd uses to identify clients on /run/systemd/private.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-priority
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_PRIORITY: Sets skb->priority for tc qdisc selection. CAP_NET_ADMIN for >6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-busy-poll
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_BUSY_POLL: Per-socket busy-polling for low-latency reads.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-SO.so-incoming-cpu
observations: socket-option-SO_*.SO_INCOMING_CPU: Hint kernel which CPU should handle this socket's RX (RFS/XPS coordination).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-nodelay
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_NODELAY: Disable Nagle's algorithm. Send writes immediately. Latency-critical apps.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-cork
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_CORK: Coalesce sends until uncorked. Linux-specific. Pairs with sendfile(2) for header+body.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-keepidle
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_KEEPIDLE: Per-socket override of net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-keepintvl
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_KEEPINTVL: Per-socket interval between keepalive probes.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-keepcnt
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_KEEPCNT: Per-socket failed-probe count before reset.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-maxseg
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_MAXSEG: Max segment size hint. Set before connect() to advertise smaller MSS.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-quickack
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_QUICKACK: Disable delayed ACKs (immediately ACK on read). Latency-helpful, throughput-hurtful. Reset to 0 after each packet.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-defer-accept
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT: Don't return from accept() until data arrives (or N seconds pass). Saves a wakeup on protocols where client speaks first (HTTP).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-syncnt
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_SYNCNT: Per-socket override of tcp_syn_retries.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-info
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_INFO: Per-connection TCP state: cwnd, ssthresh, rtt, retransmits, etc. ss -ti uses this.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-congestion
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_CONGESTION: Per-socket congestion control algorithm name.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-fastopen
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_FASTOPEN: Server-side: backlog of TFO-pending connections.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-fastopen-connect
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT: Client-side: enable TFO for next connect().

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-user-timeout
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_USER_TIMEOUT: Override default tcp_retries2 with explicit ms timeout for unACKed data.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-TCP.tcp-notsent-lowat
observations: socket-option-TCP_*.TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT: Per-socket NOTSENT low-water mark for EPOLLOUT.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-v6only
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_V6ONLY: 1 = AF_INET6 socket binds only IPv6 (no v4-mapped).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-recvpktinfo
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_RECVPKTINFO: Receive in_pktinfo ancillary data (which interface, dst addr).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-multicast-hops
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS: Multicast TTL for outgoing v6 multicast.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-unicast-hops
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_UNICAST_HOPS: Unicast TTL for outgoing v6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-multicast-loop
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_MULTICAST_LOOP: Loop multicast back to local sender.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-add-membership
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_ADD_MEMBERSHIP: Join multicast group on specified interface.

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-option-IPV6.ipv6-tclass
observations: socket-option-IPV6_*.IPV6_TCLASS: Traffic class (DSCP) for outgoing v6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.accept
observations: iptables-target-action.ACCEPT: Allow packet, end traversal of current chain.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.drop
observations: iptables-target-action.DROP: Silently discard packet. Sender sees a black hole (timeout).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.reject
observations: iptables-target-action.REJECT: Drop and send ICMP/RST back. Polite alternative to DROP — sender knows immediately. --reject-with: icmp-port-unreachable (default), icmp-net-unreachable, tcp-reset, etc.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.log
observations: iptables-target-action.LOG: Log packet to kernel ring buffer (dmesg/journald). Doesn't terminate traversal — packet continues to next rule.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.return
observations: iptables-target-action.RETURN: Return from user-defined chain to caller. In built-in chain = use chain's default policy.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.snat
observations: iptables-target-action.SNAT: Source NAT — rewrite source IP/port of outbound packets. POSTROUTING only. e.g. --to-source 1.2.3.4 or range 1.2.3.4-1.2.3.10.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.dnat
observations: iptables-target-action.DNAT: Destination NAT — rewrite dest IP/port. PREROUTING (or OUTPUT for local-out). The mechanism behind `docker -p`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.masquerade
observations: iptables-target-action.MASQUERADE: Like SNAT but auto-pick source IP from outgoing interface. POSTROUTING only. The way to NAT private network behind a dynamically-assigned public IP.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.redirect
observations: iptables-target-action.REDIRECT: DNAT to local machine. PREROUTING (or OUTPUT for local). Used by transparent proxies (incoming :80 → local :8080).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.mark
observations: iptables-target-action.MARK: Set fwmark on packet. mangle table. Used with policy routing (`ip rule fwmark X`).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-target-action.tcpmss
observations: iptables-target-action.TCPMSS: Clamp TCP MSS option. mangle FORWARD chain. Common workaround for MTU-mismatch on PPPoE/tunnel uplinks.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.protocol
observations: iptables-match-option.-p: Match protocol: tcp|udp|icmp|esp|ah|sctp|all|<num>.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.source
observations: iptables-match-option.-s: Match source IP.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.destination
observations: iptables-match-option.-d: Match destination IP.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.in-interface
observations: iptables-match-option.-i: Match input interface (PREROUTING/INPUT/FORWARD).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.out-interface
observations: iptables-match-option.-o: Match output interface (FORWARD/OUTPUT/POSTROUTING).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.sport
observations: iptables-match-option.--sport: Source port (tcp/udp). Range with colon.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.dport
observations: iptables-match-option.--dport: Destination port (tcp/udp).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.state
observations: iptables-match-option.-m state --state: Conntrack state match. The cornerstone of stateful firewalls.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.conntrack
observations: iptables-match-option.-m conntrack --ctstate: Modern equivalent of -m state. Superset of state matches; also --ctorigsrc, --ctorigdst, --ctstatus.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.tcp-flags
observations: iptables-match-option.--tcp-flags: Match specific TCP flags. e.g. `--tcp-flags ALL SYN` = SYN-only (no other flags) packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.syn
observations: iptables-match-option.--syn: Shorthand for --tcp-flags SYN,RST,ACK SYN — matches new TCP connection attempts.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.icmp-type
observations: iptables-match-option.--icmp-type: e.g. --icmp-type echo-request. iptables -p icmp -h lists names.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.multiport
observations: iptables-match-option.-m multiport --dports: Match multiple ports in one rule (up to 15).

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.limit
observations: iptables-match-option.-m limit --limit: Token-bucket rate limit. e.g. --limit 5/sec. --limit-burst sets burst size.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.recent
observations: iptables-match-option.-m recent: Per-IP rate limiting / temporary blocklist. Used for SSH brute-force protection.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.owner
observations: iptables-match-option.-m owner --uid-owner: Match by sending process UID. OUTPUT only. Used for per-user firewall rules.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.mark
observations: iptables-match-option.-m mark --mark: Match fwmark.

name: linux.networking.cfg.iptables-match-option.physdev
observations: iptables-match-option.-m physdev: Match physical interface (when bridged). Useful for FORWARD rules on br_netfilter setups.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.inet
observations: nft-family.inet: Unified IPv4+IPv6. Modern default — write rules once, applies to both. e.g. `add table inet filter`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.ip
observations: nft-family.ip: IPv4 only.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.ip6
observations: nft-family.ip6: IPv6 only.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.arp
observations: nft-family.arp: ARP packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.bridge
observations: nft-family.bridge: Bridge family — runs at L2 within Linux bridge.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-family.netdev
observations: nft-family.netdev: Per-interface ingress/egress at the lowest level (before/after the rest of netfilter). Useful for early-drop.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ip-saddr
observations: nft-match.ip saddr: IPv4 source address. Supports CIDR, ranges, named sets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ip-daddr
observations: nft-match.ip daddr: IPv4 dest address.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ip6-saddr
observations: nft-match.ip6 saddr: IPv6 source.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ip6-daddr
observations: nft-match.ip6 daddr: IPv6 dest.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.tcp-dport
observations: nft-match.tcp dport: TCP destination port. e.g. `tcp dport { 22, 80, 443 }` matches any of those.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.tcp-sport
observations: nft-match.tcp sport: TCP source port.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.udp-dport
observations: nft-match.udp dport: UDP destination port.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.tcp-flags
observations: nft-match.tcp flags: TCP flags. e.g. `tcp flags syn` matches SYN-set packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.icmp-type
observations: nft-match.icmp type: ICMP message type. e.g. `icmp type echo-request`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ct-state
observations: nft-match.ct state: Conntrack state. e.g. `ct state established,related accept`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.ct-mark
observations: nft-match.ct mark: Conntrack mark.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.meta-iif
observations: nft-match.meta iif: Input interface.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.meta-oif
observations: nft-match.meta oif: Output interface.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.meta-mark
observations: nft-match.meta mark: skb fwmark.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.meta-priority
observations: nft-match.meta priority: skb priority (for tc).

name: linux.networking.cfg.nft-match.meta-cgroup
observations: nft-match.meta cgroup: Cgroup ID of sending process. Per-cgroup firewall rules.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.host
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.host: Match packets to/from host. Combine with src/dst: `src host 1.2.3.4`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.port
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.port: Source or destination port. `port 80` matches both directions.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.src
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.src: Restrict next host/port to source side.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.dst
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.dst: Restrict next host/port to dest side.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.tcp
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.tcp: Match TCP packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.udp
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.udp: Match UDP packets.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.icmp
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.icmp: Match ICMPv4.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.icmp6
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.icmp6: Match ICMPv6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.net
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.net: Match CIDR network. e.g. `net 192.168.1.0/24`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.proto
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.proto: Match IP protocol number/name.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.ether
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.ether: L2 — `ether host MAC`, `ether broadcast`, `ether multicast`, `ether proto`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.vlan
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.vlan: Match VLAN-tagged frames. Optional ID: `vlan 10`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.tcp-flags
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.tcp[tcpflags]: Bit-mask access to TCP flags. e.g. `tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0` (SYN set).

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.greater
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.greater: Packet length filter: `greater 1500`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.tcpdump-filter-keyword.less
observations: tcpdump-filter-keyword.less: Packet length filter: `less 64`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.nameserver
observations: resolv-conf-directive.nameserver: DNS server IP. Up to 3 (MAXNS); used in order. e.g. `nameserver 8.8.8.8`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.search
observations: resolv-conf-directive.search: Domain search list. Names with fewer dots than `ndots` get search-list suffixes appended. Up to 6 domains.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.domain
observations: resolv-conf-directive.domain: Local domain. Single-element search list (deprecated; use search).

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-ndots
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options ndots:N: Threshold for relative-vs-absolute lookup. Kubernetes default ndots:5.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-timeout
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options timeout:N: Per-query timeout.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-attempts
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options attempts:N: Resend attempts before giving up.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-rotate
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options rotate: Round-robin nameservers (vs always start at first).

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-single-request
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options single-request: Send A and AAAA queries serially (vs concurrent). Workaround for buggy DNS servers.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-single-request-reopen
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options single-request-reopen: Use separate sockets for A and AAAA. Avoids race in some setups.

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-edns0
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options edns0: Enable EDNS0 (larger UDP responses).

name: linux.networking.cfg.resolv-conf-directive.options-trust-ad
observations: resolv-conf-directive.options trust-ad: Pass the AD (authenticated data) bit through to applications.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.passwd
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.passwd: Source(s) for getpwnam/getpwuid. e.g. `passwd: files systemd ldap`.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.group
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.group: Source(s) for getgrnam/getgrgid.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.hosts
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.hosts: Source(s) for getaddrinfo. e.g. `hosts: files mdns_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] resolve [!UNAVAIL=return] dns`. Order matters.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.networks
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.networks: Source(s) for getnetbyname.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.services
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.services: Source(s) for getservbyname (port ↔ service name).

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.protocols
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.protocols: Source(s) for getprotobyname (proto ↔ number).

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.shadow
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.shadow: Source for shadow passwords.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.netgroup
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.netgroup: Source for netgroups (NIS/NIS+).

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.aliases
