observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.aliases: Mail aliases.

name: linux.networking.cfg.nsswitch-conf-directive.initgroups
observations: nsswitch-conf-directive.initgroups: Source for initgroups (supplementary GIDs).

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-route
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_ROUTE: Interfaces, addresses, routes, neighbours, qdiscs, filters. The thing `ip` and `tc` use.

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-netfilter
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_NETFILTER: nftables, conntrack, ulogd.

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-audit
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_AUDIT: Linux audit subsystem (auditd talks here).

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-generic
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_GENERIC: Generic netlink — multiplexed family for new subsystems (devlink, l2tp, taskstats, drm, fou, etc.).

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-kobject-uevent
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT: Kernel ↔ udev events (device hotplug).

name: linux.networking.cfg.netlink-family.netlink-firewall
observations: netlink-family.NETLINK_FIREWALL: Old netfilter packet queueing. Largely superseded by NFQUEUE.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollin
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLIN: Data available to read.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollout
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLOUT: Buffer space available to write.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollerr
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLERR: Error condition. Always reported (don't need to register).

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollhup
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLHUP: Hang up. Always reported.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollrdhup
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLRDHUP: Peer half-closed (FIN received). Useful to detect disconnect without consuming all data first.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollet
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLET: Edge-triggered. Event reported once per state change.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epolloneshot
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLONESHOT: After event delivery, FD is disabled until rearmed via EPOLL_CTL_MOD.

name: linux.networking.cfg.epoll-event-flag.epollexclusive
observations: epoll-event-flag.EPOLLEXCLUSIVE: Wake only one waiter (avoid thundering herd when multiple epoll_wait()ers monitor the same FD).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-level-SOL.sol-socket
observations: socket-level-SOL_*.SOL_SOCKET: Socket-layer options (SO_*).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-level-SOL.sol-tcp
observations: socket-level-SOL_*.SOL_TCP / IPPROTO_TCP: TCP-layer options (TCP_*).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-level-SOL.sol-udp
observations: socket-level-SOL_*.SOL_UDP / IPPROTO_UDP: UDP-layer options (UDP_*).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-level-SOL.sol-ip
observations: socket-level-SOL_*.IPPROTO_IP: IPv4 options (IP_*).

name: linux.networking.cfg.socket-level-SOL.sol-ipv6
observations: socket-level-SOL_*.IPPROTO_IPV6: IPv6 options (IPV6_*).

name: linux.networking.cfg.hosts-file-directive.host-entry
observations: hosts-file-directive.<IP>\t<canonical-name>\t[<alias>...]: Per-line host entry. e.g. `127.0.0.1 localhost`. Tab or space separated. Consulted by glibc when nsswitch hosts has 'files' before 'dns'.

name: linux.networking.cfg.hosts-file-directive.comment
observations: hosts-file-directive.# comment: # starts a comment to end-of-line.

name: linux.networking.cfg.bridge-config-file.bridge-nf-call-iptables
observations: bridge-config-file.net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables: When 1, bridged packets traverse iptables FORWARD. The mechanism behind container-traffic firewalling on docker0. Some kubernetes setups require this.

name: linux.networking.cfg.bridge-config-file.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables
observations: bridge-config-file.net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables: Same for IPv6.

name: linux.networking.cfg.bridge-config-file.bridge-nf-call-arptables
observations: bridge-config-file.net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-arptables: ARP-level. Rarely needed.

name: linux.networking.cfg.bridge-config-file.bridge-nf-filter-vlan-tagged
observations: bridge-config-file.net.bridge.bridge-nf-filter-vlan-tagged: Filter VLAN-tagged frames at iptables level.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-map-lookup-elem
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_map_lookup_elem: Look up a key in a BPF map; return pointer to value (or NULL). The most-used helper across nearly every BPF program.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-map-update-elem
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_map_update_elem: Insert or update a key/value pair in a BPF map. Flags: BPF_ANY, BPF_NOEXIST, BPF_EXIST.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-map-delete-elem
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_map_delete_elem: Delete a key from a BPF map.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-probe-read
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_probe_read: Safely read kernel memory (handles page faults). Used to deref kernel pointers in tracing programs. Modern split: bpf_probe_read_kernel() / bpf_probe_read_user().

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-probe-read-str
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_probe_read_str: Safely read a NUL-terminated string from kernel memory (caps at buf size). Used to read filenames in syscall args.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-ktime-get-ns
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_ktime_get_ns: Current monotonic time in ns. The cheapest timestamp source in BPF.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-current-pid-tgid
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_current_pid_tgid: Returns u64 = (tgid << 32) | pid. tgid is the user-visible PID; pid is the kernel TID.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-current-uid-gid
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_current_uid_gid: Returns u64 = (gid << 32) | uid of current task.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-current-comm
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_current_comm: Get the comm (16-char process name) of current task.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-current-task
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_current_task: Pointer to current task_struct. Combined with bpf_probe_read for accessing task fields safely.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-stackid
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_stackid: Sample current call stack into BPF_MAP_TYPE_STACK_TRACE; returns key. The stack-trace primitive for flame graphs.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-stack
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_stack: Newer stack getter — returns into caller-supplied buffer (vs map). Allows variable-depth and userspace stacks.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-perf-event-output
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_perf_event_output: Push a record to a BPF_MAP_TYPE_PERF_EVENT_ARRAY (per-CPU ring buffer, consumed by userspace via perf_event ring).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-ringbuf-output
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_ringbuf_output: 5.8+ — push a record to BPF_MAP_TYPE_RINGBUF (single MPMC ring shared across CPUs).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-ringbuf-reserve
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_ringbuf_reserve: Reserve N bytes in ring buffer; returns pointer to write into.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-ringbuf-submit
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_ringbuf_submit: Commit a previously-reserved ringbuf write.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-trace-printk
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_trace_printk: Debug printf to /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/trace_pipe. Limited (1 string + 3 args). For real output, use perf_event_output or ringbuf.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-tail-call
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_tail_call: Jump to another BPF program (in BPF_MAP_TYPE_PROG_ARRAY). Doesn't return — used to chain programs and bypass the 1M-instruction verifier limit.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-spin-lock
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_spin_lock: Take a spinlock embedded in a map value. Pairs with bpf_spin_unlock. Race-free updates.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-skb-load-bytes
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_skb_load_bytes: Read bytes from skb (network packet) into BPF stack. The packet-inspection primitive for tc/socket-filter programs.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-redirect
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_redirect: Redirect skb to specified ifindex. Used by XDP for fast in-kernel packet steering.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-override-return
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_override_return: Override return value of a kprobed function. Requires CONFIG_BPF_KPROBE_OVERRIDE + ALLOW_ERROR_INJECTION. Used for fault injection.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-send-signal
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_send_signal: Send signal to current task from BPF. Useful for killing processes that hit a tracing condition.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-ns-current-pid-tgid
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_ns_current_pid_tgid: PID/TGID in a specific PID namespace. Critical for container-aware tracing — the host PID and container PID differ.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-helper.bpf-get-current-cgroup-id
observations: bpf-helper.bpf_get_current_cgroup_id: Cgroup ID of current task. Useful for filtering tracing to specific containers.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.prog-load
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_PROG_LOAD: Verify and load a BPF program into the kernel. Returns FD to the program.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.map-create
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_MAP_CREATE: Create a BPF map. Returns FD.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.prog-attach
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_PROG_ATTACH: Attach a loaded program to a hook (cgroup, sockmap, sk_skb, lirc, etc.). Modern alternative: BPF_LINK_CREATE.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.prog-detach
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_PROG_DETACH: Detach previously-attached program.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.prog-test-run
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN: Run a program in user-supplied input context for testing. Returns output + retval + duration.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.link-create
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_LINK_CREATE: 5.7+ replacement for PROG_ATTACH. Returns a link FD; closing FD detaches. Cleaner lifetime semantics.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.obj-pin
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_OBJ_PIN: Pin a BPF object (program/map/link) to a path on bpffs (/sys/fs/bpf/...). Survives the loading process exit.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.bpf-cmd-type.btf-load
observations: bpf-cmd-type.BPF_BTF_LOAD: Load BTF (BPF Type Format) — type info for CO-RE (Compile Once Run Everywhere) relocation.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.function
observations: ftrace-tracer.function: Trace every kernel function call. High overhead but complete. Filtered via set_ftrace_filter.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.function-graph
observations: ftrace-tracer.function_graph: Function entry+exit with timing per call. Renders as call tree. Slower than function but more useful for latency.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.nop
observations: ftrace-tracer.nop: Default: no tracing. Tracepoint events still active if enabled separately.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.irqsoff
observations: ftrace-tracer.irqsoff: Track longest IRQ-disabled duration. For latency-sensitive workloads.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.preemptoff
observations: ftrace-tracer.preemptoff: Track longest preemption-disabled duration.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.preemptirqsoff
observations: ftrace-tracer.preemptirqsoff: Combined: longest period where either preempt OR IRQs disabled.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.wakeup
observations: ftrace-tracer.wakeup: Track longest scheduling latency from wake to run.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.wakeup-rt
observations: ftrace-tracer.wakeup_rt: Wakeup tracer for RT-priority tasks only.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-tracer.blk
observations: ftrace-tracer.blk: Block-layer events (used by blktrace).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.tracing-on
observations: ftrace-control-file.tracing_on: Master enable. 1 = capture to ring buffer; 0 = pause.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.current-tracer
observations: ftrace-control-file.current_tracer: Active plugin tracer name.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.set-ftrace-filter
observations: ftrace-control-file.set_ftrace_filter: Restrict function tracer to listed kernel functions. Glob supported.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.set-ftrace-notrace
observations: ftrace-control-file.set_ftrace_notrace: Exclude listed functions.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.trace
observations: ftrace-control-file.trace: Read = formatted trace output. Write empty = clear ring buffer.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.trace-pipe
observations: ftrace-control-file.trace_pipe: Like trace but consumes events as they're read (vs trace which is non-destructive).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.buffer-size-kb
observations: ftrace-control-file.buffer_size_kb: Per-CPU ring buffer size.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.set-event
observations: ftrace-control-file.set_event: List of enabled tracepoint events.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.events-enable
observations: ftrace-control-file.events/<sys>/<event>/enable: Per-event enable file. e.g. echo 1 > events/sched/sched_switch/enable.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.set-pid
observations: ftrace-control-file.set_event_pid: Filter trace to specific PIDs.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.kprobe-events
observations: ftrace-control-file.kprobe_events: Add kprobes via sysfs. e.g. `echo 'p:my_probe vfs_read file=+0(%si)' > kprobe_events`.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.uprobe-events
observations: ftrace-control-file.uprobe_events: Add uprobes. e.g. `echo 'p:my_uprobe /usr/bin/myapp:0x1234' > uprobe_events`.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.tracing-thresh
observations: ftrace-control-file.tracing_thresh: Latency-tracer threshold — only record events exceeding.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.ftrace-control-file.snapshot
observations: ftrace-control-file.snapshot: Read = current snapshot. Write '0' = clear; '1' = swap snapshot↔active buffer.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.sched
observations: trace-event-class.sched: Scheduler events: sched_switch, sched_wakeup, sched_wakeup_new, sched_migrate_task, sched_process_fork, sched_process_exec, sched_process_exit, sched_stat_runtime, sched_stat_iowait, sched_stat_sleep.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.syscalls
observations: trace-event-class.syscalls: sys_enter_<name> / sys_exit_<name> for every syscall. Generated by kernel build.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.irq
observations: trace-event-class.irq: IRQ entry/exit, softirq entry/exit, tasklet entry/exit.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.mm
observations: trace-event-class.mm: Memory: page_alloc, page_free, page_reclaim, kmem_cache_alloc, mm_filemap_*, oom_kill_process.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.block
observations: trace-event-class.block: Block layer: block_rq_issue, block_rq_complete, block_rq_insert, block_bio_queue.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.fs
observations: trace-event-class.fs: File system events: do_sys_open, vfs_*, ext4_*, xfs_*, btrfs_*.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.net
observations: trace-event-class.net: Network: net_dev_xmit, netif_receive_skb.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.tcp
observations: trace-event-class.tcp: TCP events: tcp_send_reset, tcp_retransmit_skb, tcp_destroy_sock, tcp_probe.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.workqueue
observations: trace-event-class.workqueue: workqueue_queue_work, workqueue_execute_start, workqueue_execute_end.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.signal
observations: trace-event-class.signal: signal_generate, signal_deliver.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.cgroup
observations: trace-event-class.cgroup: cgroup_attach_task, cgroup_release.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.exceptions
observations: trace-event-class.exceptions: page_fault_user, page_fault_kernel.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.trace-event-class.kvm
observations: trace-event-class.kvm: VMexit reasons, instruction emulation, irq injection (KVM hypervisor events).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kprobe-syntax.entry-probe
observations: kprobe-syntax.p:NAME FUNC: Kernel function entry probe. e.g. `p:open_probe vfs_open`.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kprobe-syntax.return-probe
observations: kprobe-syntax.r:NAME FUNC: Function return probe. Captures return value via $retval.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kprobe-syntax.offset
observations: kprobe-syntax.FUNC+OFFSET: Probe at OFFSET bytes into FUNC (avoid by default; relies on instruction boundary).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kprobe-syntax.arg-fetch
observations: kprobe-syntax.%REG / +OFFSET($REG): Read register or memory: e.g. %ax (arg in rax), +0(%si) (deref rsi).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kprobe-syntax.type-suffix
observations: kprobe-syntax.:TYPE: Type for fetched value: u8/u16/u32/u64/s8/s16/s32/s64/string/x8/x16/x32/x64.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.uprobe-syntax.user-binary
observations: uprobe-syntax.BINARY:OFFSET or BINARY:SYMBOL: User-space probe location. Symbol resolved via the binary's symtab.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.uprobe-syntax.entry
observations: uprobe-syntax.p:NAME BINARY:SYMBOL: User function entry.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.uprobe-syntax.return
observations: uprobe-syntax.r:NAME BINARY:SYMBOL: User function return.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.uprobe-syntax.usdt
observations: uprobe-syntax.BINARY:PROVIDER:PROBE: User-statically-defined-tracing probe (DTrace-style). Embedded in many language runtimes.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-bootdir
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_BOOTDIR: Where to find capture kernel + initramfs (kdump-tools config).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-kernelver
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_KERNELVER: Capture kernel version.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-cmdline
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_CMDLINE: Boot params for capture kernel.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-cmdline-append
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_CMDLINE_APPEND: Additional capture-kernel boot params (the typical hardening for capture context).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-coredir
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_COREDIR: Where vmcore goes.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-makedumpfile-args
observations: kdump-config.MAKEDUMPFILE_ARGS: makedumpfile invocation in capture kernel.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.kdump-num-dumps
observations: kdump-config.KDUMP_NUM_DUMPS: Max number of saved vmcores before old ones are deleted.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.kdump-config.crashkernel
observations: kdump-config.crashkernel=: Reserved memory for capture kernel — set on host kernel cmdline. Common: 256M-1G.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.run
observations: gdb-command.run / r: Start the program. Arguments after `run` are passed to the program.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.continue
observations: gdb-command.continue / c: Continue execution after a breakpoint.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.break
observations: gdb-command.break / b: Set breakpoint at function name, file:line, or address. e.g. `b main`, `b file.c:42`, `b *0x400500`.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.tbreak
observations: gdb-command.tbreak: Temporary breakpoint (auto-deleted after first hit).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.watch
observations: gdb-command.watch / rwatch / awatch: Watchpoint on memory: write / read / either. Hardware watchpoints if available.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.print
observations: gdb-command.print / p: Evaluate expression. e.g. `p variable`, `p *ptr`, `p func(args)` (calls function).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.backtrace
observations: gdb-command.backtrace / bt: Stack trace. `bt full` includes locals; `bt N` limits depth.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.frame
observations: gdb-command.frame / f: Switch to frame N (in stack).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.up-down
observations: gdb-command.up / down: Move up/down call stack one frame.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.step
observations: gdb-command.step / s: Step into function. Stops at first source line of called function.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.next
observations: gdb-command.next / n: Step over function (don't step in).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.finish
observations: gdb-command.finish: Run until current function returns, then stop.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.list
observations: gdb-command.list / l: Show source around current line.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.disassemble
observations: gdb-command.disassemble / disas: Show machine code. `disas /m` includes source.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.info-threads
observations: gdb-command.info threads: List all threads.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.thread
observations: gdb-command.thread N: Switch to thread N.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.thread-apply
observations: gdb-command.thread apply all CMD: Run CMD on every thread. e.g. `thread apply all bt` for backtrace of every thread.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.info-registers
observations: gdb-command.info registers: Print CPU register values.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.x
observations: gdb-command.x/FMT ADDR: Examine memory. FMT = count + size + format. e.g. `x/16xw $rsp` = 16 hex words at rsp.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.set-var
observations: gdb-command.set var = value: Modify variable. e.g. `set var i = 42`.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.return
observations: gdb-command.return [VALUE]: Force current function to return immediately (with optional value). Skips remaining code.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.attach
observations: gdb-command.attach PID: Attach to running PID.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.detach
observations: gdb-command.detach: Detach from process. Tracee continues normally.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.info-sharedlibrary
observations: gdb-command.info sharedlibrary / info shared: List loaded shared libraries with addresses.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.symbol-file
observations: gdb-command.symbol-file FILE: Load symbols from FILE. Useful when separate-debug-info file isn't auto-found.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.gdb-command.handle
observations: gdb-command.handle SIGNAL OPTIONS: How to handle a signal: nostop/stop, noprint/print, nopass/pass.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.always-exit
observations: audit-rule-key.-a always,exit: Generate record on every syscall exit matching filter.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.never
observations: audit-rule-key.-a never,...: Suppress audit for matching events.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-arch
observations: audit-rule-key.-F arch=b64|b32: Architecture (always specify on multilib hosts to catch both 32+64 syscalls).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-syscall
observations: audit-rule-key.-S SYSCALL[,SYSCALL...]: Syscall name(s).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-uid
observations: audit-rule-key.-F uid=N: Effective UID match.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-auid
observations: audit-rule-key.-F auid=N: Login UID (audit UID — invariant across su/sudo).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-success
observations: audit-rule-key.-F success=0|1: Match only success or failure outcomes.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.field-path
observations: audit-rule-key.-F path=PATH: Specific path.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.key
observations: audit-rule-key.-k KEY: Tag for ausearch -k. e.g. -k 'sensitive_files'.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.watch
observations: audit-rule-key.-w PATH: Watch a file/dir for access.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.audit-rule-key.watch-perms
observations: audit-rule-key.-p r|w|x|a: Permissions to watch: read/write/execute/attribute.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cycles
observations: perf-event.cycles: CPU clock cycles. Default sampling event for perf record.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.instructions
observations: perf-event.instructions: Retired instructions. cycles/instructions = CPI (cycles per instruction); >1 = stall-heavy.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cache-references
observations: perf-event.cache-references: Last-level cache accesses.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cache-misses
observations: perf-event.cache-misses: Last-level cache misses. cache-misses/references = miss rate.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.branch-instructions
observations: perf-event.branch-instructions: Retired branches.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.branch-misses
observations: perf-event.branch-misses: Mispredicted branches. >1% = predictor unhappy.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.bus-cycles
observations: perf-event.bus-cycles: Bus cycles (memory subsystem).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.stalled-cycles-frontend
observations: perf-event.stalled-cycles-frontend: Cycles where frontend stalled (instruction fetch/decode).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.stalled-cycles-backend
observations: perf-event.stalled-cycles-backend: Cycles where backend stalled (execution, memory).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.task-clock
observations: perf-event.task-clock: Time on CPU. Useful baseline for any sampled run.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cpu-clock
observations: perf-event.cpu-clock: CPU clock (different from task-clock — counts even when not on CPU if sampled).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.context-switches
observations: perf-event.context-switches: cs counter.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cpu-migrations
observations: perf-event.cpu-migrations: Times task moved between CPUs (signal of poor affinity / NUMA crossings).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.page-faults
observations: perf-event.page-faults: Page faults total. -e page-faults:u (user) / :k (kernel).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.minor-faults
observations: perf-event.minor-faults: Page faults satisfiable without disk IO.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.major-faults
observations: perf-event.major-faults: Page faults requiring disk IO. High = thrashing or swap activity.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.alignment-faults
observations: perf-event.alignment-faults: Misaligned memory access (kernel may emulate).

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.emulation-faults
observations: perf-event.emulation-faults: Floating-point or instruction emulation.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.dTLB-load-misses
observations: perf-event.dTLB-load-misses: Data TLB load misses. Indicator of working-set spilling TLB capacity.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.iTLB-load-misses
observations: perf-event.iTLB-load-misses: Instruction TLB load misses.

name: linux.debugging.cfg.perf-event.cgroup-event
observations: perf-event.cgroup-switches: Per-cgroup context switch counter.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecStart
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecStart: The main command. Can be prefixed with `-` (ignore non-zero exit), `+` (run as root regardless of User=), `!` (skip exec privileges), `:` (don't expand specifiers). Multiple ExecStart= for Type=oneshot.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecStartPre
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecStartPre: Run before ExecStart. Failure aborts unit start. Multiple lines run sequentially; can prefix with `-` to tolerate failure.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecStartPost
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecStartPost: Run after ExecStart confirmed started (Type-dependent: simple=immediately, exec=after execve, notify=after READY=1).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecReload
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecReload: Run on systemctl reload. Often `kill -HUP $MAINPID`.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecStop
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecStop: Run on stop request. If absent, systemd sends KillSignal.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ExecStopPost
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ExecStopPost: Run after stop completes (cleanup).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.User
observations: systemd-exec-directive.User: Drop privileges to this user before ExecStart.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.Group
observations: systemd-exec-directive.Group: Group to run as.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.SupplementaryGroups
observations: systemd-exec-directive.SupplementaryGroups: Additional GIDs.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.DynamicUser
observations: systemd-exec-directive.DynamicUser: Allocate ephemeral UID/GID for this service. Implies sandboxing defaults.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.WorkingDirectory
observations: systemd-exec-directive.WorkingDirectory: CWD before ExecStart. ~ = home of User=.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.RootDirectory
observations: systemd-exec-directive.RootDirectory: chroot to this dir before exec.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.Environment
observations: systemd-exec-directive.Environment: Per-service env vars.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.EnvironmentFile
observations: systemd-exec-directive.EnvironmentFile: Read env from file (one KEY=VAL per line). Prefix with `-` to tolerate missing file.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PassEnvironment
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PassEnvironment: Inherit named env vars from systemd's environment.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.UnsetEnvironment
observations: systemd-exec-directive.UnsetEnvironment: Strip env vars.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.StandardInput
observations: systemd-exec-directive.StandardInput: stdin source.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.StandardOutput
observations: systemd-exec-directive.StandardOutput: stdout destination.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.StandardError
observations: systemd-exec-directive.StandardError: stderr destination.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.SyslogIdentifier
observations: systemd-exec-directive.SyslogIdentifier: Identifier in journal SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER field.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.SyslogFacility
observations: systemd-exec-directive.SyslogFacility: Syslog facility for forwarded log lines.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateTmp
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateTmp: Fresh /tmp + /var/tmp namespace.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateDevices
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateDevices: Minimal /dev (just null/zero/full/urandom/tty/ptmx).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateNetwork
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateNetwork: Fresh netns with only loopback.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateIPC
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateIPC: Fresh IPC namespace.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateUsers
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateUsers: Fresh user namespace (UID 0 inside, real user outside).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.PrivateMounts
observations: systemd-exec-directive.PrivateMounts: Fresh mount namespace (MS_PRIVATE).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectSystem
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectSystem: Make filesystem RO. strict = entire FS RO except /dev/proc/sys; full = /usr+/boot+/efi RO; true = /usr+/boot RO.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectHome
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectHome: Hide /home/root /run/user.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectClock
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectClock: Forbid changing system clock.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectHostname
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectHostname: Forbid changing hostname (private UTS namespace).

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectKernelLogs
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectKernelLogs: Forbid reading kernel ring buffer.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectKernelModules
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectKernelModules: Forbid loading kernel modules.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectKernelTunables
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectKernelTunables: Forbid writes to /proc/sys, /sys/kernel.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectControlGroups
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectControlGroups: Make /sys/fs/cgroup RO.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.ProtectProc
observations: systemd-exec-directive.ProtectProc: Limit /proc visibility of other processes.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.NoNewPrivileges
observations: systemd-exec-directive.NoNewPrivileges: Set the prctl PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit. Required for unprivileged seccomp.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.SystemCallFilter
observations: systemd-exec-directive.SystemCallFilter: Per-service seccomp filter. e.g. SystemCallFilter=@system-service.

name: linux.systemd.cfg.exec.SystemCallErrorNumber

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.rw
observations: mount-option-common.rw: Read-write (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.ro
observations: mount-option-common.ro: Read-only.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.exec
observations: mount-option-common.exec: Allow exec of binaries (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.noexec
observations: mount-option-common.noexec: Disallow exec. Common on /tmp, /var, /home for hardening.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.suid
observations: mount-option-common.suid: Honor setuid/setgid bits (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.nosuid
observations: mount-option-common.nosuid: Ignore setuid/setgid. Hardening for /tmp, /home, container rootfs.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.dev
observations: mount-option-common.dev: Allow access to device nodes (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.nodev
observations: mount-option-common.nodev: Block device-node access. Container rootfs always nodev.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.atime
observations: mount-option-common.atime: Update atime on every read (slow).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.noatime
observations: mount-option-common.noatime: Never update atime.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.relatime
observations: mount-option-common.relatime: Update atime only if older than mtime/ctime or > 24h. The modern default.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.strictatime
observations: mount-option-common.strictatime: Strict POSIX atime semantics. Rarely needed.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.lazytime
observations: mount-option-common.lazytime: Update timestamp in memory; flush only on stat/sync/fdatasync. Reduces metadata writes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.nodiratime
observations: mount-option-common.nodiratime: Don't update directory atimes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.sync
observations: mount-option-common.sync: All IO synchronously (huge perf hit; data integrity for removable media).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.async
observations: mount-option-common.async: Async writes (default; fast).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.dirsync
observations: mount-option-common.dirsync: Sync metadata dir ops (rename, link, unlink, ...).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.defaults
observations: mount-option-common.defaults: = rw,suid,dev,exec,auto,nouser,async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.user
observations: mount-option-common.user: Allow non-root users to mount.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.nouser
observations: mount-option-common.nouser: Only root can mount (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.auto
observations: mount-option-common.auto: Mount with mount -a (default for fstab entries).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-common.noauto
observations: mount-option-common.noauto: Skip on mount -a. Mount on demand only.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.data-ordered
observations: mount-option-ext4.data=ordered: Data written before metadata (default). Crash-safe but slower than writeback.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.data-writeback
observations: mount-option-ext4.data=writeback: Data + metadata async. Fastest; can leak data after crash (stale blocks visible).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.data-journal
observations: mount-option-ext4.data=journal: Full data journaling. Strongest crash consistency, slowest.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.barrier
observations: mount-option-ext4.barrier: Use write barriers for ordering (correctness). Default.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.nobarrier
observations: mount-option-ext4.nobarrier: Disable barriers. Faster but unsafe except on battery-backed cache controllers.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.commit
observations: mount-option-ext4.commit=N: Sync interval for delayed writes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.delalloc
observations: mount-option-ext4.delalloc: Delayed allocation (default). Reduces fragmentation.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.nodelalloc
observations: mount-option-ext4.nodelalloc: Disable delayed alloc.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.discard
observations: mount-option-ext4.discard: Issue TRIM on every delete (vs periodic fstrim).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.errors
observations: mount-option-ext4.errors=remount-ro|continue|panic: Behavior on FS error.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.journal-checksum
observations: mount-option-ext4.journal_checksum: Add checksums to journal.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.journal-async-commit
observations: mount-option-ext4.journal_async_commit: Async journal commits. Risky.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.dioread-nolock
observations: mount-option-ext4.dioread_nolock: Direct IO without inode lock. Helps parallel-DIO workloads (databases).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.user-xattr
observations: mount-option-ext4.user_xattr: Allow user.* xattrs (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.acl
observations: mount-option-ext4.acl: POSIX ACL support (default).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.quota
observations: mount-option-ext4.quota: Enable quota.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.usrquota
observations: mount-option-ext4.usrquota: User quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.grpquota
observations: mount-option-ext4.grpquota: Group quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.prjquota
observations: mount-option-ext4.prjquota: Project quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.stripe
observations: mount-option-ext4.stripe=N: RAID stripe alignment hint.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-ext4.i-version
observations: mount-option-ext4.i_version: 64-bit inode version (NFSv4 needs).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.allocsize
observations: mount-option-xfs.allocsize=N: Speculative-prealloc unit (helps reduce fragmentation).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.inode64
observations: mount-option-xfs.inode64: Allow inodes anywhere on FS (default ≥3.7). inode32 = first 1TB only (legacy 32-bit compat).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.logbufs
observations: mount-option-xfs.logbufs=N: Number of in-memory log buffers (1-8).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.logbufsize
observations: mount-option-xfs.logbufsize=N: Log buffer size (16k/32k/64k/128k/256k).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.noquota
observations: mount-option-xfs.noquota: Disable quotas (XFS is quota-on by default if mkfs.xfs included).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.usrquota
observations: mount-option-xfs.usrquota|uquota: Enable user quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.grpquota
observations: mount-option-xfs.grpquota|gquota: Group quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.prjquota
observations: mount-option-xfs.prjquota|pquota: Project quotas.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.discard
observations: mount-option-xfs.discard: Online TRIM.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.attr2
observations: mount-option-xfs.attr2: Use attr2 inode-format optimization.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-xfs.swalloc
observations: mount-option-xfs.swalloc: Stripe-width allocation.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.lowerdir
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.lowerdir=PATH[:PATH...]: Read-only base layer(s). Multiple : separated; first wins.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.upperdir
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.upperdir=PATH: Read-write top layer.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.workdir
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.workdir=PATH: Empty dir on same FS as upperdir for atomic ops.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.redirect-dir
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.redirect_dir=on|off|follow|nofollow: Allow renaming dirs across overlays via redirect xattr.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.metacopy
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.metacopy=on|off: Copy only metadata on first write (vs full file). Saves space when only chmod/chown.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.xino
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.xino=on|off|auto: Stable inode numbers across overlay layers.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.userxattr
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.userxattr: Use user.* xattrs (vs trusted.*) — required for unprivileged overlay (rootless).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.volatile
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.volatile: No fsync (faster, data lost on crash). Used by ephemeral container layers.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.index
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.index=on|off: Index dir for upper-lower hard-link tracking. Required for metacopy/redirect.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-overlayfs.nfs-export
observations: mount-option-overlayfs.nfs_export=on|off: Allow NFS export of overlay.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.size
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.size=N[%]: Max FS size. Suffix %. e.g. size=1G or size=10%.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.nr-blocks
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.nr_blocks=N: Like size but in blocks.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.nr-inodes
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.nr_inodes=N: Max inodes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.mode
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.mode=OCTAL: Root-dir permissions (default world-write+sticky for /tmp-style).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.uid
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.uid=N: Root-dir owner.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.gid
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.gid=N: Root-dir group.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.huge
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.huge=never|always|within_size|advise: Use transparent hugepages.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.mpol
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.mpol=POLICY: NUMA mempolicy: default, prefer, bind, interleave, local.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-tmpfs.noswap
observations: mount-option-tmpfs.noswap: Don't swap out tmpfs pages.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.subvol
observations: mount-option-btrfs.subvol=PATH: Mount specific subvolume.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.subvolid
observations: mount-option-btrfs.subvolid=N: Mount subvolume by ID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.compress
observations: mount-option-btrfs.compress=zstd|zlib|lzo[:LEVEL]: Transparent compression.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.compress-force
observations: mount-option-btrfs.compress-force=ALG: Force compression even on incompressible files.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.autodefrag
observations: mount-option-btrfs.autodefrag: Auto-defragment on small random writes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.discard
observations: mount-option-btrfs.discard[=async]: TRIM. async = batched TRIM (less perf hit).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.space-cache
observations: mount-option-btrfs.space_cache=v1|v2: Free-space cache version.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.degraded
observations: mount-option-btrfs.degraded: Allow mount with missing devices (RAID degraded).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.nodatacow
observations: mount-option-btrfs.nodatacow: Disable COW for new files (existing unchanged). For databases that don't want btrfs COW interfering.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.mount-btrfs.commit
observations: mount-option-btrfs.commit=N: Sync interval (seconds).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.meminfo
observations: proc-control-file./proc/meminfo: System memory snapshot: MemTotal, MemFree, MemAvailable, Buffers, Cached, SwapTotal, SwapFree, Slab, etc.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.cpuinfo
observations: proc-control-file./proc/cpuinfo: Per-CPU info: model name, MHz, cache, flags.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.loadavg
observations: proc-control-file./proc/loadavg: 1/5/15min load avg + running/total tasks + last PID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.uptime
observations: proc-control-file./proc/uptime: Seconds since boot + idle CPU-seconds.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.stat
observations: proc-control-file./proc/stat: CPU + interrupts + ctxt switches counters.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.diskstats
observations: proc-control-file./proc/diskstats: Per-block-device IO counters.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.partitions
observations: proc-control-file./proc/partitions: Major:Minor + size + name of all partitions.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.filesystems
observations: proc-control-file./proc/filesystems: FS types kernel can mount.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.mounts
observations: proc-control-file./proc/mounts: Active mounts (alias /proc/self/mounts).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.swaps
observations: proc-control-file./proc/swaps: Active swap devices/files.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.modules
observations: proc-control-file./proc/modules: Loaded kernel modules + ref counts.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.kallsyms
observations: proc-control-file./proc/kallsyms: Kernel symbol table (CAP_SYSLOG to see addresses).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.cmdline
observations: proc-control-file./proc/cmdline: Kernel boot command line.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.version
observations: proc-control-file./proc/version: Kernel version + build info.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.pid-status
observations: proc-control-file./proc/<pid>/status: Per-process status (state, UIDs, threads, mem, signal masks, caps).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.pid-io
observations: proc-control-file./proc/<pid>/io: Per-process IO counters (rchar, wchar, syscr, syscw, read_bytes, write_bytes, cancelled_write_bytes).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.pid-limits
observations: proc-control-file./proc/<pid>/limits: Per-process rlimits.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.proc-control.pid-cgroup
observations: proc-control-file./proc/<pid>/cgroup: Per-process cgroup membership.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-queue-scheduler
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/scheduler: Active IO scheduler. Selectable values in [brackets]: mq-deadline, kyber, bfq, none.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-queue-nr-requests
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/nr_requests: Per-queue request depth. Higher = more parallelism, higher latency tail.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-queue-read-ahead-kb
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/read_ahead_kb: Read-ahead window. 0 disables; databases often set 0 or low.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-queue-rotational
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/rotational: 1 = rotational (HDD), 0 = SSD.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-size
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/size: Device size in 512B sectors.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-discard-granularity
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/discard_granularity: Min TRIM size.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-discard-max-bytes
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/queue/discard_max_bytes: Max single TRIM.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.block-removable
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/<dev>/removable: Removable media (USB, CD).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.fs-ext4-mb-stream-req
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/fs/ext4/<dev>/mb_stream_req: ext4 mballoc stream request threshold.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.fs-overlay-version
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/fs/overlay/features/*: Per-feature support indicators.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.sysfs-attr.dm-name
observations: sysfs-attribute./sys/block/dm-N/dm/name: device-mapper friendly name.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_RDONLY
observations: open-flag.O_RDONLY: Read-only.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_WRONLY
observations: open-flag.O_WRONLY: Write-only.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_RDWR
observations: open-flag.O_RDWR: Read+write.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_CREAT
observations: open-flag.O_CREAT: Create if missing. Requires mode arg.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_EXCL
observations: open-flag.O_EXCL: With O_CREAT: fail if exists. Atomic 'create-only'.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_NOCTTY
observations: open-flag.O_NOCTTY: Don't make terminal a controlling tty.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_TRUNC
observations: open-flag.O_TRUNC: Truncate file to 0 if exists+writable.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_APPEND
observations: open-flag.O_APPEND: Atomically seek-to-end before each write.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_NONBLOCK
observations: open-flag.O_NONBLOCK: Non-blocking mode (read returns EAGAIN if no data).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_SYNC
observations: open-flag.O_SYNC: Synchronous IO — write returns only after data on disk.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_DSYNC
observations: open-flag.O_DSYNC: Sync data only (not all metadata).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_DIRECT
observations: open-flag.O_DIRECT: Bypass page cache. Buffer + size alignment required.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_LARGEFILE
observations: open-flag.O_LARGEFILE: 32-bit-process flag for >2GB files. Implicit on 64-bit.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_NOFOLLOW
observations: open-flag.O_NOFOLLOW: Fail if path is symlink.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_DIRECTORY
observations: open-flag.O_DIRECTORY: Fail if not a directory.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_NOATIME
observations: open-flag.O_NOATIME: Don't update atime on this open.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_CLOEXEC
observations: open-flag.O_CLOEXEC: Close FD on execve. Always-set when atomicity matters (otherwise race with fork+exec).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_PATH
observations: open-flag.O_PATH: Open as 'reference only' — no read/write, but usable for *at(dirfd, ...) syscalls. Lower-overhead than full open.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.open-flag.O_TMPFILE
observations: open-flag.O_TMPFILE: Create unnamed temp file. Made permanent via linkat with AT_EMPTY_PATH. Race-free secure-tmp pattern.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_XDEV
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_XDEV: Forbid crossing mountpoints during resolution.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS: Forbid following /proc/self/* magic-symlinks.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS: Forbid all symlinks.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_BENEATH
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_BENEATH: Forbid escaping below dirfd (no .. traversal above).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_IN_ROOT
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_IN_ROOT: Treat dirfd as root (chroot-like, but per-call). Magic for safe container fs operations.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.openat2-flag.RESOLVE_CACHED
observations: openat2-flag.RESOLVE_CACHED: Only succeed if all dentries cached (fast-path; for nginx-like 'open file or punt').

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_ACCESS
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_ACCESS: File accessed (read).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_MODIFY
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_MODIFY: File modified.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_ATTRIB
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_ATTRIB: Metadata changed (perms, owner, link count).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_CLOSE_WRITE
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_CLOSE_WRITE: Writable file closed. The 'edit done' signal.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE: Read-only file closed.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_OPEN
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_OPEN: File opened.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_MOVED_FROM
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_MOVED_FROM: File moved out (rename source).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_MOVED_TO
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_MOVED_TO: File moved in (rename target).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_CREATE
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_CREATE: Subdir/file created.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_DELETE
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_DELETE: Subdir/file deleted.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_DELETE_SELF
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_DELETE_SELF: Watched file/dir deleted.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_MOVE_SELF
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_MOVE_SELF: Watched file/dir moved.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_UNMOUNT
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_UNMOUNT: Backing FS unmounted.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inotify-mask.IN_Q_OVERFLOW
observations: inotify-watch-mask.IN_Q_OVERFLOW: Event queue overflowed (events lost — bump fs.inotify.max_queued_events).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_ACCESS
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_ACCESS: Read access.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_MODIFY
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_MODIFY: Write.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_OPEN
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_OPEN: Open.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_CLOSE_WRITE
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_CLOSE_WRITE: Writable close.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_CLOSE_NOWRITE
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_CLOSE_NOWRITE: Read-only close.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_OPEN_PERM
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_OPEN_PERM: Permission event for OPEN — kernel waits for ALLOW/DENY.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fanotify.FAN_ACCESS_PERM
observations: fanotify-event-type.FAN_ACCESS_PERM: Permission event for ACCESS.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_READV
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_READV: readv async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_WRITEV
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_WRITEV: writev async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_FSYNC
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_FSYNC: fsync async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_ACCEPT
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_ACCEPT: accept async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_OPENAT
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_OPENAT: openat async.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_READ_FIXED
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_READ_FIXED: Read into pre-registered buffers (zero-copy).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED
observations: iouring-option.IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED: Write from pre-registered buffer.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL
observations: iouring-option.IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL: Polling-mode IO (low-latency, busy-wait CPU).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.io-uring.IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL
observations: iouring-option.IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL: Kernel polls SQ — userspace doesn't need io_uring_enter syscall on submit.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-spec
observations: fstab-field.<fs_spec>: Device. UUID=, LABEL=, /dev/<name>, or //server/share for CIFS.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-file
observations: fstab-field.<fs_file>: Mount point.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-vfstype
observations: fstab-field.<fs_vfstype>: FS type. auto for autodetect.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-mntops
observations: fstab-field.<fs_mntops>: Mount options. Comma-separated.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-freq
observations: fstab-field.<fs_freq>: Dump frequency (almost always 0 these days).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.fstab.field-fs-passno
observations: fstab-field.<fs_passno>: fsck pass order. 0 = skip; 1 = root; 2+ = others (parallel within same number).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.xattr-ns.user
observations: xattr-namespace.user.: User-controlled xattrs. Anyone with write access.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.xattr-ns.system
observations: xattr-namespace.system.: Kernel-managed (POSIX ACLs as system.posix_acl_access).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.xattr-ns.security
observations: xattr-namespace.security.: Security modules: SELinux (security.selinux), file capabilities (security.capability), IMA (security.ima).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.xattr-ns.trusted
observations: xattr-namespace.trusted.: Root-only. Used by docker/runc for storage driver state.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.acl.user-entry
observations: acl-entry-format.u:USER:rwx: Per-named-user permission.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.acl.group-entry
observations: acl-entry-format.g:GROUP:rwx: Per-named-group permission.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.acl.other-entry
observations: acl-entry-format.o::rwx: Other (catch-all).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.acl.mask-entry
observations: acl-entry-format.m::rwx: Mask — caps effective permissions of named entries (named-user/group + non-owner group).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.acl.default-entry
observations: acl-entry-format.default:u:USER:rwx: Default ACL inherited by new files in directory.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.cipher
observations: cryptsetup-option.cipher: Symmetric cipher + mode + IV.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.hash
observations: cryptsetup-option.hash: Hash function for KDF.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.key-size
observations: cryptsetup-option.key-size: Key bits.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.pbkdf
observations: cryptsetup-option.pbkdf: Key derivation: argon2i / argon2id / pbkdf2.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.iter-time
observations: cryptsetup-option.iter-time: Time spent in PBKDF (passphrase-strengthening cost).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.cryptsetup-opt.allow-discards
observations: cryptsetup-option.--allow-discards: Pass TRIM through to underlying device. Information leak vs perf trade-off.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_mode
observations: stat-field.st_mode: File type + permissions. S_IFMT mask + S_IFREG/DIR/LNK/BLK/CHR/FIFO/SOCK + mode bits.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_uid
observations: stat-field.st_uid: Owner UID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_gid
observations: stat-field.st_gid: Owner GID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_size
observations: stat-field.st_size: Logical size in bytes (sparse files: > st_blocks*512).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_blocks
observations: stat-field.st_blocks: Disk usage in 512B blocks (real on-disk space).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_atime
observations: stat-field.st_atime: Access time.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_mtime
observations: stat-field.st_mtime: Modification time (data).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_ctime
observations: stat-field.st_ctime: Change time (metadata changes — chmod/chown/link).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_nlink
observations: stat-field.st_nlink: Hard link count. 0 = file deleted (still open via FDs).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_dev
observations: stat-field.st_dev: Device containing file.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.stat-field.st_ino
observations: stat-field.st_ino: Inode number.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_type
observations: statfs-field.f_type: FS magic number (0xEF53 ext4, 0x58465342 XFS, 0x9123683E btrfs, 0x01021994 tmpfs, 0x9P2000 9p, etc.).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_bsize
observations: statfs-field.f_bsize: Optimal IO block size.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_blocks
observations: statfs-field.f_blocks: Total blocks in FS.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_bfree
observations: statfs-field.f_bfree: Free blocks (incl. reserved).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_bavail
observations: statfs-field.f_bavail: Free blocks available to non-root (excludes reserved).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_files
observations: statfs-field.f_files: Total inodes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_ffree
observations: statfs-field.f_ffree: Free inodes.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_fsid
observations: statfs-field.f_fsid: FS UUID (in stat fsid format).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_namelen
observations: statfs-field.f_namelen: Max filename length (255 typically).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.statfs-field.f_flags
observations: statfs-field.f_flags: Mount flag bits (ST_RDONLY, ST_NOSUID, ST_NODEV, ST_NOEXEC, etc.).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.symlink.MAXSYMLINKS
observations: symlink-behavior.MAXSYMLINKS: Max symlinks followed in path resolution before ELOOP.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.symlink.PATH_MAX
observations: symlink-behavior.PATH_MAX: Max pathname length on Linux.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.symlink.NAME_MAX
observations: symlink-behavior.NAME_MAX: Max single-component filename length.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-mode
observations: inode-field.i_mode: Type + perms (= st_mode).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-uid
observations: inode-field.i_uid: Owner UID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-gid
observations: inode-field.i_gid: Owner GID.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-size
observations: inode-field.i_size: Logical size.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-blocks
observations: inode-field.i_blocks: On-disk blocks (512B units).

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-nlink
observations: inode-field.i_nlink: Hard link count.

name: linux.filesystem.cfg.inode-field.i-flags
observations: inode-field.i_flags: chattr flags: immutable, append-only, no-atime, journal-data, compress, etc.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.containers
observations: pod-spec.containers: Required. List of containers in pod. Each: name, image, command, args, env, resources, ports, volumeMounts, probes, lifecycle, securityContext.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.initContainers
observations: pod-spec.initContainers: Run sequentially before app containers. Each must complete (exit 0). With restartPolicy=Always = native sidecar.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.restartPolicy
observations: pod-spec.restartPolicy: Always = restart on any exit. OnFailure = only non-zero. Never. Jobs require OnFailure or Never.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds
observations: pod-spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.dnsPolicy
observations: pod-spec.dnsPolicy: How DNS is configured. ClusterFirst = cluster DNS first; None = use dnsConfig field.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.dnsConfig
observations: pod-spec.dnsConfig: Override DNS settings. nameservers[], searches[], options[]. Critical for ndots tuning (default 5 = lookup multiplication).

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.hostNetwork
observations: pod-spec.hostNetwork: Use host's network namespace. Required for some node-level pods (kube-proxy, CNI agents).

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.hostPID
observations: pod-spec.hostPID: Share host PID namespace. Used by node-level monitoring.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.hostIPC
observations: pod-spec.hostIPC: Share host IPC namespace.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.shareProcessNamespace
observations: pod-spec.shareProcessNamespace: Containers within pod share PID namespace. Useful for sidecars to see app processes.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.serviceAccountName
observations: pod-spec.serviceAccountName: ServiceAccount whose token is mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.automountServiceAccountToken
observations: pod-spec.automountServiceAccountToken: Disable to prevent SA token mount (security hardening for pods that don't need API access).

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.priorityClassName
observations: pod-spec.priorityClassName: PriorityClass to use. Higher priority pods preempt lower.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.nodeSelector
observations: pod-spec.nodeSelector: Hard node-label match for scheduling.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.affinity
observations: pod-spec.affinity: nodeAffinity, podAffinity, podAntiAffinity. Soft+hard expressions for scheduling.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.tolerations
observations: pod-spec.tolerations: Allow scheduling onto tainted nodes.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.topologySpreadConstraints
observations: pod-spec.topologySpreadConstraints: Spread pods across topology (zone, hostname). maxSkew, topologyKey, whenUnsatisfiable (DoNotSchedule|ScheduleAnyway).

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.imagePullSecrets
observations: pod-spec.imagePullSecrets: References Secret(s) of type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson for private registry pulls.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.subdomain
observations: pod-spec.subdomain: DNS subdomain. With headless service of same name, pod is reachable as <hostname>.<subdomain>.<namespace>.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.hostname
observations: pod-spec.hostname: Override pod's internal hostname.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.runtimeClassName
observations: pod-spec.runtimeClassName: Use specified RuntimeClass (e.g. for gVisor sandboxed runtime).

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.preemptionPolicy
observations: pod-spec.preemptionPolicy: Whether this pod can preempt lower-priority pods.

name: k8s.core.cfg.pod-spec.enableServiceLinks
observations: pod-spec.enableServiceLinks: Inject env vars for all services (legacy Docker-Swarm-compat). Disable for cleaner env.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.image
observations: container-spec.image: Container image. Format: [registry/]repo[:tag][@digest]. Pin to digest for reproducibility.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.imagePullPolicy
observations: container-spec.imagePullPolicy: When to pull image.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.command
observations: container-spec.command: Container entrypoint. Overrides image's ENTRYPOINT.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.args
observations: container-spec.args: Args to entrypoint. Overrides image's CMD.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.env
observations: container-spec.env: Environment variables. valueFrom: configMapKeyRef|secretKeyRef|fieldRef|resourceFieldRef.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.envFrom
observations: container-spec.envFrom: Bulk env from ConfigMap or Secret.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.resources
observations: container-spec.resources: requests + limits. Drives QoS class + scheduler behavior.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.ports
observations: container-spec.ports: Documented ports. INFORMATIONAL — doesn't affect pod IP binding (any port can be reached on pod IP).

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.volumeMounts
observations: container-spec.volumeMounts: Mount pod-spec volumes into container. name, mountPath, subPath, readOnly, mountPropagation.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.livenessProbe
observations: container-spec.livenessProbe: Failure → restart container.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.readinessProbe
observations: container-spec.readinessProbe: Failure → remove from Service endpoints.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.startupProbe
observations: container-spec.startupProbe: Long-startup probe. Suspends liveness until succeeds.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.lifecycle
observations: container-spec.lifecycle: postStart and preStop hooks (httpGet, exec, sleep).

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.securityContext
observations: container-spec.securityContext: Per-container security: runAsUser, runAsGroup, runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities, seccompProfile, privileged.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.tty
observations: container-spec.tty: Allocate TTY (combined with stdin for interactive container).

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.stdin
observations: container-spec.stdin: Keep stdin open.

name: k8s.core.cfg.container.workingDir
observations: container-spec.workingDir: Container CWD.

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.requests-cpu
observations: resource-requests.requests.cpu: CPU reservation (1 = 1 core; 500m = 0.5 core; 100m = 0.1 core). Maps to cgroup cpu.shares (v1) / cpu.weight (v2).

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.requests-memory
observations: resource-requests.requests.memory: Memory reservation (Mi/Gi/Ki/M/G binary or decimal).

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.limits-cpu
observations: resource-limits.limits.cpu: CPU hard cap. Maps to cgroup cpu.cfs_quota_us (v1) / cpu.max (v2). Throttling kicks in at limit.

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.limits-memory
observations: resource-limits.limits.memory: Memory hard cap. Maps to memory.limit_in_bytes (v1) / memory.max (v2). Exceed = OOMKilled (137).

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.requests-ephemeral-storage
observations: resource-requests.requests.ephemeral-storage: Disk reservation for emptyDir + container writable layer. Eviction triggers if exceeded.

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.limits-ephemeral-storage
observations: resource-limits.limits.ephemeral-storage: Hard ephemeral-storage cap. Pod evicted if exceeded.

name: k8s.core.cfg.resources.extended-resource
observations: resource-requests.requests.<extended>: Extended resources (e.g. nvidia.com/gpu, intel.com/qat). Integer-only.

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.httpGet
observations: probe-spec.httpGet: path, port, host, scheme, httpHeaders. Status 200-399 = success.

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.tcpSocket
observations: probe-spec.tcpSocket: port, host. Connection succeeds = success.

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.exec
observations: probe-spec.exec: command[]. Exit 0 = success.

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.grpc
observations: probe-spec.grpc: port, service. gRPC health check (1.24+).

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.initialDelaySeconds
observations: probe-spec.initialDelaySeconds: Wait before first probe.

name: k8s.core.cfg.probe.periodSeconds

name: k8s.core.cfg.deployment-spec.paused

observations: statefulset-spec.persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy: whenDeleted, whenScaled: Retain | Delete. Default Retain (PVC outlives STS).

name: k8s.core.cfg.daemonset-spec.updateStrategy
observations: daemonset-spec.updateStrategy: How DS pods updated.

name: k8s.core.cfg.job-spec.parallelism

name: k8s.core.cfg.job-spec.completionMode

name: k8s.core.cfg.job-spec.backoffLimit

name: k8s.core.cfg.job-spec.activeDeadlineSeconds

name: k8s.core.cfg.cronjob-spec.timeZone
observations: cronjob-spec.timeZone: IANA TZ name (e.g. 'America/New_York'). 1.27+ stable.

name: k8s.core.cfg.cronjob-spec.concurrencyPolicy
observations: cronjob-spec.concurrencyPolicy: Forbid = skip if previous still running. Replace = kill previous + start new.

name: k8s.core.cfg.cronjob-spec.startingDeadlineSeconds
observations: cronjob-spec.startingDeadlineSeconds: Skip schedule if N seconds late.

name: k8s.core.cfg.cronjob-spec.successfulJobsHistoryLimit
observations: cronjob-spec.successfulJobsHistoryLimit: Old successful Jobs kept.

name: k8s.core.cfg.cronjob-spec.failedJobsHistoryLimit
observations: cronjob-spec.failedJobsHistoryLimit: Old failed Jobs kept.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.type

observations: service-spec.selector: Label selector for backing pods.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.ports
observations: service-spec.ports: name, port, targetPort (container port), nodePort (for NodePort/LoadBalancer), protocol.

observations: service-spec.clusterIP: None = headless. Specific IP requires it to be in service CIDR.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.sessionAffinity
observations: service-spec.sessionAffinity: ClientIP = sticky sessions by source IP.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.externalTrafficPolicy
observations: service-spec.externalTrafficPolicy: Local = preserve client IP, only route to local pods (no cross-node hop).

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.internalTrafficPolicy
observations: service-spec.internalTrafficPolicy: Local = only route to pods on same node. For node-local services.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.publishNotReadyAddresses
observations: service-spec.publishNotReadyAddresses: Include not-ready pods in endpoints. For StatefulSets that need to discover peers before all are ready.

name: k8s.core.cfg.service-spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges
observations: service-spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges: Restrict LB access to source IPs (firewall at LB level).

name: k8s.core.cfg.configmap.data
observations: configmap-spec.data: UTF-8 string data.

name: k8s.core.cfg.configmap.binaryData
observations: configmap-spec.binaryData: Base64-encoded binary.

name: k8s.core.cfg.configmap.immutable
observations: configmap-spec.immutable: Once true, cannot modify (only delete). Allows kubelet to skip watch (perf).

name: k8s.core.cfg.secret.type
observations: secret-spec.type: Opaque, kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, kubernetes.io/tls, kubernetes.io/service-account-token, kubernetes.io/basic-auth, kubernetes.io/ssh-auth.

name: k8s.core.cfg.secret.data
observations: secret-spec.data: Base64-encoded values.

name: k8s.core.cfg.secret.stringData
observations: secret-spec.stringData: Convenience — kubectl encodes for you on apply.

observations: rbac-rule.verbs: get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete, deletecollection, impersonate. * = all.

observations: rbac-rule.resourceNames: Restrict to specific named resources.

name: k8s.core.cfg.security-context.readOnlyRootFilesystem

name: k8s.core.cfg.security-context.capabilities.drop
observations: security-context.capabilities.drop: Drop capabilities. ['ALL'] is the hardening default.

observations: well-known-taint.node.kubernetes.io/pid-pressure: PIDs low.

name: k8s.core.cfg.well-known-taint.network-unavailable

name: k8s.core.cfg.well-known-taint.unschedulable
observations: well-known-taint.node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable: Cordoned.

observations: eviction-signal.pid.available: Available PIDs.

observations: service-type.LoadBalancer: Cloud LB. Requires cloud-controller-manager.

observations: service-spec.ipFamilyPolicy: Dual-stack policy.

observations: ingress-rule.path: URL path to match. e.g. /api.

observations: ingress-rule.pathType: Match semantics. Prefix is the safe default.

observations: ingress-annotation.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: Backend read timeout.

observations: ingress-annotation.alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/inbound-cidrs: AWS ALB controller: source CIDR allowlist.

observations: kube-proxy-config.mode: Service-implementation mode.

observations: kube-proxy-config.iptables.minSyncPeriod: Min interval between iptables updates triggered by Service changes.

name: k8s.networking.cfg.kube-proxy.ipvs-scheduler
observations: kube-proxy-config.ipvs.scheduler: IPVS LB algorithm.

name: k8s.networking.cfg.kube-proxy.clusterCIDR
observations: kube-proxy-config.clusterCIDR: Pod CIDR range. Used for source-NAT detection.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.imagepullbackoff
observations: common-failure.ImagePullBackOff: Image pull failed and backoff active. Check: typo, registry auth, network, rate-limit.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.crashloop
observations: common-failure.CrashLoopBackOff: Container repeatedly crashing. Check: --previous logs, command/args correctness, missing env.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.oomkilled
observations: common-failure.OOMKilled: Memory limit exceeded. Check: actual usage, leaks, resize limit.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.failed-scheduling
observations: common-failure.FailedScheduling: No fit. Check: node capacity, taints, affinity, PVC binding.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.failed-mount
observations: common-failure.FailedMount: Volume mount failed. Check: PVC bound, secret/configmap exists, CSI driver healthy.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.evicted
observations: common-failure.Evicted: Node-pressure eviction. Check: node disk/memory pressure, pod priority, QoS.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.pending-stuck
observations: common-failure.Stuck Pending: Pod can't progress past Pending. Check: events for FailedScheduling/FailedMount/init-container failures.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.terminating-stuck
observations: common-failure.Stuck Terminating: Pod won't disappear. Check: finalizers, volume detach, node availability.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.exit-137
observations: common-failure.Exit 137: SIGKILL (128+9). Most often OOMKilled. Could also be node-eviction or `kubectl delete --force`.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.exit-143
observations: common-failure.Exit 143: SIGTERM (128+15). Graceful stop. From scale-down, rolling update, drain.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.exit-1
observations: common-failure.Exit 1: Generic app error. Check logs.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.exit-125
observations: common-failure.Exit 125: Container start error before app ran. Often runtime config issue.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.dns-resolution-fail
observations: common-failure.DNS resolution fails: Pod can't resolve names. Check CoreDNS pods, kube-dns Service endpoints, pod's resolv.conf.

name: k8s.debugging.cfg.troubleshoot-symptom.timeout
observations: common-failure.Probe timeout: Liveness/readiness/startup timeout. Check probe path, app start time, resource limits.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.cgroupDriver

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.containerRuntimeEndpoint
observations: kubelet-config.containerRuntimeEndpoint: CRI socket. e.g. unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock.

observations: kubelet-config.imageServiceEndpoint: CRI image service socket.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.staticPodPath
observations: kubelet-config.staticPodPath: Static pod manifest directory. Where control-plane pods live in kubeadm clusters.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.maxPods
observations: kubelet-config.maxPods: Max pods per node.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.podsPerCore
observations: kubelet-config.podsPerCore: Override based on CPU count. 0 = use maxPods.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.failSwapOn

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.memorySwap-swapBehavior
observations: kubelet-config.memorySwap.swapBehavior: Per-pod swap policy when swap support enabled.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.featureGates
observations: kubelet-config.featureGates: Per-feature on/off. e.g. NodeSwap=true, MemoryQoS=true.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.serializeImagePulls

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.maxParallelImagePulls
observations: kubelet-config.maxParallelImagePulls: With serializeImagePulls=false, max concurrent pulls.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.runtimeRequestTimeout

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.podPidsLimit

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.kernelMemcgNotification

observations: kubelet-config.tlsPrivateKeyFile: Server key.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.rotateCertificates

observations: kubelet-config.kubeReserved: Reserved for kubelet/runtime.

observations: kubelet-config.systemReservedCgroup: Cgroup path enforcing systemReserved (e.g. /system.slice).

observations: kubelet-config.kubeReservedCgroup: Cgroup path for kubeReserved.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.kubelet.enforceNodeAllocatable
observations: kubelet-config.enforceNodeAllocatable: Enforce: pods, system-reserved, kube-reserved.

observations: kubelet-config.evictionHard: Hard eviction thresholds.

observations: containerd-config.image_pull_progress_timeout: Timeout per image pull layer.

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.containerd.discard-unpacked-layers

name: k8s.runtime.cfg.containerd.disable-snapshot-annotations
