name: devin.enterprise.cfg.builtin-role.account-member
observations: builtin-role-account.Member (account): Built-in account-level role. Standard user access across all organizations in the enterprise.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.idp.groups-claim
observations: sso-config.groups: Required SSO assertion claim for IdP-group → role auto-assignment. SSO provider must send the `groups` array in the assertion.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.security.encryption-in-transit-at-rest
observations: security.encryption.in-transit-and-at-rest: All data is encrypted in transit AND at rest.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.security.mfa-internal-required
observations: security.mfa.internal-required: All Cognition employees and contractors required to use MFA on all primary work applications.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.security.annual-training
observations: security.security-training-cadence: All employees and contractors undergo annual security training (password management, social engineering, phishing).

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.security.vuln-disclosure-email
observations: security.vuln-disclosure-email: Address for reporting security issues.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.deployment.support-email
observations: support.enterprise-sales-email: Cognition Enterprise Sales contact email.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.training.opt-in-default-false
observations: data-controls.default-training-opt-in: By default, Cognition does NOT use customer data for model training. Enterprise customers' data is NEVER used for training regardless of toggle.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.build.typical-duration
observations: build-timing.typical-duration: Typical end-to-end build time, including all three blueprint tiers.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.build.step-timeout
observations: build-timing.step-timeout: Per-step timeout. Same as devbox-tier convention; reaffirmed for enterprise blueprints.

name: devin.enterprise.cfg.rollout.pin-age-limit
observations: snapshot-pinning.pin-age-limit: Maximum age of a build that's still pinnable. Same as devbox tier.

name: devin.product.cfg.feature-flag.devin-review
observations: feature-flag.devin-review.github-enterprise-support: Devin Review supports GitHub Enterprise Server in addition to GitHub Cloud.

name: devin.product.cfg.feature-flag.computer-use-availability
observations: feature-flag.computer-use.availability: Computer Use feature availability. Recent surface — failure modes still being characterized.

name: devin.product.cfg.feature-flag.windows-availability
observations: feature-flag.windows-devbox.availability: Windows DevBox available on a limited basis. Contact us to learn more.

name: devin.product.cfg.feature-flag.pat-availability
observations: feature-flag.personal-access-tokens.availability: Personal Access Tokens currently closed-beta and feature-flagged. NOT available for SSO/enterprise accounts. Contact support for access.

name: devin.product.cfg.plan-feature.session-acu-soft-cap
observations: plan-feature.session-acu-soft-cap: Cognition's recommended per-session ACU ceiling. Performance degrades beyond this. Soft (the product nudges, doesn't enforce).

name: devin.product.cfg.plan-feature.usage-budget-bill-trigger
observations: plan-feature.usage-budget-bill-trigger: Threshold above which usage-based billing triggers an immediate bill (rather than waiting for end-of-cycle).

name: devin.product.cfg.knowledge.scope-per-repo
observations: knowledge-feature.scope: Knowledge entries (product feature) are per-repo. Devin only sees knowledge for the repo it's working on. Distinct from blueprint knowledge sections.

name: devin.product.cfg.devin-review.surface-url
observations: ui-path.devin-review-url: Devin Review surface URL.

name: devin.product.cfg.docs.sitemap-url
observations: doc-source.sitemap.xml: Master URL inventory for the documentation. ~264 KB at fetch time.

name: devin.product.cfg.docs.llms-txt-url
observations: doc-source.llms.txt: AI-friendly index for the documentation. ~52 KB. Lists all available pages.

name: devin.product.cfg.cli-install.url
observations: cli.install-script-url: Install script for Devin for Terminal (the local CLI).

name: devin.product.cfg.frontier-models
observations: model-selection.frontier-model-options: Frontier model options available in Devin for Terminal.

name: devin.product.cfg.bug-catcher.severity-immediate
observations: devin-review-bug-catcher.severity-immediate-attention: Bug confidence label requiring immediate attention. Other levels surfaced as flags.

name: devin.product.cfg.terminal.vt100-supported
observations: terminal.vt100-supported: Devin for Terminal demonstrably runs on VT-100 terminals (the foundational terminal interface since 1978).

name: devin.product.cfg.terminal.renderer-language
observations: terminal.renderer-language: Devin for Terminal's UI uses a custom Rust terminal-rendering library for speed/responsiveness.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.knowledge.scope-tier
observations: knowledge-tier.scope-tier: Tier scopes for knowledge notes. Enterprise = company-wide. Organization = team-level. Repository = project-level. Items are additive across tiers.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.knowledge.note.name
observations: knowledge-note.name: Knowledge note name field.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.knowledge.note.trigger
observations: knowledge-note.trigger: When this knowledge applies. Devin uses to decide relevance.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.knowledge.note.body
observations: knowledge-note.body: Knowledge content body.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.playbook.name
observations: playbook.name: Playbook name.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.playbook.instructions
observations: playbook.instructions: Playbook body / instructions to Devin.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.playbook.macro
observations: playbook.macro: Optional `!`-prefixed macro identifier. Required for label-based triggers.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.playbook.scope
observations: playbook-tier.scope: Playbook tier scopes. Enterprise = visible across all orgs. Organization = scoped to one org.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.secret.tier
observations: secret-tier.tier: Secret tiers. Cascade with more specific winning on name collision.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.secret.naming-best-practice
observations: secret.naming-convention: Best practice — use descriptive UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE names. `INTERNAL_NPM_TOKEN`, not `TOKEN_1`.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.secret.reference-syntax
observations: secret.reference-syntax: Reference syntax for secrets in blueprints, sessions, and playbooks.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.secret.ban-yaml-storage
observations: secret.yaml-storage: Never put secrets directly in blueprint YAML — always use the secrets management UI. Secrets in YAML end up in logs, build artifacts, and audit trails.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.secret.refresh-cadence
observations: secret.refresh-cadence: When a rotated secret value takes effect. Recommended: place credential-writing steps in `maintenance` (not `initialize`) so credentials refresh on every periodic build.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.default-playbook.linear
observations: default-playbook.default-playbook.linear-new-connections: Default playbook used when a Linear ticket is assigned to Devin without a specific label. `!plan` for new Linear connections.

name: devin.knowledge-playbooks.cfg.macro-conventions
observations: playbook-macro.common-macro-names: Common playbook macros surfaced in the docs across Jira/Linear/Slack integrations. Customer-defined macros also supported.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.authors
observations: postmortem-template.authors: List of postmortem authors. Distinct from incident participants — these are the people accountable for the postmortem document itself.

name: methodology.cfg.four-golden-signals.errors
observations: four-golden-signals.errors: Rate of failed requests — explicit (HTTP 500), implicit (200 with wrong content), or by-policy ('any request over 1 second is an error'). End-to-end tests catch wrong-content failures load balancers can't see.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.status
observations: postmortem-template.status: Current state of the postmortem document, e.g., 'Draft', 'In review', 'Complete', 'Complete, action items in progress'. Tracks whether the doc is still being collaboratively written or has reached its final form.

name: methodology.cfg.four-golden-signals.saturation
observations: four-golden-signals.saturation: How 'full' the service is — emphasizing the most-constrained resource (memory, I/O, threads). Many systems degrade before 100% utilization, so a target threshold is essential. Latency increases are often a leading indicator of saturation.

name: methodology.cfg.incident-document.commander
observations: incident-document.commander: Current Incident Commander. Updated explicitly during handoffs ('You're now the incident commander, okay?' / firm acknowledgment).

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.trigger
observations: postmortem-template.trigger: Specific event that initiated the visible failure (often distinct from the underlying root cause). Example: 'Latent bug triggered by sudden increase in traffic.'

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.action-item.bug
observations: postmortem-template.action_items.bug: Linked bug-tracker ID (or 'n/a' if the work isn't bug-tracked). Connects postmortem follow-ups to engineering workflow.

name: methodology.cfg.slo.aggregation-region
observations: slo.aggregation_region: Spatial scope of aggregation: 'all tasks in a cluster', 'per-region', 'per-customer', etc. Standardizing this across SLOs lets you reason about them without re-deriving every time.

name: methodology.cfg.sli.metric-type
observations: sli.metric_type: What's being measured: latency, error_rate, throughput, availability, durability, correctness. Latency + availability are nearly universal across services; durability is critical for storage.

name: methodology.cfg.incident-document.incident-id
observations: incident-document.incident_id: Unique identifier for the incident — typically a sequential number ('incident #465') used throughout email, chat, and the postmortem.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.where-we-got-lucky
observations: postmortem-template.lessons_learned.where_we_got_lucky: Bulleted list of near-misses — things that helped by coincidence, not by design. Surfaces fragile dependencies that might not save us next time. ('The goat teleporter was available for emergency use despite lack of certification.')

name: methodology.cfg.slo.error-budget
observations: slo.error_budget: Allowed failure rate that complements the SLO target — '99.9% target' implies a 0.1% error budget. Tracked daily/weekly, with monthly/quarterly assessment. Used as input to release-cadence decisions.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.date
observations: postmortem-template.date: Date the incident occurred. ISO-8601 format. Top-of-document field in the SRE postmortem template.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.action-item.type
observations: postmortem-template.action_items.type: Action-item category. 'mitigate' = improve incident response; 'prevent' = stop recurrence; 'process' = procedural improvement (testing schedule, playbook); 'other' = miscellaneous (e.g., 'freeze production until error budget recovers').

name: methodology.cfg.sli.collection-side
observations: sli.collection_side: Where the SLI is captured: 'server' (most common, cheapest) or 'client' (catches user-side problems like JavaScript latency that server-side metrics miss).

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.root-causes
observations: postmortem-template.root_causes: Explanation of contributing causes. Often plural — 5 Whys (Ohno 1988) is recommended for surfacing them. Example: 'Cascading failure due to combination of exceptionally high load and a resource leak when searches failed due to terms not being in the corpus.'

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.resolution
observations: postmortem-template.resolution: Sequence of actions taken to mitigate and resolve the incident. Captures both the successful fix and any temporary mitigations that preceded it.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.action-items
observations: postmortem-template.action_items: List of follow-up tasks. Each item: action_item (text), type (mitigate / prevent / process / other), owner, bug ID. Action items translate postmortem learning into concrete change.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.timeline
observations: postmortem-template.timeline: Timestamp-ordered narrative of the incident — UTC times paired with event descriptions. Includes 'OUTAGE BEGINS', 'INCIDENT BEGINS', mitigation actions, 'OUTAGE MITIGATED', 'OUTAGE ENDS', 'INCIDENT ENDS'. Sourced from the live incident document.

name: methodology.cfg.slo.threshold
observations: slo.threshold: Numerical bound the SLI must beat. Example: '99% of calls complete in less than 100 ms' — 100ms is the threshold. Can be lower-bound (latency, error rate) or upper-bound (throughput, success rate).

name: methodology.cfg.incident-declaration.criteria
observations: incident-declaration.criteria: Conditions that escalate an event to incident: (1) need a second team to fix, (2) outage is customer-visible, (3) unsolved after an hour of concentrated analysis. Define BEFORE incidents to avoid rationalization in the moment.

name: methodology.cfg.slo.measurement-window
observations: slo.measurement_window: Time window over which the SLI is aggregated. Example: 'averaged over 1 minute'. Choosing this is non-trivial — too short = noisy, too long = hides bursts.

name: methodology.cfg.sli.aggregation
observations: sli.aggregation: How raw measurements are reduced: rate, average, percentile (median, p95, p99, p99.9). Per the SRE book, percentiles dominate — averages obscure tail behavior.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.what-went-well
observations: postmortem-template.lessons_learned.what_went_well: Bulleted list of things that worked during the incident. Often overlooked but essential for reinforcing good practices and avoiding the trap of treating every postmortem as pure failure.

name: methodology.cfg.sli.measurement-frequency
observations: sli.measurement_frequency: How frequently the underlying samples are collected. Example: 'every 10 seconds'. Per-second can be expensive to collect/store; minute-granularity hides spikes.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.detection
observations: postmortem-template.detection: How the incident was first noticed: monitoring alert, customer report, on-call observation. Surfaces gaps in monitoring (manual discovery often triggers a postmortem on its own).

name: methodology.cfg.four-golden-signals.latency
observations: four-golden-signals.latency: Time to service a request. Track success and failure latencies separately — a 500 served in 5 ms might artificially deflate average latency. Bucket as a histogram (e.g., exponential boundaries: 0–10ms, 10–30ms, 30–100ms, 100–300ms, etc.) so you see the tail.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.impact
observations: postmortem-template.impact: Effect on users, revenue, internal teams. Quantified where possible (e.g., 'estimated 1.21B queries lost, no revenue impact'). Captures why the incident matters beyond technical detail.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.supporting-information
observations: postmortem-template.supporting_information: Links to monitoring dashboards, log captures, IRC logs, IM logs, screenshots, graphs. Captures evidence trail for future reference and trend analysis.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.summary
observations: postmortem-template.summary: One- or two-sentence elevator-pitch summary of the incident: what happened, when, for how long, and the user-visible effect. The first thing a reviewer reads.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.action-item.owner
observations: postmortem-template.action_items.owner: Person responsible for completing this action item. Single owner — accountability over consensus.

name: methodology.cfg.postmortem-template.what-went-wrong
observations: postmortem-template.lessons_learned.what_went_wrong: Bulleted list of failures during incident response — gaps in monitoring, missed steps, slow communication. The action-items section addresses these.

name: methodology.cfg.slo.target
observations: slo.target: Target percentage of requests meeting the SLI bound. Example: '99% of Get RPC calls' — 99 is the target. Often expressed as a percentile (90, 95, 99, 99.9, 99.99) or 'nines' shorthand.

name: methodology.cfg.incident-document.command-post
observations: incident-document.command_post: Where stakeholders find the IC: physical war room, IRC channel ('#shakespeare'), Slack channel, video bridge. Bots in the channel log alerts and traffic for postmortem reconstruction.

name: methodology.cfg.slo.included-requests
observations: slo.included_requests: Which requests count toward the SLO: e.g., 'HTTP GETs from black-box monitoring jobs', 'all user-facing RPC calls'. Excluding internal probes or test traffic prevents skew.

name: methodology.cfg.four-golden-signals.traffic
observations: four-golden-signals.traffic: Demand placed on the system in a high-level service-specific unit: HTTP req/sec for web, network I/O or concurrent sessions for streaming, transactions/retrievals/sec for KV stores.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.user-memory
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_USER_MEMORY: Userspace can supply guest memory regions via KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION. Always present on modern kernels. Firecracker hard-requires this — without it there's no way to map guest RAM.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.user-memory2
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_USER_MEMORY2: Extended memory-region API supporting guest_memfd-backed regions for confidential VMs. Optional; Firecracker uses standard KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION today.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.irqchip
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_IRQCHIP: In-kernel IRQ controller (PIC/IOAPIC on x86). Firecracker hard-requires this — userspace irqchip would push irq emulation cost back into VM exits.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.ioeventfd
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_IOEVENTFD: Bind eventfd to MMIO/PIO write — short-circuits VirtIO doorbell exits. Required for low-overhead VirtIO.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.irqfd
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_IRQFD: Bind eventfd to GSI for in-kernel IRQ raise. Required for low-overhead VirtIO interrupt delivery.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.signal-msi
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_SIGNAL_MSI: Enables KVM_SIGNAL_MSI for direct MSI injection bypassing the routing table. Used by Firecracker for one-shot interrupts.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.tsc-control
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL: Lets userspace set the guest TSC frequency. Required for portable snapshots across hosts with different TSC frequencies. Snapshot restore on a host without this fails if the recorded TSC differs.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.xsave2
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_XSAVE2: Returns the size (bytes) of the dynamic XSAVE buffer for KVM_GET_XSAVE2 / KVM_SET_XSAVE2. Required for AVX-512 / AMX state. Firecracker queries this once at vCPU init.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.nr-vcpus
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_NR_VCPUS: Recommended max vCPUs per VM. Firecracker caps user-requested vcpu_count at this value. (KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS is the hard limit.)

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.max-vcpus
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS: Hard maximum vCPUs per VM. Firecracker's machine_config caps vcpu_count at min(this, 32) per its design constraints.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.set-tss-addr
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_SET_TSS_ADDR: Required by Intel VT-x for its TSS area. Firecracker calls KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR(0xfffbd000) at VM init. Absent on AMD-only kernels (AMD doesn't need TSS area).

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.guest-debug-hw-bps
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_GUEST_DEBUG_HW_BPS: Number of hardware breakpoints supported via KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG. The GDB stub queries this to know the breakpoint budget.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.dirty-log-ring
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_DIRTY_LOG_RING: Per-vCPU ring buffer of dirtied page indices — alternative to KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG bitmap. Lower latency for sparse-write workloads. Optional; Firecracker uses the bitmap path by default.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.manual-dirty-log-protect2
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_MANUAL_DIRTY_LOG_PROTECT2: Decouples dirty-log read from write-protect (no auto-clear on KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG). Required for the two-phase dirty tracking pattern (read, persist, then KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG).

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.x86-disable-exits
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_X86_DISABLE_EXITS: x86-only. Lets userspace ask KVM not to take exits for HLT/MWAIT/PAUSE/CSTATE — the guest's wait instructions are passed to the host CPU directly. Used for latency-sensitive workloads. Firecracker can opt in via the cpu-template configuration.

name: firecracker.kvm.cfg.kvm-cap.arm-vm-ipa-size
observations: kvm-capability.KVM_CAP_ARM_VM_IPA_SIZE: ARM-only. Max guest physical address space size in bits. Firecracker encodes this into the VM type when calling KVM_CREATE_VM on aarch64.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.vcpu-count
observations: machine-config.vcpu_count: Number of vCPUs to expose to the guest. Range 1..32 (Firecracker design cap). Each vCPU runs in its own KVM_RUN-loop thread.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.mem-size-mib
observations: machine-config.mem_size_mib: Guest RAM size in mebibytes. Backed by anonymous host memory (or hugepages, see huge_pages). Snapshot mem_file_path is this size.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.smt
observations: machine-config.smt: x86-only. Whether to expose Intel hyperthreading siblings to the guest's CPUID. Default false to avoid side-channel concerns; production deployments typically keep this off.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.track-dirty-pages
observations: machine-config.track_dirty_pages: Enable KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on the guest RAM region. REQUIRED for diff snapshots — without it, only Full snapshots are possible. Slight runtime overhead from dirty-bit page-walk on KVM exit.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.huge-pages
observations: machine-config.huge_pages: Back guest RAM with hugepages — None (4KiB) or 2M (2MiB hugepages). 2M reduces TLB pressure for large guests but requires reserved hugepages on the host (vm.nr_hugepages sysctl).

name: firecracker.api.cfg.machine-config.cpu-template
observations: machine-config.cpu_template: DEPRECATED. Static CPU template (None|T2|T2A|T2CL|T2S|C3|V1N1). Use PUT /cpu-config for custom templates instead. Affects CPUID + MSR exposure for snapshot portability.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.boot-source.kernel-image-path
observations: boot-source.kernel_image_path: Host filesystem path to an uncompressed Linux kernel (ELF on x86, PE on aarch64). Firecracker does not provide a kernel; user supplies one built per fc-docs-rootfs-kernel.md.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.boot-source.boot-args
observations: boot-source.boot_args: Linux command line passed to the guest kernel. Common additions: console=ttyS0 (serial console output), root=/dev/vda (boot disk), ip=... (static IP). Firecracker validates basic syntax but doesn't constrain content.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.boot-source.initrd-path
observations: boot-source.initrd_path: Optional initramfs file. Loaded into guest memory before kernel boot.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.drive.cache-type
observations: drive.cache_type: Block-device cache mode. Unsafe = drop guest flush requests (faster, but data loss on crash). Writeback = honor flush (correct, slightly slower). Use Writeback for any non-ephemeral data.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.drive.io-engine
observations: drive.io_engine: Block I/O backend. Sync = read/write syscalls. Async = io_uring (kernel >=5.10) for better throughput on high IOPS workloads.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.rate-limiter.bandwidth
observations: rate-limiter.bandwidth: Token bucket controlling bandwidth (bytes). size = bucket capacity, refill_time = ms to refill, one_time_burst = optional one-shot extra capacity.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.rate-limiter.ops
observations: rate-limiter.ops: Token bucket controlling I/O operations per second. Independent of bandwidth bucket.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.logger.level
observations: logger.level: Log verbosity: Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace. Trace adds significant overhead; Debug is the practical-max for production.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.logger.show-log-origin
observations: logger.show_log_origin: Prepend each log line with source-file:line. Useful for debugging Firecracker itself; usually off in production for log volume.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.mmds-config.version
observations: mmds-config.version: MMDS protocol version. V1 = unauthenticated GET (legacy). V2 = session-token-required (PUT to get token, then GET with token header). V2 mimics EC2 IMDSv2 and is recommended for SSRF protection.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.mmds-config.ipv4-address
observations: mmds-config.ipv4_address: Guest-side IPv4 address that resolves to MMDS. Default matches EC2 IMDS for compatibility with cloud-init and other guest tooling.

name: firecracker.api.cfg.snapshot-load.mem-backend.backend-type
observations: snapshot-load.mem_backend.backend_type: How guest RAM is materialized during restore. File = read snapshot mem file into anonymous memory (eager load). Uffd = userfaultfd-backed lazy load — pages copied on first guest access (lower memory footprint, slightly higher first-access latency).

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.api-sock
observations: firecracker-cli.--api-sock: Path to the Unix Domain Socket for the API server. Under jailer, automatically remapped into the chroot.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.id
observations: firecracker-cli.--id: MicroVM identifier. Surfaced in metrics and logs for orchestrator correlation.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.config-file
observations: firecracker-cli.--config-file: Pre-load a full VM config JSON. The microVM auto-starts after parsing — no API calls needed. Useful for headless / one-shot orchestrators.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.no-api
observations: firecracker-cli.--no-api: Disable the API server entirely. Only meaningful with --config-file. Saves resources and removes the API attack surface.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.no-seccomp
observations: firecracker-cli.--no-seccomp: Disable seccomp filters. DEVELOPMENT ONLY — production deployments MUST keep seccomp enabled. Pairs with --gdb-socket since GDB syscalls are blocked by default filter.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.seccomp-filter
observations: firecracker-cli.--seccomp-filter: Override the embedded seccomp filter with a custom seccompiler-bpf-compiled file. Use to permit additional syscalls (e.g., for custom build/debug; never for prod).

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.boot-timer
observations: firecracker-cli.--boot-timer: Emit a boot-timer metric on first guest jiffy. Useful for measuring the boot-time budget (target: ≤125 ms with serial console disabled).

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.gdb-socket
observations: firecracker-cli.--gdb-socket: Enable in-guest GDB stub on a Unix socket. Must be paired with KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG support. Typically requires --no-seccomp because the default filter blocks GDB-required syscalls.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.http-api-max-payload-size
observations: firecracker-cli.--http-api-max-payload-size: Maximum API request body size. Raise for orchestrators that PUT large CPU templates or MMDS payloads.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.cli.mmds-size-limit
observations: firecracker-cli.--mmds-size-limit: Maximum MMDS payload size. Distinct from --http-api-max-payload-size; this caps how large the MMDS data store can grow.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.kernel.config-ptp-1588-clock-kvm
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM: Enables KVM PTP support in the guest kernel — exposes /dev/ptp0 driven by host clock via cheap paravirt calls. Recommended NTP source at scale (avoids per-guest network NTP traffic).

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.kernel.boot-arg-reboot-k
observations: boot-args.reboot=k: Tells Linux to reset CPUs via the i8042 keyboard controller reset line on reboot. Firecracker emulates i8042 just enough to detect this and terminate the process. Required for `reboot` inside x86 guests to cleanly tear down the microVM.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.kernel.boot-arg-panic-1
observations: boot-args.panic=1: On panic, immediately reboot (and thus, via reboot=k, terminate Firecracker). Avoids zombie microVMs after guest kernel panic.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.kernel.boot-arg-pci-off
observations: boot-args.pci=off: Skip PCI bus probing — Firecracker has no PCI bus, so this saves boot time. Default in Firecracker's recommended boot_args.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.kernel.boot-arg-console-ttyS0
observations: boot-args.console=ttyS0: Routes guest kernel printks to the serial console. NOT in default boot_args because console output adds significant boot time. Add for debugging — production should leave off.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.host-sysctl.vm-min-free-kbytes
observations: host-sysctl.vm.min_free_kbytes: Min free memory the kernel keeps reserved. Raise (e.g., 256 MiB) on Firecracker hosts to combat memory fragmentation that causes 'fc_vmm: page allocation failure' errors during high-rate microVM creation.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.host-sysctl.vm-nr-hugepages
observations: host-sysctl.vm.nr_hugepages: Number of 2MiB hugepages to reserve. Required if any microVM uses machine-config.huge_pages=2M. Reserve ahead of microVM scheduling to avoid mid-boot allocation failures.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.host-fd-ulimit.nofile
observations: host-ulimit.nofile: Per-process FD limit. Each Firecracker holds 20+ FDs (eventfd-heavy). For dense hosts running many microVMs in one process tree, raise via /etc/security/limits.conf or systemd LimitNOFILE.

name: firecracker.vmm.cfg.machine-config.cpu-template-static
observations: machine-config.cpu_template (static enum): Static CPU template options: T2, T2A, T2CL, T2S, V1N1, C3. T2 is Intel-broad; T2A AMD-broad; T2CL Cascade Lake-baseline; T2S Skylake-baseline; V1N1 Graviton2-class; C3 Cascade Lake conservative. DEPRECATED in favor of PUT /cpu-config custom templates.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.create.snapshot-type
observations: snapshot-create.snapshot_type: Full = capture all guest memory; Diff = capture only pages dirtied since last snapshot. Diff requires track_dirty_pages=true on the original boot.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.create.snapshot-path
observations: snapshot-create.snapshot_path: Output path for the VM-state metadata file. Contains KVM state, device state, vCPU registers, MSRs, CPUID, and a 64-bit CRC of the file contents.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.create.mem-file-path
observations: snapshot-create.mem_file_path: Output path for the guest memory file. Size = guest RAM for Full; smaller for Diff. Must remain on host for the lifetime of resumed microVMs that point at it.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.create.version
observations: snapshot-create.version: Optional snapshot format version — emit an older format for backward compatibility with older Firecracker readers.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.load.snapshot-path
observations: snapshot-load.snapshot_path: Path to the VM-state file to restore from. Firecracker validates the embedded CRC before proceeding.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.load.mem-backend.backend-type
observations: snapshot-load.mem_backend.backend_type: File = MAP_PRIVATE the memory file (fast restore, file pinned for VM lifetime). Uffd = userfaultfd-driven on-demand load (orchestrator-supplied page handler).

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.load.mem-backend.backend-path
observations: snapshot-load.mem_backend.backend_path: For File backend: path to the memory file. For Uffd backend: path to a Unix socket where Firecracker sends the userfaultfd file descriptor to the handler process.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.load.enable-diff-snapshots
observations: snapshot-load.enable_diff_snapshots: After restore, re-enable KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES so the resumed microVM can produce further diff snapshots. Required if you plan to take diff snapshots from the restored VM.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.load.resume-vm
observations: snapshot-load.resume_vm: When true, automatically transition VM to Resumed after restore. When false (default), VM stays Paused — call PATCH /vm{state=Resumed} when ready.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.machine-config.track-dirty-pages
observations: machine-config.track_dirty_pages: Sets KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES on the guest RAM region. REQUIRED for taking diff snapshots later. Slight per-write overhead from KVM dirty-bit page-walk.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.host.cgroup-v2
observations: host-prerequisite.cgroup-v2: Snapshots restore much faster on cgroups v2 hosts. v1 imposes a significant latency tax (firecracker-microvm/firecracker#2129). Production deployments must use v2.

name: firecracker.snapshots.cfg.host.kvm-cap-tsc-control
observations: host-prerequisite.KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL: Required on the RESTORE host if the original snapshot was taken on a host with a different TSC frequency. Without it, restore fails with a TSC mismatch error.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.id
observations: jailer-cli.--id: Unique microVM identifier. Used as the cgroup leaf name and chroot subdirectory. Must be unique per host since the chroot path collides on duplicates.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.uid
observations: jailer-cli.--uid: Non-privileged uid the Firecracker process runs as. Must have read+write access to /dev/kvm (typically via the kvm group). Production: per-microVM unique uid for additional isolation.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.gid
observations: jailer-cli.--gid: Non-privileged gid. Common pattern: gid in the kvm group for /dev/kvm access.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.cgroup-version
observations: jailer-cli.--cgroup-version: Cgroup hierarchy version. v2 recommended for production (snapshot restore is significantly slower under v1 — see snapshots leaf).

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.cgroup
observations: jailer-cli.--cgroup: Cgroup setting written by jailer when creating the leaf cgroup. Examples: cpuset.cpus=0, cpu.shares=512 (v1), cpu.max='100000 100000' (v2 — 100ms quota per 100ms period), memory.max=536870912 (v2 — 512 MiB cap).

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.parent-cgroup
observations: jailer-cli.--parent-cgroup: Relative parent cgroup path. Lets orchestrators nest microVM cgroups (e.g., 'fleet/tenant_A'). On v2 + no --cgroup, jailer MOVES the process to this existing cgroup — exits with error if it has subtree-controllers enabled.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.chroot-base-dir
observations: jailer-cli.--chroot-base-dir: Base directory for chroot trees. Final chroot path: <base>/<exec_file_name>/<id>/root. Set to a fast disk (NVMe) for snapshot-heavy workloads.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.netns
observations: jailer-cli.--netns: Path to a network namespace handle (e.g., /var/run/netns/myvm or /proc/<pid>/ns/net). Jailer setns()s into it before exec. If omitted, Firecracker shares the host's netns — much weaker isolation.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.resource-limit-fsize
observations: jailer-cli.--resource-limit fsize: Max file size (bytes) the Firecracker process can create. Use to bound runaway snapshot-mem files. Applied via setrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE).

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.resource-limit-no-file
observations: jailer-cli.--resource-limit no-file: Max FD count for the Firecracker process. setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE). 2048 is sufficient for moderate device counts; raise for vsock-heavy or VirtIO-MMIO-dense guests (Firecracker uses 20+ FDs by baseline).

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.daemonize
observations: jailer-cli.--daemonize: setsid() + redirect stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null. Useful when launching from a non-systemd orchestrator. Do NOT combine with structured logging that expects the original tty.

name: firecracker.jailer.cfg.cli.new-pid-ns
observations: jailer-cli.--new-pid-ns: Spawn Firecracker into a new PID namespace via clone(CLONE_NEWPID). Firecracker appears as PID 1 inside the namespace; host-side PID is recorded in <chroot_dir>/<exec_file_name>.pid.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-mmio
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO: Required for VirtIO-MMIO transport — Firecracker's default device transport. All VirtIO devices (block, net, vsock, balloon, entropy) need this on aarch64 always; on x86_64 either this or PCI VirtIO.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-blk
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK: Guest VirtIO block driver. Required to mount any /dev/vd* disk attached via PUT /drives.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-net
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_NET: Guest VirtIO network driver. Required for any network interface attached via PUT /network-interfaces.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-vsockets
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS: Guest vsock driver. Required for any host↔guest vsock comms via PUT /vsock.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-balloon
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_BALLOON: Guest balloon device driver. Required for memory reclaim via PATCH /balloon. Pairs with CONFIG_MEMORY_BALLOON.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-hw-random-virtio
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_HW_RANDOM_VIRTIO: Guest VirtIO entropy/RNG driver. Required for the entropy device attached via PUT /entropy. Without it, guest may stall at boot waiting for entropy.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-random-trust-cpu
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_RANDOM_TRUST_CPU: Guest uses CPU RNG instructions (RDRAND etc.) to initialize the kernel RNG. Available kernel ≥5.10. Reduces boot-time entropy starvation even without virtio-rng.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-acpi
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_ACPI: x86_64. Required for the ACPI boot path. Supersedes the legacy MPTable/cmdline-virtio mechanism. CONFIG_PCI must also be enabled (ACPI initialization relies on it even when no PCI devices are exposed).

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-pci
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_PCI: x86_64. Required for ACPI boot AND for --enable-pci VirtIO transport. Counter-intuitive: needed even when no PCI devices exist (ACPI init dependency).

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-pci
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_PCI: Guest VirtIO over PCI driver. Required only when Firecracker is started with --enable-pci.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-kvm-guest
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_KVM_GUEST: x86_64. Enables KVM paravirt features in the guest including CONFIG_KVM_CLOCK (kvm-clock timekeeping). Effectively required for any modern x86_64 guest.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-x86-mpparse-deprecated
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_X86_MPPARSE: x86_64 LEGACY. Enables MPTable parsing — the pre-ACPI device-enumeration mechanism. Disabling it (CONFIG_X86_MPPARSE=n) avoids the double-init warnings when the guest also has CONFIG_ACPI=y. Recommended off for ACPI-only guests.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.guest-kernel.config-virtio-mmio-cmdline-devices-deprecated
observations: guest-kernel.CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO_CMDLINE_DEVICES: x86_64 LEGACY. Enables device enumeration via virtio_mmio.device= kernel cmdline params. Disable when using ACPI to avoid double-init.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.kernel-cmdline.nomodule
observations: boot-args.nomodule: Disables loadable kernel module support. Smaller attack surface; faster boot. Default in Firecracker's boot_args.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.kernel-cmdline.8250-nr-uarts-0
observations: boot-args.8250.nr_uarts=0: Disables 8250 UART probing. Combined with `console=ttyS0` being absent from defaults, makes serial-console output a deliberate opt-in for debugging.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.kernel-cmdline.i8042-flags
observations: boot-args.i8042.noaux i8042.nomux i8042.dumbkbd: Skips probing the i8042 keyboard controller for an auxiliary mouse, multiplexing, and state control. Saves boot time. Firecracker emulates i8042 only enough to detect the reset-line write that terminates the process.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.kernel-cmdline.swiotlb-noforce
observations: boot-args.swiotlb=noforce: Disables forced software bounce-buffer (SWIOTLB) usage. Faster I/O when not needed for high memory or DMA constraints.

name: firecracker.security.cfg.cli.enable-pci
observations: firecracker-cli.--enable-pci: x86_64 only. Switch all VirtIO devices to PCI transport instead of MMIO. Higher throughput + lower latency. Requires PCI-enabled guest kernel and removing pci=off from boot_args.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.network-interface.iface-id
observations: network-interface.iface_id: Firecracker-internal identifier. Used in URLs (PUT /network-interfaces/{iface_id}) and MMDS network_interfaces[] lists. NOT visible inside the guest — guest names its own interfaces (typically eth0, eth1...).

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.network-interface.host-dev-name
observations: network-interface.host_dev_name: Host TAP interface name (must already exist). Firecracker opens /dev/net/tun and binds via TUNSETIFF. Permission: requires the running uid to have access to the TAP (typically by being in the netdev group or via uid match on tap-creation).

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.network-interface.guest-mac
observations: network-interface.guest_mac: Guest-side MAC address. If null, randomly generated. Convention with default rootfs: encode the guest IP in the last 4 bytes (06:00:AC:10:00:02 ↔ 172.16.0.2).

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.rate-limiter.bandwidth.size
observations: rate-limiter.bandwidth.size: Token-bucket capacity in bytes. Bucket fills at refill_time interval to this maximum.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.rate-limiter.bandwidth.refill-time
observations: rate-limiter.bandwidth.refill_time: Time in milliseconds to refill the bucket from empty to full. Throughput = size / (refill_time/1000) bytes/sec at sustained rate.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.rate-limiter.bandwidth.one-time-burst
observations: rate-limiter.bandwidth.one_time_burst: Optional one-shot extra capacity available at startup. Lets a guest burst once above the steady-state limit (e.g., for initial download). Once consumed, never refills.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.rate-limiter.ops.size
observations: rate-limiter.ops.size: Operations-per-period bucket capacity. For network: operations = packets. Independent of bandwidth bucket — both must permit the action.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.mmds-config.network-interfaces
observations: mmds-config.network_interfaces: List of network interface iface_ids on which MMDS-destined packets are intercepted. At least one required — without it, MMDS returns 400 on any request.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.mmds-config.imds-compat
observations: mmds-config.imds_compat: Forces all MMDS responses to use AWS IMDS plain-text format regardless of Accept header. Lets EC2-IMDS-targeted guest tooling (cloud-init, AWS SDK metadata libs) work unmodified against Firecracker.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.host-sysctl.ip-forward
observations: host-sysctl.net.ipv4.ip_forward: Required to be 1 on host for any NAT-based or bridge-based microVM routing. Without it, packets from TAP to physical NIC are dropped at the FORWARD chain.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.host-tap.txqueuelen
observations: host-tap.txqueuelen: TAP send queue length on the host. Tunable for high-throughput workloads — too small drops packets; too large adds latency. Set via `ip link set <tap> txqueuelen <N>`.

name: firecracker.networking.cfg.mmds-config-version
observations: mmds-config.version: MMDS protocol version. V1 = simple GET (deprecated, removed in next major); V2 = session-token-required (mimics IMDSv2). Always use V2 for multi-tenant or untrusted guest workloads.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.host-kernel-cmdline.quiet
observations: host-kernel-cmdline.quiet: Suppresses non-critical kernel messages on the host console. Recommended for Firecracker production hosts to avoid console-write latency degrading snapshot restore times.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.host-kernel-cmdline.loglevel
observations: host-kernel-cmdline.loglevel=1: Reduce kernel log verbosity to KERN_ALERT only. Pairs with `quiet` for minimal serial-console writes. Recommended for Firecracker hosts.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.host-kernel-cmdline.nosmt
observations: host-kernel-cmdline.nosmt: Disable SMT (Hyperthreading) at boot. Required for tenant-separation hosts to mitigate speculation side channels (Spectre, MDS).

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.modprobe.kvm.min-timer-period-us
observations: modprobe-kvm.min_timer_period_us: Minimum interval between KVM-injected timer interrupts. Higher values reduce kvm-pit kthread CPU overhead but also coarsen APIC timer granularity. Workload-test before raising.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.cpu-shares
observations: cgroup-v1.cpu.cpu.shares: Relative CPU-time weight when CPUs are contended. Per-microVM share calculation: this_share / sum(all_shares_at_this_level). v1; in v2 use cpu.weight.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.cpu-cfs-period-us
observations: cgroup-v1.cpu.cpu.cfs_period_us: CFS scheduler period. Combined with cfs_quota_us yields a hard CPU bandwidth cap. v2 equivalent: cpu.max (period/quota pair).

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.cpu-cfs-quota-us
observations: cgroup-v1.cpu.cpu.cfs_quota_us: Max CPU time in μs allowed per cfs_period_us window. quota=50000, period=100000 → 50% of one CPU. Hard cap (vs cpu.shares which is a weight).

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.memory-limit-in-bytes
observations: cgroup-v1.memory.memory.limit_in_bytes: Hard memory cap. OOM-kills the cgroup if exceeded. v2 equivalent: memory.max.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.memory-memsw-limit-in-bytes
observations: cgroup-v1.memory.memory.memsw.limit_in_bytes: Memory + swap cap. Required to prevent the OOM killer from being bypassed via swap. v2 equivalent: memory.swap.max + memory.max combined.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.memory-soft-limit
observations: cgroup-v1.memory.memory.soft_limit_in_bytes: Soft cap — only enforced under host memory contention. Lets cgroups use surplus memory normally but reclaims down to the soft limit when other workloads need it. v2 equivalent: memory.high.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.sysfs.ksm-run
observations: sysfs./sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run: 0 = stop KSM and unmerge all pages; 1 = run KSM; 2 = stop KSM but keep merged pages. Set to 0 on Firecracker hosts to mitigate page-dedup side channels.

name: firecracker.setup.cfg.cgroup-v1.blkio-throttle-io-serviced
observations: cgroup-v1.blkio.blkio.throttle.io_serviced: Bound the number of disk I/Os issued by the cgroup. Format: '<major>:<minor> <read_iops> <write_iops>'. v2 equivalent: io.max.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-cluster
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CLUSTER: Cluster name the agent registers into. Common cause of 'instance not appearing in cluster' = wrong value or unset.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-reserved-ports
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_RESERVED_PORTS: TCP ports excluded from task placement on this instance. Add ports any host-process needs.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-reserved-ports-udp
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_RESERVED_PORTS_UDP: UDP ports excluded from task placement.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-engine-auth-type
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_TYPE: Format of registry credentials in ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-engine-auth-data
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA: Docker registry credentials; format per ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_TYPE. Stored on instance — sensitive; consider per-task repositoryCredentials with Secrets Manager instead.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.aws-default-region
observations: ecs-agent-env.AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: AWS region for ECS API calls. Override only if cross-region debugging.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.docker-host
observations: ecs-agent-env.DOCKER_HOST: Docker daemon endpoint. Override for non-default Docker socket location.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-loglevel
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOGLEVEL: Agent log verbosity.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-loglevel-on-instance
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOGLEVEL_ON_INSTANCE: Override log level for the on-instance log file separately from logging-driver-collected logs.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-logfile
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOGFILE: Where the agent writes its log file. Bind-mounted to /var/log/ecs/ecs-agent.log on Amazon Linux.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-checkpoint
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CHECKPOINT: Persist agent state across restarts. Loss of state forces re-discovery of running tasks.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-datadir
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_DATADIR: Inside the agent container, where state is persisted. Pair with ECS_HOST_DATA_DIR via bind-mount.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-host-data-dir
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_HOST_DATA_DIR: Host-side directory bind-mounted into the agent container for state + metadata files.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-updates-enabled
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_UPDATES_ENABLED: Whether to exit-for-update when ECS service requests an agent update. Required for managed agent updates.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-disable-metrics
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_DISABLE_METRICS: Disable per-task metrics gathering. Saves CPU on instances with very high task density.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-poll-metrics
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_POLL_METRICS: Switch from streaming docker stats to polling. Reduces dockerd CPU usage on dense instances.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-polling-metrics-wait-duration
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_POLLING_METRICS_WAIT_DURATION: Interval for ECS_POLL_METRICS=true. Range 5-20s. Recommended <18s to avoid memory-reservation metric instability.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-reserved-memory
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_RESERVED_MEMORY: MiB to subtract from the instance's reported memory capacity. Used by scheduler when placing tasks. Doesn't actually reserve.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-available-logging-drivers
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_AVAILABLE_LOGGING_DRIVERS: Docker logging drivers tasks can use. Must include 'awslogs' for CloudWatch Logs integration.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-disable-privileged
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_DISABLE_PRIVILEGED: Forbid task definitions from setting privileged=true. Recommended for multi-tenant clusters.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-selinux-capable
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_SELINUX_CAPABLE: Advertise SELinux support to ECS so task defs can request SELinux opts (Z-mode mounts only).

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-apparmor-capable
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_APPARMOR_CAPABLE: Advertise AppArmor support to ECS so task defs can request AppArmor profiles.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-engine-task-cleanup-wait-duration
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENGINE_TASK_CLEANUP_WAIT_DURATION: How long to keep stopped task containers around (for log + exit-code retrieval) before cleanup.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-engine-task-cleanup-wait-duration-jitter
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENGINE_TASK_CLEANUP_WAIT_DURATION_JITTER: Random jitter added to per-task cleanup wait. Prevents thundering-herd cleanup.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-manifest-pull-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_MANIFEST_PULL_TIMEOUT: Timeout for image manifest fetch. Raise on slow networks or large image registries.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-container-stop-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CONTAINER_STOP_TIMEOUT: Instance-scoped default time to wait for SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL on container stop. Per-task override available via stopTimeout in task def.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-container-start-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CONTAINER_START_TIMEOUT: Timeout for docker-start to complete. Raise for slow-starting containers.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-container-create-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CONTAINER_CREATE_TIMEOUT: Timeout for docker-create. Minimum 1m enforced.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-task-iam-role
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_TASK_IAM_ROLE: Master switch for IAM Roles for Tasks. Must be true for task-IAM credentials endpoint to work.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-task-iam-role-network-host
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_TASK_IAM_ROLE_NETWORK_HOST: Extend task-IAM-role injection to host-network-mode tasks (requires extra iptables setup).

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-disable-image-cleanup
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_DISABLE_IMAGE_CLEANUP: Disable automated image cleanup. Set to true if you want full control over image GC.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-image-cleanup-interval
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_IMAGE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL: Time between image cleanup cycles. Min 10m enforced.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-image-minimum-cleanup-age
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_IMAGE_MINIMUM_CLEANUP_AGE: Minimum age (since pull) before an image is eligible for cleanup.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-image-pull-behavior
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_IMAGE_PULL_BEHAVIOR: Image-pull policy. 'always' is the secure choice (always pull, fail task on pull failure). 'default' falls back to cache.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-image-pull-inactivity-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_IMAGE_PULL_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT: After Docker pull completes, wait this long for extraction. Raise for large Windows containers.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-image-pull-timeout
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_IMAGE_PULL_TIMEOUT: Total docker-pull timeout. Raise for huge images on slow networks.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-instance-attributes
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_INSTANCE_ATTRIBUTES: Custom attributes registered on initial instance registration only. After registration, use PutAttributes API.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-instance-ip-compatibility
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_INSTANCE_IP_COMPATIBILITY: Override instance IP-stack. Set to ipv6 for IPv6-only instances.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-task-eni
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_TASK_ENI: Enable per-task ENI (awsvpc network mode). Must be true for awsvpc-mode tasks to launch.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-high-density-eni
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_HIGH_DENSITY_ENI: ENI trunking — exceed per-instance ENI limit for awsvpc tasks. Requires Nitro instance + IAM perms.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-cni-plugins-path
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CNI_PLUGINS_PATH: Where the ECS CNI binaries live. Override if vendoring custom CNI.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-awsvpc-block-imds
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_AWSVPC_BLOCK_IMDS: Block 169.254.169.254 from awsvpc tasks. Defends against SSRF leaking the instance role. Recommend true for multi-tenant.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-awsvpc-additional-local-routes
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_AWSVPC_ADDITIONAL_LOCAL_ROUTES: In awsvpc mode, route these prefixes via the host bridge instead of the task ENI.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-container-metadata
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_CONTAINER_METADATA: Write per-container metadata file inside each container; path injected as $ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_FILE. Older alternative to Task Metadata Endpoint.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-task-cpu-mem-limit
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_TASK_CPU_MEM_LIMIT: Enforce task-level cpu+memory cgroup. Sum of containers can't exceed task-level cap.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-cgroup-cpu-period
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CGROUP_CPU_PERIOD: CFS period for task-level CPU bandwidth. Range 8-100ms. Lower = finer scheduling granularity, more overhead.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-task-metadata-rps-limit
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_TASK_METADATA_RPS_LIMIT: Steady-state and burst rate limits (req/sec) for task-metadata + agent-API endpoints. Raise for metadata-heavy workloads.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-enable-spot-instance-draining
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_ENABLE_SPOT_INSTANCE_DRAINING: Auto-DRAIN on Spot interruption notice. STRONGLY recommend true on any Spot-backed cluster.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-log-driver
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOG_DRIVER: Logging driver for the AGENT container itself (not tasks).

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-log-output-format
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT: Agent log line format. JSON pairs better with structured-log shippers.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-log-rollover-type
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOG_ROLLOVER_TYPE: Log rotation trigger.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-log-max-file-size-mb
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_LOG_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB: Max log file size before rotation (when rollover-type=size).

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-container-instance-tags
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CONTAINER_INSTANCE_TAGS: Tags applied to the container instance on registration.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-container-instance-propagate-tags-from
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_CONTAINER_INSTANCE_PROPAGATE_TAGS_FROM: If ec2_instance, propagate EC2 instance tags to the container instance. Requires ec2:DescribeTags IAM perm.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-disable-docker-health-check
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_DISABLE_DOCKER_HEALTH_CHECK: Disable Docker container HEALTHCHECK monitoring by the agent.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-nvidia-runtime
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_NVIDIA_RUNTIME: Docker runtime name for NVIDIA GPU passthrough. Linux only.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-agent-pid-namespace-host
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_AGENT_PID_NAMESPACE_HOST: Run agent container with --pid=host. Required for SELinux-enforcing + Docker SELinux policy. DISABLES Exec/EBS-attach/ServiceConnect/FireLens. Agent ≥1.94.0.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-agent-labels
observations: ecs-agent-env.ECS_AGENT_LABELS: Labels added to the agent container itself (visible via docker inspect). Read by ecs-init, not the agent.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-skip-localhost-traffic-filter
observations: ecs-init-env.ECS_SKIP_LOCALHOST_TRAFFIC_FILTER: Disable ecs-init's iptables rule that drops non-local packets to 127.0.0.0/8. Insecure; for diagnostic use only.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-allow-offhost-introspection-access
observations: ecs-init-env.ECS_ALLOW_OFFHOST_INTROSPECTION_ACCESS: Disable ecs-init's iptables rule blocking off-host access to introspection port 51678. Insecure; diagnostic only.

name: ecs.agent.cfg.env.ecs-offhost-introspection-interface-name
observations: ecs-init-env.ECS_OFFHOST_INTROSPECTION_INTERFACE_NAME: Primary interface used for the off-host introspection block rule. Override if auto-detection picks the wrong interface.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.family
observations: task-definition.family: Logical name of the task definition. Revision numbering is per-family. Required.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.task-role-arn
observations: task-definition.taskRoleArn: IAM role assumed by container code (the AWS APIs the app calls).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.execution-role-arn
observations: task-definition.executionRoleArn: IAM role for ECS agent infrastructure (ECR pull, CloudWatch Logs write, Secrets/SSM fetch, EFS attach). Required for most non-trivial task defs.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.network-mode
observations: task-definition.networkMode: awsvpc | bridge | host | none. Fargate REQUIRES awsvpc.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.requires-compatibilities
observations: task-definition.requiresCompatibilities: FARGATE, EC2, EXTERNAL — pre-flight validation against the launch type.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.cpu
observations: task-definition.cpu: Task-level CPU. Required on Fargate; optional on EC2. Fargate restricted to discrete values.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.memory
observations: task-definition.memory: Task-level memory. Required on Fargate; combo with cpu must match Fargate matrix.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.runtime-platform.os
observations: task-definition.runtimePlatform.operatingSystemFamily: LINUX | WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_FULL | WINDOWS_SERVER_2019_CORE | WINDOWS_SERVER_2022_FULL | WINDOWS_SERVER_2022_CORE | WINDOWS_SERVER_2025_FULL | WINDOWS_SERVER_2025_CORE.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.runtime-platform.cpu
observations: task-definition.runtimePlatform.cpuArchitecture: X86_64 | ARM64. Linux+ARM64 → Graviton tasks. Service.platformFamily must match.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.ephemeral-storage.size-in-gib
observations: task-definition.ephemeralStorage.sizeInGiB: Fargate-only. Per-task scratch disk size.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.ipc-mode
observations: task-definition.ipcMode: host | task | none. host shares with all containers; task shares within the task; none isolates each container.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.pid-mode
observations: task-definition.pidMode: host | task. Containers see host PIDs (host) or sibling-container PIDs (task). Forbidden on Fargate.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.placement-constraints
observations: task-definition.placementConstraints: EC2 only. memberOf with cluster-query-language expression (e.g., attribute:ecs.instance-type =~ m5.*).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.proxy-configuration
observations: task-definition.proxyConfiguration: App Mesh sidecar proxy config: type=APPMESH, containerName, properties (IgnoredUID, ProxyIngressPort, ProxyEgressPort, AppPorts, EgressIgnoredIPs, EgressIgnoredPorts).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.task.volumes
observations: task-definition.volumes: Task-level volumes. Each entry: name + (host | dockerVolumeConfiguration | efsVolumeConfiguration | fsxWindowsFileServerVolumeConfiguration | configuredAtLaunch).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.volume.efs.filesystem-id
observations: volume.efsVolumeConfiguration.fileSystemId: EFS filesystem to mount. fs-XXXXXXXX format.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.volume.efs.transit-encryption
observations: volume.efsVolumeConfiguration.transitEncryption: TLS for EFS mount traffic. Recommend ENABLED.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.volume.efs.iam
observations: volume.efsVolumeConfiguration.authorizationConfig.iam: Use task-IAM-role for EFS access (vs filesystem-policy alone).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.name
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.name: Per-container identifier within the task. Used in dependsOn, links, mountPoints.sourceContainer references.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.image
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.image: registry/repo:tag or registry/repo@digest. Pull failure = CannotPullContainerError.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.cpu
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.cpu: Per-container CPU shares. Sum across containers ≤ task-level cpu (Linux). 0 = unbounded share.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.memory
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.memory: Hard memory limit. Container OOM-killed if exceeded.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.memory-reservation
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.memoryReservation: Soft memory reservation (lower bound). Used by scheduler. memory and memoryReservation can both be set; reservation < memory.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.command
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.command: Overrides Docker CMD. Each element is one argument (no shell).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.entry-point
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.entryPoint: Overrides Docker ENTRYPOINT. Combined with command for full argv.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.environment
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.environment: Plain-text env vars. Don't put secrets here — use 'secrets' field with Secrets Manager / SSM ARN.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.environment-files
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.environmentFiles: Env vars sourced from S3 .env file. Loaded at task start.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.secrets
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.secrets: Env vars sourced from Secrets Manager (full ARN or with json-key suffix) or SSM Parameter Store. Resolved by agent using executionRoleArn perms.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.essential
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.essential: true: container exit terminates the task. false: sidecar — exit doesn't stop task. ≥1 essential required.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.port-mappings
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.portMappings: Per-container port bindings. Each: containerPort, hostPort (0 = ephemeral on EC2; must = containerPort on awsvpc), protocol (tcp|udp), name (for serviceConnect), appProtocol (http|http2|grpc).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.mount-points
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.mountPoints: Bind a task-level volume into a container path.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.volumes-from
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.volumesFrom: Inherit mounts from another container in the same task. Lets you build init-container patterns where one container populates a volume that another reads.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.depends-on
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.dependsOn: Conditions: START, COMPLETE, SUCCESS, HEALTHY. Defines startup ordering and lifecycle gates.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.start-timeout
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.startTimeout: Per-container override of how long to wait for dependsOn conditions to be satisfied.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.stop-timeout
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.stopTimeout: Per-container SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL grace period.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.health-check.command
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.healthCheck.command: First element: 'CMD' (exec form) or 'CMD-SHELL' (shell form). Rest is the command/args.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.health-check.interval
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.healthCheck.interval: Seconds between health checks.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.health-check.timeout
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.healthCheck.timeout: Per-check timeout.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.health-check.retries
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.healthCheck.retries: Consecutive failures before container marked UNHEALTHY.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.health-check.start-period
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.healthCheck.startPeriod: Grace period after container start during which failures don't count toward retries.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.log-driver
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.logConfiguration.logDriver: awslogs | awsfirelens | splunk | fluentd | gelf | journald | json-file | syslog. Must be in agent's ECS_AVAILABLE_LOGGING_DRIVERS.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.log-options
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.logConfiguration.options: Driver-specific KV. For awslogs: awslogs-group, awslogs-region, awslogs-stream-prefix, awslogs-create-group, mode (blocking|non-blocking).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.log-secret-options
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.logConfiguration.secretOptions: Driver options sourced from Secrets Manager / SSM (e.g., splunk-token).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.repository-credentials
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.repositoryCredentials: Secrets Manager ARN holding {username, password} for private registry. Per-task alternative to ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA on the agent.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.user
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.user: Run container process as this user. Best practice: non-root (UID > 0).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.working-directory
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.workingDirectory: Override Docker WORKDIR.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.privileged
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.privileged: Docker --privileged. Forbidden on Fargate. Blocked instance-wide via ECS_DISABLE_PRIVILEGED.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.readonly-root-filesystem
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.readonlyRootFilesystem: Mount container's root FS read-only. Strongly recommend true for security; pair with tmpfs / volumes for writable scratch.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.docker-labels
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.dockerLabels: Docker labels on the container. Used by log-routing (e.g., FireLens), monitoring tag-extraction.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.docker-security-options
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.dockerSecurityOptions: Docker --security-opt. SELinux / AppArmor labels (e.g., 'apparmor:my-profile', 'label:type:my-domain'). Requires ECS_SELINUX_CAPABLE / ECS_APPARMOR_CAPABLE.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.ulimits
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.ulimits: Per-container ulimits. Common: nofile (raise to 65535+ for fd-heavy apps), nproc, memlock.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.capabilities-add
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.capabilities.add: Linux capabilities to grant beyond Docker default. e.g. NET_ADMIN, SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.capabilities-drop
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.capabilities.drop: Drop capabilities. Recommend ['ALL'] + add only what's needed.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.devices
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.devices: Host device passthrough. permissions: read|write|mknod array.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.init-process-enabled
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.initProcessEnabled: Inject tini as PID 1. Reaps zombies; forwards signals. Recommend true for any non-init-aware container.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.shared-memory-size
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.sharedMemorySize: /dev/shm size. Forbidden on Fargate.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.linux-parameters.tmpfs
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.linuxParameters.tmpfs: tmpfs mounts. Pairs well with readonlyRootFilesystem=true.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.firelens-config.type
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.firelensConfiguration.type: FireLens log-router engine.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.firelens-config.options
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.firelensConfiguration.options: Common: enable-ecs-log-metadata=true|false, config-file-type=s3|file, config-file-value=<path-or-arn>.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.system-controls
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.systemControls: Per-container sysctls. e.g. net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time. Restricted set on Fargate.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.dns-servers
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.dnsServers: Override container /etc/resolv.conf nameservers.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.container.extra-hosts
observations: task-definition.containerDefinitions.extraHosts: Inject /etc/hosts entries. Doesn't apply on Fargate (use service-discovery).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.desired-count
observations: service-definition.desiredCount: Number of running tasks the service maintains. Scheduler launches replacements when tasks stop.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.deployment-minimum-healthy-percent
observations: service-definition.deploymentConfiguration.minimumHealthyPercent: % of desiredCount that must remain healthy during deployment. Lower = faster but riskier.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.deployment-maximum-percent
observations: service-definition.deploymentConfiguration.maximumPercent: % of desiredCount the deployer may run simultaneously. 200% = double-up before scale-down (rolling).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.deployment-circuit-breaker-enable
observations: service-definition.deploymentConfiguration.deploymentCircuitBreaker.enable: Auto-rollback failed deployments after threshold consecutive task failures.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.deployment-circuit-breaker-rollback
observations: service-definition.deploymentConfiguration.deploymentCircuitBreaker.rollback: When circuit-breaker fires, automatically rollback to last-known-good revision.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.capacity-provider-strategy
observations: service-definition.capacityProviderStrategy: Replaces launchType with weighted distribution across capacity providers (e.g., FARGATE 70%, FARGATE_SPOT 30%; base reserves N tasks for one provider before weighting).

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.placement-strategy
observations: service-definition.placementStrategy: EC2 only. spread (across attribute), binpack (cpu|memory), random.

name: ecs.task-defs.cfg.service.health-check-grace-period-seconds
observations: service-definition.healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds: Grace period after task start before unhealthy LB checks count toward task replacement. Critical for slow-starting apps behind a load balancer.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cluster.settings.container-insights
observations: cluster.settings.containerInsights: Cluster-level Container Insights opt-in. Enables CloudWatch metrics + log aggregation. 'enhanced' adds container-level metrics (more cost, more detail).

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cp.managed-scaling.target-capacity
observations: capacityProvider.autoScalingGroupProvider.managedScaling.targetCapacity: Target % utilization that ECS-driven scaling tries to maintain. <100 keeps slack capacity for fast scale-out at the cost of unused EC2.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cp.managed-scaling.minimum-scaling-step-size
observations: capacityProvider.autoScalingGroupProvider.managedScaling.minimumScalingStepSize: Smallest delta ECS will request. Raise to avoid thrashing on small load changes.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cp.managed-scaling.maximum-scaling-step-size
observations: capacityProvider.autoScalingGroupProvider.managedScaling.maximumScalingStepSize: Largest delta per scaling event. Lower to throttle large bursts.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cp.managed-scaling.instance-warmup-period
observations: capacityProvider.autoScalingGroupProvider.managedScaling.instanceWarmupPeriod: How long after instance launch until ECS considers it 'in service' (eligible for tasks). Match to AMI warm-up time + agent registration time.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cp.managed-termination-protection
observations: capacityProvider.autoScalingGroupProvider.managedTerminationProtection: When ENABLED, ECS sets ASG instance scale-in protection on instances running tasks. Critical to prevent ASG from terminating busy instances during scale-in.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.cluster.default-strategy
observations: cluster.defaultCapacityProviderStrategy: Used by run-task / create-service when no strategy is explicitly given. The base+weight semantics described under capacity-provider concept.

name: ecs.launch-types.cfg.task.platform-version
observations: task.platformVersion: Fargate platform version. 1.4.0+ required for: ephemeralStorage, secret-options, EFS in-transit-encryption, x86_64 runtime improvements. Pin if you need behavioral stability across rotations.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.cfg.instance-type.suffix-metal
observations: ec2-instance-type.<family>.metal: Bare-metal variant naming. e.g. i3.metal, m5.metal. Distinguishes from non-bare-metal members of the same family.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.cfg.nitro-version.tcp-idle-timeout
observations: nitro-v6.tcp_idle_timeout: Default established-TCP-connection idle timeout. Reduced from 432,000s to 350s in Nitro v6 — apps relying on long-idle connections must implement keepalives.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.cfg.nitro-version.max-network-bandwidth
observations: nitro-vN.max_network_bandwidth: Per-network-card max bandwidth ceiling. Actual instance throughput may be lower; check per-instance specs.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.cfg.bare-metal.boot-timeout-budget
observations: bare-metal-launch.boot_timeout_budget: Operational consideration: account for up to 20 minutes from 'running' to 'network-reachable' on bare-metal launches. Tune ASG / orchestrator timeouts accordingly.

name: ecs.nitro-baremetal.cfg.host.intel-vt-required
observations: host-cpu.intel-vt-x or amd-v: Required CPU feature for nested KVM (running Firecracker / KVM / VMware as a guest). Bare-metal: always present. Virtualized Nitro: present only on C8i/M8i/R8i (with ~10% overhead).

name: ecs.networking.cfg.network-config.awsvpc.subnets
observations: task.networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.subnets: Subnets the task ENI may be placed in. Multiple subnets = AZ-spread. Required for awsvpc tasks on Fargate or with create-service.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.network-config.awsvpc.security-groups
observations: task.networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.securityGroups: SG(s) attached to the task ENI. Per-task isolation point — tighter than instance-level SG.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.network-config.awsvpc.assign-public-ip
observations: task.networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.assignPublicIp: Assign a public IP to the task ENI. Required ENABLED for tasks in public subnets that need to reach the internet without NAT.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.account-setting.awsvpc-trunking
observations: account-setting.awsvpcTrunking: Account-wide opt-in for ENI trunking. Increases per-instance awsvpc task density (5-20x). Per-IAM-principal scope.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.account-setting.container-instance-long-arn
observations: account-setting.containerInstanceLongArnFormat: New ARN format with cluster name embedded. Required for tagging-authorization features.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.account-setting.task-long-arn
observations: account-setting.taskLongArnFormat: New ARN format for tasks. Required for tagging.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.task-eni.eni-id
observations: task-eni.eniId: The ENI attached to an awsvpc task. Returned in DescribeTasks attachments[]. Use to look up the IP, SG, subnet.

name: ecs.networking.cfg.tmds.uri-env
observations: container-env.ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI / ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4: Per-container env vars pointing at the task-metadata endpoint. v4 adds /task/stats. Apps should prefer v4 if available.

name: ecs.troubleshooting.cfg.events-history-size
observations: service.events[]: DescribeServices returns the last 100 service events. Older events are dropped — capture continuously via EventBridge if you need long-term audit.

name: ecs.troubleshooting.cfg.task-stopped-reason-max-length
observations: task.stoppedReason: Free-form reason string. 255-char cap means long error messages are truncated. Pair with stopCode (TaskFailedToStart | EssentialContainerExited | UserInitiated | ServiceSchedulerInitiated | SpotInterruption | TerminationNotice) for machine-classifiable signal.
